text: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey 76th ORDINARY GENERAL ASSEMBLY MEETING OPENING SPEECH DURMU? YILMAZ PRESIDENT 24th Apr 2008, Ankara I. Introduction 1. Dear Shareholders of our Bank, Distinguished Guests, Distinguished Members of the Press, 76th Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey Welcome to the Ordinary General Assembly Meeting. 2. I will begin my speech by making a brief assessment of the international financial crisis, which has recently caused significant turmoil on a global scale and whose direct and indirect effects are felt on our country's economy. Then, after summarizing the main macroeconomic developments in our country for 2007, I will share with you my evaluations on inflation developments and monetary policy implementations in the last part of my speech. II. Developments in International Markets Dear Guests, 3. Since August 2007, the first effects of the financial crisis, which started from high-risk housing loans in the US real estate markets and then spread to the money and capital markets, began to be felt in the real economy, and the expectations that the US economy would enter a recession strengthened. In addition, the view that the financial crisis will lead to an increasingly global economic slowdown has become clear. However, uncertainties remain about the extent and severity of this slowdown. These uncertainties have led international banks to focus on the risk of non-repayment, to be reluctant to extend loans and to experience liquidity problems in financial markets. 4. The high rate of losses incurred by major financial institutions that provide loans to real estate markets in the United States and the increase in recession concerns in the United States led to a significant deterioration of risk perception and increased risk premiums in developing countries. Turkey has also been adversely affected by these developments and Turkey's risk premium has increased in parallel with other developing countries. 1 Chart 1: Risk Indicators 400 2 500 YTL/Kur Sepeti (0.5 Euro0.5 USD) 370 340 1,9 EMBI Turkey EMBI 5-year KIFT Rates (right axis) 400 310 1,8 300 280 1,7 250 1,6 200 220 1,5 190 100 160 1,4 130 0 1,3 100 1,2 -100 01/03/2006 02/13/2006 03/24/2006 05/04/2006 06/14/2006 07/25/2006 09/01/2006 10/13/2006 11/22/2006 01/04/2007 02/14/2007 03/27/2007 05/07/2007 06/15/2007 07/26/2007 09/05/2007 10/16/2007 11/27/2007 01/08/2008 02/19/2008 03/31/2008 02.01.2006 02.03.2006 02.05.2006 02.07.2006 02.09.2006 02.11.2006 02.01.2007 02.03.2007 02.05.2007 02.07.2007 02.09.2007 02.11.2007 02.01.2008 02.03.2008 Source: Bloomberg. 5. However, it should be noted here that the effects of the international financial crisis on the Turkish economy at this stage are more limited than those created by the deterioration in global liquidity conditions in May-June 2006. This shows that our country's economy has become relatively more resilient and resilient in the face of international shocks. However, I would like to emphasize that the fact that vulnerabilities have decreased compared to past periods should not be perceived as the absence of risks. 6. Fiscal discipline and the continuity of structural reforms remain critical to our economy's resilience if risk perceptions continue to deteriorate. In this context, the continuation of the process of harmonization and convergence with the European Union and the continuity of the efforts to implement the structural reforms foreseen in the economic program are of great importance. In addition, I would like to point out that it is imperative to protect and further improve the gains made in public finances and the reforms carried out in the institutional infrastructure. Dear Guests, 7. Another important development observed in the international markets in 2007 is the increase in the prices of crude oil, agricultural products and other commodities. These increases create an upward pressure on inflation not only in our country but also in the world. 8. International crude oil prices, harsh winter conditions in the US and China, rapid declines in US and OECD stocks, geopolitical uncertainties in Nigeria and rapid depreciation of the US dollar 2 03.01.2006 03.03.2006 03.05.2006 03.07.2006 03.09.2006 03.11.2006 03.01.2007 03.03.2007 03.05.2007 03.07.2007 03.09.2007 03.11.2007 03.01.2008 03.03.2008 factors. Sudden supply disruptions caused by geopolitical uncertainties are putting pressure on prices in the crude oil market, where idle capacity ratios are low, which increases the interest of speculative investors and exacerbates price pressure. The price of a barrel of crude oil rose to USD 95 at the end of 2007, and in the current month it has risen to USD 114, leaving behind the highest level since 1979 in real terms. Prices of commodities and agricultural products in international markets also showed an upward trend throughout 2007. The use of agricultural products such as corn, wheat and sugar beet in biofuel production for energy purposes and the yield losses caused by adverse weather conditions in the producer countries have led to an increase in food prices on a global scale. In addition, the improvement in the overall welfare levels of developing countries, especially China and India, leads to demand-driven pressures on commodity prices. In addition to the increasing demand, the resulting supply-side problems attract the attention of speculative investors and cause price movements to harden even more. I will touch on the effects of the increase in international energy and commodity prices on our country's economy in more detail in the last part of my speech when I talk about inflation developments. 3 Chart 3: Commodity Price Developments 800 530 Commodity Prices Metal Prices 750 Energy Prices (right axis) Agricultural Prices (right axis) 480 700 650 430 600 380 550 500 330 450 280 400 230 350 300 180 03.01.2006 03.04.2006 03.07.2006 03.10.2006 03.01.2007 03.04.2007 03.07.2007 03.10.2007 03.01.2008 03.04.2008 Source. After briefly summarizing the developments in the international markets in 2007, I would like to mention the main macroeconomic developments related to our country in this part of my speech. III. Macroeconomic Developments 11. As I have stated in some of my previous presentations and speeches, a radical transformation took place in the Turkish economy following the crisis in 2001. The prudent monetary and fiscal policies implemented after the crisis and the comprehensive structural reforms implemented together with them formed the cornerstones of this transformation process. With the stable environment provided in the economy, inflation entered a rapid downward trend and high growth rates were achieved one after another. In the period from 2002 to the present day, the average annual real growth rate has been 6.8 percent. 12. The uninterrupted growth observed in our economy since 2002 continued in 2007 and the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased by 4.5 percent in this year. The GDP growth rate, which was 7.6 percent and 4.0 percent in the first two quarters of the year, respectively, was 3.4 percent in the last two quarters. GDP growth in 2007 was the lowest annual growth since 2002. In the slowdown in the growth rate this year, uncertainties about the general elections, agriculture due to drought 4 The contraction of the value added in the sector, the fluctuations in international markets and the monetary tightening implemented since mid-2006 have been effective. Due to the revival in private sector demand in the second half of 2007, the contribution of final domestic demand to growth increased compared to the first half of the year. On the other hand, net external demand, which made a positive contribution to growth in the first half of 2007, contributed negatively to growth with the acceleration in imports in the second half of the year. Although domestic demand, which has been in a slowdown trend since the second half of 2006, showed a gradual recovery in 2007, the support of aggregate demand conditions to the process of decline in inflation continued. 14. The transformation process observed in the Turkish economy since 2001 has also led to significant changes in the structure of employment. While 35 percent of the total employees were employed in the agricultural sector in 2002, this rate decreased to 25 percent by the end of 2007. The increase in employment demand of non-agricultural sectors has been one of the important factors in the decline in agricultural employment. In this context, it is observed that the labor used as a production input is redistributed among the sectors. The shift of the labor force in the low-productivity agricultural sector to the non-agricultural sectors with higher productivity is a positive process in terms of economic development. However, this 5 The situation has been one of the main reasons why the rapid growth that emerged in the post-2001 period could not create a significant decline in the unemployment rate. 15. In addition to the decline in agricultural employment, another important change in the structure of employment is the decrease in the rate of informal employment. While 52 percent of the total employees were employed without being registered with any social security institution in 2002, this rate decreased to 45 percent as of the last quarter of 2007. 16. While the slowdown in economic activities in 2007 caused the employment growth in non-agricultural sectors to be halted, the decline in agricultural sector employment accelerated with the effect of the drought in agriculture. In 2007, as a result of the decrease in the employment growth rate of the non-agricultural sectors to 2.3 percent and the decrease in the employment of the agricultural sector by 2 percent, the total employment growth was realized as 1.1 percent. Agriculture Non-Farm (Right Axis) 17. The demographic change process experienced by our country leads to an increase in the share of the working population in the total population, which leads to a certain level of rigidity in the unemployment rate. Considering that the labor force participation rate of women will increase in the coming period and the redistribution of labor between sectors will continue, the increase in non-agricultural labor supply is expected to continue. It should not be forgotten that the creation of new employment opportunities for the increased labor supply depends largely on reforms that increase flexibility and reduce costs in labor markets. 6 This will also contribute significantly to the elimination of problems in our social security system by increasing formal employment. 18. Real unit wages have declined continuously in the post-2001 period as a result of productivity increases in the manufacturing industry. However, as of the second quarter of 2007, a slowdown in this trend was observed and real unit wages in the manufacturing industry increased by 2.5 percent in the third quarter of the year. In the last quarter of the year, there was a decrease of 2.3 percent in real unit wages. 19. In order for real unit wages to continue to contribute to the decline in inflation, it is of great importance to implement regulations that will support productivity and improve the investment environment in the medium term. Partial Efficiency (per hour) Dear Guests, 20. As it is known, during the 90s, a permanent discipline in public finances could not be achieved, and public deficits that reached high levels were financed mainly by domestic borrowing. As a result, the total debt stock of the public sector increased rapidly, and with the restructuring of the banking sector after the economic crisis in 2001, the ratio of total net public debt stock to GDP (1998 basic year national income series) reached a level that can be considered quite high as 66.4 percent. But, as I mentioned earlier, the crisis 7 In the aftermath period, with the resolute implementation of the stabilization program and the maintenance of fiscal discipline, budget deficits decreased significantly, while the ratio of total net public debt stock to GDP decreased to 29.1 percent in 2007 as a result of the high level of non-interest budget surplus targets to a large extent. Despite the deviations observed in some expenditure items in 2006 and before, the vitality in domestic demand increased revenues from indirect taxes made a significant contribution to the achievement of non-interest surplus targets. However, with the slowdown in domestic demand in 2007, tax revenues were below the targeted level. In addition, due to the failure to finalize reforms aimed at eliminating structural problems in the public sector, primary expenditures exceeded the target and deviated from the program-defined non-interest surplus target as a result of the increase in health, pension and social assistance expenses items above the projected level. 22. Despite significant reforms aimed at increasing the effectiveness of fiscal policy in the public sector and strengthening the institutional structure, the price of fiscal policy in 2007 was not effectively implemented as a result of the failure to effectively implement measures to control expenditures, especially those arising from structural problems in the social security system. 8 its contribution to ensuring its stability has been limited. As a matter of fact, due to the fact that 2007 was an election year, the increase in expenditures on some items more than the predicted level and the indirect tax increases made on tobacco and petroleum products in November 2007 had an effect on increasing the inflation rate. As can be seen from this assessment, the completion of public sector reforms remains of vital importance in terms of placing public finances on a more solid basis on the one hand and ensuring the permanence of price stability on the other. Dear Guests, 23. In this part of my speech, I would like to briefly touch on the recent developments regarding the current account deficit and its financing, which have been frequently discussed recently. 24The increases observed in export performance in recent years continued in 2007. In this year, exports increased by 23.1 percent compared to last year and reached USD 113.2 billion as a result of the strong performance of traditional sectors such as textile and clothing, as well as the land vehicles and iron and steel sectors. Imports, on the other hand, accelerated in the second half of the year with the effect of a partial recovery in domestic demand and a strong YTL, increasing by 20.6 percent in 2007 compared to the previous year to USD 160.7 billion. As a result, the foreign trade deficit amounted to USD 47.5 billion. 25. The positive performance in exports, strong industrial production and the fact that oil prices have been above the level of 2006 since September have led to a high increase in imports of intermediate goods throughout the year. On the other hand, services revenues increased due to tourism revenues rising to USD 18.5 billion in 2007, but the income balance deficit widened. As a result of these developments, the current account deficit reached USD 38 billion in 2007. The ratio of the current account deficit to GDP, which reached 6.1 percent at the end of 2006, decreased slightly to 5.8 percent at the end of 2007. 9 98-IV 99-II 99-IV 00-II 00-IV 01-II 01-IV 02-II 02-IV 03-II 03-IV 04-II 04-IV 05-II 05-IV 06-II 06-IV 07-II 07-IV Chart 7: Current Account Balance / GDP* (Percent) 3 2 1 0 -1 -2 -3 -4 -5 -6 -7 * With annualized data. Source: CBRT. 26. The fact that the increasing private investments in Turkey in recent years are concentrated in sectors such as automotive, machinery-equipment and electronics, which have a higher share of imported inputs, has been effective in increasing the current account deficit. The rapid rise in the prices of energy imports, especially crude oil, also contributed significantly to the increase in the current account deficit. 27. Despite the increase in the current account deficit, there is a significant improvement in the financing structure of the deficit, especially in the 20062007 period. Direct investments and long-term loans have reached a level that can cover the entire current account deficit. The weight of portfolio investments and short-term loans in financing sources decreased significantly. These positive developments observed on the financing side reduce concerns about the sustainability of the current account deficit. However, it should not be forgotten that achieving a healthier structure of the current account balance and ensuring the continuity of sustainable growth depend on export performance based on productivity and competition increase in the medium and long term. 28. The comprehensive structural reforms implemented in our country after the 2001 crisis have made the functioning of the credit mechanism more effective and healthy. The expectations of the banking system and individuals changed positively, and an increase was observed in the maturities and amounts of loans. As a reflection of these positive developments, the loan volume was increased from the second quarter of 2003 10 has risen markedly from onwards. The expansion in the volume of loans continued in 2007 with the contribution of the continuation of foreign capital inflows into the banking sector and the continuation of the decline in the public debt burden. Although the upward trend in consumer loans continues, the rate of increase slowed down somewhat in the last quarter of the year. It is observed that the slowdown in consumer loans in the last quarter of the year was influenced by decreasing financing opportunities due to fluctuations in international financial markets and an increase in uncertainty perceptions. The recent turmoil in global markets has also once again revealed the importance of banks' liquidity risk management. In this context, it is of great importance for banks to maintain effective liquidity management carefully. In addition, it should not be forgotten that the real sector's foreign currency deficit position poses an indirect credit risk for the banking sector. It is critical that companies do not make one-way exchange rate assumptions and that they protect against currency risk with the help of various financial instruments. Dear Guests, 30. In the last part of my speech, I would like to share with you my evaluations on inflation developments and monetary policy practices in our economy as of the past year and the period we are in. 11 IV. Inflation Developments and Monetary Policy Applications 31As it is known, within the framework of the economic program put into practice after the financial crisis in 2001, our Bank carries out a policy targeting price stability under the floating exchange rate regime. This framework has been called implicit inflation targeting since 2002 and open inflation targeting was introduced in 2006 after the necessary prerequisites such as fiscal discipline, macroeconomic and financial stability were established and all institutional, technical and operational preparations were completed. In this period, a significant distance was taken towards reducing inflation, and after 30 years, the inflation rate fell to single digits in 2004. However, this process of decline in inflation was interrupted in 2006, and inflation targets were significantly exceeded in the first two years of inflation targeting. 32When we look at the experiences of countries that have implemented inflation targeting, it is seen that it is common for inflation to exceed the target. A 2005 study of more than twenty countries that have implemented inflation targeting reveals that countries that have achieved price stability experience significant and long-term deviations from the target by 30 percent and countries that are in the process of reducing inflation by 60 percent.1 In none of these countries, regardless of the magnitude, duration and frequency of the deviation, even if some adjustments have been made to the operational framework, the inflation targeting regime has not been abandoned. 33On the other hand, in the event of deviation from the inflation target, it is critical that transparency and accountability mechanisms are effectively operated. In open letters written to the Government in July and October 2006 and in January 2007, the Central Bank shared with the public the reasons for deviation from the target and the measures to be taken to bring it closer to the target again. Dear Guests, 34. The main reasons why inflation in our country in 2006 and 2007 exceeded the set targets depends largely on external factors. Since the first months of 2006, high increases in oil prices, unprocessed food prices and gold prices have started to adversely affect inflation. This impact has been reflected in global risk perceptions since May. 1 Roger, S. and Stone, M. (2005), d2On Target? The International Experience with Achieving Inflation Targetsd3, IMF Working Paper No. 05/163. 12 With the change and international liquidity conditions turning against developing countries, the YTL has weakened significantly as a result of its depreciation, and inflation expectations have significantly deteriorated. 35. In the face of these negative developments, the Central Bank has pursued a strong monetary tightening route, both by raising policy interest rates and by attracting excess Turkish lira liquidity in the market. Although the 2006 year-end inflation target was exceeded, inflation was brought under control and the inflation rate remained within the uncertainty range determined around the path compatible with the target in the first three quarters of 2007. However, ongoing supply shocks and increases in the prices of managed/directed goods, developments that monetary policy cannot control, have led to a pause in the decline in inflation. At the end of 2007, the inflation rate measured by consumer prices exceeded the upper limit of the uncertainty range announced around the target with 8.4 percent. In the inflation developments in 2007, the increase in food prices was the most important factor limiting the decline in inflation. The increase in food prices is also based on two main reasons, one internal and the other external: First, the decline in the yield of agricultural products due to the drought that was effective in our country in 2007 created a supply-side shock. Secondly, as I mentioned in the first part of my speech, the use of some agricultural products such as corn, wheat and sugar beet in alternative fuel production, the increase in food demand in the world and the increases in agricultural commodity prices have adversely affected domestic food prices through foreign trade. Title: Interview with Anadolu Agency
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: -CENTRAL BANK GOVERNOR SERDENGE82T: (1) -"THE ERA OF MAKING MONEY FROM FOREIGN CURRENCY IS OVER IN THIS COUNTRY" -"INTEREST RATES HAVE REACHED REASONABLE LEVELS WHERE THEY SIT" -"INTEREST RATES ARE AT REASONABLE LEVELS WITH ITS DECLINE, IT IS AT EXORBITANT LEVELS OF INTEREST THE ERA OF MONETIZATION IS ALSO COMING TO AN END" -"AS OF 2006, INTEREST RATE DECISIONS WILL BE VOTED ON IN THE MONETARY POLICY BOARD AND DECISIONS WILL BE TAKEN ACCORDINGLY" ANKARA (A.A)- 16.01.2005 - G9frb9fz Ziya AKKIRAN - The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey Governor S9freyya Serdenge8dti said that the era of making money from foreign currency is over in Turkey, and that the period of making money from interest rates at exorbitant levels is coming to an end with the general level of interest rates falling to reasonable levels. Serdenge8dti answered the questions of Anadolu Agency correspondent about the monetary policies implemented by the Central Bank. The Central Bank Governor reminded that they faced wide opposition in the whole process of reducing inflation. Although this opposition does not have a homogeneous structure, it is possible to talk about its two main wings, Serdenge8dti said, adding that the first of these is the group that has been keeping its assets in foreign currency as much as possible in the inflation environment since before. This group, in the environment of inflation, the Turkish currency is constantly worth Explaining that they protected themselves against inflation because they lost, Serdenge8dti said that only when they switched to the floating exchange rate regime, things changed, and the Turkish currency could gain value as well as lose value from time to time. Serdenge8dti continued as follows: "When it became difficult to predict the exchange rates, with their old habits (somehow its value will increase even more), they had to sometimes buy foreign currency at a high price and then see the Turkish currency gain value. That is why, every time they lose money, they see those who, unlike themselves, invest in Treasury bills and make money, and they say (Is this possible; if calculated in dollars, big money is earned from treasury bonds). In order to get out of the difficult situation they have fallen into with the appreciation of the Turkish currency, on the one hand, they want to keep the current account deficit on the agenda continuously, on the one hand d0 they do not have to be exporters d0 on the other hand, they want the Central Bank to reduce short-term interest rates." Pointing out that those in this group think that both the Turkish currency will lose value and the general level of interest rates will decrease, Serdenge8dti said, "However, as I said before, the Central Bank's lowering of interest rates, on the contrary, adds value to the Turkish currency, and the general level of interest rates or real interest rates are shaped according to the level of public debt, which is still high." -THOSE IN THE SECOND GROUP- Serdenge8dti, the second group has been in the long-term period of foreign exchange He said they knew that "Turkish money has not made as much profit as deposits, let alone Treasury bonds." Therefore, Serdenge8dti stated that they have always invested in Treasury bonds and that they have earned good money for years when public finances are broken, inflation and real interest rates are high, and they want this to continue. Serdenge8dti said: "In this case, how will they oppose so that inflation does not fall, stability is not achieved, so that interest rates do not fall? They constantly try to disrupt the waits. According to them, inflation targets will not be metd1there are thresholdsd1there will be no floating exchange rate regime -because they want a low exchange rated1There will be no growth with tight fiscal policyd1the opposite has been proven; You say (New Turkish Lira will come out), they say (No way). In short, they reject all positive developments. As you will remember last, when the introduction of the New Turkish Lira approached, they spread rumors of devaluation and consolidation of the public debt." -OTHER DISSIDENTS- In response to the question "Is the opposition so much?", Serdenge8dti said "of course it is not", and said: "There's another group. According to them, the ratio of emissions to national income is low in this country, it is true. The Central Bank has not been printing as much money as it should have been before, and it has done so to keep interest rates high. If you stop serving the rentier and print a lot of money interest rates will fall, production and investment will increase, and when production increases, inflation will also fall. In other words, the Central Bank does not deliberately lower interest rates. What do they not understand? What they don't understand is that printing more money than the demand for money will lead to nothing but inflation, while inflation, on the contrary, will cause production and investment to fall over time." Moreover, since inflation constantly depreciates the national currency and as a result people avoid holding the national currency, the demand for money, in other words, the ratio of emissions to national income has fallen even more, Serdenge8dti said, adding that the process has turned into a vicious cycle. Stating that the fight against inflation is not a priority for any of these groups, Serdenge8dti said: "Some criticize the central bank's focus on the goal of price stability. However, in my opinion, inflation is first and foremost a moral problem. Some want us to extend credit to the Treasury as they did before 2001, which the world has already learned is wrong. Others only look at their own financial assets, portfolios and try to manipulate public opinion accordingly." -CENTRAL BANK'S POSITION- Serdenge8dti also clarified the Central Bank's stance against these approaches. That the Bank's position is very clear, with its communication policy, Stating that they are trying to convince these segments, Serdenge8dti continued: "Of these, he listens to those who are in good style, tells them that they will do what they do, and then do what is necessary to achieve the goal of price stability, which is an essential element of economic stability. In this country, the era of making money from foreign currency is over, and with the decline of the general level of interest rates to reasonable levels, the period of making money from interest at exorbitant levels is also ending." -CLEAR INFLATION TARGETING- Answering the question on "inflation targeting", Serdenge8dti said that this is an issue that the Central Bank has been working on intensively since 2000 and that has been provided by the accumulation of knowledge. reminded me that it was. Serdenge8dti, while referring to the announcement announced on February 22, 2001 that the floating exchange rate regime was passed, said that the inflation targeting regime would be switched when the conditions were met, he said: "Those conditions, as we have made public many times since 2001, were partly of interest to the Central Bank d0 the development of inflation forecasting capability, the expansion of the inflation-related information set, the development of communication policy. In part, the decline in the dominance of public finances, wages in the economy and such conditions as the indexation of prices largely to future inflation instead of the past." Stating that they called the monetary policy they have been implementing since 2002 "implicit inflation targeting" since the conditions have not yet been formed, Serdenge8dti said that they have finally decided to start the transition process, the main feature of which is institutionalization and transparency, with the progress achieved in the conditions he has listed and the emergence of the "medium-term program", which is an indispensable condition of even a gradual transition to inflation targeting. "Institutionalization and transparency, in my opinion, could not be considered independent of the inflation targeting process, as some suggest, and that process itself could not be considered independent of a medium-term stabilization program," Serdenge8dti said. -FARKLILIKLAR- "What are the differences between 2005, which is the transition to open inflation targeting, and the implicit inflation targeting period of 2002-2004 in terms of institutionalization and transparency?" "The first is the announcement of the meeting dates of the Monetary Policy Kumlu, which was formed in 2001 when the Central Bank was made independent and has been meeting and evaluating every month since May of the same year. The second is that the announcement of the short-term interest rate decisions taken by the Central Bank management, as it has been so far, is due to this. then, the meeting is to be held the next day following the meeting. Monthly inflation and outlook announcement shall also be made no later than two days following the meeting. will be done." -INTEREST RATE DECISIONS TO BE VOTED ON IN THE BOARD IN 2006- Serdenge8dti stated that as of 2006, interest rate decisions will be voted on in the Monetary Policy Committee and decisions will be taken accordingly. Serdenge8dti said that the Monetary Policy Report will be replaced by the Inflation Report as of 2006, and that the content of this report will be further enriched and quantitative analyses of inflation forecasts, for example, will be included. Serdenge8dti also stated that the summaries of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting minutes will start to be published. -CENTRAL BANK GOVERNOR SERDENGE82T?: (2) -"WE CANNOT SAY THAT WE HAVE SOLVED THE INFLATION PROBLEM YET, THE PRICE STABILITY MUST BE PERMANENT" -"THIS WILL BE WITH THE PUBLIC ACKNOWLEDGING THAT SINGLE-DIGIT INFLATION IN 2005 WILL NO LONGER REACH DOUBLE DIGITS" -"THE POSITIVE GROWTH FIGURES THAT HAVE BEEN BROUGHT TO US BY THE FALL IN INFLATION FOR THREE CONSECUTIVE YEARS" -"THE INCOME DISTRIBUTION THAT HAS ALMOST DESTROYED THE MIDDLE CLASS FOR YEARS HAS STOPPED DETERIORATING" "WE ARE NOW ENTERING A PERIOD IN WHICH THE INCREASE IN EMPLOYMENT IS PROGRESSING BUT WILL BE LARGELY PERMANENT. THIS IS THE BEST RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM THAT THE STABILITY PROGRAM THAT IS IMPLEMENTED DOES NOT HAVE A SOCIAL DIMENSION THAT IS SOMETIMES BROUGHT TO THE LANGUAGE" - "THE 8 PERCENT TARGET DOES NOT NEED TO BE REVISED" ANKARA (A.A) - 16.01.2005 - The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey Governor S9freyya Serdenge8dti said that in an environment where inflation has fallen below 1 percent, it cannot yet be said that "we have solved the inflation problem" and that price stability must be permanent in order to say this. Serdenge8dti, meanwhile, reported that the first thing brought about by the decline in inflation was "positive growth figures that have been consecutive for 3 consecutive years". Central Bank Governor Serdenge8dti asked Anadolu Agency's correspondent about the monetary policies implemented by the Central Bank. Replied. "Since inflation is below 1 percent, can we say that we have solved the inflation problem?" asked Serdenge8dti, "not yet," Serdenge8dti said. "We are below 1 percent, but when inflation in Turkey is compared to the inflation of about 30 developing countries, we are still sixth to last in terms of price stability. I don't want to talk about developed countries at all. In order to say that we have solved the inflation problem, price stability must be permanent. This will happen when society agrees that single-digit inflation will no longer reach double digits in 2005. Of course, that is not enough, inflation should reach even lower levels in the coming years." Serdenge8dti said that there are many reasons why inflation has finally fallen after years, the first of which is the independence of the Central Bank in 2001 after a delay that lasted almost 30 years. Stating that the Central Bank has not given loans to the public since November 2001 and that inflation has fallen more or less since then, Serdenge8dti said, "What the whole world discovered years ago, we put it into practice only in 2001. Not only was no credit opened to the public, but the Central Bank directed its monetary policy and the tools of this policy to reduce inflation in an uncompromising manner." As a second point, Serdenge8dti, who showed the "resolute implementation" of tight monetary and fiscal policies, although it sometimes provoked reactions, said, "In this period, it was not understood that the tight fiscal policy would not prevent growth under the conditions of high public debt. (Is there a need for such a high non-interest surplus?) Although it was said, it was ultimately implemented with determination. In the past, it was said (What should we do to loosen fiscal policies, reduce the non-interest rate surplus), but today it is understood how important the tight fiscal policy plays as much as the tight monetary policy in the fight against inflation." Spoke. -FACTORS AFFECTING THE FALL OF INFLATION- Serdenge8dti answered the question about "what other factors are effective in reducing inflation" as follows: "When the policy of incomes was more or less within the framework of the inflation target, when the relationship between exchange rates and inflation began to break thanks to the floating exchange rate regime, and when all this led to both productivity increase and the formation of a competitive structure by changing producer and consumer behaviors with the changing dynamics of the economy, it was possible to reduce inflation." Stating that it is necessary to add to all of them "the communication policy based on transparency and honesty and which enables to break inflation expectations", Serdenge8dti said that the communication policy largely eliminates the habit of indexing to past inflation rates in the pricing mechanism, in other words, the inertia in inflation. Serdenge8dti said, "We dug a well with a needle; but in the end, the concepts of economic stability that we want to establish and its most important element, price stability, are largely adopted by society." -WHAT HAS THE FALL IN INFLATION BROUGHT?- Serdenge8dti, on another question, said that the decline in inflation The first thing he brought was the "positive growth figures" that had been coming in a row for three consecutive years, he said. "However, in the past, in the inflation environment, if we grew for two or three years, then we were shrinking and moreover, we were facing crises," Serdenge8dti said. "It will be seen better in the future, but it should be noted that. The deterioration of income distribution, which has almost destroyed the middle class for years, has stopped. Because inflation, which is a form of corruption, meant taking the money out of the pockets of fixed income earners over time without asking for their opinions. On the other hand, while in the past, our workforce, most of which was unskilled, found a job late in periods of growth and immediately lost its job during periods of contraction, now we are entering a period in which the increase in employment is gradual but will be largely permanent. This is the best response to the claim that the stability program implemented from time to time has no social dimension." Stating that the fact that macroeconomic stability is finally achieved along with price stability increases its competitiveness in the international arena and its integration with the world economy, Serdenge8dti said that the source of wealth accumulation is increasingly no longer excessive speculative movements, and that production and investment have come to the forefront. Serdenge8dti emphasized that both the fall in inflation and the rapidly decreasing uncertainties due to the environment that led to this decrease supported the increase in investment, and therefore growth. -WHAT ELSE WILL THE FALL IN INFLATION BRING IN THE FUTURE?- Serdenge8dti also said that as inflation and the public debt problem are solved, the decline in the general level of interest rates will lead to the development of futures markets and instruments, the orientation of banks to the real sector and the strengthening of the real sector banking relationship. Stating that as the inflation target becomes an anchor, the real sector, which sees the way better, will increase its financing opportunities with reasonable costs, Serdenge8dti stated that the contribution of the stability program to the real sector will be in these areas. "Of course, the creation of a more favorable environment for foreign direct investments that have not come to our country due to the high inflation environment so far is another return," Serdenge8dti said. -IS THERE A PROBLEM FOR THE 2005 TARGET OF 8 PERCENT?- Serdenge8dti said, "Three consecutive years have kept inflation targets. Are there any problems with the 2005 target of 8 percent, what are the risks?" he said in response to the question, as an independent central bank would always say, that there are risks. Stating that the increase in domestic demand should be controlled as it has been so far, Serdenge8dti continued as follows: "We are closely following the demand developments in both durable, semi-durable and non-durable consumer goods. We always try to draw attention to rents. Tight monetary and fiscal policies need to be continued. We need to pay attention to the revenue policy." From international oil prices or the agricultural sector Stating that neither central banks nor governments can do anything against the primary effects of the negative shocks that may come, Serdenge8dti stated that they expect the developments in raw material and world commodity prices to be more positive in the coming period compared to 2004. -"REFORM YORGUNLUGU OLU?MAMALI"- In addition to these, Serdenge8dti explained that 'reform fatigue' should not occur, and said: "We know from Latin American examples that the expected returns from reforms are achieved not only by maintaining and maintaining those reforms, but by taking further steps. Signs of a pause or reversal in reforms lead to the loss of gains made and unsatisfactory growth and employment growth. In addition, good management of waits is extremely important. Our history is full of examples of this. The slightest mistake should not be made." On the other hand, Serdenge8dti stated that external shocks can always have a negative effect, and that what needs to be done against these shocks is to strengthen the macroeconomic foundations, and that the effect of external shocks will decrease as the foundations of the economy strengthen. -SHOULD THE 8 PERCENT TARGET BE REVISED?- On the question of "Should the 8 percent inflation target be revised?", Serdenge8dti said, "No, there is no need", and said: "We have a habit of thinking only in the short term, which will be affected by all these years of economic instability. If the inflation figure turns out to be better than expected for a month d0 as it was last September d0 we immediately say let's revise the inflation target downwards. If the following month turns out to be higher than expected d0 as it was last October d0 then we say inflation will not meet the target. As a serious institution, the Central Bank is trying to predict inflation with scientific methods and see a longer term. Of course, as I just said, there are risks. But there is also a positive outlook that the fundamentals of the economy and the indicators point to. In my opinion, there is no need to review at this stage." -CENTRAL BANK GOVERNOR SERDENGE82T: (3) -"WE HAVE TAKEN THE DECISIONS TO REDUCE SHORT-TERM INTEREST RATES BY TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE 'INFLATION OUTLOOK AND INFLATION TARGET' AND TAKING INTO ACCOUNT ALL OTHER ELEMENTS RELATED TO THE ECONOMY, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE 'INFLATION OUTLOOK AND INFLATION TARGET' AND TAKING INTO ACCOUNT ALL OTHER ELEMENTS RELATED TO THE ECONOMY, TOGETHER WITH THE RATIO OF NATIONAL INCOME, WILL CONTINUE TO FALL TOGETHER WITH THE RATIO OF NATIONAL INCOME" -"WE HAVE TAKEN THE DECISIONS TO REDUCE SHORT-TERM INTEREST RATES BY TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE 'INFLATION OUTLOOK AND INFLATION TARGET'" -"IN THIS SENSE, IT IS VERY IMPORTANT THAT BOTH THE MONTHLY ANNOUNCEMENTS OF THE CENTRAL BANK AND THE MONETARY POLICY REPORTS ARE READ AND UNDERSTOOD WELL" -"THE THRESHOLD IN INFLATION IS WHERE INFLATION EXPECTATIONS ARE. IF YOU RESOLUTELY MAINTAIN YOUR STABILITY PROGRAM, INFLATION EXPECTATIONS, I.E. THE THRESHOLD WILL CONTINUE TO FALL DOWNWARDS. SO THERE IS NO PROBLEM." ANKARA (A.A) - 16.01.2005 - The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey Governor S9freyya Serdenge8dti, reminding that real interest rates have reached high levels as a result of the rise in public debt and crises in this country since before, said, "As long as stability is achieved and confidence can be given, I hope it will be better understood in 2005 that public debt will continue to fall together with the ratio of national income, as seen in 2003 and 2004." Serdenge8dti answered Anadolu Agency's correspondent's questions about the monetary policies implemented by the Central Bank. -LOWERING OF INTEREST RATES- Central Bank Governor Serdenge8dti said, "Since September, you have reduced short-term interest rates 3 times. What factors were influential in your decisions?" he said in the announcements they made each time, explaining the developments that were a factor in their decisions. "What did we say? In the second half of 2004, compared to the first half, We said at the beginning of 2004 that there would be a relative slowdown in the economy," Serdenge8dti said. "In addition, from the summer months onwards, many indicators confirmed the relative slowdown. A relative slowdown in demand for money, consumer loans, white goods and auto sales was evident. The excess liquidity in the markets since 2001 began to decrease by 2004. Real sector and consumer confidence indices stabilized after significant increases in the first half of the year. Moreover, despite the rapid growth in the first half of the year, we did not see the inflation target under threat. We've said it all." Pointing out that they took their decision to reduce short-term interest rates by considering the 'inflation outlook and inflation target' and taking into account all other factors related to the economy in the extent of their effects on inflation, Serdenge8dti stated that in this sense, it is 'very important' that both the monthly announcements and the monetary policy reports of the Central Bank are read and understood well. - "ARE YOUR SHORT-TERM INTEREST RATE DECISIONS UNDERSTOOD?" - On another question, Serdenge8dti said that although short-term interest rate decisions are increasingly understood, they still see from time to time that short-term interest rates are only a 'policy tool for inflation'. "Just like what I say in my explanations of the relationship between the current account balance and growth, or how growth is progressing, is sometimes good. such as not being able to be followed, not being understood," Serdenge8dti said. He said: "Not only that. We need to constantly explain that the reduction of short-term interest rates may not necessarily bring about the depreciation of the Turkish currency, on the contrary, it will be perceived as the Central Bank sees the situation positively, and will lead to the transition from foreign currency to the Turkish currency, thus causing the Turkish currency to appreciate contrary to some expectations. Likewise, it is not yet fully understood that the reason why treasury rates, which mean the general level of interest rates in our country, and therefore real interest rates, are high is not the high short-term interest rates, but the high debt burden, and that real interest rates are high in most of the countries with high debt burden like us." Explaining that it is not yet fully understood that the general level of interest rates may not come down by artificially reducing short-term interest rates, as in countries where stable and public debt is not a problem, Serdenge8dti said, "Real interest rates will continue to fall together with the ratio of public debt to national income, as we saw in 2003 and 2004, as we saw in 2003 and 2004, as long as the public debt has risen in this country and has reached high levels as a result of crises, stabilization has been achieved and confidence can be given, I hope it will be better understood in 2005." -INTEREST DISCOUNT- "Last September, I was asked what day your short-term interest rate decisions were. The issue of his receipt led to polemics. It was said to have put the Treasury in a loss because it was held the day after the Treasury auction. What do you think?" asked Serdenge8dti, emphasizing that the last interest rate cut took place on the day of the Treasury auction. Serdenge8dti continued as follows: "Look, this has been said all along. In the past, when I was managing the markets department at the Central Bank, we used to open repo auctions when we deemed it necessary in terms of liquidity. If it happened on Tuesday, they would call us "Treasury friendly" because it was a Treasury auction on the same day. If it happened on Wednesday, they would have accused the Treasury of putting it in harm's way because we did it the day after the auction. If it were possible to solve the problem of public debt and Treasury interest rates according to the day on which the Central Bank gives liquidity or reduces short-term interest rates, our predecessors would have already solved it. Interestingly, I say this because I have been in this business for all these years, as in some unfair evaluations of the security features of banknotes in the recent period, such accusations, which would leave institutions under unfair suspicion, are fortunately not considered worthy of public opinion in any way." -GOVERNMENT PRESSURE- Serdenge8dti said, "In the past, there was speculation that there was government pressure on you in your interest rate decisions," and that governments all over the world had a higher level of interest rates than He said that they want it to be below because the primary preference of the political powers in every country is to urgently try to ensure growth and employment, and that a lower general level of interest rates will bring more growth and employment growth. Underlining the need to pay attention to two issues here, Serdenge8dti expressed the following views: "First, the cause-and-effect relationship I have described applies under conditions where there is price stability, where this stability is not endangered by a rate cut, and where public debt is not a problem. Under those conditions, falling interest rates really helps growth and employment. The second point is that if there is a threat of inflation or if the public debt is a problem, it is now accepted all over the world that interest rates, which are lowered due to political concerns, will ultimately provide growth and employment in the short term, but will bring instability and crisis if measures are not taken in the continuation by increasing inflation and the general level of interest rates before too long. That's why central banks are independent." -BANKANIN G86VEN?L?RL?G? Serdenge8dti also said that the central bank's nearly four-year post-independence performance clearly shows that it is lowering short-term interest rates "only if it feels comfortable with the inflation outlook." In this way, since 2001, both inflation and interest rates have increased by 60 points. Explaining that it is possible for it to fall by 50 points, Serdenge8dti said, "On the other hand, it is not the right behavior in my opinion for some circles that do not want interest rates to fall, to try to damage the Bank's credibility by saying that the Central Bank behaved differently than they thought (acted under government pressure)." -INFLATION TARGET- In the meantime, while touching on the issue of inflation, Serdenge8dti said, "Achieving the targets for 3 years is a success, but this time there are those who say that they are far below the target. What do you think?" to which he replied, "If the target for realization was 12.1 percent instead of 12 percent, even if it was 11.9 percent, there could still be those who said that the target did not meet. There is no criterion for this." Explaining that in many countries it is seen that there are various intervals around the inflation target, Serdenge8dti said that for example, in the UK, the target is 2 percent, but if it can be explained, there can be a downward and upward point movement around the target. "In Mexico, the target is 3 percent range of movement plus minus l'er points, in Hungary the target 4 range of movement is again plus minus 1 point each. Proportionally, these areas of action correspond to quite wide ranges. Moreover, there is another point to be considered. Our process is the process of reducing inflation. We are not yet in the process of being kept under control. The target in the countries I have just mentioned is that The symmetrical bands around it are not yet valid for Turkey. In addition, what has the fact that the inflation targets have been below in the last 3 years prevented in this country? Has it hindered growth, which is the ultimate goal of all policies? No, thanks to the decrease in inflation, a growth based on healthy resources has been achieved at high rates in the last 3 years, and significant progress has been made towards sustainable growth." -THRESHOLD LEVEL- "From time to time, threshold levels are mentioned that will prevent inflation from falling further. Accordingly, inflation falls until it reaches a certain threshold, and then it becomes difficult to fall. What do you say?" "Yes, that's what is mentioned from time to time. When we announced a 35 percent target in 2002, it was said (it doesn't hold). When it fell short of the target, this time it was said (35 percent was easy; 20 percent target was difficult, there are thresholds). When it was below 20 percent, somehow this time (the 20 percent target was easy, the 12 percent goal was difficult, there are thresholds). Now they are saying (The 8 percent target is difficult.'" Serdenge8dti said, "However, it should be known that the threshold in inflation is where inflation expectations are. Serdengeti, "Ancak 2004 ylnn ikinci yarsnda ekonomideki greli yavalamayla birlikte, henz belirgin olmasa da cari denge bozulmas da yavalama sinyalleri vermektedir" dedi. Yerli para deer kaybna urar" dedi. Gemiteki gibi, demeler dengesi krizleri yaama ihtimalinin yok denecek kadar az olmasnn, dalgal kur rejimi ile sk para ve maliye politikalarndan baka nedenleri de olduunu belirten Serdengeti, bankaclk sisteminin dvizdeki ak pozisyonun gemile kyaslanamayacak lde az olduunu bildirdi. Gerektiinde talebi ksc seici nlemler alnabilmektedir. Ayrca ekonomimiz daha istikrarl bir ortamdadr. Dk enflasyon, orta vadeli ekonomik program, bir st dengeye tanm ekonomik dengeler. Dnya ile artan ticari ve finansal btnleme ile birlikte eskiye oranla daha yksek aklarn srdrlebilirlii sz konusudur. Dikkat edilmesi gereken, dalgal kurun salad esneklie ramen, baka sorunlarn olup olamayacadr. Ancak Trkiye iin, bankaclk sektr reformu sonrasnda bu alandaki yapsal bozukluklarn hzla dzeldiini grdklerini syleyen Serdengeti, daha da ileri admlar atlacan, irketler kesiminin de yeni ekonomik ortama uyum salama abalarnn hzlandn grdklerini, verimliliin n plana ktn, rekabetin arttn sermaye birikim srecinin deitiini ifade etti. Direncimizin zaman iinde ne kadar artm olduu, 11 Eyll olaylarnda, stanbul'daki terr olaylarnda ve 2003 Irak savanda gayet iyi grld. OLSA OLSA UZUN SRM BR BALANGICIN SONUDUR" -"AB'YE KATILMAMIZ DEMEK OLAN SONU NE KADAR UZAKTA OLURSA OLSUN, O SONUCA ULAMA SREC, BANA GRE VARILACAK SONUTAN OK DAHA NEML" -"BZ EKONOMK STKRARI, HER EYDEN EVVEL KENDMZ N YAPMAK ZORUNDAYIZ" -"KUR POLTKAMIZDA DEGKLK YOK" -"2005 N ALACAGIMIZ DVZ MKTARI, YAKLAIK 3.8 MLYAR DOLAR LE 11.3 MLYAR DOLAR ARASINDA OLACAK" ANKARA (A.A) - 16.01.2005 - Trkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankas Bakan Sreyya Serdengeti, 17 Aralk'n Trkiye iin, Avrupa Birlii (AB) srecinin sonu olmadn sylerken, "Sonun balangc bile deildir. Nitekim, zel hukuk tzel kiiliini haiz, zel sermayenin de katld bir anonim ortaklk eklinde kurulduunu anlatan Serdengeti, "Maalesef 1970 kanununda bamszlk asndan geriye gittiimizi gryoruz ve yine 1970 ylndan itibaren, bunu ilgin bulacaksnz, Trkiye yava yava enflasyon ortamna giriyor" dedi. Title: Turkey's Europeanization Problem in the European Union Process
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: TURKEY'S EUROPEANIZATION PROBLEM IN THE EUROPEAN UNION PROCESS GAZ ERCEL PRESIDENT REPUBLIC OF TURKEY HURIYET M ERKEZ BANK ANCHOR A 24 M ART 1997 Dear Guests, Dear Faculty Members, Dear Representatives of Our Media, As we enter the two millennia, our world is moving towards integration in the economic, financial and commercial spheres. This integration brings with it the need for harmony between countries in cultural and social fields. International integration creates a world where borders are removed. In the changing world conditions of the two-thousands, it is clear that there will be more opportunities and at the same time more responsibility for everyone. However, I still believe that no one will want to bear the cost of not taking advantage of the globalization trend of the 21st century. It would not be rational to expect that our country will not take its share of this trend observed in the world and will not take advantage of the opportunities. In the changing world, Turkey will take its place in the New World Order in accordance with its interests. The primary condition for this is the provision and maintenance of macroeconomic stability. One pillar of international integration is the efforts to create a European Union. Our country's efforts to integrate with Europe in every field go back a long time. Turkey's inclusion in the European Community, with the exception of various intermittent periods, is part of a long-term programme. The integration efforts of our country into the European Economic Community, which started in the 1960s, have reached a certain point today. The contributions of joining the European community to the economic and commercial life of our country and what our country should realize in these areas have been discussed in various dimensions and on various occasions. However, the cultural dimension of integration is also of great importance. Turkey's westernization efforts go back a long time, before the work of the European community. With the establishment of our Republic, Turkey has established its place in Europe and has also been able to benefit from the developments of the "civilized world". Westernization involves a cultural dimension. In this context, it is important to ensure cultural harmony with Europe. Turkey is increasingly moving towards greater integration with Europe. On this path, it is clear that Turkey's new role in Europe will become stronger and stronger. Turkey is forming a synthesis by adapting Western norms to its own national norms. We see signs that the coming years will bring significant developments in terms of relations with the European Union. As a matter of fact, at the last meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the European Union, it was accepted that Turkey would be evaluated among the 11 countries applying for full membership to the European Union and with the same criteria; and it was underlined once again by the member ministers of the union that Turkey is European. It is known that Turkey is a country with a strong economic infrastructure and great potential. One of our most important issues in the coming period is to activate this potential. At this point, the importance of education and renewal in the social field emerges. Today, our Central Bank organized the third of a series of seminars on the European Union - Turkey relationship. Offers. Our first seminar "European Union and Turkey - European Union Relations" was more of an introductory quality and aimed to present basic information. In the "Policies and Practices in the Customs Union Process" seminar we organized last year, the practices carried out in Turkey and the theoretical structure on which they are based were discussed. However, we all know that full integration with Europe includes economic, military and commercial dimensions, as well as social and cultural cohesion. This seminar, which starts today and will last for five days, is about the last dimension. While concluding my words here, I hope that the program will be beneficial for the participants, our bank and our country.
