Bu gelimeler sonucunda, ekonomik daralma srm, enflasyon oran ilk tahminlerin zerine kma eilimi gstermitir. Enflasyonda grlen bu sramann temel sebebi dviz kurlarnda gzlenen yksek orandaki arttr. Buna paralel olarak enflasyonist bekleyilerdeki bozulma ve kamu kesimi fiyat ayarlamalar da enflasyonu artrc ynde etkileyen faktrler olmulardr. Talep gelimelerine daha hassas olan tketici fiyatlar Ekim ay itibaryla bir nceki senenin ayn ayna gre yzde 66,5 artmtr. Buna karn, kamu fiyatlar ve dviz kurundaki gelimelerden daha fazla etkilenen toptan eya fiyatlar ayn dnemde yzde 81,4 ykselmitir. Ekonomik daralmaya bal olarak ithalat azalm, Trk lirasnn reel olarak deer kaybetmesi ve yurt ii talebin kesilmesi nedenleriyle ihracat artmaya balamtr. Bylelikle, cari ilemler hesab fazla verme srecine girmitir. Austos aynn ortalarna doru gelindiinde, programn nihayet ilemeye baladna ynelik sinyaller de artmaya balamtr. Bu gelimenin arkasnda drt temel neden vardr. Birincisi ve en nemlisi, yapsal reformlar erevesinde oluan ve programn artk srdrlemeyecei beklentilerine yol aan tartmalarn kesilmesidir. kincisi, bankaclk sisteminin dvizdeki ak pozisyonunun Hazine ve Merkez Bankasnn da abalar ile kapatlmasdr. ncs, dviz ak pozisyonlarnn kapatlmas ile, Merkez Bankasnn dviz piyasasna mdahalelerinin yok denecek bir dzeye inmesinin mmkn olmas ve bylelikle ekonomik birimlerin dalgal kur rejimine almalarnn kolaylamasdr. Drdncs, olumsuzluklar yaayan Arjantin ekonomisiyle Trkiye ekonomisinin uygulanan iktisadi politikalar, zellikle de dviz kuru rejimi bakmndan, ok farkl olduklarnn giderek daha iyi anlalmasdr. Bu ortamda, bankalar sendikasyon kredilerini yenilemeye (1-23 Kasm tarihleri arasnda bankalarn d ykmllkleri net 396,2 milyon dolar artmtr). Hazine de i borlanma ihalelerini sorunsuz atlatmaya balamtr. Bu olumlu gelimeler, faiz oranlarnn dmesine, dviz kurunun ise belli bir dzey etrafnda salnmaya balamasna yol amtr. Mali piyasalarda zlenen istikrarn olumaya baladnn bylelikle ilk iaretleri alnmtr. Ancak, 11 Eyllde yaanan trajik olaylar, birka gn ierisinde faiz oranlarnda ve dviz kurlarnda yksek artlara yol am, dviz kurunda tekrar yukarya doru bir eilim oluturmutur. ktisadi ierii kuvvetli ve tutarl olan mevcut programn nemli miktarda yeni d kaynakla desteklenmesi ihtimalinin nemli lde artmasyla birlikte, bu olumsuz gidiat sona ermitir. Ekim aynn ortalarndan balayarak dviz kurunda yeniden aa doru bir eilim olumu, kur volatilitesi yeniden azalm ve faiz oranlarnda nemli dler yaanmtr. Sayn Bakan, deerli yeler, Konumamn bundan sonraki blmnde ksaca dnya ve Trkiye ekonomisinde 2002 ylna ait beklentilere deindikten sonra, bu olumlu gidiatn sreklilik kazanmasnn temel koullarndan bahsedeceim. V. GELECEK DNEME BAKI Gl Ekonomiye Gei Programmzn temel dayanaklarndan olan ihracat ve turizm gelirleri ile sermaye girilerinin 11 Eyll saldrlarnn yarataca olumsuzluklardan etkilenme ihtimali yksektir. Zaten durgunlukta olan dnya ekonomisinin 2002 ylnda beklenen canlanmas bir miktar yavalayabilecek olsa da, bir ok lkenin temel ekonomik gstergelerinin nceki yllara gre daha salam olmas ve merkez bankalarnn oklara egdml olarak tepki vermi olmas, mit vericidir. Yine de daralma eiliminin srmesi mallarmza olan d talebi azaltacaktr. Dier taraftan, dnya ekonomisindeki durgunluk eilimi, petrol talebini de ksarak ham petrol fiyatlarnn gerilemesine ve dolaysyla Trkiyenin ithalat faturasnn azalmasna yol aabilecektir. Dnya ekonomisindeki toparlanmann bata ABD olmak zere dier gelimi ekonomilerdeki canlanmaya bal olarak 2002 ylnn ilk yarsnda balayaca tahmin edilmektedir. Dnya ekonomisinin 2002 ylnda son on yln ortalama rakamlarna kyasla daha dk olarak yzde 2,5 orannda, dnya ticaret hacminin ise yzde 2,7 orannda byyecei beklenmektedir. Trkiye ekonomisinin 2002 ylnda, zellikle sanayi ve hizmetler sektrleri kaynakl olarak tekrar byme srecine girecei ve GSMH ile GSYHnin yzde 4 orannda byyecei tahmin edilmektedir. Bu erevede, 2002 ylnda cari ilemler dengesinin 1,9 milyar ABD dolar ak vermesi beklenirken, sk maliye politikasnn srdrlmesiyle faiz d bte fazlasnn 2001 ve 2002 yllarnda GSMHnin srasyla yzde 5,7si ve yzde 6,5i olaca tahmin edilmektedir. Merkez Bankas ve Hkmetin 2002 yl iin beraberce belirlemi olduu hedefler dorultusunda TFEnin yzde 35, TEFEnin ise yzde 31 orannda artmas beklenmektedir. Ekonomimizin kalc bir byme srecine girmesinde, mali piyasalardaki olumlu gelimelerin devam etmesi byk nem tamaktadr. Mali piyasalarda olumaya balayan istikrarn srdrlebilmesinin n koulu ise i borlanmann srdrlebilir olduunun ekonomik birimlere gsterilmesidir. Srdrlebilirlik iin drt temel koul salanmaldr. Birincisi, 2002 ylnda ok nemli miktarda faiz d bte fazlas verilmesi planlanmtr. Bu, gerekletirilmelidir. kincisi, program ek d kaynakla desteklenmelidir ki desteklenecei ihtimali son derece glenmitir. ncs, risk primini artrarak reel faiz oranlarn ykselten davranlardan, Programdan vaz m geiliyor? phesini yaratan tartmalardan kanlmal ve i borcun srdrlebilirlii ok iyi anlatlmaldr. Drdncs, bugne kadar gerekletirilen yapsal reformlarn iktisadi temellerimizi nasl dzelttii hususu kamuoyuna daha iyi anlatlmal ve reform srecine aksatmadan devam edilmelidir. Bu drt koulun salanmasyla birlikte, faiz oranlarnda d ve dviz kurunda istikrarl bir seyir gzlenilebilecektir. Bylelikle, enflasyon orannn giderek azalaca ve yl sonu iin hedeflenen yzde 35 dzeyine ulalabilecei tahmin edilmektedir. Bu istikrarn yurt ii talebi uyaracan dnyoruz. Ancak, uyarlan yurt ii talebin retime dnebilmesi iin mali sektrn tekrar kredi aabilir bir bnyeye kavuturulmas gerekmektedir. Bu erevede, kamu bankalarnda ok nemli yapsal bir dnm salandn bir kez daha vurgulamak isterim. Grev zararlar altnda bunalan kamu bankalar, artk, yeniden bankaclk yapabilecek, kendi balarna kaynak yaratabilecek bir yapya kavumulardr. Bilindii gibi, Gl Ekonomiye Gei Program ile balatlan bankaclk reformunun ilk aamas kamu bankalar ve TMSFye aktarlan bankalar kapsyordu. Bu aama yl sonu itibaryla baarl bir biimde tamamlanm olacaktr. Bunlarn dnda kalan zel sermayeli bankalarn glendirilmesi iin balatlan almalar ise nmzdeki dnemde hzla ve baaryla sonulandrlmak durumundadr. Bylelikle, ekonomik byme iin gerekli olan fonlarn reel sektre daha rahat aktarlabilecei bir ortam yaratlm olacaktr. Mali piyasalardaki istikrarn temini dorultusunda, Merkez Bankas, dier ilgili kurumlarla birlikte, dviz kuru dviz piyasalar ileyiinin etkinletirilmesi iin: (i) vadeli dviz piyasalarnn gelitirilmesi; (ii) vadeli dviz ilemleriyle ilgili vergi ve muhasebe mevzuatlarnn akla kavuturulmas; ve (iii) kamu iktisadi kurulularnn mali idarelerinin gelitirilerek dviz piyasas ileyiini bozan sorunlu yntemlere dayanan yksek hacimli dviz ilemlerinin nlenmesi alanlarnda idari dzenlemeler yapmaktadr. Buraya kadar deindiim koullarn yerine gelmesiyle salanacak istikrar ortam, yerleiklerin portfylerinde giderek daha az dviz cinsinden mali varlk tutacaklar bir ortam anlamna gelmektedir. Bylelikle zellikle 2001 yl iinde TLden uzaklaan yatrmcnn tekrar TLye dnebilecei bir ortam doacaktr. Nitekim, kriz sonras TLnin ar deer kayb nedeniyle dviz tevdiat hesabnn toplam mevduat iindeki ykselen pay, son aylarda greceli olarak artan istikrarla Kasm ay itibaryla azalmaya balamtr. Dviz tevdiat hesabnn getiimiz yl ulam olduu en yksek deerinden, 9 Kasm 2001 itibaryla sadece yzde 5 artarak 40 milyar dolara ulam olmas, dolarizasyon oranndaki artta TLnin deer kaybnn nemli bir rol oynadn gstermektedir. Bu erevede, dviz arznn ve Trk liras talebinin giderek artt bir srece doru gidilecei dnlmektedir. Bu sre ierisinde mali piyasalardaki istikrarn daha da kuvvetlenecei aktr. Bu srecin oluturulmasnda para politikasna da phesiz nemli bir rol dmektedir. Bu balamda, para tabannn nominal apa grevini etkinletirmek ve para programn glendirmek amalar dorultusunda, nceki programda gsterge hedef olan para taban performans kriterine evrilmitir. Para taban, tahmininin gl ve Merkez Bankasnn tamamen kontrol altnda olmamas gibi genel kabul gren kstlamalarna ramen, para program iin son derece etkili ve kolay izlenebilir bir byklk olacaktr. Para program, para tabannn reel byme ve enflasyon hedefine paralel bir art gstermesinin hedeflemektedir. Para tabannn bu erevedeki art, mali disiplin ve yapsal reform nlemleri ile birlikte, ekonomik birimlerin enflasyon beklentilerini, hkmetin ekonomik programnda ngrlen fiyat artlarna yaklatracaktr. Deerli Bakan, sayn yeler, ok nemli ve bazen dikkatlerden kaan bir iktisadi geree deinmekte yarar gryorum. Her ekonomide cari enflasyon oran, gemite yaananlarn bir sonucu olarak ortaya kmaktadr. Dier bir deyile, yakn gemiteki maliyet ve talep unsurlar ile ekonomik birimlerin bekleyileri, belli bir gecikmeyle cari dnemdeki enflasyon orann belirlemektedir. Eer, cari dnemdeki enflasyon orann belirleyen bu unsurlarn gemite kalan hareketlerinin aynen gelecekte de devam sz konusu ise, phesiz, gelecein enflasyon oran da cari dnemdekinden ve gemitekinden farkl olmayacaktr. Aksine, enflasyon orann belirleyen unsurlardaki gemi hareketlerin gelecekte srmeyecei ve tersine dnecei ihtimali ok kuvvetli ise, gelecek dnemin enflasyonunun cari dnem enflasyonundan giderek farkllamas ihtimali de ok kuvvetli olacaktr. Bu nedenle, fiyat istikrarn amalayan merkez bankalar gemi ve cari enflasyonda yaanan gereklemelerin arkasndaki nedenleri deerlendirmekte, bu nedenlerin gelecekte ne lde geerli olacaklarn irdelemekte ve kararlarn bu irdelemenin sonularna gre almaktadrlar. Trkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankas da, nominal apa olan para taban iin belirlenen hedefe ilave olarak, (i) cretlerdeki; (ii) uluslararas ekonomik gelimelerdeki; (iii) enflasyonist beklentilerdeki; (iv) toplam arz ve talepteki; (v) dviz kurundaki; (vi) kamu kontrol altndaki mal ve hizmet fiyatlarndaki; (vii) ihracat, ithalat ve sermaye hareketlerindeki gelimelerin genel fiyatlarn trendi zerindeki etkilerini deerlendirerek, fiyat istikrarna ulama temel amac dorultusunda alaca para politikas kararlarn belirleyecek ve faiz oranlarnda gerekli grlen deiikleri yapacaktr. 2002 ylnda para politikas uygulamasn daha da gl klacak unsurlardan birisi de saydamlk olacaktr. Yce Meclisin ats altnda yaptm bu konuma da bu saydamln bir parasn oluturmaktadr. Merkez Bankas, temel politika arac olan ksa vadeli faiz oranlarna ynelik ald kararlarn gerekelerini Temmuz ayndan itibaren ayrntlaryla aklamaya balamtr. Bu uygulama srdrlecektir. Ayrca, periyodik olarak Para Politikas ve daha sonra Enflasyon Raporlar yaymlanacaktr. Bu raporlarda gemiin ve cari dnemin analizi yaplacak, bu analiz nda ileriye ynelik baz senaryolar oluturulacaktr. Keza, yeni yasamz erevesinde oluturulan Para Politikas Kurulu, para politikas stratejisi ve uygulamalar hakknda kamuoyunu aydnlatan aklamalar yapacaktr. Merkez Bankas Yasasnda yaplan son deiiklikler de fiyat istikrarnn salanmas abalarna yardmc olacaktr. Bu yasayla Merkez Bankasnn, Hazine ve kamu kurum ve kurulularna avans vermesi, kredi amas ve bu kurulularn ihra ettii borlanma aralarn birincil piyasadan satn almas nlenmitir. Avrupa Birliinin ekonomik kriterleri olan Maastricht kriterlerine de uygun olan bu ilke, karlksz para basmn nleme asndan da son derece nemli bir bamszlk ilkesidir. Sayn Bakan, deerli yeler, konumamn son blmnde koullar olutuunda gemeyi dndmz enflasyon hedeflemesi politikas zerinde durmak istiyorum. VI. PARA HEDEFLEMES POLTKASININ NHA EREVES: ENFLASYON Merkez Bankas olarak 2002 yl banda Enflasyon Hedeflemesi sistemine geileceini kamuoyuna aklamtk. Fakat bu srete gerek i gerek d konjonktr baarl bir enflasyon hedeflemesi iin gerekli artlarn olumasna engel olmutur.  konjonktrde, kamu finansmannn mali piyasalar zerindeki basksnn srmesi ve yksek enflasyon seviyesi, enflasyon hedeflemesi sistemine geiin bir sre ertelenmesi ihtiyacn ortaya karmtr. D konjonktrde ise zellikle, ABDye ynelik terrist saldrdan sonra i ve d finans piyasalarndaki belirsizlik bu kararda etkili olmutur. Sayn Bakan, deerli yeler, gnmzde merkez bankalar tarafndan kabul edilen temel gr, dk ve istikrarl bir enflasyon orannn uzun vadeli ekonomik bymenin temel art olduu, uygulanan genilemeci para politikalarnn ksa vadede retim art ve isizlik orannda dler gibi olumlu sonular verse de, orta ve uzun dnemde ksa dnemde edinilmi olan bu kazanlarn korunamayacadr. Genilemeci para politikasnn ksa dnem etkileri uzun srmeyecek, ekonomi genilemeci para politikas uygulamasndan nceki retim ve isizlik oranna daha yksek bir enflasyon oranyla beraber geri dnecektir. Dier bir ifade ile, nominal bir deiken olan para ile reel deikenler olan retim ve isizlik oran arasnda uzun dnemde iliki mevcut deildir. Dnya apnda parasal otoriteler farkl para politikas stratejileri uygulayp, farkl aralar kullansalar da, dk ve istikrarl enflasyon orann salamay temel ama olarak benimsemilerdir. Son yllarda poplaritesi artan ve baarl sonular veren para politikas stratejisi ise enflasyonu hedefleyen para politikasdr. Bu uygulama altnda parasal otorite gelecek dnemler iin resmi enflasyon hedeflerini aklar ve bu hedeflere ulalmasnn kendisi iin tek ve en nemli ama olduunu ilan eder. Enflasyon Hedeflemesi Rejimi, merkez bankasnn tek hedefinin fiyat istikrar olduu ve kendi bnyesinde oluturduu enflasyon tahminlerinin ara hedef olarak belirlendii bir para politikas erevesidir. Enflasyon Hedeflemesi uygulayan merkez bankalar, kamuoyuna akladklar orta vadeli enflasyon hedefini gerekletirmeye ynelik politika aralarn belirlerken, parasal byklk ve kurlar gibi deikenler dnda enflasyon hakknda bilgi ieren tm verileri kullanr. Enflasyon hedeflemesinin bir ok gelimi ve gelimekte olan lkede yaygnlamas bir tesadf deildir. Enflasyon hedeflemesi uygulamas, para politikas zerindeki belirsizlikleri azaltmakta ve belirsizlikler azald lde, enflasyonist bekleyileri olumlu ynde etkilemektedir. Bu balamda, etkin bir enflasyon hedeflemesi politikas, uzun vadeli finansal piyasalarn gelimesine katkda bulunmas ve konjonktrdeki dalgalanmalarn skln ve iddetini azaltmas kanallaryla toplumsal refah zerinde etkili olmaktadr. Dier lke tecrbelerine baktmzda enflasyon hedeflemesi rejiminde gerekleen enflasyon oranlar hedeflenen enflasyon oranlarndan farkllklar gsterebilmektedir. Bilindii zere, merkez bankalarnn hedefleyecei fiyat endeksi merkez bankalarnn kontrol dndaki deikenlerden de etkilenebilir. Enflasyon hedeflemesi rejiminin uyguland lkelerde merkez bankalar, bu deikenlerdeki beklenmeyen hareketlerin hedeflenen enflasyon dzeyine ulamay engelleyebilecei gereinden yola karak, enflasyon hedefinden sapmalar aklayabilecek birtakm faktrleri gz nnde bulundurmaktadr. TCMB bu erevede, dolayl vergilerdeki kademeli artlar; enflasyon zerinde etkili olan kamu fiyatlarndaki artlar; dnyada petrol ve hammadde fiyatlarndaki dalgalanmalar; tarm retiminde tarm fiyatlarn etkileyebilecek dalgalanmalar; beklenmeyen doal afetleri; enflasyon hedefinden sapmalar aklayabilecek faktrler olarak gz nnde bulundurmaktadr. Merkez Bankas Enflasyon Hedeflemesi rejimine 2002 ylnda gemek iin gerek yasal, gerek teknik gerekse kamuoyu ile iletiim alannda birok hazrln tamamlama aamasndadr. Yasal dzenlemelere baktmz zaman Enflasyon Hedeflemesi rejiminin en nemli koullarndan biri olan Merkez Bankasnn temel amacnn fiyat istikrar olmas koulunun Mays aynda deien Merkez Bankas Yasas ile salandn grmekteyiz. Dier bir nkoul olan Merkez Bankas bamszl hakknda da yasa, hem enflasyon hedefine ynelik politika aralarnn bankaca belirlenmesine ilikin ara bamszl; hem Merkez Bankasnn karlksz para basmayacan belirten ekonomik bamszlk; hem de para politikasn belirleyen ve uygulayan kiilerin atama ve grevden alnma usullerini belirleyen politik bamszlk konusunda dzenlemeler getirmitir. Enflasyon Hedeflemesi rejiminin dier zellii Merkez Bankasnn artan effafl ve hesapverebilirliidir. Deien yasa her iki alanda da kkl yenilikler iermektedir. Enflasyon hedeflemesi rejimine geme amacyla teknik hazrlklar da yaplmtr. Merkez Bankas enflasyon ngrlerini enflasyonla ilikili olan tm deikenlerin kullanld geni bir veri seti zerinden yapacaktr. Bu balamda, Merkez Bankasnn enformasyon bazn gelitirmesinde, zel imalat sanayi firmalarnn TEFE beklentilerinin elde edilmesi amacyla kullanlan ktisadi Ynelim Anketine ilave olarak, arlkl olarak finans kesiminin enflasyon, kur ve faiz beklentilerini ayda iki kez elde etmeyi amalayan Enflasyon Beklenti Anket verilerinin toplanlmasna da balanmtr. Buna paralel olarak, Merkez Bankas bnyesinde enflasyon ile ilgili modelleme almalarn gerekletirme amacyla ksa ve orta vadeli tahmin gruplar kurulmutur. Enflasyon Hedeflemes rejiminin gerektirdii en temel konulardan biri ise Merkez Bankasnn kamuoyu ile artan iletiimidir. Merkez Bankas, ald kararlar, para politikas amalar ve sonular hakknda ekonomik birimleri, dnemsel olarak karaca raporlar ve dier iletiim aralar yoluyla bilgilendirecektir. Bu ama ayn zamanda Merkez Bankasnn effafl ve hesap verebilirlii ile de yakndan ilikilidir. Enflasyon Hedeflemesi rejiminin gerek enflasyon hedefinin nominal apa olmas yoluyla para politikas zerindeki belirsizlikleri azaltmas, gerek bamsz para politikas uygulamasnn getirecei d oklara kar esneklik, gerekse de kamuoyu ile iletiimi artan ve kamuoyuna neyi, ne amala yapacan anlatacak effaf bir para politikas erevesi oluturmas asndan lkemize birok yarar salayacaktr. lkemizde enflasyon hedeflemesi rejiminin uygulanmasyla enflasyonist bekleyilerin azalmas, dviz kurunda meydana gelen deiimlerin fiyatlara yansmasnn azalmas, ve faiz oranlarnn d sonucunda borcun srdrlebilirliinin kolaylamas gibi olumlu gelimeler gzlemlenebilecektir. Enflasyon Hedeflemesi, genel ekonomik programn nemli bir paras olarak dnlmelidir. Bu erevede, Enflasyon Hedeflemesi uygulamasnn baars, dier ekonomi politikalaryla desteklenmesine baldr. Ksaca, bu rejimin baars, nce ekonomide baz olumlu gelimelere, rnein dalgal kur rejiminde kurun istikrar kazanmasna ve enflasyon zerindeki etkisinin azalmasna, gemi enflasyona endeksleme sisteminin terk edilerek ileriye ynelik endekslemeye geilmesine, ayrca Hazinenin bor piyasalarndaki hakimiyetinin azalmasna baldr. Bunlara ilave olarak, mali disiplinin salanmas; finansal derinleme; mal ve hizmet piyasalarnn greli fiyat deimelerine kar daha esnek bir yapya ulamas da bu rejimin baars iin son derece nemli faktrlerdir.

Title: Speech "Policy Applications; Past, Today, Future"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: POLICY APPLICATIONS; PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE SuREYYA SERDENGEcT PRESIDENT Erzurum 4 September 2001 STRUCTURAL REFORMS Mr. Governor, Mr. Commander, Mr. President, dear listeners, within the framework of a program initiated by our Central Bank 5 years ago, we explain our monetary policy in a city of our country quarterly and exchange views on the economy; we also carry out social and artistic activities. In this context, this visit is the second visit of our Central Bank and my first development to Erzurum, I greet you all with respect. Today, we briefly ask you about the structural reforms in the Turkish economy, the role of expectations in the economy; domestic debt stock, floating exchange rate regime and exchange rate policies, finally the framework of the new monetary policies and the inflation targeting regime in the near future. Within the framework of the stability program that has been implemented in Turkey for the last two years and was revised in February 2001, great progress has been made in many areas, including many structural problems that have been going on for years, leading to the implementation and unsuccessful termination of many stabilization programs, the effects of which will be seen as much stronger in the coming years. Within the scope of the Program, for Economic Foundations;  Structural reforms that effectively change the economic structure have been carried out rapidly in the recent period.  Over two years, various reforms have been undertaken, which can be considered quite challenging to even design, both nationally and internationally. The main importance of these reforms is that they are effectively changing the deteriorating economic structure, which was one of the main reasons that dragged the Turkish economy into a series of crises in the 1990s. Thus, the foundations of our economy are getting stronger. The reforms related to the banking sector, which were the subject of the most criticism during the past program implementations and the revision of the current program and constituted the weakest link in the programs, were carried out faster than ever with the latest program and a strong scalpel was struck at the deteriorating structure in the banking sector. In this context, The pressure created by public banks, especially in the overnight borrowing market, has been prevented and the system has been cleared of problematic banks. Very important steps have been taken to strengthen the capital structures of the other banks remaining in the system. A discipline has been introduced in public expenditure and fiscal discipline has been ensured, which is extremely important for the effective implementation of monetary policy. The non-interest surplus provided within this framework is quite ambitious even in terms of international criteria. It is clear that without fiscal and monetary discipline, stability cannot be brought to the economy only through structural reforms. Therefore, in this respect, what has been done so far is very positive. Both the budget and monetary policy are implemented in the discipline required by economic stability. Thanks to the economic policy implementation summarized so far, both Turkey's economic foundations are being corrected and institutional arrangements are being made to prevent the deterioration of these foundations again. However, there is one point that should not be forgotten: Although it is necessary to correct the economic foundations in order to achieve the desired results of society, such as low inflation, rapid and sustainable growth, more equitable income distribution, it is not enough on its own. Depending on whether economic expectations are positive or negative, the same economic fundamentals can produce very different economic results. From the point of view of expectations, we see that despite all the economic policy implementations carried out within the framework of the program and highly successful in terms of all international criteria, the expectations still have not reached the level of positivity they deserve. However, within the framework of these policies, both economic indicators and expectations in Turkey should have been positive. Negative economic expectations not only lead to movements in exchange rates moving away from economic fundamentals and at times becoming foamy. At the same time, interest rates are also rising, as perceived risks increase. It is obvious that it is only possible to achieve the desired results by the society in a short time by turning the expectations into positive. Looking at the reasons for the negative expectations, although there has been a short period of political instability and a short-lived reluctance to reform in the recent period, the most frequently voiced issues in the public opinion are:  We see that the Domestic Debt Stock is Sustainable and  Floating Exchange Rate Regime. The political instability and unwillingness to reform from late May to mid-July created a series of negative shock effects on our economy. These developments were not foreseen during the design of Turkey's Transition to a Strong Economy Program. It is clear that such an environment fuels negative expectations. However, starting from mid-July, discussions that led to instability and reluctance gradually began to fall off the agenda. DOMESTIC DEBT STOCK Political debates aside, at first glance there seem to be two more fundamental reasons behind the high interest rate and exchange rate: These are the problem of the domestic debt stock and the floating exchange rate regime, which the implemented program has inherited from the past. In our opinion, a sustainable situation began to be perceived as unsustainable with the Treasury interest rate coming from 70% to 110% in a month in May and June. Despite the reforms and policies implemented, the fact that economic expectations do not turn positive is also effective in this. The positive developments in August and the composition of the domestic debt stock and the better perception of the maturity structure in the public opinion and the Treasury interest rates, which fell to 80%, show that the problem has begun to be solved. However, this is not considered sufficient by us. The forgotten point is this: Under the economic expectations that will be formed at the level of positivity that such highly successful economic policy implementations deserve in terms of all international criteria, a sustainable debt stock can easily be perceived as a problem under the undeserved economic expectations. FLOATING EXCHANGE RATE REGIME Now I want to come to the floating exchange rate regime; First, from a theoretical point of view, it is not possible to say that this exchange rate regime is better than others. They all have their positive and negative aspects. What is important is that the monetary authority knows these things and shapes its policies within this framework. The point that needs to be known is that no matter which exchange rate regime is applied, the economic foundations must be sound. When we look at the world practices, it is seen that in recent years, many countries have switched to this regime, sometimes out of necessity and sometimes due to economic conditions. As for the case of Turkey, the choice of such a regime stemmed from a necessity caused by the crisis for Turkey. Turkey has not moved into a floating exchange rate regime, as predicted by the previous stabilization program, in which economic fundamentals are based on conditions of stability, the banking system is eliminated from risks such as open positions, and an increasingly open exchange rate band is implemented. On the contrary, as has been the case in most developing countries, the stabilization program based on fixed or predictable exchange rates has had to pass with the collapse of the program for various reasons. That being the case, I would like to draw your attention to the following important point: You cannot restore confidence by replacing a fixed or predictable exchange rate regime that has collapsed with a crisis of confidence: If people have no confidence in the previous one, they have no reason to trust the next. However, unfortunately, even those who should have known these issues well advocated a return to the fixed/predictable regime, created false expectations, even though the MB has not changed its discourse for 5 months. What has the Central Bank been saying since 5 months? . This issue has been answered many times, both in the Letters of Intent outlining the program being implemented and in the various statements and speeches we have made regarding the program with the program implementation. To state once again, with the new program, the floating exchange rate system was adopted and the principle of determining the exchange rate under market conditions was adopted. In this context, the Central Bank has stated at every opportunity that the exchange rate will not interfere with the long-term equilibrium value and that foreign exchange interventions will be aimed either to attract the liquidity caused by the disbursement of IMF money to the Treasury or to eliminate the excessive volatility that occurs from time to time in the exchange rate. When the ultimate goal was for the exchange rate to find its equilibrium value through its own internal dynamics and with as little Central Bank intervention as possible, all studies were aimed at this goal. By mid-July, the picture that emerged was this: the open position of the banking system, which was caught with a high open position and unprepared like everyone else, the Central Bank foreign exchange sales of 7 billion in 5 months and a total of 13 billion swap plus fund banks and Treasury papers denominated in foreign currency or indexed to foreign currency given to public banks for duty losses. Contrary to what some circles think, the closure of this open position is essential for exchange rate stability in a floating exchange rate regime and market observations confirm our view. In other words, the view that if banks close their open positions, the exchange rate becomes more unstable is completely wrong. However, the sometimes intense Central Bank interventions have a negative consequence, which we know from the experience of other countries from the beginning: As long as the intervention continues intensely or is thought to be continuing, no one believes that the exchange rate has reached its equilibrium value, which is quite natural. When we look at the last month, since we said that the Central Bank has intervened less and will intervene less for the reasons I have now mentioned, it is not a coincidence that the TL has gained value, the same developments have taken place in similar countries. Finally, in the section on floating exchange rate regime and exchange rate policies, I would like to mention a few points:  We must follow very well what is happening in the world. Turkey is not alone in this world, what we are going through now has happened in many other countries as well. The Central Bank has followed these developments very well and continues to do so. Yet a significant part of our intellectuals unfortunately, it does not attach enough importance to this. The discussions on the floating exchange rate regime in Turkey are a very good example of this.  The campaign to respect the Turkish Lira, which has been widely echoed in the press and developed on the initiative of non-governmental organizations as it should be, is the most important reaction against dollarization in Turkey to date. Of course, it is not possible to get results with the campaign alone, but if you look at why the reaction is coming out now and in what environment, you can see important clues for the future. As seen in many developing countries, the most important example of which in the world is Argentina, in fixed or predictable exchange rate regimes, foreign exchange controls are low and capital movements are free but stability cannot be achieved; then economic agents want to keep both their assets and liabilities in dollars. It is quite natural, because keeping their assets in dollars protects them against inflation, while borrowing foreign currency seems less costly than borrowing in domestic currency, since the exchange rate is predictable. Whenever risks are realized and countries switch to a floating exchange rate regime, after the initial devaluation, economic agents begin to be unable to manage both their assets and liabilities, because the exchange rate is no longer predictable, and there is a reaction to dollarization. In short, it is not a coincidence that dollarization cannot be broken in Argentina, where the Monetary Board regime is applied, but that there is a reaction against dollarization only after the transition to this regime in countries that have switched to a floating exchange rate regime. WHAT DO WE EXPECT NEXT? It is clear that we will move towards better days within the framework of what has been discussed so far. As long as what is done is better evaluated and cooler thinking. If all these steps taken towards the consolidation of the economic foundations are better understood, the points we have drawn attention to above about the convertibility of the domestic debt stock and the floating exchange rate regime that we think are very important are better understood, and considering that the political debates that have a negative shock effect on the economy have gradually fallen off the agenda starting from August, there is no reason why the economic expectations should not turn positive. As a matter of fact, it is seen that the perceived risks have decreased in recent weeks and the economic expectations are directed towards the level of positivity that the program being implemented deserves. This environment, as I mentioned before, has contributed to the healthier functioning of the foreign exchange markets by making it possible for the Central Bank's interventions to be reduced to a level that can be ignored. On the other hand, a continuous downward trend is observed in Treasury interest rates. FRAMEWORK OF THE NEW MONETARY POLICY I would now like to reiterate the main objective of the Central Bank and the framework of monetary policy it will pursue to achieve this goal.  Within the framework of the final version of the Law, the main purpose of the Central Bank is to ensure price stability. The main tool that the Central Bank will use against developments that it considers destabilizing prices is the short-term interest rate.  No concern other than price stability plays a role in determining the short-term interest rate and will not play a role. When it sees a permanent change of trend in any of the leading indicators of inflation that threatens price stability, and if there is no compensatory development in other leading indicators of inflation, it is clear that the Central Bank will change short-term interest rates within the framework of its commitment to price stability. There is a point we would like to draw your attention to here: The fact that one of the leading indicators of inflation has movements that change the trend of inflation is not enough to change short-term interest rates. What matters is the direction and strength of the net impact of movements in all leading indicators on inflation. In this context, the Central Bank will turn to 'inflation targeting' in the very near future, and now I want to address this issue. With the implementation of an inflation targeting-type policy, the Central Bank, together with the Government, will make an inflation forecast for a certain period and make it public. Then the Center The Bank's monetary and exchange rate policies will be solely and exclusively aimed at meeting this target. The aim is to shed light on economic units about inflation expectations through a selected 'nominal anchor'. 'Inflation targeting' is this kind of nominal anchor. There are some prerequisites for the implementation of a policy in the form of inflation targeting. First of all, the sole purpose of the Central Bank should be price stability. With the new Central Bank Law, price stability has been made the sole target of our Bank. Strong inflation forecasting models are essential to be able to do this kind of targeting in a purposeful way. To this end, it is necessary to determine the strategies of communication, expand the information base for economic and financial indicators. Similarly, fiscal discipline must be ensured. One of the most important points regarding inflation targeting is that the exchange rate-price relationship must be weakened. Political stability is also extremely important within this structure. Inflation targeting is not just about announcing an inflation target. It is a well-known fact from the practices in the world that with the implementation of such a policy together with all the institutional arrangements required, the markets will have a very satisfactory level of information about monetary policy. Thus, a significant part of the uncertainties in the decision-making processes of economic units will be eliminated. However, 'inflation targeting' alone is not an economic policy that will reduce inflation. It is possible for the inflation target to acquire a strong nominal anchor function and therefore to be successful if it is considered together with a policy bundle that consolidates the economic foundations and that the economic expectations are formed at the positive levels that this policy bundle deserves. FINALLY, in the very near future, as the current policies achieve their goals, with the expectations turning positive, the desired results from the implementations will be more visibly obtained, and all segments of society will be able to feel a certain relief.

Ama, seilen bir nominal apa vastasyla enflasyon bekleyileri hakknda ekonomik birimlere k tutmaktr. Enflasyon hedeflemesi bu tr bir nominal apadr. Enflasyon hedeflemesi eklindeki bir politikann uygulanmasnn baz n koullar vardr. Hereyden nce, Merkez Bankasnn tek amacnn fiyat istikrar olmas gerekir. Yeni Merkez Bankas Kanunu ile fiyat istikrar Bankamzn tek hedefi haline getirilmitir. Bu trden bir hedeflemeyi amacna uygun bir ekilde yapabilmek iin gl enflasyon ngrs modelleri olmas arttr. Bu amala, iletiimin stratejilerinin belirlenmesi, ekonomik ve mali gstergelere ynelik enformasyon tabannn geniletilmesi gerekir. Benzer ekilde mali disiplinin mutlaka salanmas zorunludur. Enflasyon hedeflemesine ilikin en nemli noktalardan birisi de kur-fiyat ilikisinin mutlaka zayflamas gereidir. Siyasi istikrarda bu yap ierisinde son derece nemlidir. Enflasyon hedeflemesi, sadece bir enflasyon hedefinin aklanmasndan da ibaret deildir. Bu tr bir politikann gerektirdii tm kurumsal dzenlemelerle birlikte uygulamaya konulmasyla, para politikas hakknda piyasalarn ok doyurucu dzeyde enformasyona sahip olacaklar dnyadaki uygulamalardan bilinen bir gerektir. Bylece, ekonomik birimlerin karar alma srelerindeki belirsizliklerin nemli bir ksm ortadan kalkacaktr. Ancak, enflasyon hedeflemesi tek bana enflasyonu drecek bir iktisat politikas deildir. Enflasyon hedefinin kuvvetli bir nominal apa ilevi kazanmas, dolaysyla baarl olmas, iktisadi temelleri salamlatran bir politika demetiyle birlikte ele alnmasna ve iktisadi bekleyilerin bu politika demetinin hak ettii olumlu dzeylerde olumasyla mmkndr. SON OLARAK ok yakn bir gelecekte, mevcut politikalar hedeflerine ulatka, bekleyilerin de olumluya dnmesi ile birlikte, uygulamalardan arzu edilen sonular daha gzle grlebilir bir ekilde alnabilecek ve toplumun tm kesimleri belli bir rahatlama hissedebilecektir.

Title: Speech of President Ba at the Press Conference on the Introduction of the "Inflation Report-IV"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: 2012 OCTOBER INFLATION REPORT PRESS CONFERENCE Erdem BACI 24 October 2012, Istanbul Dear Guests, Welcome to the press conference where we will share the main messages of the Inflation Report with you. I would now like to make an overview of the Report, which will be published on our website in a moment. In the Report, as always, we share our assessments of macroeconomic developments with the economic outlook that form the basis for monetary policy decisions and present our medium-term inflation forecasts and monetary policy stance updated in line with the developments in the last three months. In addition to the main sections of the Report, we have included nine boxes on various topics. Each of these boxes contains analyses of current and interesting topics. For example, the Report includes a box that examines the effects of managed prices and indirect tax adjustments on consumer inflation. We also have an enlightening box on the Reserve Option Mechanism, which we attach importance to and actively use in the financial stability wing of monetary policy. Another study introduces the index of financial conditions for Turkey, which is derived using various monetary and financial indicators. You see the titles of the boxes on the mirror. I recommend you to read these studies, which will be published on our website within the scope of the Inflation Report in a moment. For those who are interested, I would like to add that a larger version of some of these boxes can be accessed from the research publications tab on our website as "Economic Notes" or "Study Communique". Dear Guests, Today, I will summarize the recent developments in the country and present our updated inflation forecasts within this framework. At the end of my speech, I will convey our views on the short-, medium- and long-term growth outlook. 1. Monetary Policy Practices and Monetary Conditions Recently released data shows that the policies we have implemented have largely achieved their purpose. While the growth composition is getting an increasingly healthy outlook, the balancing process in the economy continues. As you can see in the reflection, while the improvement in the current account balance continues (Chart 1), the contribution of net exports to growth increases significantly (Chart 2). 2 0110 0410 0710 1010 0111 0411 0711 1011 0112 0412 0712 Chart 1. Accordingly, we expanded the interest rate corridor upwards in late 2011 and achieved a strong monetary tightening with effective liquidity operations. Until mid-2012, we periodically underwent additional monetary tightening due to fluctuations in risk appetite and upside risks to the inflation outlook. During this period, we maintained the upward tightening flexibility by keeping the upper limit of the interest rate corridor at high levels (Chart 3). We see that this stance prevents the deterioration of medium-term expectations in an environment where negative supply-side effects are becoming evident and inflation is in double digits (Chart 4). Source: CBRT. Since mid-2012, we have gradually brought monetary policy to a more supportive position. Both the re-recovery trend of global risk appetite and the current account balance and the composition of growth 3 The fact that the announced data indicated that the balancing process in the economy was strengthening had a positive effect on risk perceptions towards Turkey. On the other hand, the contribution of domestic demand to inflation in the direction of decline became evident in this period. As a result of all these developments, we have gradually reduced the average cost of funding by increasing the liquidity we have given to the market since the beginning of June. In this process, we ensured that the interest rates formed in the overnight market remained at low levels (Chart 3). Since September, we have gradually lowered the upper limit of the interest rate corridor while increasing the liquidity supplied to the market, both in view of the reduction of the worst possibilities for the global financial system and in order to support the credit market. Dear Guests, Although we have recently moved liquidity conditions to a more supportive position, we have generally taken a cautious stance. Accordingly, we emphasized that the increases in managed/directed prices and energy prices pose a risk to pricing behaviors and stated that the cautious stance will continue. In addition, we pointed out that uncertainties about the global economy continue, and it would be appropriate to maintain flexibility in both directions in monetary policy. We reiterated that we will carefully monitor the effects of the measures we have taken on loans, domestic demand and inflation expectations and in this direction, we will adjust the amount of Turkish lira funding downwards or upwards when necessary. Depending on the liquidity policy we implemented, a significant decrease in short-term interest rates was observed in the third quarter of the year. Long-term interest rates declined to a limited extent due to the decrease in the risk premium. As a result of these developments, market interest rates shifted down in each term compared to the previous reporting period, while the slope of the yield curve was upward (Charts 5 and 6). 4 Return (percent) 0111 0311 0511 0711 0911 1111 0112 0312 0512 0712 0912 Chart 5. In the last quarter, we think that both supply and demand side factors will work to support the credit volume. As a matter of fact, in parallel with the decline in market interest rates, consumer loan rates continue their downward trend (Chart 8). With the effect of the reductions in the upper limit of the interest rate corridor, we expect commercial loan rates to decrease in the coming period. In this context, we estimate that the growth rate of total loans at the end of the year will be close to 14 percent as predicted. Chart 7. Source: CBRT. Another prominent development in the financial stability wing of monetary policy in the third quarter of the year was the steps we took regarding the Reserve Option Mechanism (ROM). A part of the required reserves in Turkish lira to banks 5 ROM, which allows you to hold in foreign currency and gold, is basically a new tool that we have developed to increase the resilience of the economy against external financial shocks. We expect this system to reduce the imbalances that may occur between foreign exchange supply and demand due to changes in capital flows. We aim for the mechanism to function mainly as an automatic stabilizer after the construction process is completed. For a more comprehensive analysis on this topic, you can take a look at a study we published as an Economic Note on our website earlier this week. 2. Macroeconomic Developments and Basic Assumptions Dear Guests, I will now touch upon the macroeconomic outlook and assumptions that form the basis of our forecasts. First of all, I would like to compare our short-term forecasts, which we shared in July, with the realizations in the third quarter of 2012 and summarize the recent inflation developments. Then I will talk about the domestic and international demand outlook. In the third quarter of 2012, inflation rose to 9.2 percent as of September, slightly above the forecasts presented in the July Inflation Report (Chart 9). Inflation was higher than predicted by the recent increases in oil and unprocessed food prices and public price adjustments. Chart 9. National income data for the second quarter of 2012 showed that domestic demand conditions were weaker compared to the outlook we set out in the July Inflation Report (Chart 12). Recent data indicate that final domestic demand continued to slow in the third quarter. Accordingly, we have updated the output gap forecasts for the short term to the downside compared to the previous report. 7 Chart 12. Preliminary data point to a moderate recovery trend in consumption demand for the last quarter of the year. Considering the recent credit developments and the delayed effects of the supportive monetary policy we have implemented since mid-year, we expect consumption demand to increase in the coming period. We anticipate that the investment trend will recover more slowly due to global uncertainties. In the third quarter of the year, external demand continued to slow down like domestic demand. Since the publication of the July Inflation Report, the external demand outlook has been weaker than predicted. As a matter of fact, the downward updates made in the global growth forecasts in the third quarter of the year point to lower levels for the export-weighted global growth index (Chart 13). In particular, the weak growth outlook for the Eurozone limits our external demand. However, with the contribution of market and product diversification, we expect that exports will maintain their relatively positive course in the coming period. 8 Chart 13. Source: CBRT, Bloomberg, Consensus Forecasts July and October 2012 Releases. In summary, in producing our forecasts, we have based on an outlook in which the contribution of aggregate demand conditions to the decline in inflation has increased compared to the previous Report. I would like to state that the impact of this development on our 2012 year-end inflation forecast is in the direction of reducing by 0.1 percentage point. Dear Guests, As you know, food, energy and import prices also play an important role in inflation forecasts. So, before we move on to the predictions, I will briefly convey our assumptions about the variables in question. In the period since the publication of the July Inflation Report, oil prices have exceeded our forecasts due to supply-side factors (Chart 14). Accordingly, we have updated the 2012 average oil price assumption, which we stated as USD 110 in the July Inflation Report, to USD 112 by updating it upwards. While this update for the full year may seem limited, it does mean that our assumption of an average oil price for the second half of the year has been significantly raised. Accordingly, we increased our assumptions for 2013 from USD 100 to USD 107. Import prices have similarly exceeded our assumptions in the recent period. Taking into account recent realizations and futures prices, we have updated our import price assumption upwards compared to the previous Report (Chart 14). These updates to oil and import prices 9 Together with the developments in the exchange rate, we can say that it affects the 2012 year-end inflation forecast by 0.4 points in total. Chart 14. Source: Bloomberg, CBRT. * Scanned area shows the forecast period. Source: CBRT, TurkStat. Volatility in unprocessed food prices continues to create uncertainty over short-term forecasts. As we enter the last quarter of the year, we observe that the prices of unprocessed food are much more positive than the averages of previous years. Despite this, we have maintained our assumption of the annual rate of increase in food prices at 7 percent, as cautiously as in the previous Report. Before proceeding to the estimates, I will finally convey our assumptions about public finances. The most fundamental development that required an update to short-term inflation forecasts compared to the outlook we presented in the July Inflation Report was the recent tax increases and energy price adjustments. I would like to point out that the impact of these regulations on our 2012 year-end inflation forecast is in the direction of increasing by 0.9 percentage points. In producing our medium-term forecasts, we assumed that tobacco prices would rise in early 2013 at the rates implied by the tax regulations announced in October 2011. On the other hand, I would like to point out that we are based on an outlook in which other tax adjustments and managed/directed prices will be in line with inflation targets and automatic pricing mechanisms. 10 As always, we have taken the Medium Term Program (MTP) projections as the basis for the fiscal policy stance. In this context, we assumed that fiscal discipline would continue in the coming period and that there would be no significant change in the structural budget balance. 3. Inflation and Monetary Policy Outlook Dear Guests, I will now present to you our inflation and output gap estimates that we have produced within the framework I have drawn up to this point. While creating our forecasts, we assumed that monetary policy would maintain its cautious and flexible stance and that the growth rate of loans would be around 14 percent. In this context, we estimate that inflation will be in the range of 6.9 percent to 7.9 percent at the end of 2012, with a midpoint of 7.4 percent. Our forecast for the end of 2013 is in the range of 3.8 percent to 6.8 percent, with a midpoint of 5.3 percent. In the medium term, we anticipate that inflation will stabilize at the level of the 5 percent target (Chart 15). Percent Chart 15. Source: CBRT. In summary, we have updated our 2012 year-end inflation forecast by 1.2 percentage points to 7.4 percent, mainly due to adjustments in energy prices. In the table on the mirror, you see a summary accounting of the update in question. 11 Table 1 Sources of Update to 2012 Year-End Inflation Forecast Oil and Import Prices 0.4 points Tax and Managed Price Adjustments Output Gap Total Update to Year-End Forecast 0.9 points -0.1 points 1.2 points Here I would like to emphasize that our assumption about the prices of unprocessed food is quite prudent. With a cautious approach for the end of the year, we assumed that the annual rate of increase in food group prices would be 7 percent. For example, if food inflation is 5 percent instead of 7 percent at the end of the year, it will be possible to finish the year with an inflation of around 6.9 percent. Our updated forecasts show that there will be a significant decrease in inflation despite price and tax adjustments on managed/directed products in the last quarter of the year. We anticipate that moderate domestic demand conditions will limit the secondary effects of increases in energy prices and that core inflation indicators will continue to decline gradually. In this context, we anticipate that inflation will be close to the 5 percent target at the end of 2013. At this point, I would like to emphasize again that any new data and news to be released may cause us to change the monetary policy stance. Therefore, the assumptions I have made about the outlook for monetary policy in formulating our forecasts should not be taken as a commitment made by us. In addition to this base scenario I have mentioned, we also touch on alternative scenarios in the Risks section of the Inflation Report. You can review the Report for details. 4. Price Stability, Financial Stability and Growth Dear Guests, Now, I would like to summarize our views on Turkey's growth outlook for the short, medium and long term. We can list the messages we want to give in this regard as follows. 12 Starting from the last quarter of the year, inflation in Turkey is expected to decrease and growth to accelerate. In the medium and long term, the three main determinants of the growth rate are price stability, financial stability and productivity-enhancing structural reforms. Reducing inflation to single digits has eliminated the biggest obstacle to Turkey's growth potential. Stabilizing inflation around the 5 percent target will provide additional benefits for both growth and financial stability. A long time above GDP in domestic demand can lead to the accumulation of risks to financial stability. Therefore, the harmonious growth of domestic demand and production together will be healthy and sustainable. With the measures taken recently in Turkey, the mismatch between domestic demand and production has begun to be eliminated. This development will contribute to achieving the healthy and sustainable growth trend foreseen in the Medium Term Program in the coming period. Progress on structural reforms could further increase the potential growth rate. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey supports growth by maintaining price stability and contributing to financial stability. In the coming period, the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey will continue to contribute to financial stability with the measures it will take. Price stability will continue to be the primary goal. Dear Guests, While concluding my speech here, I would like to express my gratitude to all my colleagues and participants who contributed to the preparation of the Report, especially the employees of our General Directorate of Research and Monetary Policy and the members of the Monetary Policy Committee, and wish you a happy and peaceful Eid. 13

Title: Speech at the 3rd Istanbul Financial Summit
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: STANBUL FINANCE SUMMIT 2012 Erdem BAcI 24 September 2012, stanbul 1 Distinguished Guests and Esteemed Members of the Press, I am glad to address you at the third stanbul Finance Summit. I would like to greet distinguished participants and guests on behalf of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey and myself. In my last years summit speech, I mentioned that stanbul is the candidate to be the most beautiful global financial center in the world. I tried to demonstrate the relationship between aesthetics and stability by referring to the golden ratio that is frequently used in geometry. However, in todays speech, I would like to place particular emphasis on how the harmony between credit growth and economic growth is linked to financial stability. I will start my speech by addressing the importance of financial stability and potential problems that might emerge if financial stability is overlooked. Then, I will mention Turkeys achievements regarding financial stability and the countrys contributions to global financial stability. There are three essential factors that determine the growth potential of a country; these are price stability, financial stability and productivity. Any weakness in any of these three factors may cause considerable harm to growth prospects. Economic history has many examples of this. The social costs of loss of price stability are now very well known by economists. Academic studies indicate that an inflation rate that is on average higher by 10 percentage points leads to a reduction in the GDP growth rate an average of a quarter point1. Meanwhile, the loss of financial stability has deep and long-term impacts on growth and employment.2 The cost of preventing a financial crisis is much lower than the cost of the crisis itself. Turkeys recent history is a very good example of this statement. The economic crisis, which Turkey went through in 2001, increased the countrys sovereign debt by 30 percentage points, and severely 1 Barro, Robert J. (1995). "Inflation and Economic Growth." NBER Working Paper Series, No: 5326. 2 Reinhart, Carmen M., and Kenneth S. Rogoff. (2009). This Time is Different: Eight Centuries of Financial Folly. Princeton, NJ: Princeton Press.; Taylor, A. (2012). The Great Leveraging, NBER Working Papers, No. 18290. 2 affected growth and employment prospects. As of 2002, Turkey focused on establishing price stability, financial stability and introducing structural reforms aimed at increasing productivity. As a result, while the countrys economic prosperity grew at a rapid pace, the financial sector gained a structure resilient to external shocks. The steps taken towards fostering financial stability helped Turkey recover rapidly after the 2008-2009 global financial crisis and it weathered the European sovereign debt crisis of 2011-2012 with minimum damage. Recent experiences by advanced and emerging economies reveal that there are two predominant approaches to financial stability, each with fundamentally different principles. The first of these is the approach adopted by Alan Greenspan, who was the Chairman of the Federal Reserve between 1987 and 2006; in my presentation I will call it the Greenspan Doctrine. The other approach is the one followed by Stefan Ingves, currently the Governor of the Sveriges Riksbank and at the same time the Chairman of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision; I will call this approach the Ingves Doctrine. While the Greenspan Doctrine asserts that financial crises are unavoidable, the Ingves Doctrine states that financial crises are avoidable if the necessary measures are taken by central banks and other supervisory authorities. First of all, lets see what happens in the case of the Greenspan Doctrine. Excessive credit growth due to loosening of financial regulations, and the resulting financial balloons might severely damage the economy in subsequent years if they are ignored by policymakers. This process is triggered by a rapid financial meltdown on the back of pricing behavior detached from economic fundamentals. Those who have become home owners through mortgage loans might lose their homes as the value of their assets falls short of covering their debts. Increased credit risk and a rapid tightening in credit conditions take hold of the whole economy, and unemployment rates soar. Meanwhile, outstanding loans continue to increase, which eventually leads to further decline in house prices and financial firms carrying a large amount of housing sector-based financial instruments on their balance sheets come under strain. This situation triggers a massive public response. To protect depositors, banks are nationalized and injected with capital. Besides, fiscal expansion is implemented by increasing public expenditures and reducing tax rates in order to revive the economy. This, in turn, leads to a rapid increase in the 3 public debt burden. Thus, an ignored financial problem results in a reduction in future generations welfare. Meanwhile, central banks opt for monetary expansion by injecting liquidity into the system. The Ingves Doctrine, however, defends the concept that financial crises are avoidable by adopting effective and prudent arrangements. According to this doctrine, macro-prudential measures taken to this end can prevent excessive credit growth and asset bubbles, the two main causes of financial crises. Distinguished Guests, The cost of preventing a financial crisis is much lower than the cost of the crisis itself. The most important leading indicator of a financial crisis is excessive credit growth. Developing countries learned this lesson by experiencing it several times. Developed countries, however, learned this lesson only in the financial crisis of 2008-2009. The importance of systemic risk along with macroprudential measures to mitigate this risk to ensure financial stability has necessitated reconsidering the link between regulatory frameworks and central banks. The enforcement of the Dodd-Frank Act in the US and the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB) in Europe as well as new regulations introduced in other countries all aim to mitigate systemic risk by means of macro-prudential measures. In this context, the Financial Stability Committee was established on 3 June 2011 in Turkey. The Committee is composed of the Central Bank of Turkey, the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency (BRSA), the Capital Markets Board of Turkey (CMB), the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund (SDIF) and the Undersecretariat of Treasury. Monetary easing policies implemented by central banks of advanced economies in the wake of the global financial crisis led to excessive credit growth in many emerging market economies with strong economic fundamentals including Turkey, and credit growth in Turkey exceeded 35 percent by the end of 2010. The authorities set the target for credit growth as 25 percent for end-2011 and below 15 percent for end-2012. These targets have been attained on account of the macro-prudential measures taken. Today, credit growth in Turkey has smoothly been brought to sustainable levels. 4 Distinguished Guests, Now I would like to briefly mention Turkeys contributions to global financial stability. Turkey became a member of the Financial Stability Board (FSB) on 29 April 2009. In 2014, Turkey will participate in G20 Troika and assume Annual Presidency of the G20 in 2015. During the period from 2014 to 2016, when Turkey will be taking part in G20 Troika, our representative from the Undersecretariat of Treasury will be assigned to the FSB Steering Committee. The Central Bank of Turkey became a member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) on 25 May 2009 and the Group of Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS) on 4 June 2009. The Bank will participate in the FSB Steering Committee during the period 2013  2015 when it will chair the FSB Regional Consultative Group for the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). At G-20 meeting held in Los Cabos, a number of emerging market countries including Turkey declared their intention to contribute to global financial stability by increasing the resources of the IMF. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey intends to contribute to IMF resources up to USD 5 billion, to be counted as part of its international reserves. As part of the governance reform of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), a New Constituency was established with countries Turkey, Austria, Hungary, the Czech Republic, the Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Belarus and Kosovo. According to this agreement, in the new group that will act from 2012 to 2022, Turkey will assume the Executive Director position for two-year term between 2014  2016 and 2018  2020. Austria will assume the Executive Director position between 2012-2014; the Czech Republic between 2016-2018, and Hungary between 2020-2022. In the upcoming period, the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey will continue to play its part in order to achieve and maintain price stability and to contribute to financial stability within the limits of its purview. Turkey will continue to contribute to global financial stability by sharing at 5 global platforms the lessons the country has learned from past experiences and the outstanding performance delivered on the back of the policies implemented for the past 10 years. Thank you very much for your attention. 6

CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Istanbul Finance Summit 2011 Erdem BAcI President 28 September 2011 Istanbul Ladies and Gentlemen, Distinguished Members of the Press; My talk will be about Istanbul as a financial center in 2023. What kind of a target can we set for Istanbul in 2023? When we ask ourselves what kind of financial center Istanbul is right now, we see that Istanbul is a beautiful financial center, one of the beautiful financial centers in the world. What does a beautiful financial center mean, let's do a thought exercise on this together. In 2023, Istanbul may become the most beautiful financial center in the world. We can set such a goal. It may not be the largest, most advanced, most complex financial center in the world, but it may be the most beautiful financial center. If we work in this direction, if we always take our steps in this direction, this will be a very positive development for Turkey and for the world. Alphonse de Lamartine, a French poet, writer and statesman who lived in the 19th century and served as the French Minister of Foreign Affairs, said: "If I were given the chance to look at only one city in the world, the city I would choose would be Istanbul." This is what Istanbul looks like from the outside. In terms of finance, Istanbul looks like this again from the outside today, especially for those who look at it from Europe. And that's an inside look. Two poets have said this about Istanbul and aesthetics. Title: Speech in Press Conference for the Presentation of the Inflation Report-II
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: 2013 APRIL INFLATION REPORT PRESS CONFERENCE Erdem BAcI 30 April 2013, stanbul Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the press conference held to convey the main messages of the Inflation Report. I will now present an overview of the report, which will soon be published on our website. The report typically summarizes the economic outlook underlying monetary policy decisions, shares our evaluations on macroeconomic developments and presents our medium-term inflation forecasts, which were revised in view of the developments in the last quarter, along with our monetary policy stance. In addition to the main text, the report includes eleven boxes entailing interesting and up-to-date analyses on various topics. For example, the report presents a box to contribute to a better understanding of the relationship between credit and economic environment. Moreover, there is a box offering a comprehensive analysis of the effect of employment initiatives of 2008 on various demographic groups. We also included informative studies on the influence of the revisions in the Manufacturing Industry Index and the capital accumulation on the Capacity Utilization Rates. Titles of the boxes are shown on the slide. I strongly recommend that you read these boxes, which will be on our website. Now, I would like to convey the main messages of the report. Firstly, I will review the global economic outlook, given its undeniable influence on our policies. Global economic activity continued to be weak in the first quarter of the year. Meanwhile, risk appetite and capital flows displayed a volatile outlook amid persisting uncertainties regarding the global economy (Chart 1). Problems related to the Euro Area and uncertainties regarding the economic policies of advanced economies stood out as the leading factors underlying the increase in the volatility of the risk appetite in this period. While the recent additional monetary easing by the BoJ stimulated the appetite for investment in risky assets, developments in Southern Cyprus and Italy proved that fragilities in the global economy remained significant. 2 Sustained quantitative easing in advanced economies causes global rates to remain at historic lows, and fuels capital flows towards emerging economies. On the other hand, lingering fragilities in the global economy lead to an unstable risk appetite. This outlook for global liquidity and risk appetite brings about large and volatile portfolio flows towards emerging economies (Chart 2). This underlines the importance of maintaining a flexible policy framework with multiple instruments. Chart 1. Due to these policies, 2012 was marked as a year of re-balancing. As seen on the slide, the composition of growth displayed a healthier outlook, while the current account continued to improve (Chart 3). The contribution of net exports to growth increased markedly (Chart 4). In the second half of 2012, credits decelerated further, domestic demand remained subdued and inflation followed a downward trend. Accordingly, we adopted a more accommodative monetary policy stance by gradually increasing the liquidity injected into the market. On the other hand, as of late 2012, accelerated capital inflows, revived credit growth and the appreciation pressure on the Turkish lira led us to re-focus on macro financial risks. As you may recall, we stated that in such an environment, the proper policy would be to keep interest rates low while preserving macro prudential measures. Accordingly, we reduced short-term interest rates in the first quarter of the year, while continuing with a moderate tightening through required reserves (Chart 5). The winding down of risks regarding the Euro Area, owing to the support of the ECB as well as the more effective use of the ROM, alleviated the need for a wide interest rate corridor as of end-2012. Therefore, we gradually narrowed the interest rate corridor by lowering the overnight lending rate (Chart 5). 4 Chart 5. In order to slow down the credit growth rate, which remained well above the reference value of 15 percent, we normalized the liquidity stance in late February. This has recently resulted in overnight market rates to hover around the policy rate (Chart 5). Moreover, we continued with a moderate tightening through required reserves so as to contain the excessively expansionary effects of capital inflows on credit growth. Strong capital inflows in this period necessitated further increases in ROCs, ensuring a more effective use of ROM. In the first quarter of the year, due to the ongoing uncertainties regarding the global economy as well as the volatility in capital flows, we maintained our stance that monetary policy should be kept flexible in both directions. In this context, I would like to remind you that the impact of the measures undertaken on credit, domestic demand, and inflation expectations will be monitored closely and the funding amount will be adjusted in either direction, when needed. Title: Speech in Press Conference for the Presentation of the Inflation Report-III
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: 2013 JULY INFLATION REPORT PRESS CONFERENCE Erdem BAcI 30 July 2013, Ankara Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the press conference held to convey the main messages of the Inflation Report. I will now present an overview of the report, which will be published on our website soon. The report typically summarizes the economic outlook underlying monetary policy decisions, shares our evaluations on macroeconomic developments and presents our medium-term inflation forecasts, which were revised in view of the developments in the last quarter, along with our monetary policy stance. In addition to the main text, the report includes nine boxes entailing interesting and up-to-date analyses on various topics. For example, the report presents a box to contribute to a better understanding of the dynamics regarding the underlying trend of the current account balance in recent years. What is more, there are studies elaborating on the effects of the reserve options mechanism and our liquidity policy. There is also a box analyzing the effects of domestic cost factors on inflation. We also included studies on the hours worked and exports dynamics in the non-farm sector regarding the real sector in this report. Titles of the boxes are shown on the slide. All of these shed light on noteworthy issues in the Turkish economy. I strongly recommend that you read these boxes, which will soon be published on our website. Now, I would like to convey the main messages of the report. Firstly, I will review the global economic outlook given its undeniable influence on our policies. Developments regarding the global monetary policy influenced financial markets in the second quarter of the year. Persisting fragilities in the global economy in addition to increased uncertainty over the monetary policies of advanced economies led to higher volatility in the risk appetite (Chart 1). In particular, the Feds signals for a pullback on bond purchases in the near future have resulted in capital outflows from emerging economies as of May (Chart 2). 2 Chart 1. Despite the stable growth in the US economy, the weak course of the Euro area economies and the slowdown in emerging economies still persist. The recent surge in the volatility of capital flows has exacerbated the downside risks on emerging economies through the credit and expectations channel. In such an economic environment, maintaining a flexible monetary policy framework with multiple instruments remains crucial in order to preserve price stability while observing financial stability. 1. Monetary Policy and Monetary Conditions Since end-2010, the CBRT has been implementing a monetary policy framework designed to take macro financial risks into account. Accordingly, we place special emphasis on containing the distortionary effects of capital flow volatility on price stability and financial stability. In fact, the new policy framework contributed greatly to the considerable decline in the portion of the current account balance stemming from cyclical effects. As seen on the slide, the current account balance excluding gold displayed a notable improvement in 2012. The stabilization trend has recently lost pace; still, a deterioration is out of the question. As you will recall, owing to the improved inflation outlook and strengthened capital inflows as of the third quarter of 2012, the CBRT opted for a gradual monetary easing. Despite occasional fluctuations stemming from the global risk appetite, liquidity policy in this period has been largely accommodative (Charts 4 and 5). We reduced short-term interest rates and the CBRT average funding rate until May 2013. Moreover, in order to alleviate the adverse effects of capital inflows on macroeconomic stability, reserve options coefficients were gradually raised. Chart 4. Elevated uncertainties regarding global monetary policies caused rapid capital outflows from all emerging economies, including Turkey. This resulted in an 4 excessive depreciation of the Turkish lira and fluctuations in financial markets, which led the CBRT to tighten the liquidity policy by changing the composition of the liquidity injected into the market (Chart 4). Multiple elements to fuel inflation appeared simultaneously in the last couple of months, leading inflation to record a higher-than-expected increase in the shortterm. In the July meeting, the MPC decided to raise the upper band of the interest rate corridor by 75 basis points to contain the distortionary effects on the pricing behavior and to support financial stability. I will elaborate on these effects shortly. Moreover, we introduced some arrangements to strengthen the effects of the interest rate corridor and the liquidity policy on the days of additional monetary tightening. I would like to emphasize that the monetary policy will remain cautious until the inflation outlook aligns with the medium-term targets and we may implement additional monetary tightening when deemed necessary. Meanwhile, the Turkish lira liquidity policy was provided with more flexibility in the face of the persisting uncertainties regarding the global economy and the volatility in capital flows. Accordingly, I would like to remind you that developments regarding price stability and financial stability will be closely monitored and necessary adjustments will be made regarding the composition of the Turkish lira liquidity. These decisions on the interest rate corridor have been helpful in alleviating the exchange rate volatility. As you know, the rise in the risk premiums of emerging economies and fluctuations in the foreign exchange markets caused our exchange rate volatility to record a relative increase. Before moving on to forecasts, I will talk about our assumptions regarding public finance. Medium-term projections are based on the assumption that no additional tax adjustments will be introduced to tobacco and energy products the rest of the year. Meanwhile, we assumed other tax adjustments and administered prices would be consistent with the inflation targets and automatic pricing mechanisms. In other words, we assume that the liquidity policy will be tight, the interest rate corridor will be actively used when necessary, and the annual growth rate of credit will fall to 15 percent by mid-2014.
