Source: Bloomberg, CBRT. * Shaded region indicates the forecast period Source: CBRT, TURKSTAT. There was a limited downward revision in the assumption for food price inflation for end-2012. Due to the favorable course of unprocessed food prices in the first half of the year, food prices increased at considerably lower rates compared to historical averages. However, the overall effect of these lower rates was not reflected on our forecasts. Instead, forecasts were based on a cautious stance, which entailed the assumption that the favorable course of food prices in the first half would be largely reversed in the second half. Accordingly, the assumption for the annual rate of increase in food prices, which was 7.5 percent in the previous report, was revised downwards by only 0.5 percentage points to 7 percent in the current report. The contribution of this revision to the inflation forecast for end-2012 was around 0.15 percentage points on the downside. Before moving on to forecasts, I would like to finally share with you our assumptions regarding the public finance. As usual, we base our assumptions on the revised projections of the Medium Term Program (MTP). Accordingly, the ratio of primary expenditures (accumulated over 12-months) to GDP is assumed to remain largely unchanged in the second half of the year. As per the arrangements introduced to taxes imposed on tobacco products in the last quarter of 2011, tobacco prices are envisaged to remain unchanged throughout 2012, and increase at the beginning of 2013 at rates implied by the tax adjustments announced in October 2011. Furthermore, other tax adjustments and administered prices are assumed to be consistent with the inflation targets and the automatic pricing mechanisms. 11 3. Inflation and Monetary Policy Outlook Distinguished Guests, Now, I would like to present our inflation and output gap forecasts based on the outlook I have described so far. When forming our forecasts, we have assumed that monetary policy will maintain its cautious and flexible stance, and annual loan growth rate will be around 14 percent by the end of the year as in the previous report. Accordingly, inflation is expected to be between 5.3 and 7.1 percent (with a mid-point of 6.2 percent) at the end of 2012, and between 3.4 and 6.8 percent (with a mid-point of 5.1 percent) at the end of 2013. Inflation is expected to stabilize around 5 percent in the medium term (Chart 15). Percent Chart 15. Inflation and Output Gap Forecasts Forecast Range* Output Gap 12 10 8 6 4 2 0 -2 -4 Uncertainty Band Year-End Inflation Targets Control Horizon * Shaded region indicates the 70 percent confidence interval for the forecast. Source: CBRT. 0611 0911 1211 0312 0612 0912 1212 0313 0613 0913 1213 0314 0614 0914 1214 0315 0615 Overall, the year-end inflation forecast is lowered by 0.3 percentage points to 6.2 percent mainly owing to the downward revisions in energy and food prices (Chart 15). Revised forecasts indicate that inflation will resume a downward trend following a slight increase in July. However, I would like to emphasize that we will see the significant decline in inflation in the last quarter of the year. We expect that the fall in inflation will become more evident in the last quarter of the year since the base effect stemming from tax adjustments in administered products and unprocessed food will be removed. As for the core inflation indicators, the downward trend is expected to continue in the rest of the year. 12 At this point, I would like to emphasize that any new data or information regarding the inflation outlook may lead to a change in the monetary policy stance. Therefore, assumptions regarding the monetary policy outlook underlying our inflation forecasts should not be perceived as a commitment on behalf of the CBRT. 4. Risks and Monetary Policy In the last part of my speech, I would like to share our assessment of the risks on inflation outlook. As I have mentioned at the beginning of my speech, the lingering uncertainties regarding the global economy requires the maintenance of a flexible approach in monetary policy. The perception that leading central banks will keep interest rates at low levels for a prolonged period encourages the search for alternative yields. Meanwhile, despite the steps taken for the resolution of problems regarding the Euro area, risk appetite remains highly sensitive to news due to ongoing fragilities in the financial system, elevated levels of sovereign borrowing costs and weakening growth outlook. Therefore, it is highly likely that short-term capital inflows will continue to be volatile in the forthcoming period. I would like to emphasize again that, it is important to preserve the flexibility of monetary policy in either direction in these circumstances. In current circumstances, many different risk scenarios may be developed on the global economy. Now I would like to touch upon some of them, which we consider important, and inform you about how the monetary policy might be shaped should these risks materialize. A further weakening in global economic outlook may prompt central banks of developed economies to implement additional monetary easing in the period ahead. We think that such an event may feed into macro financial risks for emerging economies like Turkey. A resurge in short term capital inflows may slow down the rebalancing process within the Turkish economy through rapid credit growth and appreciation pressures on domestic currency. Should such a risk materialize, the CBRT may keep short-term rates at low levels while tightening through reserve requirements, including the mechanism it has developed for reserve requirements by increasing the coefficients, which define 13 the amount of foreign exchange to be held per unit of Turkish lira reserve requirements. It is also likely that problems in the Euro area may further intensify, given the ongoing deleveraging process in banking, household and public sector balance sheets and possible delays in the institutional mechanisms to resolve the related problems. Should such a risk materialize and lead to a new global turmoil, the immediate reaction could be to implement an active liquidity policy via the interest rate corridor; to be followed by measures to relieve the tension in the banking system through the use of reserve requirements as well as other liquidity instruments. At this point, I would like to underline that our existing rich policy tools as well as having a flexible monetary policy make it possible for us to promptly take the necessary measures to relieve the tension in the financial system during these periods. In the meantime, aggregate demand and commodity prices may increase faster than expected, should the measures taken towards the solution of problems regarding the global economy are completed sooner and more decisively than envisaged. Materialization of such a risk would possibly require a tightening using all policy instruments, as it would mean increased pressures on the medium-term inflation outlook. Distinguished Guests, Uncertainty regarding the commodity prices might be cited as another risk for the forthcoming period. Although weak global outlook dampens the upside pressures on commodity prices, prevailing geopolitical and supply-side problems pose upside risks regarding energy prices in the short term. Moreover, the recent rapid increase in agricultural commodity prices pose risks regarding processed food prices. Should such risks materialize, the CBRT will not respond to temporary price movements, yet will not tolerate any permanent deterioration in expectations and pricing behavior. Unprocessed food prices pose downside risks on the inflation outlook in 2012, as indicated in the April Inflation Report. We have adopted a rather cautious approach in the current report, assuming a reversal in the favorable trend observed during the first half of the year. End-year inflation may be lower than 14 projected in the baseline scenario, should the unprocessed food prices display a more favorable course than expected. Inflation will continue to stay above the target for some time, necessitating a cautious stance regarding pricing behavior. Although the monetary tightening implemented since last October and the moderate outlook of aggregate demand reduces the likelihood of second round effects, pricing behavior will be monitored closely in the forthcoming period. Distinguished Guests, The CBRT will continue to monitor fiscal policy developments closely while formulating its monetary policy. As I have already mentioned, the forecasts presented in the baseline scenario take the framework outlined in the Medium Term Program as given. In this respect, it is assumed that there will be no additional deterioration in the budget balance in the second half of the year as well as no unforeseen hikes in administered prices. A revision in the monetary policy stance may be considered, should the fiscal stance deviate significantly from this framework and have a consequent adverse effect on the medium-term inflation outlook. I would like to highlight that maintaining the prudent fiscal policy implemented in recent years is crucial for preserving the resilience of our economy against existing global uncertainties. Strengthening the structural reform agenda that would ensure the sustainability of the fiscal discipline and reduce the saving deficit would support the relative improvement of Turkeys sovereign risk, and thus facilitate price stability and financial stability in the medium term. This will also provide more flexibility for monetary policy and contribute to social welfare by keeping interest rates on long-term government securities at low levels. In this respect, steps towards implementation of the structural reforms envisaged by the Medium Term Program remain to be of utmost importance. While concluding my remarks, I would like to thank all my colleagues, who contributed to the Report, primarily those at the Research and Monetary Policy Department as well as the members of the Monetary Policy Committee, and thank every one of you for your participation. 15

Title: Speech at the Press Conference on the Introduction of the Inflation Report
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: ON THE INTRODUCTION OF THE INFLATION REPORT Sureyya Serdengecti January 31st, 2006, Ankara Dear Members of the Press, Dear Guests, The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey adopted the inflation targeting regime as of January 2006. In the inflation targeting regime, the Central Bank announces its inflation targets in figures, undertakes to achieve these targets and is obliged to answer to the public in case the announced targets are not achieved. Inflation reports are of particular importance in terms of making this framework functional. I want to open up about this a little bit more. Since monetary policy decisions require a certain period of time to affect the economy, the Central Bank can have an impact on future inflation, not on current inflation. Therefore, the creation of inflation forecasts at certain time intervals and the presentation of these forecasts to the public are critical in the inflation targeting regime. At this point, the necessity of a communication tool through which the Central Bank can share its evaluations of the macroeconomic outlook and inflation forecasts with the public is also raised. The Inflation Report undertakes exactly this function. In other words, the Inflation Report will be one of the communication tools of the Central Bank in the new period. Contents of the Inflation Report In the report, general macroeconomic developments are evaluated in a way to shed light on the trend that inflation will take in the medium term and future forecasts are presented. The report consists of six sections. The first part of the report provides a brief assessment of the year 2005 and summarizes the outlook for the whole Report. In the next four chapters, the latest developments in the economy are discussed in detail with an approach that will shed light on the future. These sections are listed as inflation, supply-demand, financial sector and public finance related developments. While explaining the developments, it is also clearly revealed how the Central Bank interprets the outlook of the economy in terms of inflation and monetary policy. In the last section of the Inflation Report, the economic developments evaluated throughout the Report and the outlook of the factors affecting inflation were aggregated and converted into inflation forecasts. In this section, the Central Bank's medium-term inflation forecasts are presented and the main risks are examined. Taking into account a framework in which the duration of the impact of monetary policy includes an average period of one and a half years, the forecasts are presented to cover the first half of 2007. The report also includes boxes that examine issues that are closely related to inflation dynamics. For example, the answer to the questions about the inflation-exchange rate relationship and how this relationship differs depending on the index change over time is included as a box in the report. Again in this first issue of the report, Special Comprehensive CPI indicators, the concept of core inflation, productivity 2 There are boxes that inform the public about the interpretation of data and fiscal policy commitments. Dear Guests, After this general introduction, I would like to summarize the evaluations in the new report that will be published on our website today and the inflation forecasts of the Central Bank. Supply-Demand Developments Dear Guests, Now I want to dwell on supply and demand developments. At the beginning of the main indicators of the developments in economic activity is the national income data published quarterly. Since there is a close relationship between economic activity and future inflation, these data become even more important in the era of inflation targeting. The Central Bank takes national income figures as the basic input when creating its inflation forecasts and creates its final forecasts, which I will present in a moment, after a process of forecasting and policy analysis that internalizes all the information and analysis produced within the Bank, within a 5-week period following the announcement of these figures. You will appreciate that in this process, the correct interpretation of data on economic growth and demand conditions is extremely critical. These efforts will also support the fight against inflation. In the light of all these evaluations, it is estimated that the contribution of supply-demand conditions to the decline of inflation in the coming period will be more limited compared to previous years. Financial Markets and Financial Brokerage Dear Guests, In parallel with the ongoing improvements in expectations in the recent period, the decrease in risk perception continued. As a result of the cautious stance of monetary policy, the continuation of budget discipline and the fact that the realized inflation is in line with the target, expectations have maintained their positive course. In addition, developments such as progress in structural reforms, the transition to three-year planning in the budget, the resolute continuation of the medium-term program, the start of negotiations for full membership to the European Union, the monetary reform and the strengthening of financial stability have reduced the risk premium and increased the demand for investment instruments denominated in the New Turkish lira. Following these developments, maturities began to extend throughout the economy, the gradual decline in medium- and long-term real interest rates continued, and the strong position of the New Turkish lira continued. Medium-Term Forecasts Dear Guests, The developments I have summarized so far indicate that the process of decline in inflation will continue, albeit slowly. The important question at this point is what this determination means in terms of the attainment of medium-term goals. Because, while establishing monetary policy, it is taken as a basis that the outlook of inflation in the medium term is in line with the targets, taking into account the delayed effects. Here is the answer to this question 17 In order to be able to give inflation forecasts that are produced in accordance with the macroeconomic outlook, they are presented in detail in the last section of the Inflation Report. Since the period in which the delayed effects of Monetary Policy are seen intensely covers a period of one and a half years, inflation forecasts are given until mid-2007. This framework also allows for an immediate lack of an immediate response to the temporary effects of external shocks on inflation, allowing for an emphasis on medium-term goals and for policy response to be spread over time. In this context, the short-term effects of increases in tobacco products prices in December and oil prices in January on inflation should be evaluated. The medium-term inflation forecasts have been obtained by quantifying the macroeconomic outlook that I have outlined so far. When generating forecasts; model results, expert opinions and assessments of the Monetary Policy Committee were also taken into account. At this point, I would like to underline an extremely important point that should be considered when interpreting forecasts: The values that inflation will take in the future are the combination of many factors affecting inflation. One of these elements is how monetary policy will be shaped today and in the future. Accordingly, forecasts are considered under various assumptions about the future behavior of monetary policy. This form of presentation has been preferred both because it increases transparency and because it allows more information to be transferred. Undoubtedly, over time, as the perceptions of economic units about inflation targeting develop, this representation may also change. Accordingly, the first forecast chart in the report is presented under a monetary policy stance in which short-term interest rates, the Central Bank's policy instrument, followed a horizontal course at the beginning of the year and then gradually declined. In such a perspective, inflation is projected to be in the range of 4.7 to 6.3 percent at the end of 2006 and will continue to decline over a period of time from now to one and a half years. The points that need to be noted here are that the interest rate path in question is a path that is derived in the light of today's information consistent with medium-term targets, that it "certainly does not have" the character of a commitment given by the Central Bank, and that this path will naturally change when economic conditions and assumptions change. 18 Chart 20. I feel the need to emphasize here again that the estimates are produced in the light of today's set of information. It should be noted that all the assumptions underlying the forecasts are likely to change over time, and in such a case, naturally, both the forecasts and the future stance of monetary policy will change. For example, volatility in food prices, indirect tax adjustments, or developments that may affect other assumptions I just mentioned will lead to a review of forecasts and policy perspectives. Dear Guests, In the last part of the presentation, I would like to elaborate on some of the risks that may lead to a significant review of the forecasts. Forecasts made in the world about oil prices change frequently and do not present a consistent appearance. For this reason, the Central Bank considers the possibility of continuation of oil price increases among the main risk factors. The effects of oil prices on inflation can be divided into two as primary and secondary effects. The primary effects are seen in goods and services for which oil prices are heavily input. Primary effects, particularly manifested in some sub-items of the transport and housing group, contributed negatively to inflation in 2005. Although the contribution of oil-sensitive sub-items to inflation was up to 1.5 points during the year, the total effect of the year decreased to around 1 point with the relaxation of oil prices in the last period of the year. Secondary effects are mostly manifested through relative prices and expectations. For example, the fact that the rise in oil prices affects the general CPI index and thus inflation expectations increase and this situation is reflected in pricing behavior and wages can be expressed as a secondary effect. It is a generally accepted view that if oil prices rise, central banks should not react to the primary effects of this rise. As a matter of fact, in 2005, the secondary effects of oil prices were limited and therefore the Central Bank did not react. Although inflation fell by 1.6 points during 2005, inflation expectations for 12 months later fell by about 2.9 points, indicating that secondary effects will continue to be limited at the beginning of 2006. The second factor, which creates the potential for a significant deviation in the forecasts for the coming period, is the developments that may lead to volatility in the risk premium. Risk premium; It is possible in any case to be affected by possible fluctuations in international liquidity conditions, possible problems on the way to the EU or other developments. In recent years, long-term interest rates in developed countries have fallen to historically low levels. 21 This has led to global funds being directed especially to developing countries such as Turkey, which have taken important steps towards stability. If these trends reverse, there may be fluctuations in the financial markets. Although recent developments contain signals that this trend may continue in 2006, shocks from this direction may have an impact on inflation in the current conjuncture. In such a case, if the shock is perceived temporarily, the medium-term approach will be acted upon and there will be no reaction in the short term. On the other hand, a permanent increase in the risk premium could put pressure on inflation by causing the New Turkish lira to depreciate permanently. Although the exchange rate-inflation relationship has slowed down in the floating exchange rate regime, the effects of permanent increases in this period have not been fully tested. In this context, a permanent movement in the risk premium may require monetary policy to react. Apart from these; volatility in the prices of agricultural products, other energy and commodity prices, indirect tax adjustments, and risks from publicly controlled prices of goods and services are also always present. Dear Guests, It should be remembered that in the economy such shocks can always occur. The main thing in the inflation targeting regime is that the Central Bank makes a commitment to keep inflation close to the target in the medium term, can explain its forecasts transparently in this context, and when a shock comes to inflation, it informs the public about the time of convergence to the target again and the monetary policy to be followed in this regard. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey has set out to fulfill these principles. That the inflation targeting regime is not the end of monetary policy; rather, it should be remembered that it is the beginning of an uninterrupted process of "development". In this process, it is of great importance to read the Inflation Report carefully in order to increase mutual interaction and information sharing with the public and to make the regime more functional. Thank you. 22

Title: Speech at the Press Conference on the Introduction of the "Inflation Report-IV"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: ON THE INTRODUCTION OF THE INFLATION REPORT Durmu YILMAZ October 31st, 2008, Ankara Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the launch meeting of the fourth issue of the 2008 fourth issue of the Inflation Report, one of the most important communication tools of the inflation targeting regime we are implementing. In this meeting, I would like to summarize the Central Bank's inflation forecasts with our evaluations in the Inflation Report that will be published on our website and the open letter that will be published today. 1. Inflation Developments Dear Members of the Press, Starting with our general assessments of the inflation developments in the past period, I would like to share with you the strategy we have implemented as the Central Bank to reveal the reasons for the deviation of inflation from the targeted path and to achieve the medium-term targets as the Central Bank. Dear Guests, the upper limit of the uncertainty range of 8.5 percent for the end of the third quarter of 2008 has been exceeded by the annual CPI increase of 11.13 percent. In the Inflation Reports and open letters we published in April and July, we stated that the target was expected to be significantly exceeded by the end of 2008 and shared the reasons for this with the public in detail. I would like to briefly recap these reasons. Developments in food and energy prices continued to be the main determinant of inflation in the third quarter. Although energy and other commodity prices have declined since September, delayed effects have continued to keep inflation at high levels. In this context, approximately 7 points of the annual inflation of 11.1 percent as of September was caused by the direct effects of food and energy prices (Chart 1). 2 Chart 1. With favorable weather conditions and declines in agricultural commodity prices, the annual rate of increase in food prices decreased from 14 percent at the end of the second quarter to 11.1 percent in the third quarter. Monetary Policy Response Dear Guests, After briefly evaluating the inflation developments in the past period, in this part of my speech, I would like to mention the policies we have followed as the Central Bank in this process. In order to stop the deterioration in inflation expectations and to prevent supply-side shocks from reflecting on general pricing behavior, a 150 basis point tightening was made in the May-July period. The strategy of implementing the change in inflation targets together with monetary tightening was successful in controlling inflation expectations, and inflation expectations improved in the third quarter of the year (Chart 5). In this context, short-term interest rates were kept constant in the August-October period (Table 1). In a statement issued after its last meeting, the Monetary Policy Committee assessed that the impact of the movements observed in exchange rates on inflation would be compensated by the positive outlook in food prices and the sharp decline in oil prices. However, it has been stated that the increasing global uncertainties in the recent period requires caution in both inflation forecasts and monetary policy decisions. First of all, I would like to summarize the economic framework that forms the basis of these estimates. In the second quarter of 2008, there was a significant slowdown in private consumption and investment expenditures. In addition, the contribution of total public expenditures to growth during this period was negative. In parallel with the slowdown in domestic demand, the slowdown in imports of goods and services, the preservation of the strength of external demand and the increase in tourism revenues ensured that the contribution of net exports to growth was positive. In an open letter published in July, we stated that we expected a gradual recovery in economic activity. However, the fact that the problems in global markets have become evident in the meantime has indicated that the slowdown in economic activity will continue. As a matter of fact, the recent course of domestic sales, production and confidence indices indicates that the slowdown in domestic activity has become more pronounced since July (Chart 6). While the turbulence in global financial markets is felt all over the world, it is estimated that private consumption and investment expenditures in our country will continue to follow a stagnant course. At this point, I think it is useful to remind you that in the October Inflation Report, which will be published on our website a little later, you can find indicators of the trend of domestic demand in more detail. However, it is anticipated that the slowdown in the economic activity of our trading partners will have a partially limiting effect on this contribution. At this point, I would like to open a parenthesis and emphasize that the forecasts made according to the current data indicate a significant improvement in the current account deficit next year. As a result, in parallel with the slowdown in both domestic and foreign demand, we anticipate that aggregate demand will continue its stable course in the coming period. Therefore, when creating our forecasts, we foresee a framework in which the support of aggregate demand conditions to the decline in inflation increases compared to the previous period (Chart 10). We anticipate that a significant slowdown in domestic demand will limit the transition from exchange rate to prices. Therefore, the relationship between exchange rate and inflation is expected to be weaker in the current period compared to past periods. However, we estimate that the direct effects of exchange rate movements on annual inflation will be 1.2 points at the end of 2008 and 1.5 points at the end of 2009. A sharp decline in oil prices over the past period has led to a downward update of our assumptions (Chart 12). Taking into account the expected positive course of unprocessed food prices and the decline in agricultural commodity prices, our assumptions about food prices have been updated downwards. Within this framework, the assumption of food price inflation was reduced from 14 percent to 11 percent for 2008 and from 9 percent to 7.5 percent for 2009. This change caused the inflation forecasts for 2008 and 2009 to be updated downwards by 0.8 and 0.4 percentage points, respectively. In addition, food price inflation was reduced from 7 percent to 6 percent for the end of 2010. With the cumulative effects of supply-side shocks, service inflation increased higher than expected in the third quarter of the year. This development had an upward effect of 0.6 points in our 2008 year-end inflation forecasts compared to the previous period. In the coming year, due to the slowdown in aggregate demand, service inflation is expected to show a significant decline. As a result, it was anticipated that the pressures created by the developments in the exchange rate on inflation would be compensated by the positive course of food and energy prices and the slowdown in domestic demand, and accordingly, no significant changes were made in our medium-term inflation forecasts. I find it useful to emphasize that monetary policy should maintain its flexibility especially in the current conjuncture where uncertainties have reached high dimensions. 4. Risks Dear Members of the Press, I would like to devote the last part of my speech to the upside and downward risks related to inflation and monetary policy in the coming period. Due to the problems experienced in international credit markets in the recent period, there has been a loss of confidence in global financial markets. These developments have adversely affected the flow of global liquidity, creating an extraordinary demand for US dollar liquidity in particular. Central banks act quickly and in a coordinated manner 12 It is trying to eliminate the liquidity squeeze in money markets in order to ensure the effective functioning of the markets. In this direction, we have taken a series of measures to make the functioning of our markets regular. The first of these measures was the resumption of intermediary activities in the Foreign Exchange Warehouse Market under the Central Bank. Secondly, foreign exchange purchase tenders were suspended in order to further strengthen the liquidity situation of Turkish banks. Thirdly, in order to prevent unhealthy price formations in the foreign exchange market, foreign currency liquidity has started to be provided to the market through foreign exchange auctions. In recent days, with the effect of positive developments in global markets, it has been decided to stop foreign exchange auctions with the decrease in concerns about the depth in the foreign exchange market. In addition, it has been publicly announced that other measures may be resorted to if necessary in order to ensure the effective functioning of our markets. It is estimated that the tightening in credit conditions will continue in the coming period. These developments pose an upward risk to inflation through possible portfolio movements in the short term and downside to the downside in the medium term through a slowdown in domestic demand. Given the current global uncertainties, monetary policy needs to be flexible in both directions. As a matter of fact, unlike previous reports, the report to be published today did not give a concrete signal about the outlook for short-term interest rates while presenting forecasts. Therefore, monetary policy decisions to be taken will be determined depending on the nature of the domestic repercussions of ongoing problems in global financial markets. Uncertainties in commodity prices continue to pose risks to inflation forecasts. Despite the downward update in food and energy prices, our estimates are based on rather cautious assumptions. For this reason, I would like to point out that the downside risks related to energy and food prices are at least as obvious as the upside risks. The inflation outlook, which is based on assumptions that food and energy prices are higher and lower than the base scenario, is presented in the last section of the Report. In the first scenario, food price inflation will show higher increases than the base scenario and will be realized as 12.5, 10 and 9 percent in 2008, 2009 and 2010, respectively; oil prices are assumed to remain stable after rising to USD 110 at the end of 2008. The projections we have made according to this scenario indicate that inflation will be around 8.9 percent at the end of 2009 and 7.1 percent at the end of 2010 under the assumption that monetary policy responds appropriately (Chart 14). Dear Guests, Since the Inflation Report and the open letter we published in July, there has been an extraordinary movement in the international markets. This process affects the inflation outlook through many different channels. First of all, the sharp depreciation observed in the New Turkish lira in the recent period will adversely affect inflation, especially in the short term. Secondly, the emergence that there may be a slowdown in domestic demand beyond what was predicted has increased the support of aggregate demand to reduce inflation. Finally, look at the sharp declines in commodity prices. 14 Our assumptions about food and energy prices have been updated downwards. When all these developments are evaluated together, it is estimated that the pressure of the exchange rate on inflation will be compensated by the positive course of food and energy prices and the slowdown in domestic demand. In this context, our updated estimates indicate that the targets set at 7.5, 6.5 and 5.5 percent in line with the Medium-Term Program for the next three years are achievable even under very cautious assumptions regarding food and energy prices. As the Central Bank, I find it useful to emphasize again that we are closely monitoring the developments in liquidity conditions. Recently, a number of measures have been taken to ensure that our financial markets continue to function effectively. The Central Bank will continue to do its part to limit the effects of turbulence in international markets on our economy. In this context, I find it useful to underline that the next policy decisions will be shaped largely according to the developments in the global markets and their reflections on the domestic market. In order to limit the impact of the current shocks on the economy, maintaining fiscal discipline and strengthening the structural reform process are at least as important as monetary policy. In this context, the continuation of the process of harmonization and convergence with the European Union and the continuity of the efforts to implement the structural reforms foreseen in the program remain important. In particular, I would like to end my speech by stating that we are closely following the developments in structural reforms aimed at improving the quality of fiscal discipline and ensuring the continuity of productivity increases in terms of both macroeconomic stability and price stability, and I thank you all. 15

Title: Speech of President Ylmaz at the Press Conference on the Introduction of the Inflation Report-IV
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: ON THE INTRODUCTION OF THE INFLATION REPORT Durmu? Yf5lmaz 31 October 2006, Ankara Dear Members of the Press, Dear Guests, The fourth issue of the Inflation Report, which is one of the most important communication tools of the open inflation targeting regime that we have started to implement since the beginning of 2006, is being published today on the website of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey. The Inflation Report analyzes macroeconomic developments that are decisive in the medium-term trend of inflation and includes inflation forecasts produced according to updated assumptions about key macroeconomic variables. In addition, the Report presents possible risks that may cause deviation in inflation forecasts to the public. Contents of the Inflation Report The Inflation Report consists of seven sections. In the first part of the Report, a general assessment of macroeconomic developments is made in the light of the latest data, inflation forecasts and possible risks are summarized. In the five following chapters of the Report, international economic developments, inflation, supply and demand, financial markets and public finances, respectively, are analyzed in detail. In the last section of the Inflation Report, inflation forecasts prepared to cover the first quarter of 2008 are included in line with the determinations and assumptions made regarding the main macroeconomic variables at home and abroad. This section also examines in detail the main risks that may lead to deviations from medium-term inflation forecasts. As in previous reports, this issue of the Inflation Report contains boxes in which evaluations are made on some of the issues on the agenda. The report includes boxes that examine price developments in international commodity markets and analyze the relative importance of domestic and international factors that determine capital movements towards Turkey. Dear Members of the Press, After this brief briefing on the content of the fourth issue of the Inflation Report, which will be published on our website today, I would like to summarize the evaluations contained in the Report and the inflation forecasts of the Central Bank. 1 International Economic Developments The strong growth trend observed in the world economy in the last three years has led to rapid demand and price increases in commodity markets. However, with the effect of the slowdown in the US economy since the second quarter of the year, a decline in commodity prices was observed (Chart 1). Chart 1. Annual inflation, which accelerated in the second quarter of the year, remained high in the third quarter as well, staying above the uncertainty range created around the path in line with the target as of the end of September. The main factors causing inflation to rise are the delayed effects of the depreciation of the New Turkish lira in the second quarter of the year due to the deterioration in international liquidity conditions on prices and the rapid upward trend in unprocessed food prices. The continuation of the high annual increase in service group prices was another factor that adversely affected inflation. The declines observed in oil and gold prices in international markets had a positive effect on inflation dynamics. Chart 3. It is observed that the fluctuation created an increase of approximately 4.1 points compared to the pre-volatility inflation expectation at the end of the year. Asked for the longer term, inflation expectations for the next twelve and twenty-four months were 7.3 percent and 5.6 percent, respectively, as of the second survey period in October. These results show that economic units expect that the process of decline in inflation will continue gradually in the medium term. Despite the fact that it is in the process of recovery, the fact that inflation expectations for both the next twelve months and the next twenty-four months are still above the targets in terms of level emerges as a risk factor in determining wages and prices and requires caution. 7 Supply and Demand Developments Dear Members of the Press, After summarizing inflation developments in this way, I would like to present our evaluations of supply and demand developments in the light of the latest data. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased by 7.5 percent in the second quarter of 2006 compared to the same period last year (Chart 11). When the growth of the economy is examined in terms of production, it is seen that the added value of the industrial sector, which slowed down significantly in the first quarter of the year, increased at a high rate in the second quarter of the year and made the highest contribution to growth. In response to the revival in industrial production, the added value of the agricultural sector declined and the contribution of the services sector to growth decreased compared to the first quarter of the year. The increase in spending on durable goods has been an important determinant of consumption expenditures. The slowdown in the increase in investment expenditures was caused by the decrease in the increase in private sector machinery and equipment investments as well as the decrease in the investments of the public sector. Leading indicators of demand indicate that total domestic final demand will slow in the second half of the year, driven by sectors that are more sensitive to financing conditions. High non-interest surpluses and resulting privatization revenues limit the rate of increase of the debt stock, while New 12 The depreciation of the Turkish lira after the fluctuation in May and June was a development that increased the debt stock (Chart 16). However, this increase in the exchange rate is related to recognition and it should be taken into account that the real cost will arise as the debt payment takes place. Therefore, the level of exchange rate on the dates of the payment of foreign currency denominated debt will have an impact on the debt stock rather than the current increase. As a matter of fact, the central government debt stock increased in May and June due to the depreciation of the New Turkish lira, but with the reinforcement of the New Turkish lira in the following months, the increase in the debt stock remained limited. However, the relatively long-term nature of the current stock of foreign currency denominated debt and the fact that the Treasury holds a large amount of foreign currency deposits limit the risks arising from currency volatility to the public sector. Medium-Term Predictions Dear Members of the Press, In the last part of my speech, I would like to present our medium-term inflation forecasts, which are prepared to shed light on the questions of how inflation will proceed in the coming period and how long it will converge to the target. Determinations on the Current Situation, Short-Term Outlook and Assumptions First, I will summarize the macroeconomic outlook that forms the basis for our medium-term forecasts. As I have just mentioned, the GDP data released in September pointed to an acceleration in economic activity and strong domestic demand in the second quarter of the year. Our forecast that domestic demand will slow down from the second half of the year is maintained. As a matter of fact, the leading indicators of demand in the past three months support our prediction. On the other hand, increases in net external demand continue due to the strong global growth trend observed in the recent period. In addition, the acceleration in public expenditures is also remarkable. Thus, while indicators of private sector domestic demand, which are components of aggregate demand, point to a slowdown, the increase in public spending and net external demand is a limiting factor in the slowdown in aggregate demand. However, despite the increase in net external demand, the slowdown in domestic demand is expected to prevail and the growth rate is expected to decrease compared to past periods. In this context, there is a framework in the production of inflation forecasts in which demand conditions contribute to the process of decline in inflation. In the last Inflation Report, it was predicted that the annual CPI inflation, which accelerated in the second quarter of the year, would remain high in the third quarter. As a matter of fact, as of the end of September, CPI inflation was above the uncertainty range around the path in line with the target. In the last quarter of the year, the delayed effects of the depreciation of the new Turkish lira will be partially eliminated, the positive developments observed in crude oil prices and the expectation that unprocessed food prices will remain more positive towards the end of the year. 13 The rise in inflation is expected to stop, however, at the end of the year inflation is nevertheless projected to occur above the uncertainty range around the path in line with the target. The assumptions regarding foreign factors are as follows: that growth in the euro area will continue without acceleration and is in the range of 2.5-3 percent as of the end of 2006; During 2007, it is expected to decline and be in the range of 1.5-2 percent by the end of the year. Eurozone Harmonised Consumer Price inflation is expected to be close to the 2 percent target. The upward movement created by the strong global growth trend seen in recent periods on crude oil prices has reversed in recent months, and crude oil prices have entered a downward trend. In this context, our assumptions regarding international oil prices have been reduced from USD 70 to USD 60. Despite this short-term conjecture update in oil prices, our forecasts were produced and it was taken into account that the delayed effects of the high oil price increases observed in the past period will continue to adversely affect inflation, especially through increases in natural gas and electricity prices. Forecasts Dear Members of the Press, The Central Bank announces at every opportunity that it focuses on the consistency of future inflation with the target and creates monetary policy decisions with a medium-term perspective. In this context, what is important for the Central Bank is not the temporary fluctuations in inflation, but the convergence of inflation to the target in the medium term. In this part of my speech, I would like to present the inflation forecasts produced with this medium-term perspective and covering the first quarter of 2008. 14 Chart 17. Risk Factors Dear Members of the Press, Possible changes in global risk appetite and the resulting new fluctuations in financial markets continue to be one of the main risk factors in the inflation outlook. Inflation concerns in the economies of developed countries seem to have been replaced by concerns about economic slowdowns in the recent period. Both situations could lead to increased global risk perception and lead to volatility in emerging market economies. 1 The projected figure for the year-end of 2007 is between 3.5 and 6.8 percent. 15 may adversely affect inflation in the short term. If medium-term expectations are adversely affected, the Central Bank will not refrain from monetary tightening. On the other hand, it should also be taken into account that a global cooling may mean a more positive inflation outlook in the medium term, through the decline in oil and other commodity prices. Another factor that creates uncertainty in terms of the inflation outlook is the risks that may be caused by high medium-term inflation expectations and retrospective pricing habits in the service group. Service inflation, which is around 12 percent in the current period, is expected to decline slightly in the coming year in parallel with the expected slowdown in domestic demand. However, the continuation of the retrospective pricing behavior, the fact that the 2007 revenues policy is not fully compatible with the inflation target and that the service price inflation continues to remain high due to other structural factors emerge as a risk. Given that the contribution of income policy to the process of decline in inflation in 2007 will be limited, the risk of inertia in inflation becomes even more pronounced. The fact that the impact of increases in non-interest public expenditures on inflation in 2007 is not fully known and other uncertainties related to the monetary transmission mechanism are considered among the risk factors that may lead to the differentiation of the framework we have drawn regarding the total inflation outlook. The Central Bank will continue to closely monitor the effects of the recent monetary tightening on the economy. Monetary policy will tighten further if the improvement in the medium-term inflation outlook is slower than expected as a result of the realization of the risks listed above. Apart from all these, from the point of view of the medium and long-term outlook, the continuation of the process of harmonization and convergence with the European Union and the implementation of structural reforms related to the economic program as planned without interruption remain critical. Continuing the decisive steps taken in these areas in recent years with the same determination in the coming period will contribute to overcoming the changes in the international conjuncture with the least fluctuation. Orta Vadeli ngrler Deerli Basn Mensuplar, Konumamn son ksmnda, enflasyonun nmzdeki dnemde nasl bir seyir izleyeceine ve hedefe hangi srede yaknsayacana ilikin sorulara k tutmak zere hazrlanm olan orta vadeli enflasyon tahminlerimizi sunmak istiyorum. Mevcut Duruma likin Saptamalar, Ksa Vadeli Grnm ve Varsaymlar ncelikle, orta vadeli tahminlerimize temel oluturan makroekonomik grnm zetleyeceim. Biraz nce deindiim gibi, Eyll aynda aklanan GSYH verileri, yln ikinci eyreinde ekonomik faaliyette hzlanmaya ve gl i talebe iaret etmitir. Yln ikinci yarsndan itibaren i talebin yavalayacana dair ngrmz ise korunmaktadr. Nitekim, getiimiz  aylk dnemde talebe ilikin aklanan nc gstergeler de bu ngrmz destekler niteliktedir. te yandan, son dnemde gzlenen gl kresel byme eilimine bal olarak net d talepteki artlar devam etmektedir. Bunun yannda kamu harcamalarndaki hzlanma da dikkat ekicidir. Dolaysyla, toplam talebin bileenleri olan zel kesim i talebine ilikin gstergeler yavalamaya iaret ederken, kamu harcamalar ve net d talepteki art, toplam talepteki yavalamay snrlayan bir unsur olmaktadr. Ancak, net d talepteki arta ramen, i talepteki yavalamann baskn olaca ve byme hznn gemi dnemlere kyasla azalaca ngrlmektedir. Bu balamda, enflasyon tahminlerinin retilmesinde, talep koullarnn enflasyondaki d srecine katk yapt bir ereve sz konusudur. Getiimiz Enflasyon Raporunda, yln ikinci eyreinde hzlanan yllk TFE enflasyonunun, nc eyrekte de yksek seyredecei ngrlmt. Nitekim, Eyll ay sonu itibaryla TFE enflasyonu hedefle uyumlu patika etrafndaki belirsizlik aralnn zerinde gereklemitir. Yln son eyreinde ise, Yeni Trk lirasnda meydana gelen deer kaybnn gecikmeli etkilerinin ksmen ortadan kalkmas, ham petrol fiyatlarnda gzlenen olumlu gelimeler ve ilenmemi gda fiyatlarnn yl sonuna doru daha olumlu seyretmesi beklentisine bal olarak yllk 13 enflasyondaki ykseliin duraca, ancak, yine de yl sonunda enflasyonun hedefle uyumlu patika etrafndaki belirsizlik aralnn zerinde gerekleecei ngrlmektedir. Yurt d faktrlere ilikin varsaymlar ise, zetle u ekildedir: Euro blgesinde bymenin ivmelenme olmakszn devam edecei ve 2006 yl sonu itibaryla yzde 2,5-3 aralnda; 2007 yl boyunca ise derek yl sonu itibaryla yzde 1,5-2 aralnda gerekleecei ngrlmektedir. Euro Blgesi Uyumlulatrlm Tketici Fiyatlar enflasyonunun yzde 2 hedefine yakn gereklemesi beklenmektedir. Son dnemlerde grlen gl kresel byme eiliminin ham petrol fiyatlar zerinde yaratm olduu yukar ynl hareket son aylarda tersine dnm, ham petrol fiyatlar dme eilimine girmitir. Bu erevede uluslararas petrol fiyatlarna ilikin varsaymlarmz, 70 ABD dolarndan 60 ABD dolar seviyesine ekilmitir. Petrol fiyatlarndaki bu ksa dnemli varsaym gncellemesine ramen, tahminlerimiz retilirken, gemi dnemde gzlenen yksek petrol fiyat artlarnn gecikmeli etkilerinin, zellikle doalgaz ve elektrik fiyatlarndaki artlar yoluyla, enflasyonu olumsuz etkilemeye devam edecei dikkate alnmtr. Tahminler Deerli Basn Mensuplar, Merkez Bankas, gelecekteki enflasyonun hedefle tutarllna odaklandn ve para politikas kararlarn orta vadeli bir perspektif ile oluturduunu her frsatta kamuoyuna duyurmaktadr. Bu balamda, Merkez Bankas iin nemli olan, enflasyonda meydana gelen geici dalgalanmalar deil, enflasyonun orta vadede hedefe yaknsamasdr. Konumamn bu ksmnda, sz konusu orta vadeli bak asyla retilen ve 2008 ylnn ilk eyreini kapsayan enflasyon tahminlerini sunmak istiyorum. 14 Grafik 17. Buna gre, 2006 yl sonunda enflasyonun yzde 70 olaslkla yzde 9,2 ile 10,6 aralnda gerekleecei tahmin edilmektedir. Para politikasnn mevcut sk duruunun 2007 ylnn son eyreinin bana kadar korunduu ve sonrasnda ll bir faiz indirimine gidildii bir senaryo altnda enflasyon orannn 2008 ylnn ilk eyrei sonunda yzde 1,7 ile yzde 5,2 aralnda gerekleecei ve bylece enflasyonun bir buuk yllk bir zaman diliminde hedef patikaya yaknsayaca tahmin edilmektedir.1 Anlan faiz patikasnn, mevcut bilgi setine dayanarak oluturulan bir politika erevesini ifade ettii ve yeni bilgilerin bu patikay deitirebilecei unutulmamaldr. Sonu olarak, enflasyondaki d eiliminin 2007 ylnn ikinci eyreinden itibaren belirginleecei ve para politikasnn ortalama kontrol ufku olan bir buuk yllk bir sre iinde enflasyonun orta vadeli hedeflere yaknsayaca tahmin edilmektedir. Risk Unsurlar Deerli Basn Mensuplar, Kresel risk itahndaki olas deiimler ve buna bal olarak finansal piyasalarda ortaya kabilecek yeni dalgalanmalar, enflasyon grnm konusundaki temel risk unsurlarndan biri olmaya devam etmektedir. Son dnemde gelimi lke ekonomilerindeki enflasyon kayglar yerini ekonomik yavalama kaygsna brakm grnmektedir. Her iki durum da, kresel risk alglamasnn artmasna yol aabilecek ve ykselen piyasa ekonomilerinde dalgalanmalara yol 1 2007 yl sonu iin ngrlen rakam ise yzde 3,5 ile 6,8 arasndadr. 15 aarak ksa dnemde enflasyonu olumsuz etkileyebilecektir. Orta vadeli bekleyilerin olumsuz etkilenmesi durumunda Merkez Bankas parasal sklatrmaya gitmekten kanmayacaktr. Dier yandan, kresel bir soumann, petrol ve dier emtia fiyatlarndaki d kanalyla orta vadede daha olumlu bir enflasyon grnm anlamna gelebilecei de gz nne alnmaldr. Enflasyon grnm asndan belirsizlik oluturan bir dier unsur ise yksek seyreden orta vadeli enflasyon bekleyilerinin ve hizmet grubundaki geriye dnk fiyatlama alkanlklarnn yol aabilecei risklerdir. Mevcut dnemde yzde 12 civarnda seyreden hizmet enflasyonunun, yurt ii talepte beklenen yavalamaya paralel olarak nmzdeki ylda bir miktar daha gerilemesi beklenmektedir. Ancak, yine de gemie ynelik fiyatlama davrannn srmesi, 2007 yl gelirler politikasnn enflasyon hedefi ile tam olarak uyumlu olmamas ve dier yapsal unsurlar nedeniyle hizmet fiyat enflasyonunun yksek seyretmeye devam etmesi bir risk olarak ortaya kmaktadr. Gelirler politikasnn 2007 ylnda enflasyondaki d srecine verecei katknn snrl olaca gz nne alndnda, enflasyondaki atalet riski daha da belirginlemektedir. Faiz d kamu harcamalarndaki artlarn 2007 yl enflasyonu zerindeki etkisinin tam olarak bilinmemesi ve parasal aktarm mekanizmasna ilikin dier belirsizlikler, toplam enflasyon grnmne ilikin izdiimiz erevenin farkllamasna yol aabilecek risk unsurlar arasnda deerlendirilmektedir. Merkez Bankas, getiimiz dnemde yaplan parasal sklatrmann ekonomi zerindeki etkilerini yakndan izlemeye devam edecektir. Yukarda sralanan risklerin gereklemesi sonucu orta vadeli enflasyon grnmndeki iyilemenin beklenenden yava olmas halinde para politikas daha da sklatrlacaktr. Btn bunlarn dnda, orta ve uzun vadeli grnm asndan, Avrupa Birliine uyum ve yaknsama srecinin devam etmesi ile ekonomik programa ilikin yapsal reformlarn planland gibi kesintiye uramakszn hayata geirilmesi kritik nemini korumaktadr. Son yllarda sz konusu alanlarda atlan kararl admlarn nmzdeki dnemde de ayn kararllkla srdrlmesi, uluslararas konjonktrdeki deiimlerin en az dalgalanmayla atlatlmasna katkda bulunacaktr. text: ON THE INTRODUCTION OF THE INFLATION REPORT Durmu Ylmaz 29 January 2007, Ankara Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the launch meeting of the first issue of the Inflation Report for 2007, one of the most important communication tools of the open inflation targeting regime we are implementing. The Inflation Report analyzes macroeconomic developments that are decisive in the medium-term trend of inflation and includes inflation forecasts produced according to updated assumptions about key macroeconomic variables. In addition, the Report presents possible risks that may cause deviation in inflation forecasts to the public. At this meeting, I would like to summarize the assessments in the Inflation Report, which will be published on our website today, and the inflation forecasts of the Central Bank. International Economic Developments Dear Members of the Press, I would like to begin with a brief overview of international economic developments. The price increases experienced in the commodity markets in recent years have been replaced by a decline in energy prices with the third quarter of 2006 (Chart 1). Chart 1. Medium-Term Predictions Dear Members of the Press, In the last part of my speech, I would like to present our medium-term inflation forecasts, which are prepared to shed light on the course of inflation in the coming period and how long it will converge to the target. 14 Current Situation, Short-Term Outlook and Assumptions First, I will summarize the macroeconomic outlook that forms the basis for our medium-term forecasts. As I mentioned earlier, the Gross Domestic Product data released in December was in line with our projections in the October Inflation Report. In the third quarter of the year, with the effect of developments in private consumption expenditures, it was seen that the predicted slowdown in domestic demand was realized. On the other hand, the increase in net external demand was also realized in line with our forecasts, causing the slowdown in total demand to be limited together with the upward trend in public consumption expenditures. Therefore, demand conditions continued to contribute to the downward trend of inflation in the third quarter of the year. On the other hand, the current data on demand conditions covering the past three months indicate that there was no slowdown in domestic demand in the last quarter of 2006 beyond the decline seen in the third quarter. Despite this, with the tight stance of monetary policy, the support given by demand conditions to the decline in inflation is expected to continue in the last quarter of 2006 and the first quarter of 2007. In the previous Inflation Report, we had predicted that annual inflation would decrease slightly in the last quarter of 2006 due to the partial elimination of the delayed effects of the depreciation of the New Turkish lira after May, the positive developments observed in crude oil prices and the expectation that unprocessed food prices would remain more positive towards the end of the year. As a matter of fact, a partial improvement in the inflation outlook was observed in the last quarter of the year. Another development that may contribute to the decline of inflation in the coming period will be the disappearance of the high base effect created by the supply-side shocks I have just mentioned. Factors such as the easing in energy and other commodity prices, the return of food prices to their normal trends, and the weakening of the impact of the exchange rate shock in 2006 on prices may lead to a significant decrease in annual inflation, especially from the second quarter of 2007 onwards. The assumptions regarding foreign factors can be summarized as follows: Growth in the Eurozone is expected to continue without acceleration and will be approximately 2 percent by the end of 2008. Eurozone Harmonized Consumer Price inflation is expected to be close to the 2 percent target by mid-year 2008. The slowdown in global growth, favorable weather conditions, the high crude oil stockpile in the United States, the relative stability in the Middle East and production increases have caused oil prices to develop more positively than our assumptions for October. In this context, our assumptions regarding international oil prices have been reduced from USD 60 in the previous Inflation Report to USD 55. Despite this assumption update in oil prices, when producing our forecasts, it was taken into account that the cumulative increases observed in the past period in oil prices could lead to an increase in items such as natural gas and electricity. On the other hand, October 15 The predictions we made regarding the risk premium in the month are maintained in this Report, and it is assumed that the risk premium will not change significantly in the coming period. Predictions Dear Members of the Press, Since the effects of monetary policy on the economy require a certain period of time to emerge, the Central Bank focuses on the consistency of future inflation with the target, not today's inflation, when formulating its policies. In this context, the Central Bank formulates its policy response with a medium-term perspective and does not react to the temporary effects of elements beyond the control of monetary policy on inflation. In this part of my talk, I would like to present our forecasts, which are created with a medium-term perspective in mind. The forecasts in the Inflation Reports published in 2006 were presented for a period of one and a half years. However, in order to contribute to the economic units to better see ahead and to create a forecast horizon comparable to the results of the Expectations Survey, it was decided to give the forecasts for two years starting from 2007 and this decision was announced to the whole public with the text of "Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy in 2007". Therefore, the estimates that I will present in a moment include the years 2007 and 2008 to cover a period of two years. Chart 17. The forecasts indicate that the downward trend in inflation will become evident in the second and third quarters of 2007 and that the current tight stance of monetary policy should be maintained for a while in order for inflation to converge to the medium-term target of 4 percent. The point I want to emphasize here is that this perspective on policy rates is derived under the current set of information and assumptions consistent with medium-term goals and is not a commitment made by the Central Bank. Therefore, it should not be forgotten that when the economic conditions and assumptions that form the basis of these predictions change, this path may naturally change. Risk Factors Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, I would like to devote the last part of my talk to the key risk factors that could lead to a significant deviation of the estimates I have presented in both directions. The main risk to the medium-term inflation outlook is the possibility of a stronger-than-expected resistance to inflation downwards. As a matter of fact, this resistance manifests itself in inflation expectations and service inflation. In the coming period, due to the slowdown in domestic demand as a result of monetary tightening, the annual price increase of the service group is expected to slow down. However, considering that the relative productivity in the service sector is low, pricing behavior tends to index to past inflation and is sensitive to wages, it is thought that service inflation will continue to be a risk factor in achieving medium-term targets in the coming period. Recent wage adjustments have made this risk even more pronounced. Another risk to the inflation outlook is uncertainty about the delayed effects of monetary policy on aggregate demand. The slowdown in economic activity in the third quarter of 2006 is thought to be due to the decline in consumer and producer confidence following fluctuations in financial markets rather than the tightening in monetary policy. Although the impact of the monetary tightening carried out since June 2006 on private sector demand has recently begun to be seen, it is not yet clear how long the slowdown in the economy will last and to what extent. In addition, the continued uncertainty regarding public expenditures poses an upside risk factor on aggregate demand and inflation. Another risk factor that has the potential to delay the convergence of inflation to the target is the sudden fluctuations that may arise in global markets. A faster-than-expected global growth 17 The possibility of a slowdown or a correction movement that may arise due to global imbalances remains among the scenarios that may adversely affect the economies of developing countries. The Central Bank will be able to review its policy rates if the fluctuations that are likely to be observed in the financial markets have permanent negative effects on the inflation outlook. On the other hand, if there is a cooling in the global economy or if the easing in commodity prices continues, there may be fluctuation in the financial markets of developing countries and our economy may be adversely affected. However, since our country is a net importer of commodities, it should not be forgotten that the improvement in foreign trade may have positive results in terms of the medium-term inflation outlook. Dear Guests, Developments in the field of structural reforms, which will improve the quality of fiscal discipline in the medium and long term, are closely monitored in terms of both macroeconomic stability and price stability. It remains critical that the process of harmonization and convergence with the European Union continues and that structural reforms related to the economic program are implemented as planned without interruption. Continuing the decisive steps taken in these areas in recent years with the same determination in the coming period will contribute to overcoming the changes in the international conjuncture with the least fluctuation. Thank you. 18
