Title: Speech at the Press Conference on the Introduction of the "Inflation Report-II"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: ON THE INTRODUCTION OF THE INFLATION REPORT Durmu Ylmaz 27 April 2007, Ankara Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the launch meeting of the second issue of the 2007 Inflation Report, one of the most important communication tools of the open inflation targeting regime we are implementing. The Inflation Report analyzes the developments that are decisive in the medium-term trend of inflation and includes inflation forecasts produced according to updated assumptions regarding key macroeconomic variables. In addition, the Report presents possible risks that may cause deviation in inflation forecasts to the public. At this meeting, I would like to summarize the assessments in the Inflation Report, which will be published on our website today, and the inflation forecasts of the Central Bank. International Economic Developments Dear Members of the Press, I would like to begin with a general assessment of international economic developments. Global growth and inflation developments, expectations regarding these indicators and the decisions of central banks stand out as risk factors that may affect developing countries in the international economy. As a matter of fact, the negative US economy data announced at the end of February 2007 and the concerns about the US real estate markets combined with the statements made on the possibility of the US economy entering a recession caused a new wave of sales in international markets. The Credit Suisse Global Risk Appetite Index, which reflects the attitudes of international investors towards risk, shows that risk appetite was interrupted by the fluctuation in the US in late February (Chart 1). However, the data released in March supported the view that the slowdown in the US economy developed at a moderate level and thus limited the effects of the financial volatility at the end of February. On the other hand, the rapid growth trend in the Eurozone and the recovery signals of the Japanese economy are expected to limit the effects of the possible soft slowdown caused by the US economy. 1 Chart 1 Credit Suisse Global Risk Appetite Index 10 6 2 -2 02/01/2006 02/05/2006 Source : Credit Suisse 02/09/2006 02/01/2007 As I mentioned at the beginning of my speech, the uncertainties regarding inflation and growth developments in industrialized countries, which caused sharp fluctuations in international relative prices during the fourth quarter of 2006, stand out as the most important risk factors for the international economy that may affect developing countries in the coming period. In this context, the rise in interest rates of developed countries and the economic performance of the United States in the coming period have the potential to adversely affect the demand for financial assets of developing countries. On the other hand, the suitability of global liquidity opportunities and the high level of risk appetite suggest that international conditions will remain positive in the second quarter of 2007. Crude oil prices, which declined in the last quarter of 2006, started to rise again starting from mid-January. The increase in demand caused by the aggravation of winter conditions, the production cuts of OPEC countries, the imbalances observed in the US crude oil and petroleum product stocks, and the political tensions in the Middle East caused oil prices to rise (Chart 2). 2 Chart 2. Oil Prices US dollar / barrel 90 80 70 60 50 40 03.01.2006 11.05.2006 14.09.2006 23.01.2007 Source: Bloomberg. Inflation Developments Dear Guests, In the first quarter of 2007, consumer prices increased by 2.36 percent, a higher rate than in the last three years, and annual inflation was 10.86 percent. Despite this year-on-year increase, inflation remained within the uncertainty range formed around the path in line with the target as of the end of the first quarter (Chart 3). The rise in annual consumer inflation observed in the first quarter is considered to be temporary and it is estimated that inflation will enter a significant downward trend from the coming months as the effect of the exchange rate shock in 2006 on prices weakens. Chart 3. Year-End Inflation Target and Annual CPI Inflation 12 11 10 9 8 7 6 Annual Inflation 5 4 Goal 3 Uncertainty Range 2 01.05 03.05 05.05 07.05 09.05 11.05 01.06 03.06 05.06 07.06 09.06 11.06 01.07 03.07 05.07 07.07 09.07 11.07 Source: TurkStat. 3 The increase in annual inflation was influenced by the developments in unprocessed food prices and the prices of "energy and unprocessed non-food goods". In the first quarter, the rate of increase in energy prices declined compared to the same period last year, while there was a limited decrease in the rate of increase in service prices (Chart 4). Chart 4. Consumer Prices (First Quarter Percentage Change) 12 10 2005 2006 8 2007 6 4 2 0 -2 Service Source: TurkStat, CBRT. Energy Unprocessed Food Energy and Unprocessed Food Non-Goods Unprocessed food prices, which increased by 11.74 percent in the first quarter, were one of the determining factors in the rise in consumer inflation. The fact that vegetable and fruit prices, which showed a slowing trend in the last quarter of 2006, accelerated again in the first quarter of 2007 by increasing above the seasonal trend indicates that the risks related to unprocessed food prices remain important. Inflation of goods other than energy and unprocessed food has risen as a result of developments in tobacco products, durable goods, clothing and footwear group, and processed food prices. (Chart 5). At this point, we think that a more detailed examination of these commodity groups will be useful in terms of a healthier evaluation of the reasons for the rise in annual inflation. As a result of the reflection of the adjustment made in the Special Consumption Tax on tobacco products on cigarette prices in the second half of February, the prices of tobacco products increased by 10.37 percent in the first quarter, which contributed approximately 0.5 points to annual consumer inflation. 4 In the first quarter of the year, annual inflation in the durable goods group excluding gold increased by 4.4 points. In this case, as a reflection of the long-term cumulative strengthening in YTL in the first quarter of last year, the low base effect of the significant decreases observed in the prices of the durable goods group played an important role. Currently, among durable goods, the highest response to the fluctuation in May 2006 was largely given by the imported car group. On the other hand, the increase in white goods group prices by approximately 8 percent in the first quarter of the year is thought to be influenced by both cost and strong external demand factors. The fact that seasonal movements in clothing prices show irregularities from time to time leads to volatility in annual increases in this group. In this context, while the annual inflation in the clothing and footwear group increased to 4.19 percent in the first quarter, it is observed that the winter season discount covering the December-March period was close to the previous year. In the upward trend in the inflation of processed food products, which became evident with the second quarter of 2006, it is seen that the price increases observed due to supply-side effects in grain production played an important role in the bread and cereals group  in addition to the delayed effects caused by the depreciation of YTL. Chart 5. Selected Non-Energy and Unprocessed Food Group Prices (First Quarter Percentage Change) 12 9 6 3 0 -3 -6 -9 -12 -15 -18 Processed Food Tobacco 2005 2006 2007 Apparel & Footwear Durable Goods (Excl. Gold) Source: TurkStat, CBRT. 5 The annual inflation of service group prices shows a more limited downward trend (Chart 6). Although the slowdown trend in domestic demand continued in the recent period and oil prices did not follow a negative course compared to the last quarter of last year, the fact that wage increases in general were above the medium-term inflation target, the fact that the service group was not as open to competition and productivity increases as the goods group, and the prevalence of indexing mechanisms to the past cause service price inflation to maintain high levels. Chart 6. Service Group Prices (Annual Percentage Change) 24 21 18 15 12 9 6 3 0 03.05 05.05 07.05 09.05 11.05 01.06 03.06 05.06 07.06 09.06 11.06 01.07 03.07 Other Services Real Rent Transportation Services Restaurants and Hotels Source: TurkStat, CBRT. The improvement process observed in medium-term inflation expectations since August 2006 showed a tendency to pause in the first four months of the year (Chart 7). It can be said that the uncertainty created by the rise in consumer inflation in the first quarter and the short-term fluctuation in international markets in March were effective in this development. However, it is estimated that there will be a gradual improvement in inflation expectations with the decline in annual inflation in the coming period. 6 Chart 7. CPI Expectations in 12 and 24 Months* (Annual Percentage Change) 12 12 Is 24 Is 10 8 6 4 2 0 08-04 10-04 12-04 02-05 04-05 06-05 08-05 10-05 12-05 02-06 04-06 06-06 08-06 10-06 12-06 02-07 04-07 * The CBRT Expectations Survey is the expectations for the second survey period. Source: CBRT. Supply and Demand Developments Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, After summarizing inflation developments in this way, I would now like to present our evaluations of supply and demand developments in the light of the latest data. Gross Domestic Product increased by 5.2 percent in the last quarter of 2006 and grew by 6.1 percent in 2006, with the effect of the updates made for the first three quarters of the year. In the last quarter of 2006, final domestic demand was below Gross Domestic Product, similar to the third quarter (Chart 8). While the slowdown in investments in durable goods and machinery and equipment limited final domestic demand, public spending did not make a significant contribution to final domestic demand. External demand significantly compensated for the decline in domestic demand. While the industrial added value continued to increase with the effect of the positive trend in exports, the construction sector continued to grow at a high rate, although not as much as in previous periods. The slowdown in domestic demand and imports has limited the value added increases in the trade and transport sectors. 7 Chart 8: GDP and Total Final Domestic Demand (Seasonally Adjusted for Seasons) 40000 Thousand YTL 38000 36000 34000 32000 30000 28000 26000 24000 03-I 03-II 03-III 03-IV 04-I 04-II 04-III 04-IV 05-I 05-II 05-III 05-IV 06-I 06-II 06-III 06-IV GDP Total Final Domestic Demand Source: TurkStat, CBRT. The trend in car and white goods sales, the stagnant course in consumer loans and the import of consumer goods do not indicate a significant change in private consumption expenditures in the first quarter of the year. While the statistics of building permits indicate that the vitality in construction investments will continue, the slowdown in machinery and equipment investments is expected to continue in the short term. With the contribution of the positive performance observed in exports, industrial production is thought to continue to increase in the first quarter of the year. March data on capacity utilization rate also support this view (Chart 9). Chart 9. Industrial Production Index  Capacity Utilization Ratio (Seasonally Adjusted 3-Month Moving Average) 85 145 140 83 135 130 81 125 79 120 Total CCO 115 SUE (Right Axis) 77 110 12/03 06/04 12/04 06/05 12/05 06/06 12/06 Source: TurkStat, CBRT. 8 Dear Guests, As I have just mentioned, as a result of the slowdown in domestic demand and the increase in the contribution of external demand to growth, the upward trend in the ratio of the current account deficit to Gross National Product stopped as of the end of 2006 (Chart 10). In the January-February period, the increase in exports was higher than the increase in imports in real terms. Preliminary data for March and April indicate that exports remain strong. Strong external demand, continued productivity growth and a slowdown in domestic demand are expected to support the improvement in the foreign trade deficit, and therefore the contribution of external demand to growth in the first half of 2007 is expected to continue. Chart 10. Current Account Balance / GNP* (Percent) 4 2 0 -2 -4 -6 -8 -10 * With annualized data. Source: CBRT. In summary, the available data suggest a similar composition of growth in the first quarter of 2007 to the second half of 2006. Accordingly, it is thought that the contribution of domestic demand to growth will be limited and that external demand will significantly support growth. The output gap estimates formed in the light of these evaluations on supply and demand conditions indicate that the support given by demand conditions to inflation towards a decline continues. 9 98-III 99-II 00-I 00-IV 01-III 02-II 03-I 03-IV 04-III 05-II 06-I 06-IV 00-I 00-III 01-I 01-III 02-I 02-III 03-I 03-III 04-I 04-III 05-I 05-III 06-I 06-III 07-I Chart 11. Output Gap (Percent) 8 6 4 2 0 -2 -4 -6 -8 -10 Source: CBRT However, taking into account the revisions made to 2006 growth, the output gap has been updated upwards compared to the January Inflation Report for the last quarter of 2006. In other words, it is assessed that the support given by the demand conditions in 2006 to the process of decline in inflation may be lower than that expressed in the January Inflation Report. In the first quarter of 2007, since no significant growth in aggregate demand is expected, the output gap is expected to be at a more positive level in terms of inflation compared to the previous quarter. Financial Markets and Financial Brokerage Dear Members of the Press, In this part of my speech, I would like to briefly talk about the developments in the financial markets. In the first quarter of 2007, international liquidity conditions and global risk appetite continued to favor developing countries. Although, at the end of February, there was volatility in the financial markets, this situation was short-lived and did not affect the inflation outlook. As a result, the positive trend in international liquidity conditions is reflected in the observed decline in Turkey's risk premium indicators (Chart 12). 10 Chart12. Risk Premium Indicators 5-Year KIF (CDS) Rates 800 700 600 500 400 300 200 100 JP Morgan EMBI Turkey Index 600 550 500 450 400 350 300 250 200 150 100 02/01/04 02/05/04 02/09/04 02/01/05 02/05/05 02/09/05 02/01/06 02/05/06 02/09/06 02/01/07 02/01/04 06/04/04 07/07/04 30/09/04 06/01/05 11/04/05 12/07/05 07/10/05 13/01/06 27/04/06 26/07/06 27/10/06 08/02/07 Source: Bloomberg. In the first quarter of 2007, with the effect of the Central Bank's resumption of foreign exchange purchase auctions, the excess liquidity sterilized in the overnight market was slightly higher than in the previous quarter. In this period, the continuation of the stable stance in monetary policy led to a decrease in inflation uncertainty, supporting the decline in long-term interest rates. The returns generated on 20 April 2007 were below the returns generated at the end of 2006 in each term due to the decrease in the risk premium and the decrease in inflation expectations. In addition, the fact that yield curves are downward from 18 months of maturity indicates that economic units maintain their expectation that the process of decline in inflation will continue in the medium term (Chart 13). Chart 13. Yield Curves Interest Rates 22 21 20 19 18 17 16 15 1 IS Source: ISE 2 IS 29 December 2006 20th Apr 2007 3 IS 4 MONTHS 6 MONTHS 9 MONTHS Number of Months Remaining to Maturity 12 IS 18 IS 24 IS 11 On the other hand, the strengthening process in YTL continued in parallel with the increase in YTL-denominated assets in the portfolios of investors residing abroad and the high foreign direct capital inflows. Global bond issuances carried out by foreign financial institutions in YTL, which is an indicator of the demand for YTL-denominated financial instruments abroad, continued their upward trend in the first quarter of 2007. This development indicates that in addition to seasonal effects, there is no deterioration in the risk perceptions of investors based abroad (Chart 14). Chart 14 Bonds Issued by Foreign Financial Institutions in YTL 5,0 New Issuance Amount 20 5000 (Billion YTL, Left Axis) 4,5 18 4500 Total Issuances (Billion 4,0 YTL) 16 4000 3,5 14 3500 Quantity (Million YTL) 3,0 12 3000 2,5 10 2500 2,0 8 2000 1,5 6 1500 1,0 4 1000 0,5 2 500 0,0 0 0 2007 2009 2011 2013 2015 2017 2019 2005-I 2005-II 2005-III 2005-IV 2006-I 2006-II 2006-III 2006-IV 2007-I Source: CBRT. Maturity Year When the credit developments are examined, it is observed that the credit growth rate, which slowed down after the Central Bank tightened its monetary policy in June 2006, exhibited a similar trend in the first quarter of 2007. In this context, while consumer loans continue to increase at a low pace, it is seen that the increase in question is mostly due to the "other loans" item consisting of short-term consumer loans and that vehicle loans and credit cards decrease in real terms (Table 1). Table 1. Receivables from Consumer Loans and Credit Cards (Real Quarterly Percentage Change) Consumer Loans Home Loans Car Loans Other Loans Credit Cards 2005 I 14,4 33,3 6,0 1,6 2,3 2006 I II II 17,2 20,0 1,5 29,2 22,8 0,9 1,9 5,1 -6,4 11,7 24,3 6,0 2,0 6,8 2,1 2007 IV I 3,3 2,6 2,0 2,7 -5,5 -8,9 8,7 6,6 4,4 -1,6 Source: CBRT. 12 In the recent period, although the liquidity in the domestic market has been on an upward trend and the positive course of external borrowing facilities have relatively improved the credit supply conditions, the fact that loan interest rates are still at high levels compared to the first half of 2006 continues to limit credit demand. Public Finance Dear Members of the Press, When the budget developments in the first three months of 2007 are evaluated, developments such as the fact that a savings package aimed at reducing non-interest expenses is on the agenda and the total receivables remaining from the sale of Turk Telekom were paid to the Treasury early in March and entered the budget as non-tax income reinforce the expectations that the central government budget targets for 2007 will be met. Dear Guests, We know from past experience that developments in debt dynamics affect the expectations of economic units, which have serious repercussions on risk premiums, interest rates and inflation. Therefore, developments in the debt stock are of great importance for macroeconomic stability. The central government debt stock, which constitutes a large part of the total public debt stock, increased by 3.7 percent as of February 2007 compared to 2006. On the other hand, the ratio of total public net debt stock to Gross National Product continued its downward trend in recent years, reaching 44.8 percent at the end of 2006 (Chart 15). Chart 15. Public Debt Stock Indicators (Billion YTL) 120 357,7 400 100 350 300 80 250 60 59,9 200 40 44,8 150 100 20 50 0 0 Percent 2001 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 2007 Central Government Total Debt Stock (Right axis) Total Public Net Debt Stock/GNP Source: Treasury. Central Management Total Debt Stock/GNP 13 In line with the implemented financing strategy, the average maturity of cash borrowing was 27.5 months in 2006, showing a significant extension trend since September. Recently, the share of fixed-income and variable-rate debt securities in the central government debt stock has increased, while the share of exchange rate-sensitive debt securities has decreased. Within the framework of the Treasury's 2007 borrowing program, it is estimated that the sensitivity of the debt stock to the exchange rate will continue to decrease in the coming period and that there will be an increase in the share of variable interest debt securities due to the effect of government bond issuances indexed to CPI. The fact that the current stock of foreign currency denominated debt in the public sector is relatively long-term and that the Treasury holds a large amount of foreign currency and YTL denominated deposits limits the risks that may arise from the volatility in the exchange rate for the public sector. Dear Guests, In addition to not using possible revenue increases for expenditures within the budget discipline, it is important that the necessary adjustment is not made through indirect taxes in order to reach the non-interest surplus target. I find it useful to emphasize once again the importance of continuing uninterruptedly reforms aimed at increasing the efficiency of public finances in order to make the gains from the tight fiscal policy permanent and to reduce the public debt stock to lower levels. In addition, the structural reforms made and being carried out in the public sector are of vital importance in terms of bringing the public finance to healthier foundations on the one hand and the establishment of a competitive structure in the economy on the other hand and thus the elimination of inflation rigidities that arise in some sectors. Medium-Term Predictions Dear Members of the Press, In this part of my speech, I would like to present our medium-term inflation forecasts, which are prepared to shed light on the course of inflation in the coming period and how long it will converge to the target. Current Situation, Short-Term Outlook and Assumptions First, I would like to summarize the macroeconomic outlook that forms the basis for our medium-term forecasts and the assumptions that form the basis for our forecasts. 14 The Gross National Product data released in April was in line with the projections we put forward for the last quarter of 2006 in the January 2007 Inflation Report. Accordingly, as I mentioned at the beginning of my speech while summarizing the supply and demand developments, the data announced on the demand conditions in the past three months indicate that the contribution of domestic demand to growth will remain at limited levels in the first quarter of 2007 and that the growth will be mainly due to external demand. In the light of this information and taking into account the tight stance of monetary policy, a framework was drawn in which the support given by demand conditions to the process of decline in inflation continued throughout 2007. On the other hand, our forecast that the real exchange rate represents a level that supports the process of decline in inflation, but that this support is at lower levels compared to the beginning of 2006, has been maintained as in the January 2007 Inflation Report. Likewise, in parallel with the January 2007 Inflation Report, an outlook is drawn in which the current level of real interest rates expresses a tight monetary policy and will continue to contribute to the process of decline of inflation by limiting demand conditions. Due to the fact that the expected correction movement in unprocessed food prices was not observed in the first quarter of 2007 and the decline in service inflation was slower than predicted, annual inflation as of the end of March was above the forecast stated in the January Inflation Report. In this context, the near-term forecasts for annual inflation have been updated upwards. In the rest of the year, the effect of the depreciation observed in the YTL last year on annual inflation is expected to disappear and services inflation is expected to decrease to some extent due to the slow domestic demand. However, under the forecast that the effects of wage increases will continue throughout the year, that oil prices will not show a significant decline and that structural elements in the housing sector will continue to exist, it is estimated that the decline in service inflation in 2007 will be limited. Dear Guests, I would like to summarize our assumptions regarding foreign factors as follows: The growth in the Eurozone, which was in the range of 2.5-3 percent as of the first quarter of 2007, is expected to be approximately 2 percent by the end of 2007; this figure is estimated to be in the range of 2-2.5 percent by the end of 2008. Eurozone Harmonized Consumer Price Inflation in Mid-2008 15 is expected to align with the 2 percent target and remain at that level until the end of 2008. In addition, due to the reasons I have summarized in the international economic developments section, we see that oil prices are above our forecasts in the January Inflation Report. Therefore, crude oil barrel prices, which were assumed to be 55 during the last Inflation Report period, were assumed to be at 60 when the forecasts in this Report were generated. On the other hand, the predictions we made regarding the risk premium in January were preserved and it was assumed that the risk premium would not change significantly in the coming period. Forecasts and Monetary Policy Dear Members of the Press, Since the effects of monetary policy on the economy require a certain period of time, I have emphasized on several occasions that we focus on the consistency of future inflation with the target, not today's inflation, when formulating our policies. In this context, the Central Bank formulates its policy response with a medium-term perspective and does not react to the temporary effects of elements beyond the control of monetary policy on inflation. In this part of my talk, I would like to present our forecasts, which are created with a medium-term perspective in mind. The updates and inflation expectations I have just summarized and the first quarter data on service price inflation indicate that a more cautious stance in monetary policy may be required in terms of the alignment of the medium-term outlook with the targets compared to the January Inflation Report. In this context, I would like to point out that the forecasts I will present in a moment are based on the assumption that interest rates have been lowered from the last quarter after being kept stable in the second and third quarters of the year, but that these reductions have been more moderate compared to the path expressed in January. 16 Chart 16. Inflation and Output Gap Forecasts Forecast Range* 12 Uncertainty Range for 2007 10 8 6 4 2 0 -2 -4 -6 Medium-term target Output Gap 06-IV 07-I 07-II 07-III 07-IV 08-I 08-II 08-III 08-IV 09-I * The probability that inflation will remain within the forecast range is 70 percent. According to the projections created within this framework, the downward trend in inflation will become evident as of the second quarter of 2007; inflation is projected to remain between 4.5 and 7.1 percent (midpoint 5.8) at the end of 2007 and between 1.3 and 5.0 percent (midpoint 3.2) by the end of 2008, with a probability of 70 percent. The main message that can be drawn from these forecasts is that, in the light of the available data, the tight stance of monetary policy must be maintained for a while in order for inflation to reach the medium-term target of 4 percent. Under such a policy perspective, it is estimated that demand conditions in the economy throughout 2007 will continue to support the process of inflation decline (Chart 16). As a result, taking into account the developments in the last three months, the 2007 year-end inflation forecast has been updated slightly upwards according to the January 2007 Inflation Report; The cautious stance in monetary policy has been strengthened to achieve medium-term targets. The point I would like to emphasize here is that this perspective on policy rates is derived under the current set of information and assumptions and does not constitute a commitment made by the CBRT. Therefore, when the economic conditions and assumptions that form the basis of the forecasts change, the monetary policy perspective may also change. 17 Risks Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, I would like to devote the last part of my talk to the key possible risk factors that could lead to a significant deviation from the estimates I have just presented. Although the data released in the last three quarters are largely in line with the projections on macroeconomic developments in the Inflation Reports published since July 2006 and the effects of monetary tightening on demand in the second half of 2006 begin to be seen, uncertainties regarding the transmission mechanism continue to pose a risk factor for the medium-term outlook of inflation. Although the recent increases in non-interest public expenditures increase the uncertainty on this issue, the measures taken to cut expenditures are considered as a positive development. As a result, there is a risk that the impact of aggregate demand developments on inflation will be lower than expected. Another important risk factor for the medium-term inflation outlook is the rigidity in inflation expectations and the possibility that historical pricing habits may not be sufficiently broken. Both situations could lead to a stronger than predicted resistance in inflation to come down. Although it is estimated that the decline in inflation in the coming period will bring about an improvement in expectations, the possibility of continuing the rigidity in medium-term inflation expectations poses a significant risk to the inflation outlook through wages and pricing behavior. If this risk is realized, the cautious stance in monetary policy will be maintained for a longer time. As I mentioned at the beginning of my speech, another risk factor that has the potential to delay the achievement of inflation is the sudden fluctuations that may occur in global markets. The continuation of uncertainties in the US economy and the continuation of global imbalances can cause market fluctuations that may affect developing countries from time to time. In addition, the high levels reached by crude oil prices increase the risks related to foreign markets. On the other hand, the slowdown in the increase in the current account deficit and the high level of the Treasury's cash assets are developments that may limit the impact of the fluctuations that may be experienced. However, if shocks arise that could increase perceptions of uncertainty, the Central Bank will determine the source of the shock. 18 After determining, it will act with a medium-term perspective and openly share with the public the most appropriate strategy for inflation to be in line with the target again. Dear Guests, I would like to reiterate the critical importance of achieving price stability in order for the economy to achieve a sustainable and high potential growth rate and to further increase social welfare. Inflation and inflation expectations will be in line with the target and price stability will be possible with the continuation of the prudent stance of monetary policy. It is of great importance that economic units are patient in this process and do not sacrifice long-term gains for the sake of short-term interests. Undoubtedly, fiscal policies and structural reforms are of great importance in addition to monetary policy in order to ensure price stability in the long term. Developments in structural reforms, which will improve the quality of fiscal discipline in the medium and long term, are closely monitored in terms of both macroeconomic stability and price stability. It remains important that the process of harmonization and convergence with the European Union continues and that the structural reforms related to the economic program are implemented as planned without interruption. Continuing the decisive steps taken in these areas in recent years with the same determination in the coming period will contribute to overcoming the changes in the international conjuncture with the least fluctuation. Thank you. 19

Title: Speech of President Ylmaz at the Press Conference on the Introduction of the "Inflation Report-III"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: ON THE INTRODUCTION OF THE INFLATION REPORT Durmu? YILMAZ 27 July 2007, Ankara Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the launch meeting of the third issue of the 2007 Inflation Report, one of the most important communication tools of the open inflation targeting regime we are implementing. The Inflation Report analyzes the developments that are decisive in the medium-term trend of inflation and includes inflation forecasts produced according to updated assumptions regarding key macroeconomic variables. In addition, the Report also presents possible risks that may cause deviation from inflation forecasts to the public. At this meeting, I would like to summarize the assessments in the Inflation Report, which will be published on our website today, and the inflation forecasts of the Central Bank. International Economic Developments Dear Members of the Press, I would like to begin with a general assessment of international economic developments. In the last three months, international financial markets continued to maintain their positive course and it was observed that historical extreme values were reached in many indicators and even exceeded these values and reached record levels. This development was especially influenced by the strong course of global growth and high levels of risk appetite. As a matter of fact, the Credit Suisse Global Risk Appetite Index, which reflects the attitudes of international investors towards risk, has reached a high level of plateau after the turmoil at the end of February (Chart 1). On the other hand, concerns about the sustainability of the historical record values reached in international financial markets are increasingly raised. In addition, the increase in market interest rates and volatility in the US and the troubles experienced in the real estate market also emerge as important uncertainty factors. 1 Chart 1. Credit Suisse Global Risk Appetite Index 8 6 4 2 0 -2 03.01.2006 03.07.2006 03.01.2007 03.07.2007 Source : Credit Suisse The upward trend observed in international crude oil prices as of the beginning of 2007 has become more evident in recent years (Chart 2). Following OPEC's production cuts, the above-expected demand growth and the production cuts resulting from the ongoing turmoil in Nigeria led to the continuation of the upward trend in crude oil prices despite the increases in US crude oil inventories. In addition, imbalances in crude oil and crude oil product inventories in the United States and tensions in the Middle East are other factors that determine the upward course of crude oil prices. In the coming period, the start of the hurricane season, the lack of upward adjustment in OPEC quotas and the continuation of the troubles originating from Nigeria are seen as possible developments that may cause sudden increases in crude oil prices. Chart 2. Oil Prices 80 USD/Barrel 70 60 50 03.01.2006 11.05.2006 14.09.2006 23.01.2007 31.05.2007 Source: Bloomberg. 2 Inflation Developments Dear Guests, Despite rising oil prices and unprocessed food prices failing to make the expected correction, inflation fell by 2.26 percentage points in the last three months to 8.60 percent, remaining within a range of uncertainty in line with the target as in the first quarter. As we emphasized in the April Inflation Report, the increase in annual inflation in the first quarter was not permanent, and the downward trend started with the second quarter. The delayed effects of monetary tightening through the expenditure groups on services and durable goods and the disappearance of the base effect of the high increases in the same period last year have made this decline evident (Chart 3). Chart 3. Source: TurkStat, CBRT April 2007 Inflation Report In the first half of the year, the significant slowdown in the increase in service prices is remarkable. In the same period, there was a decline in the rate of increase in energy prices compared to last year, while unprocessed food prices increased even above last year. Prices of goods other than energy and unprocessed food maintained their high level of increase last year (Chart 4). 3 Chart 4. Consumer Prices (Six-Month Cumulative Percentage Change) 12 10 2005 2006 8 2007 6 4 2 0 -2 Service Energy Unprocessed Food Energy and Unprocessed Food Non-Goods Source: TurkStat, CBRT. Dear Members of the Press, Price increases for unprocessed food products slowed in the second quarter. In this development, the correction movement in fruit prices, which increased at a high rate in the first quarter of the year, was decisive. The significant decline in fruit production in the first quarter of the year draws attention to the fact that the price increase in this group has developed largely in the supply direction. Prices for the goods group, excluding energy and unprocessed food products, increased at a lower rate in the second quarter compared to the previous year and showed a slowing trend. In response to the high increases in the prices of the clothing and footwear group, the significant improvement in the prices of the durable consumer goods group was effective in this development. When the course of the first half of the year is examined, it is observed that prices in expenditure groups other than durable consumer goods increased at a higher rate compared to the same period of the previous year (Chart 5). 4 Chart 5. Selected Non-Energy and Non-Food Prices (Six-Month Cumulative Percentage Change) 12 2005 2006 2007 9 6 3 0 -3 -6 Processed Food Tobacco Apparel & Footwear Durable Goods (Excl. Gold) Source: TurkStat, CBRT. Annual inflation in the durable goods (excluding gold) group declined to 0.32 percent at the end of the second quarter due to both the strengthening in the YTL and the slowdown in demand for this group. The impact of the monetary tightening carried out last year was mostly observed on the prices of the electrical and non-electrical appliances group, and the prices of this group were below the level before the fluctuation period in May 2006. On the other hand, it is noteworthy that the highest price increase among durable goods in the period from fluctuation to the present day was experienced in the furniture group, where the prevalence of the use of imported inputs and indexing behavior was relatively low. The second quarter price developments indicate that the clothing and footwear group's positive contribution to the inflation decline process over the past two years will be interrupted in 2007. The annual inflation of this group continued to rise, reaching 7.15 percent as of June. In this development, both cost and strong external demand factors are effective. Annual inflation of processed food products remained stable in the second quarter. In June, the VAT rate reduction of certain processed food products had positive effects on group prices. However, losses in wheat production continue to pose risks to processed food and therefore consumer prices through bread and cereals group price developments. As a result, the possibility of loss of yield in certain crops, especially grain, due to air temperatures and lack of precipitation that differ from seasonal normals, and 5 The use of some of the world's wheat and corn production in biofuel production is the factors that increase the uncertainty on food prices through both processed and unprocessed food products in the coming period. Dear Guests, Recent price developments indicate an improvement in the service group. The delayed effects of monetary tightening began to be evident in the group prices, which saw the lowest first-half increase in the 2003-based index with 4.61 percent in the first six months of the year. In the second quarter, annual inflation decreased in all service subgroups except transportation services, and the most significant slowdown in service price increases was seen in the restaurant-hotels group. Rent, which has a significant share in the rigidity of service group prices, showed a very limited improvement in the first six months (Chart 6). With the continuation of the slowdown in domestic demand, we anticipate that the improvement in service prices will continue gradually. Chart 6. Dear Members of the Press, The downward trend in annual inflation is also reflected in inflation expectations. Medium-term inflation, which has generally followed a horizontal course since the beginning of 2007 6 expectations have entered a downward trend in recent months. Since the April Inflation Report, the decline in annual inflation has been instrumental in the 25 and 19 basis point reduction in inflation expectations for the next 12 and 24 months, respectively. However, the fact that medium-term expectations are still above the targets continues to be a risk factor in wage and price determination (Chart 7). Chart 7. Supply and Demand Developments Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, After summarizing inflation developments in this way, I would now like to present our evaluations of supply and demand developments in the light of the latest data. In the first quarter of 2007, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased by 6.8 percent compared to the same period of 2006. The growth composition in the second half of 2006 continued in this period; While the contribution of domestic demand to growth remained limited, external demand was the main source of growth (Chart 8). The demand for durable goods and the decline in machinery and equipment investments continued to be the most important items limiting domestic demand. While the value added of the industrial sector increased at a high rate annually with the base effect created by the low rate increase in the same period of the previous year, it is significant compared to the previous period when adjusted for seasonality. 7 it has not changed. While external demand supported industrial production, the slowdown in domestic demand restricted industrial production. Chart 8. Among the indicators related to durable goods demand, car and white goods sales continued to decline in the second quarter of the year with seasonally adjusted data. Real consumer credit utilization and consumer goods imports data also do not indicate a revival in private consumption spending. No revival is expected in machinery and equipment investments as of the second quarter. Despite the positive price effect created by the strong position of YTL, the high interest rates on loans lead to the postponement of expenditures on investment goods along with durable consumption. In this context, leading indicators for the second quarter of 2007 show that growth exhibits a similar composition to the first quarter. Although the annual growth rate remains below the first quarter, seasonally adjusted data indicate an increase in industrial production compared to the previous quarter (Chart 9). The continuation of the strong performance in exports is the basis for the increase in industrial production. 8 Chart9. Dear Guests, The slowdown in domestic demand, the low level of oil prices, especially in the first quarter of 2007, compared to the same period last year, and the strong external demand led to the cessation of the upward trend in the ratio of the current account deficit to Gross National Product (Chart 10). In the April-May period, the improvement trend in foreign trade continued. In addition, tourism revenues, which performed negatively in 2006, started to increase again in 2007 and exceeded the level of 2005. Thus, the trend of improvement in the current account deficit continued in April and May. In addition, according to provisional data published by the Turkish Exporters Assembly, the increase in exports continued in June, although it slowed down slightly due to the high base in 2006. On the other hand, with a possible revival in domestic demand in the second half of the year, capital and consumer goods imports are expected to enter an upward trend, while intermediate goods imports are expected to continue their high growth in parallel with export and oil price increase. Accordingly, it will not be surprising if the current account deficit tends to increase again in the second half of the year. However, in 2007, it is estimated that there will be a decrease in the ratio of the current account deficit to the Gross National Product compared to the previous year. Dear Members of the Press, In the light of the current data, when the moderate growth in domestic demand is evaluated together with the strong course in external demand, it is thought that aggregate demand conditions continue to support the decline in inflation (Chart 11). However, if the improvement in borrowing costs continues in the coming period, it is evaluated that domestic demand, which has been postponed for a while, may accelerate again. I find it useful to remind you that we closely follow the developments related to this assessment in terms of monetary policy based on the fight against inflation with a medium-term perspective. In the second quarter of 2007, international liquidity conditions and global risk appetite continued to favor developing countries despite the upward trend observed in US secondary market bond yields in June and concerns that possible losses in low-grade mortgage-based mortgage loans in the US could increase (Chart 12). The most important factor in this development was the indicators that core inflation is under control in the US and the continuation of the positive course of growth expectations for the US and the Eurozone. Excess liquidity sterilized in the overnight market increased in the second quarter of the year compared to the previous quarter. Despite exceeding the debt conversion rate stipulated by the Treasury at the beginning of the year, the foreign exchange purchase tenders we organized as the CBRT were the most important determinants in this development. As a result of these developments in the liquidity level, we issued the first liquidity bond with a maturity of 32 days on July 19, 2007 in order to increase the effectiveness of liquidity management as well as existing instruments used in open market transactions. The returns generated on 20 July 2007 were below the returns generated at the end of the first quarter of 2007 in each term, driven by a reduction in the risk premium (Chart 13). In addition, the fact that yield curves are downward from 18 months of maturity indicates that economic units maintain their expectation that the process of decline in inflation will continue in the medium term. Dear Guests, This recent downward trend in loan rates is largely due to the partial improvement in inflation. However, it is important to remember that despite this decline in nominal interest rates, real consumer loan rates are still at high levels. In this context, I would like to emphasize that it would be beneficial for our consumers to take into account the knowledge that real interest rates will fall to much lower levels when price stability is permanently reached when determining the timing of long-term consumer credit uses. Public Finance Dear Members of the Press, I find it useful to emphasize again that the faster increase in public expenditures than anticipated is of great importance in terms of budget discipline and price stability. As of the first half of 2007, the rate of increase in central government non-interest expenditures exceeded the high rate of increase target foreseen for the whole of 2007. As of the first half of the year, unforeseen and one-off revenue developments were decisive in the realization of the central government budget balance at a level compatible with the targets. 14 It is thought that the achievement of the central government budget targets alone will not be sufficient for fiscal policy to provide support for the 2007 inflation target. In this context, it is important that the necessary adjustment to achieve the non-interest surplus target is made through measures to slow down the rapid increase in public expenditures rather than indirect taxes. Dear Guests, It remains important to carry out structural reforms effectively so that the gains from the tight fiscal policy can become permanent, the support for the decline in inflation continues, and the public debt stock can be reduced to lower levels. The reforms that have been made and are being made to ensure discipline and efficiency in the public sector are of vital importance in terms of bringing public finances to healthier foundations on the one hand and the establishment of a competitive structure in the economy and thus the elimination of inflationary rigidities in some sectors. Medium-Term Predictions Dear Members of the Press, In this part of my speech, I would like to present our medium-term inflation forecasts, which are prepared to shed light on the course of inflation in the coming period and how long it will converge to the target. 16 Current Situation, Short-Term Outlook and Assumptions First of all, I would like to summarize our macroeconomic outlook and assumptions that form the basis for our medium-term forecasts. As I mentioned at the beginning of my speech, the Gross National Product data announced for the first quarter of 2007 was very close to the forecasts set out in the April Inflation Report. While net exports, whose increase accelerated in this period, were the main determinants of growth, the contribution of domestic demand to growth was limited. Leading indicators for the second quarter of the year also signal that economic growth continues to moderate due to external demand. Therefore, taking into account the tight stance of monetary policy, while producing forecasts, the framework in which the contribution of demand conditions to the process of decline in inflation continued throughout 2007 was preserved. While producing the forecasts, the assumption that the current level of real interest rates indicates a tight monetary policy and that inflation will continue to contribute to the downward process by limiting demand conditions has been maintained. In addition, it is assumed that the real exchange rate continues to support the process of decline in inflation as stated in the April 2007 Inflation Report. Consumer inflation showed a gradual downward trend in the second quarter of 2007, consistent with the projections in the April 2007 Inflation Report, and after the first quarter, annual inflation in the second quarter of the year remained within the uncertainty range in line with the target. Taking into account the strong position of the YTL, the delayed effects of monetary tightening and the high base in the second half of 2006, it is foreseen that consumer prices will continue their gradual decline in the third quarter of 2007. The projected slowdown in annual price growth in the services group was clearly observed in the second quarter of 2007. However, under the forecast that the effects of wage increases will continue throughout the year, oil prices will continue to be a risk factor throughout the year, and structural elements in the housing sector will continue to exist, this decline is expected to be limited. Our assumptions about the overseas factors that form the basis of our forecasts can be summarized as follows: growth in the euro area was 2.7 percent in 2007; In 2008, it is estimated at 2.2 percent. Eurozone consumer price inflation is projected to remain at 2 percent by the end of 2008. Recently, as a result of the sharpening of the upward trend in international oil prices, the April Inflation Report showed that it was 60 US dollars. 17 The default price of a barrel of crude oil has been raised to 65 in this Report. Since April, there have been no developments that would have led to a significant change in risk perception, so our assumptions regarding the risk premium have been maintained. Forecasts and Monetary Policy Dear Members of the Press, After summarizing the assumptions that form the basis of our forecasts, I would like to share with you our forecasts created within the framework of a medium-term perspective and with a focus on the consistency of future inflation with the target. The inflation forecasts and monetary policy stance we presented in April have been broadly maintained, as recent developments are largely in line with our projections. In this context, under the assumption that policy rates have been reduced moderately since the beginning of the last quarter of the year; inflation is projected to be between 5.1 and 6.9 percent (midpoint 6.0) at the end of 2007 and between 1.5 and 4.9 percent (midpoint 3.2) by the end of 2008 with a probability of 70 percent (Chart 19). With the upward update of the oil price assumption, the 2007 year-end forecasts increased slightly compared to the previous Report, but it was assessed that the medium-term inflation outlook would not be affected by the cautious stance of monetary policy. 18 The message of these forecasts should not be taken as "interest rates will be lowered in October". The main message to be drawn from this is that even if there is a moderate reduction in short-term interest rates in the last quarter of the year, the delayed effects of tight monetary policy will support the process of decline in inflation for a while. Accordingly, possible interest rate cuts may come to the agenda earlier or be postponed further, depending on the flow of data and information on external demand, public expenditures and other variables affecting the medium-term inflation outlook. The point I would like to emphasize here is that this perspective on policy rates is derived under the current information set and assumptions and does not constitute a commitment given by the CBRT. In the upcoming period, there are significant uncertainty elements that may require the monetary policy stance to be significantly updated in both directions. Risks Dear Guests, In the last part of my talk, I would like to address the main possible risk factors that could lead to a significant deviation from the estimates I have just presented. The high levels of inflation over the past year, the continued uncertainties regarding the prices of unprocessed food and oil, and the implementation of the revenues policy in 2007 have been the factors that increased the rigidity in inflation expectations. The fact that medium-term inflation expectations are not yet at a level compatible with the target indicates that the rate of economic units taking target inflation as an indicator has decreased recently. This poses a particular risk to wage adjustments and thus to service sector inflation. If this risk is realized, a more cautious stance in monetary policy may be required as the process of decline in inflation will be slower than predicted. Due to structural factors, prices in some service items, which are rigid beyond indexing to the past, are outside the sphere of influence of monetary policy. For example, the increases in the rent item in the last three years have been very high, and the contribution of rent increase alone to annual inflation is approaching one point. It is thought that the annual rate of increase in rents will slow down partially in the coming months and will have a more stable outlook in the medium term with the increase in housing supply. Nevertheless, the possibility that rent increases will continue to be high compared to other service prices is considered as a risk factor that may slow down the process of decline in inflation. Our research shows that rolling habits are still common in leases. This behavior is not compatible with the falling inflation environment. Both tenants and landlords need to abandon their pricing habits from the period of high inflation and change their contracts 19 It is important that they take into account that the inflation target is 4 percent in the medium term. In the past year, it has been observed that the monetary transmission mechanism has started to operate more effectively. Although increases in non-interest budget expenditures and strong external demand slowed down the process of decline in inflation, inflation came under control with the delayed effects of monetary tightening and headed towards the target again. However, in order for inflation to reach its target of 4 percent in the medium term, domestic demand must follow a moderate course before accelerating for a while. If uncertainty perceptions disappear in the second half of 2007 and long-term interest rates continue to fall, the contribution of demand conditions to the process of decline in inflation may decrease. If the probability of such a risk is strengthened, a more cautious stance than foreseen may be exhibited, and if necessary, other than short-term interest rates, compulsory reserves and other similar instruments may be used. However, if the cautious stance of monetary policy is supported by fiscal discipline, such a risk will be unlikely to occur. Possible fluctuations in international liquidity conditions remain among the risk factors for the inflation outlook. In the current situation, the fact that the direction of the basic indicators of developed countries has not yet been clarified causes the data sensitivity of the markets to continue. The persistence of uncertainty perceptions regarding the balances in the global economy stands out as an important risk factor that may lead to sudden fluctuations in international investors' portfolio preferences and liquidity flow. In the event of a significant change in risk perceptions, the CBRT will ensure that the effects of possible fluctuations on the inflation outlook remain limited through effective liquidity management. Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, Before concluding my remarks, I would like to remind once again that fiscal policies and structural reforms are of great importance in addition to monetary policy in terms of ensuring price stability. In this context, the continuation of the process of harmonization and convergence with the European Union and the implementation of structural reforms related to the economic program remain important for long-term stability. I end my speech by stating that we are closely monitoring the developments in structural reforms, which will improve the quality of fiscal discipline, in terms of their effects on both macroeconomic stability and price stability, and I thank you all. 20

Bu dnemde art hzlanan net ihracat bymenin temel belirleyicisi olurken, yurt ii talebin bymeye katks snrl kalmtr. Yln ikinci eyreine ilikin nc gstergeler de, ekonomik bymenin d talep kaynakl olarak lml bir ekilde devam ettii ynnde sinyal vermektedir. Dolaysyla, para politikasnn sk duruu da dikkate alndnda, tahminler retilirken, talep koullarnn enflasyondaki d srecine olan katksnn 2007 yl boyunca devam ettii ereve korunmutur. Tahminler retilirken, reel faizlerin mevcut dzeyinin sk bir para politikasn ifade ettii ve talep koullarn snrlandrarak enflasyonun d srecine katk yapmaya devam edecei varsaym korunmutur. Bunun yannda reel kurun, Nisan 2007 Enflasyon Raporu'nda belirtildii ekilde enflasyondaki d srecine destek vermeye devam ettii varsaylmtr. Tketici enflasyonu 2007 ylnn ikinci eyreinde, Nisan 2007 Enflasyon Raporundaki ngrlerle tutarl olarak kademeli bir d eilimi sergilemi ve ilk eyrein ardndan, yln ikinci eyreinde de yllk enflasyon hedefle uyumlu belirsizlik aralnn iinde kalmtr. YTLnin gl konumu, parasal sklatrmann gecikmeli etkileri ve 2006 ylnn ikinci yarsndaki yksek baz gz nne alnarak, tketici fiyatlarnn 2007 yl nc eyreinde de kademeli dn srdrecei ngrlmektedir. Hizmet grubunda yllk fiyat artnda tahmin edilen yavalama, 2007 yl ikinci eyreinde aka gzlenmitir. Ancak, cret artlarnn etkilerinin yl boyunca srecei, petrol fiyatlarnn yl genelinde risk unsuru olmaya devam edecei ve konut sektrndeki yapsal unsurlarn varln srdrecei ngrs altnda, bu dn snrl olaca ngrlmektedir. Tahminlerimize baz oluturan yurt d faktrlere ilikin varsaymlarmz ise u ekilde zetlenebilir: Euro blgesindeki byme, 2007 ylnda yzde 2,7; 2008 ylnda ise yzde 2,2 olarak tahmin edilmektedir. Euro blgesi tketici fiyat enflasyonunun ise 2008 yl sonuna kadar yzde 2 dzeyinde kalaca ngrlmektedir. Son dnemde, uluslararas petrol fiyatlarndaki ykseli eiliminin keskinlemesi sonucunda, Nisan ay Enflasyon Raporunda 60 ABD dolar olarak 17 varsaylan ham petrol varil fiyat, bu Raporda 65 ABD dolar seviyesine ykseltilmitir. Nisan ayndan bu yana risk alglamasnn belirgin olarak deimesine yol aacak herhangi bir gelime yaanmadndan, risk primine ilikin varsaymlarmz korunmutur. Tahminler ve Para Politikas Kymetli Basn Mensuplar, Tahminlerimize temel oluturan varsaymlar zetledikten sonra, orta vadeli bir perspektif erevesinde ve gelecekteki enflasyonun hedefle tutarllna odakl olarak, oluturulan tahminlerimizi sizlerle paylamak istiyorum. Bu dorultuda, olas faiz indirimleri d talebe, kamu harcamalarna ve orta vadeli enflasyon grnmn etkileyen dier deikenlere dair veri ve bilgi akna bal olarak, daha erken gndeme gelebilecei gibi daha ileriye de ertelenebilecektir. Burada nemle vurgulanmak istediim nokta, politika faizlerine ilikin bu perspektifin mevcut bilgi seti ve varsaymlar altnda tretilmi olduu ve TCMB tarafndan verilmi bir taahht nitelii tamaddr. nmzdeki dnemde, para politikas duruunun her iki ynde belirgin olarak gncellenmesini gerektirebilecek nemli belirsizlik unsurlar bulunmaktadr. Riskler Saygdeer Konuklar, Konumamn son blmnde, az nce sunmu olduum tahminlerin belirgin olarak sapmasna yol aabilecek olas temel risk unsurlarna deinmek istiyorum. Enflasyonun getiimiz bir yl iinde yksek seviyelerde seyretmesi, ilenmemi gda ve petrol fiyatlarna ilikin belirsizliklerin srmesi ve 2007 ylndaki gelirler politikas uygulamalar enflasyon beklentilerindeki katl artran unsurlar olmutur. Orta vadeli enflasyon beklentilerinin henz hedefle uyumlu dzeyde olmamas, son dnemde ekonomik birimlerin hedef enflasyonu gsterge olarak alma orannn azaldna iaret etmektedir. Bu durum zellikle cret ayarlamalarna ve dolaysyla hizmet sektr enflasyonuna ilikin risk oluturmaktadr. Bu riskin gereklemesi durumunda enflasyondaki d sreci ngrlenden daha yava olacandan, para politikasnda ngrlenden daha temkinli bir duru gerekebilecektir. Yapsal unsurlar nedeniyle gemie endekslemenin de tesinde katlk gsteren baz hizmet kalemlerinde fiyatlar para politikasnn etki alan dndadr. rnein, son  ylda kira kalemindeki artlar ok yksek seyretmekte ve tek bana kira artnn yllk enflasyona katks bir puana yaklamaktadr. nmzdeki aylarda kiralardaki yllk art hznn ksmen yavalayaca, konut arznn artmasyla da orta vadede daha istikrarl bir grnme kavuaca dnlmektedir. Yine de, kira artlarnn dier hizmet fiyatlarna kyasla yksek seyretmeye devam etme ihtimali enflasyondaki d srecini yavalatabilecek bir risk unsuru olarak deerlendirilmektedir. Yaptmz aratrmalar kira kontratlarnda halen yuvarlama alkanlklarnn yaygn olduunu gstermektedir. Bu davran, den enflasyon ortamyla uyumlu deildir. Gerek kiraclarn gerekse ev sahiplerinin yksek enflasyon dneminden kalma fiyatlama alkanlklarn terketmeleri ve kontratlarn 19 yaparken orta vadede enflasyon hedefinin yzde 4 olduunu hesaba katmalar nem tamaktadr. Getiimiz bir ylda, parasal aktarm mekanizmasnn daha etkin ilemeye balad gzlenmitir. Faiz d bte harcamalarndaki artlar ve gl d talep enflasyondaki d srecini yavalatsa da parasal sklatrmann gecikmeli etkileriyle enflasyon kontrol altna girmi ve tekrar hedefe doru ynelmitir. Ancak, enflasyonun orta vadede yzde 4 hedefine eriebilmesi iin i talebin bir sre daha ivmelenmeden lml bir seyir izlemesi gerekmektedir. 2007 ylnn ikinci yarsnda belirsizlik alglamalarnn ortadan kalkmas ve uzun vadeli faizlerin dmeye devam etmesi halinde talep koullarnn enflasyondaki d srecine verdii katk azalabilecektir. Byle bir riskin gerekleme olaslnn glenmesi halinde ngrlenden daha temkinli bir duru sergilenebilecei gibi, gerektiinde ksa vadeli faizler dndaki, zorunlu karlklar ve benzeri dier aralara da bavurulabilecektir. Ancak, para politikasnn temkinli duruu mali disiplinle desteklendii taktirde byle bir riskin gerekleme olasl dk olacaktr. Uluslararas likidite koullarndaki olas dalgalanmalar enflasyon grnmne dair risk unsurlar arasndaki yerini korumaktadr. Mevcut durumda gelimi lkelere dair temel gstergelerin ynnn henz netlemi olmamas, piyasalarn veri hassasiyetinin devam etmesine neden olmaktadr. Kresel ekonomideki dengelere ilikin belirsizlik alglamalarnn srmesi uluslararas yatrmclarn portfy tercihlerinde ve likidite aknda ani dalgalanmalara yol aabilecek nemli bir risk unsuru olarak ne kmaktadr. Risk alglamalarnda nemli bir deiim olmas halinde TCMB etkin likidite ynetimiyle olas dalgalanmalarn enflasyon grnm zerindeki etkilerinin snrl kalmasn salayacaktr. Deerli Basn Mensuplar, Saygdeer Konuklar, Szlerimi tamamlamadan nce, fiyat istikrarnn salanmas asndan para politikasnn yannda maliye politikalar ve yapsal reformlarn da byk nem tadn bir kez daha hatrlatmakta fayda grmekteyim. Bu erevede Avrupa Birliine uyum ve yaknsama srecinin devam etmesi ile ekonomik programa ilikin yapsal reformlarn hayata geirilmesi uzun vadeli istikrar asndan nemini korumaktadr. zellikle mali disiplinin kalitesini artracak olan yapsal reformlar konusundaki gelimeleri, gerek makroekonomik istikrar gerekse fiyat istikrar zerindeki etkileri asndan yakndan izlediimizi belirterek konumama son veriyor ve hepinize teekkrlerimi sunuyorum. 20

Title: Speech at the Press Conference on the Introduction of the "Inflation Report-IV"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: ON THE INTRODUCTION OF THE INFLATION REPORT Durmu YILMAZ 26 October 2007, Ankara 1 Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the launch meeting of the fourth issue of the 2007 edition of the Inflation Report, one of the most important communication tools of the open inflation targeting regime we are implementing. The Inflation Report examines recent macroeconomic developments, analyzes the factors that determine the medium-term trend of inflation, and includes inflation forecasts produced according to updated assumptions about key macroeconomic variables. In addition, the Report presents the possible risks that may cause deviation from inflation forecasts and the monetary policy decisions that may be taken in the event of these risks being realized. In this meeting, I would like to summarize the evaluations in the Inflation Report that will be published on our website in a moment and the inflation forecasts of the Central Bank. 1. Inflation Developments Dear Members of the Press, I would like to begin my speech with our general assessments of inflation developments. Recently, inflation and economic activities have followed a course in line with the forecasts of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey. It is seen that the delayed effects of the monetary tightening applied since June 2006 on inflation have become evident since the second quarter of 2007 in line with our projections and that this trend continued in the third quarter. Despite the increase in public expenditures and the recovery trend in domestic demand, the cumulative effect of monetary tightening on private consumption demand and the support of aggregate demand conditions to the process of decline in inflation continued. Accordingly, the slowdown in the rate of price growth of items such as services and durable consumer goods, which are particularly sensitive to demand, has become evident. Annual inflation in durable goods (excluding gold) group prices reached minus 4 percent as of the end of the third quarter (Chart 1). In service inflation, one of the most striking developments in the third quarter of the year is the slowdown in rent inflation. Annual inflation in restaurant and hotel services decreased by 5.1 points and rent inflation decreased by 3 points compared to the same period last year. The salient aspect of service prices is that the improvement extends to all subgroups. 2 (Chart 2). It is anticipated that the decline in service inflation will continue in the coming period. Although the main trend of inflation is downward in line with the Central Bank's forecasts, it is estimated that the decline in inflation will temporarily pause in the coming months, mainly due to the effect of price developments in items that are outside the control of monetary policy, such as energy and food products. Accordingly, our short-term inflation forecasts have been updated upwards compared to the previous Report. The developments that have raised our short-term forecasts can be briefly summarized as follows:  In the July Inflation Report, oil prices were assumed to be at US 65 per barrel. However, in the last three months, oil prices have averaged around USD 75 per barrel, and after this development, our assumption about the price of oil in the coming period has been increased to USD 70. In addition, unlike the previous Report, a high rate of increase in electricity prices was foreseen in the last quarter of the year. These developments in energy prices raised our 2007 year-end inflation forecasts by approximately 0.8 percentage points.  In the previous Report, we assumed that increases in food prices would slow down over time, helped by the high base after rapid increases since 2006. However, over the past period, food prices have continued to exhibit high increases in our country as well as all over the world. This development has caused our short-term inflation forecasts to be updated slightly higher.  In addition to these updates for 2007, it was assumed that tax increases and/or price adjustments could take place on items such as tobacco and fuel oil within the framework of budget adjustments in the first quarter of 2008 and that these adjustments would slightly increase inflation during the following year (from the beginning of 2008 to the beginning of 2009). As a result, despite positive developments in core inflation indicators, we have updated our short-term inflation forecasts upwards due to tax adjustments and developments beyond the control of monetary policy, such as energy, food, and managed/driven price increases. Risks and Monetary Policy Dear Guests, In the policy texts we publish as the Central Bank, it is not only the current level of short-term interest rates that is meant by the "monetary policy stance". The "monetary policy stance" also refers to a path that seems likely to be followed in short-term interest rates in a period of time from today to the medium term. The fact that the path pronounced in the Inflation Reports regarding the policy stance was produced according to the current set of information and that each new data to be released on the medium-term inflation outlook caused the future stance of monetary policy to be reviewed. 13 It should be emphasized again (Figure 1). In other words, any development other than the one predicted regarding the variables affecting the inflation outlook will bring about the redefinition of the monetary policy stance. Therefore, the assumption about the monetary policy stance created by today's information should not be perceived by the public as a commitment to the future. I find it very useful to underline that updating the monetary policy stance in the inflation targeting regime is a norm, not an exception (Figure 2). Depending on the announced data, it may be possible to keep the policy rates fixed for a period of time from next month, or if the conditions allow, a faster or longer reduction process than I have just stated may come to the agenda. In terms of a better understanding of the issue, the Board's September 14 decision sets an important example: As it will be remembered, July Inflation 14 The medium-term forecasts in the Report were formed under the assumption that short-term interest rates had been cut moderately since the beginning of the last quarter of the year. In the same Report, where this assumption is not a commitment "... possible rate cuts may come to the fore earlier or postpone further, depending on the flow of data and information on external demand, public expenditures and other variables affecting the medium-term inflation outlook." As a matter of fact, the Board made a moderate interest rate cut in September without waiting for the last quarter, as the improvement in service sector inflation was positive than expected and the problems in the US credit market pushed down expectations for domestic and foreign demand. Dear Members of the Press, In this last part of my speech, I would like to summarize the main risk factors that may cause the outlook for inflation and monetary policy to be updated in both directions in the coming period: Developments in international liquidity conditions and credit markets are closely monitored. As of today, the view that there will be no sharp slowdown in the world economy comes to the fore and there is no significant decrease in capital flows to developing countries. However, the fact that there is still difficulty in pricing in risks in financial markets requires caution. If the risk aversion trend deepens in the coming period and this reduces investment appetite in emerging markets, the Central Bank will aim to limit the effects of possible fluctuations on the medium-term inflation outlook by using effective liquidity management and other policy instruments when necessary. The recent volatility in the credit markets has partially mitigated the upside risks expressed in the previous Inflation Report regarding aggregate demand conditions. However, there are risks in both directions related to aggregate demand developments. The upside risks are mainly due to uncertainties about the extent to which the recent downward movement in long-term interest rates will stimulate credit demand. On the other hand, in the event of a faster-than-expected slowdown in the world economy, domestic demand may be weaker than expected due to both external demand and a possible contraction in financing conditions. Due to these downward and upside risks, the Central Bank will continue to closely monitor financing conditions and credit developments in the coming period. If the foreign financing conditions are more positive than expected and there is an acceleration in domestic demand, a more cautious stance may be taken in policy rates, as well as regular provisions and other similar policy instruments may be resorted to. Emerging downside risks on aggregate demand 15 In the event of a loss, the policy stance may also be updated to address downside risks related to inflation. While creating the medium-term inflation and monetary policy outlook, it was assumed that the spending targets in the 2008 budget would be adhered to. Deviations from this assumption could affect the outlook for inflation and monetary policy. The fact that the revenues policy will be carried out in 2008 in accordance with the inflation target to a large extent is a positive development in terms of the management of expectations and domestic demand. However, the fact that efforts to partially eliminate the deviation in the non-interest rate budget balance are directed towards indirect tax increases poses a risk for the predictability of inflation. Increases in food prices are considered as an important risk factor related to the inflation outlook. Our medium-term forecasts assume that the rise in food prices will gradually slow to closer to target inflation levels. However, the continuation of production losses in grain products in 2007 and the transformation of food price growth into a global trend increased the upside risks. On the other hand, the high base in food prices increased the likelihood of a downward correction. The high weight of food prices within the CPI and the continued volatility in food prices pose risks in both directions regarding inflation forecasts. The Central Bank will not react to developments in food prices as long as the secondary effects remain limited. There are uncertainties regarding the impact of developments in energy prices on the medium-term inflation outlook. In the near future, a high rate of price adjustment in electricity prices may take place. Water prices, which are another energy item in the CPI, show high increases in the last quarter of the year, although they differ on a provincial basis. In addition, the increase in international oil prices continues. As long as inflation expectations and pricing behavior are not adversely affected, the effects of developments in energy prices on medium-term inflation will be limited. However, I should also mention that the risks related to energy prices have led the Central Bank to be relatively more cautious in interest rate cuts, as energy prices constitute an important input in economic activities. On the other hand, if the transition to cost-based automatic pricing in electricity will be reduced, the risks on both supply security and price stability will be reduced. Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, Significant progress has been made in the fight against inflation in recent years. However, it is not yet possible to define the point reached as price stability. The Central Bank will continue to use its monetary policy instruments to ensure price stability and thus contribute to the long-term prosperity of society. Accordingly, other economic units are also in short-term interest 16 their failure to compromise on long-term lasting gains will reduce the cost of achieving macroeconomic stability. Before concluding my remarks, I would like to remind once again that the support of fiscal policies and structural reforms is of great importance in addition to monetary policy on the road to price stability. In this context, the continuation of the process of harmonization and convergence with the European Union and the continuity of the efforts to implement structural reforms related to the economic program remain important. I end my speech by stating that we are closely monitoring the developments in terms of structural reforms, which will improve the quality of fiscal discipline, both in terms of macroeconomic stability and price stability, and I thank you all. 17

Riskler ve Para Politikas Deerli Konuklar, Merkez Bankas olarak yaymladmz politika metinlerinde para politikas duruu ile kastedilen sadece ksa vadeli faizlerin mevcut seviyesi deildir.
