Title: Speech on "Central Banks and Communication" at Hacettepe University
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey CENTRAL BANKS AND CONTACTS: TURKEY EXPERIENCE 25 December 2006, Ankara Dear Academicians, Students and Valuable Participants, I am very pleased to be here with you today. Considering that the young population constitutes a large proportion of the total population in our country and that this situation is an important trump card in competition with other countries, it is seen how important education is in shaping our future. As the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, we are aware that our youth and their education are the determinants of the future of this country. That's why I'm also glad to have the opportunity to give this talk here. I would like to take this opportunity to thank Hacettepe University for this organization. First of all, I would like to state that; The ultimate goal of economic policies all over the world is to increase economic prosperity. Prosperity growth can only be achieved through sustainable growth and sustainable employment growth. For sustainability, economic stability is essential. The prerequisite for economic stability is price stability. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey also carries out its policies resolutely within the framework of its main objective of ensuring and maintaining price stability. We, as the Central Bank, believe that the more openly, honestly and consistently we share our policies, the decisions we take towards price stability and the underlying reasons for these decisions with the public, the higher our success on the road to social welfare increase. Therefore, today I would like to give you a speech on the theme of "Central Banks and Communication Policies". In my speech, I will first touch on the changing face of central banks' communication policies over time and the concept of transparency. Then I would like to talk about the factors that are effective in the prominence of communication policies and the design of these policies. In the second part of my speech, I will try to convey to you the development of the communication policy of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey by adhering to the monetary policy framework. Dear Listeners, When we look at about fifteen years ago, we see that the concepts of transparency and communication do not come together with the central bank, and even the view that central banks should carry out their practices in secrecy is generally accepted. The basis of this view is the monetary policy 1 lies the assumption that the decisions he makes in order to influence economic activity must come as a surprise. In the economic literature, studies using "time inconsistency" models that argue that monetary policy can be effective through surprises1 suggest that transparency will weaken the effectiveness of monetary policy. Therefore, according to this view, the probability of a central bank succeeding increases to the extent that it can hide its decisions from the public and keep them secret. When we look at the past practices of central banks, we see that these views have also been adopted in their policy practices. Richard Lambert2, a former member of the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of England, one of the most transparent central banks in the world today, told the Financial Times that when he was a journalist, he often hit his head against the famous thick walls of the Bank of England and could not find any information; for he says that the duty of the Bank's press adviser at that time was to keep the Bank out of the press and the press out of the Bank. Similarly, the fact that former U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Alan Greenspan3 stated in 1989 that it would not be healthy to announce decisions on policy interest rates immediately, that the market might overreact to it, and that this practice could prevent the Fed from making the right decisions, is surprising when we look at the concepts of transparency and communication today. Today, central banks of both developed and developing countries are increasingly attaching importance to transparency in their policy practices. Within the framework of the importance given to communication, central banks can not only announce their decisions to the public immediately, but also signal what kind of decisions they can take going forward, publish their forecasts about the course that interest rates can follow, and share the models they use in inflation forecasts with the public. 1 Kydland, F.E., Prescott, E.C. (1977). Rules Rather than Discretion: The Inconsistency of Optimal Plans. Journal of Political Economy, 85, 3, 473-91. Cukierman, A., Meltzer, A.H. (Eyl9fl 1986). A Theory of Ambiguity, Credibility, and Inflation Under Discretion and Asymmetric Information. Econometrica, 54, 5, 1099-1128. 2 Lambert, R. (2006). d2Central Bank Communications: Best Practices in Advanced Economiesd3. 3 Blinder, A., Reis, R. (2005). d2Understanding the Greenspan Standardd3. 2 In parallel with the increasing transparency in central banks, the number of studies on this subject in the economic literature is also increasing. In these studies, the concept of transparency is defined from various angles. In some studies, transparency is defined in a general expression as a public understanding of the objectives and practices of the central bank4, while in studies classifying transparency5, it is emphasized that the reflections of the target, the tools used for this goal, the transparency of the econometric models and data, and the policy practices should be known by the public. Fed St. Louis President William Poole defines transparency as "the accurate provision of all information that can enable market participants to view monetary policy as a whole as much as possible" with a functional approach6. Dear Participants, Some factors have been effective in bringing transparency and communication policies to the forefront in recent years. I would like to examine them under three headings. The independence of central banks and accountability, which is an integral part of this independence, is the first of these elements. In order for a central bank that is committed to ensuring price stability to achieve this goal, it must have a medium- and long-term perspective, and it must be able to implement its policies in a way that is free from the daily vicious debates and the effects of politics that have a short-term perspective by nature. Independence is therefore a vital element of central banking. But instead of talking about why it's important for central banks to be independent, which we've repeatedly said on various platforms, I want to talk about the responsibility that comes with that independence. The result of the independence of central banks is accountability. Being accountable means that the central bank is accountable to society for the decisions it makes and their consequences. All of this makes transparency and an effective communication policy an important part of independence and accountability. 4 Winkler, B. (2002). Which Kind of Transparency? On the Need for Effective Communication in Monetary Policy-Making. Ifo Studien, 48, 3, 401-27. 5 Hahn, V. (2002). Transparency in Monetary Policy: A Survey. Ifo Studien, 48, 3, 429-55. Carpenter, S.B. (Nisan 2004). Transparency and Monetary Policy: What Does the Academic Literature Tell Policymakers?. The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. 6 Poole, W. (Kasf5m/Aralf5k 2003). Fed Transparency: How, Not Whether. Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Review, 85, 6, 1-8.Poole (2003). 3 On the other hand, as policies are shared with the public in a transparent manner, the credibility of central banks increases and the environment of trust required in the decision-making processes of economic units is created. Therefore, reliability is the second important factor in the prominence of communication policies. Consistency between policy practices and policy statements is critical to building credibility. Maintaining credibility is closely related to the achievement of policy objectives. At this point, when it comes to reliability, I can easily say that what is done makes more noise than what is said. This whole process makes reliability a "difficult to gain and maintain, easy to lose" quality. In this context, an effective and transparent communication policy comes to the forefront in minimizing the negative effects that unexpected developments may cause on reliability. Various studies support this view. According to a survey study among economists,7 transparency ranks third in building credibility after independence and past honest and credible policy implementations. Another study8 shows that even if there are deviations from the target, these deviations do not cause public concern about the fulfillment of commitments, thanks to increased trust through communication. Dear Listeners, The relationship between independence and reliability and communication policies offers us a corporate perspective. All dimensions of this approach are closely related to each other, each complementary to the other. The third element that I will mention today that requires an effective communication policy is closely related to increasing the effectiveness of monetary policy. The basis of this relationship is based on the thesis that "the more predictable the monetary policy, the more effective it is". In other words, explaining the reasons behind policy implementations ensures that these practices are understood and supported on the one hand, and on the other hand, it contributes to the formation of expectations in line with the objectives in a credible manner. 7 Waller, S., Haan, J. (Mayf5s 2004). Credibility and Transparency of Central Banks: New Results Based on IFOd5s World Economic Survey, CESifo. 8 King, M. (1997). Changes in UK Monetary Policy: Rules and Discretion in Practice. Journal of Monetary Economics, 39, 81-97. 4 When we look at the economic literature on this subject, the generally accepted view in the 1950s and 1960s is that expectations are formed according to past experiences. This view is called the theory of "harmonious waiting". In 1961, an alternative theory called "rational expectations" was developed9. Accordingly, economic units use not only their past experiences but also every new knowledge they acquire while creating their expectations. Although the assumption that all expectations in the markets are rational is controversial, it is accepted that every new piece of information will change the predictions, and therefore the expectations, while the waits will affect the decisions taken over time and create realizations. This places the management of waits and therefore communication policy in an extremely important position in policy implementation. Dear Listeners, Now I would like to tell you in more detail about the role of communication and the management of expectations in monetary policy. Considering that the ultimate goal of central banks is to ensure and maintain price stability, and that they do this by controlling domestic demand, it is seen that the expectations in the traditional monetary policy transmission mechanism can affect total demand through two channels. The first of these channels is the interest rate channel, which we can define as the effect / determination of short-term interest rates on long-term interest rates. Central banks that choose short-term interest rates as their main policy tool can only directly control this interest rate. On the other hand, long-term interest rates are taken into account as a reference when making investment and savings decisions that determine economic activity, but these interest rates may move in different directions from policy rates from time to time. The most important factor that connects short-term interest rates with long-term interest rates is waiting. In this context, one of the important contributions of managing expectations with an effective communication policy to monetary policy is the increase in predictability in the markets, which contributes to the reduction of risk and volatility in the markets and to the increase of the harmony between policy interest rates and the general level of interest rates. 9 Muth, J. (1961). Rational Expectations and the Theory of Price Movements. Econometrica, 29, 31535. 5 Therefore, central banks aim to influence long-term interest rates by managing communications policies and waits. As stated by the Chairman of the US Federal Reserve, Bernanke; Communication is a crucial tool for central banks to influence long-term interest rates, thus ensuring the effectiveness of monetary policy10. Secondly, the management of waits and the communication policy implemented for this purpose help to keep inflation under control through direct expectations. Increased predictability through the management of expectations influences the behavior of economic units such as wage determination and pricing, ensuring that inflation expectations and consequent realizations are shaped in line with the central bank's objectives. Predictability also contributes to the efficient operation of other transmission channels, such as asset prices and loans. All this makes an effective communication policy an integral part of central bank independence, credibility and the effectiveness of the monetary policies implemented. Therefore, the creation of an effective communication policy is a necessity for central banks. In the literature on this subject, there are many studies showing that communication policy can substitute other policies that are being implemented and increase the effectiveness of policy implementations. Central bankers generally agree that communication, and transparency within this scope, is not only an obligation for the institution to fulfill the principle of accountability, but also an opportunity for the effectiveness of the institution and the policies it pursues11. Moreover, in developing countries like ours, which have an inflationary and unstable macroeconomic past, an effective communication policy is even more important because of its contribution to the elimination of the bad effects of past experiences by ensuring that economic policies and their possible consequences are well understood by the public. 10 Bernanke, B. (2004). d2Fedspeakd3. Remarks at the Meetings of the American Economic Association. 11 Issing, O. (Mart-Nisan 2005). d2Communication, Transparency, Accountability: Monetary Policy in the Twenty-first Centuryd3. Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Sf. 65 d0 83. 6 Dear Participants, Although it is a widely accepted view today that transparency and an effective communication policy increase the effectiveness of monetary policy, there is no accepted consensus on the degree of transparency and how the most effective communication strategy should be. The unique traditions and backgrounds of countries, the presence of different target groups and different economic conditions make it impossible to have a single best strategy suitable for each country. On the other hand, an effective communication policy requires a certain strategic approach. This strategy; In addition to clearly stating the objectives of communication, it requires the definition of communication principles, target audiences, communication channels and means of communication, the right timing and the determination of what, why and how to explain. All this makes it clear that creating and implementing a communication strategy is a challenging process. At this point, I would like to specifically mention the difficulties encountered in policy implementations in terms of communication within the framework of monetary policy and some elements that are not understood much in the public opinion. The first of these, as we have closely experienced, is aimed at the period of time in which monetary policy shows its effect. More specifically, the delayed impact of a change in central bank policy rates on economic activity and inflation requires an assessment of the policies implemented from a medium-term perspective. The fact that economic units can understand this perspective and the delayed effect necessitates an effective communication policy. In countries like ours, which have lived with high inflation for many years, it takes time for this perspective to be established and this constitutes a significant obstacle to the fight against inflation. Another important element is that an effective communication strategy should clearly reflect the existing information on monetary policy while at the same time drawing attention to the fact that any new information obtained can reshape this policy. In this context, the content of announcements and discourses and the words used are also of particular importance. On the other hand, as I mentioned earlier in the context of defining transparency, more information means more transparency and more effective communication. 7 Does not. As Paul Jenkins, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Canada, points out, what matters in transparency and communication is quality, not quantity12. In this context, it is important to determine how the message to be transmitted can be transmitted most effectively, which tools and which channels will be taken as the basis for the communication policy. The most important conclusion that can be drawn from all this is that the communication strategies of central banks should be in a continuous development. This development expresses the process of understanding the views and information of market participants and the public on the monetary policy of the central bank on the one hand, and the process of better understanding of the markets and public opinion of the central bank on the other. In our country, this process has shown great progress especially in the recent period. Now I would like to tell you about the development of the communication policies of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey in a general framework. Dear Listeners, Our Bank's communication policy has changed and developed over time in a process similar to other central banks. In the most general terms; The tendency towards increasing the weight of transparency and communication policies in central banking, which I mentioned in the first part of my speech, has also been adopted by our Bank depending on the monetary policy and institutional structure implemented. When we describe the year 2001 when the Central Bank gained its independence as a turning point, it would be correct to convey the development of communication policy in two periods, before and after 2001. When we look closely at the monetary policies before 2001, it is seen that in the second half of the 1980s, when the financial liberalization in the Turkish economy was completed, and afterwards, the Central Bank, which did not have the opportunity to carry out an active monetary policy, turned to implement a policy to ensure stability in financial markets. In this period, two factors played a decisive role in monetary policy as well as in the communication of the Central Bank. 12 Jenkins, P. (2001). Communicating Canadian Monetary Policy: Towards Greater Transparency. , 46, 1-5. 8 The first element is that neither legally nor in practice a policy priority was defined for the Central Bank during the period in question. In this period when an increasing number of central banks in the world are tasked with ensuring only price stability, the Central Bank in our country has had to observe many variables such as growth, exports, employment, and even many purposes that contradict each other from time to time. The second element is that the Central Bank is obliged to finance the government's budget deficits by lending to public institutions, especially the Treasury. The monetization of budget deficits using Central Bank resources has been contrary to the basic elements of anti-inflation programs, which can be summarized as the implementation of disciplined fiscal and monetary policies, and on the other hand, it has been a very important obstacle to the independent policy implementation of the Central Bank. The reflection of these factors on the Turkish economy is high and chronic inflation. The reflection of the Central Bank's communication policy is that transparency cannot be ensured to the desired extent and prevents the design of an effective strategy. Pursuing different priorities in policy implementation, lacking a clear objective and legal independence made it difficult for the Central Bank to establish consistency in its public messages. With the effect of the fact that transparency in central banking was not yet a widespread and weighted concept in the world at that time, our Bank followed a more conservative path in communication policy. In this process, two prominent developments in our Bank's communication policy stand out. The first is that since financial markets started to be established in our country and these markets were structured within our Bank in 1987, the Central Bank was more effective in communication, especially in communication with financial markets. In this context, on the one hand, the Central Bank has established a strong communication with market players in order to ensure stability in the increasingly complex financial markets and on the other hand to play a leading role in the deepening and development of these markets. The second important development is the 1990 Monetary Program, which was announced for the first time in the history of the Central Bank. In 1990, the Central Bank began to control monetary quantities. 9 has publicly announced that it will implement a money program based on it. In this program, economic developments were explained with a medium-term perspective and expectations for the future were conveyed. However, the fact that the announcement of this program is not part of a specific communication strategy that has been planned and put into practice, and that the information work on the subject is not continued after the program is announced, does not make it possible to evaluate this statement as an element of communication policy as we understand it today. After 1990; Until 2000, due to the Gulf War, early elections and the increasing uncertainty in the economy, there was no strong communication of the monetary and exchange rate policies that were being implemented. Dear Listeners, The year 2000 is important in terms of monetary policies. On this date, an exchange rate-based stabilization program based on the fight against inflation and bringing discipline to public finances was put into practice in order to establish macroeconomic stability, which could not be achieved in the 90s. Even if communication strategies are not included as an important element of exchange rate-based stability programs in the economic literature, the Central Bank has become more active in communication with this program. At this point, I would like to express that the fact that the Central Bank has been given a mission to combat inflation with the year 2000 program contributes to the efforts to create a communication strategy is very important. In this context, the communication strategy of the Central Bank with this program was realized in the form of committing a certain exchange rate level and announcing the results of implementation related to monetary quantities and the value of the exchange rate basket to the public at regular intervals. In addition, in this period, joint informative meetings were started to be organized with the chambers of industry and commerce throughout the country. However, the 2000 program could not be continued and ended in a crisis with the loss of confidence in the stabilization program. 10 Dear Listeners, The year 2001 was a turning point for the Central Bank as well as for the Turkish economy. With the significant amendments made to the Central Bank Law in May 2001, the main objective of the Bank was determined as ensuring price stability and the Bank was authorized to freely determine the monetary policy instruments to be used to achieve its objectives. In other words, the Central Bank has achieved instrument independence. Taking responsibility in an area such as inflation, which directly affects the daily life of everyone in society, and implementing policies in this direction has brought the Central Bank to the agenda of public opinion as never before in the past; has made transparency and accountability an integral part of the Bank's policies. In such an environment, the Central Bank has placed public communication at the center of its practices. In this context, I would like to first talk about the reflections of accountability on our communication policies. Within the framework of accountability, the Council of Ministers is informed about the activities of the Central Bank and the monetary policies that have been implemented and will be implemented by the Central Bank Governor himself in April and October and twice a year by the Planning and Budget Commission of the Turkish Grand National Assembly. Another important means of accountability is that if our Bank fails to reach or is likely to fail to reach the specified inflation targets within the announced periods, it is obliged to notify the Government in writing and to explain to the public the reasons for this and the measures to be taken. The second factor that has been effective in bringing communication policies to the forefront after 2001 is the inflation targeting regime, which has been implemented "implicitly" in 2002 and has been implemented "openly" since 2006. The inflation targeting regime, which is a strategy in which inflation is directly targeted and monetary policy is institutionalized for this purpose, requires an active communication strategy to be followed, as it is often mentioned in the economic literature. 11 In the inflation targeting regime, which is successful to the extent that economic units use the inflation targets as nominal anchors, it is a necessity to follow an appropriate and effective communication policy in this direction and to provide an institutional structure of communication. With the establishment of the General Directorate of Communications within our Bank in 2002, an important step was taken towards the Central Bank's communication strategy to have an institutional structure as required by the inflation targeting regime. In this context, ensuring the correct perception of the policies implemented in achieving price stability, conducting relations with the press and announcing the policies to the public from a single source are defined as the main duties of this General Directorate. Since 2001, the Central Bank has also focused on developing and diversifying the tools it uses in communication. As in the examples of other countries, our Bank uses press releases effectively in the announcement of policy decisions to the public first-hand. The decisions of the Central Bank on short-term interest rates are sent to all media organizations in a way that does not include asymmetric information in electronic environment within the scope of the simultaneous information strategy after the Monetary Policy Committee meeting and announced to the public through our website. The regular meetings we hold with media representatives, the conferences we hold in various cities of Anatolia before non-governmental organizations and the speeches we make at universities aim to directly convey our policy practices to the public within the framework of a certain communication strategy. In addition to these, information on monetary policy and economic developments is conveyed to the public through the publications of our Bank. With the Inflation Report, which we publish after a press conference four times a year, we share the developments regarding inflation and our views on the inflation outlook with the public. With the Financial Stability Report that we publish twice a year, we share with you our evaluations on financial stability, which is our supportive and complementary goal as well as our main goal of price stability. On the other hand, we also use our website as an effective means of communication. All our press releases, publications, reports, data and all speech texts and presentations can be accessed from our site. 12 Dear Participants, After mentioning the distance taken by our Bank in both institutional and strategic terms within the framework of communication in this way, I would like to briefly talk about the direct and indirect reflections of this structure on our policy practices. First of all, within the framework of the inflation targeting regime, the year-end inflation targets set jointly by the Government and our Bank since 2002 have been met for four consecutive years, and inflation has fallen to single digit levels after thirty years. These gains contributed to the process of gaining the reputation of the Turkish currency by removing six zeros from our currency at the beginning of 2005; Together with the effective communication policy we have implemented, it has increased the reliability of both the policies implemented and the Central Bank. Achievement of targets and increased credibility through communication policy have been increasingly effective in shaping inflation expectations over time. As of today, the most effective channel in the Turkish economy is the waiting channel. Of course, the inertia created by the nearly three-decade history of high inflation creates a significant challenge in managing expectations. However, when we look at it today, we are pleased to see that the inflation target is increasingly being used as a nominal anchor in decision-making processes. The results of the Expectations Survey, which is applied twice a month by our Bank, show that although fluctuations are seen from time to time, the inflation expectations of economic units converge more to the inflation target over time. However, considering that the gains achieved in the economy in our country have only been in the last five years, it is not surprising that the waits due to the slightest negative development react much stronger than this development requires. This situation always keeps communication policy and the management of waits at the top of the agenda. On the other hand, the inflation targeting regime and the institutional arrangements carried out within this framework have also contributed to the increase in the predictability of policies. The establishment of the Monetary Policy Committee, the announcement of the dates of the meetings in advance and the announcement of the decisions on short-term interest rates after the meeting, and the timing and direction of these decisions becoming more transparent and more predictable contributed significantly to the management of the expectations. 13 Although it is not yet as strong and permanent as desired, the relationship between short-term interest rates and long-term rates is also getting stronger. In other words, within the framework of our transparent, consistent and honest communication policy and expectation management, interest rate decisions and signals given about the course of the economy are more effective than in determining the investment and consumption decisions and pricing behaviors of economic units. In parallel with the strengthening of the transmission mechanism and the increase in predictability, according to the studies we have carried out within our Bank13, the effect of the change in Central Bank policy interest rates on the economy of our country is gradually increasing and this effect is realized more slowly than in the past. This requires consideration of a process that extends to the medium term in the monetary policy decision-making process. In this context, inflation targets started to be announced for a three-year target horizon in 2006. Our economy has made significant progress towards normalization. As we stated in our announcement titled "Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy in 2007", unlike in 2006, we will take into account a 2-year perspective instead of 1.5 years when creating our forecasts for the course of inflation next year. I would also like to point out that in this way, we aim for economic units to make investment and savings decisions in a more predictable environment. Dear Listeners, While concluding my words here, I would like to state that the basis of the communication policies that have been increasingly emphasized by central banks in the last fifteen years is the importance of monetary policy practices and the mutual understanding process that will develop by sharing the underlying reasons for these practices with you and the public. Therefore, your contribution to this process is very important for us. Since 2001, the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey has started to follow a certain communication strategy unlike previous periods. As of this date, all kinds of information, predictions and risks have started to be shared with the public and it is foreseen that this structure will continue to strengthen. 13 Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2007. 14 In this context, although I do not deny the importance of the distance we have taken in terms of communication policies, I would also like to express that there are still important distances we will take in front of us, considering that communication characterizes a dynamic process as a concept. Thank you. 15

Econometrica, 29, 31535. 5 Dolaysyla merkez bankalar, iletiim politikalar ile bekleyileri yneterek ksa vadeli politika faiz oranlarnn uzun vadeli faiz oranlarn etkilemesini hedeflerler. ABD Merkez Bankas Bakan Bernankenin de belirttii gibi; iletiim, merkez bankalarnn uzun vadeli faiz oranlarn etkileyebilmesi, dolaysyla para politikasnn etkinliini salamas asndan ok nemli bir aratr10. kinci olarak bekleyilerin ynetimi ve bu amala uygulanan iletiim politikas, enflasyonun dorudan bekleyiler kanal ile kontrol altnda tutulmasna yardmc olur. Bekleyilerin ynetimi ile artan ngrlebilirlik, ekonomik birimlerin cret belirleme ve fiyatlama gibi davranlarn etkileyerek, enflasyon bekleyilerinin ve sonucunda gereklemelerin merkez bankasnn hedefleri dorultusunda ekillenmesini salar. ngrlebilirlik ayn zamanda varlk fiyatlar ve krediler gibi dier aktarm kanallarnn da etkin almasna katkda bulunur. Tm bunlar, etkin bir iletiim politikasn merkez bankas bamszlnn, gvenilirliinin ve uygulanan para politikalarnn etkinliinin ayrlmaz bir paras haline getirmektedir. Dolaysyla etkin bir iletiim politikas oluturulmas merkez bankalar iin bir zorunluluktur. Bu konu ile ilgili literatrde de iletiim politikasnn uygulanmakta olan dier politikalar ikame edebileceini ve politika uygulamalarnn etkinliini artracan gsteren birok alma bulunmaktadr. Merkez bankaclar da iletiimin ve bu kapsamda effafln kurum iin sadece hesap verme ilkesini yerine getirmek iin bir ykmllk olmad, ayn zamanda kurum ve izledii politikalarn etkinlii bakmndan bir frsat olduu konusunda genel olarak bir uzla iindedirler11. stelik bizim gibi enflasyonist ve istikrarsz bir makroekonomik gemie sahip gelimekte olan lkelerde etkin bir iletiim politikas, ekonomi politikalarnn ve olas sonularnn kamuoyu tarafndan iyi anlalmasn salayarak gemi tecrbelerin kt etkilerinin ortadan kaldrlmasna yapt katk nedeniyle daha da nemlidir. 10 Bernanke, B. (2004). Fedspeak. Remarks at the Meetings of the American Economic Association. 11 Issing, O. (Mart-Nisan 2005). Communication, Transparency, Accountability: Monetary Policy in the Twenty-first Century. Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Sf. 65  83. 6 Deerli Katlmclar, effafln ve etkin bir iletiim politikasnn para politikasnn etkinliini artrd bugn hemen herkes tarafndan kabul edilen bir gr olsa da, effafln derecesi ve en etkin iletiim stratejisinin nasl olmas gerektii konusunda kabul edilmi ortak bir gr bulunmamaktadr. lkelerin kendine zg gelenekleri ve gemileri, farkl hedef kitlelerin varl ve farkl ekonomik koullar her lkeye uygun tek bir en iyi stratejinin varln imkansz klmaktadr. te yandan etkin bir iletiim politikas elbette belirli bir stratejik yaklam izlenmesini gerektirmektedir. Bu strateji; iletiim amalarnn aka belirtilmesinin yan sra iletiim ilkelerinin, hedef kitlelerin, iletiim kanallarnn ve iletiim aralarnn tanmlanmasn, doru zamanlamay ve neyin, niin ve ne ekilde anlatlacann belirlenmesini gerektirmektedir. Tm bunlar bir iletiim stratejisi oluturmann ve uygulamann zorlu bir sre olduunu aka ortaya koymaktadr. Bu noktada para politikas erevesinde iletiim anlamnda politika uygulamalarna ynelik karlalan zorluklardan, kamuoyunda ok fazla anlalmayan baz unsurlardan zellikle bahsetmek istiyorum. Bunlardan ilki, bizim de yakndan tecrbe ettiimiz zere, para politikasnn etkisini gsterdii zaman dilimine yneliktir. Daha ak bir ifadeyle, merkez bankas politika faiz oranlarnda yaplan bir deiikliin ekonomik aktivite ve enflasyon zerindeki gecikmeli etkisi, uygulanan politikalarn orta vadeli bir bak asyla deerlendirilmesini gerektirmektedir. Ekonomik birimlerin bu bak asn ve gecikmeli etkiyi anlayabilmeleri, etkin bir iletiim politikasn gerekli klmaktadr. Bizim gibi uzun yllar yksek enflasyonla yaam lkelerde bu bak asnn yerlemesi zaman almakta ve bu, enflasyonla mcadelenin nnde nemli bir engel oluturmaktadr. Bir dier nemli unsur, etkin bir iletiim stratejisinin bir yandan para politikasna ilikin mevcut bilgileri aka yanstrken, bir yandan da elde edilen her yeni bilginin bu politikay yeniden ekillendirebileceine de dikkat ekmesi gerektiidir. Bu kapsamda, duyuru ve sylemlerin ierii ve kullanlan kelimeler de ayr bir nem tamaktadr. te yandan, effafln tanmlanmas kapsamnda daha nce de bahsettiim gibi, daha fazla bilgi, daha fazla effaflk ve daha etkili bir iletiim anlamna 7 gelmemektedir. Kanada Merkez Bankas Bakan Yardmcs Paul Jenkinsin de belirttii gibi, effaflk ve iletiim kapsamnda nemli olan nicelik deil, niteliktir12. Bu kapsamda iletilmek istenen mesajn en etkin nasl iletilebilecei, hangi aralarn ve hangi kanallarn iletiim politikasnda temel alnacann belirlenmesi nem tamaktadr. Tm bunlardan karlabilecek en nemli sonu, merkez bankalarnn iletiim stratejilerinin srekli bir geliim iinde olmas gerektiidir. Bu geliim bir yandan piyasa katlmclarnn ve kamuoyunun merkez bankasnn para politikasna dair gr ve bilgilerini anlama, dier yandan da merkez bankasnn piyasalar ve kamuoyunu daha iyi anlama srecini ifade etmektedir. lkemizde de bu sre zellikle son dnemde byk ilerleme gstermitir. imdi sizlere Trkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasnn iletiim politikalarnn geliimini genel bir ereve ierisinde anlatmak istiyorum. Deerli Dinleyiciler, Bankamzn iletiim politikas, dier merkez bankalarna benzer bir sre iinde zamanla deierek gelimitir. En genel ifadesiyle; konumamn ilk blmnde de deindiim, merkez bankaclndaki effaflama ve iletiim politikalarnn arlnn artmas ynndeki eilim, uygulanan para politikasna ve kurumsal yapsna bal olarak Bankamzca da benimsenmitir. Merkez Bankasnn bamszln kazand 2001 yln bir dnm noktas olarak nitelediimizde, iletiim politikasnn geliimini de 2001 ncesi ve sonras olmak zere iki dnemde aktarmak doru olacaktr. 2001 yl ncesi para politikalarna yakndan bakldnda, Trkiye ekonomisinde finansal serbestlemenin tamamland 1980lerin ikinci yars ve sonrasnda, aktif bir para politikas yrtme olana olmayan Merkez Bankasnn, finansal piyasalarda istikrar salama ynnde bir politika uygulamasna yneldii grlmektedir. Bu dnemde, para politikasnda olduu kadar Merkez Bankasnn iletiiminde de iki unsur belirleyici rol oynamtr. 12 Jenkins, P. (2001). Communicating Canadian Monetary Policy: Towards Greater Transparency. BIS Review, 46, 1-5. 8 lk unsur, sz konusu dnemde ne yasal olarak, ne de uygulamada Merkez Bankas iin bir politika nceliinin tanmlanmam olmasdr. Dnyada giderek artan sayda merkez bankasnn sadece fiyat istikrarn salamakla grevlendirildii bu dnemde lkemizde Merkez Bankas, byme, ihracat, istihdam gibi birok deikeni, hatta zaman zaman birbiriyle elien pek ok amac ayn anda gzetmek zorunda kalmtr. kinci unsur ise, Merkez Bankasnn kamu kurulularna, zellikle Hazineye kredi vermek suretiyle hkmetin bte aklarn finanse etmekle ykml tutulmu olmasdr. Bte aklarnn Merkez Bankas kaynaklar kullanlarak parasallamas, bir taraftan enflasyonla mcadele programlarnn disiplinli maliye ve para politikalar uygulanmas olarak zetlenebilecek temel unsurlarna ters derken, dier taraftan Merkez Bankasnn bamsz politika uygulamalarnn nnde ok nemli bir engel tekil etmitir. Bu unsurlarn Trkiye ekonomisine yansmas yksek ve kronik enflasyon eklindedir. Merkez Bankas iletiim politikasna yansmas ise effafln arzu edildii lde salanamamas ve etkin bir strateji tasarlanmasna engel olmasdr. Politika uygulamalarnda farkl ncelikler izlenmesi, net bir hedefinin ve yasal bir bamszlnn olmamas Merkez Bankas asndan kamuoyuna verilen mesajlarda tutarlln tesisini gletirmitir. Merkez bankaclnda effafln dnyada o dnemlerde henz yaygnlam ve arlk kazanm bir kavram olmamasnn da etkisi ile Bankamz da iletiim politikasnda daha tutucu bir yol izlemitir. Bu srete Bankamzn iletiim politikasnda ne kan iki gelime gze arpmaktadr. lki lkemizde finansal piyasalarn kurulmaya balanmas ve 1987 ylnda bu piyasalarn Bankamz bnyesinde yaplanmas nedeniyle Merkez Bankasnn iletiim konusunda, zellikle finansal piyasalarla iletiim konusunda daha etkin olmasdr. Bu kapsamda bir taraftan giderek daha karmak bir yap kazanan finansal piyasalarda istikrar salamak, te yandan bu piyasalarn derinlemesini ve gelimesinde nc rol oynamak amacyla Merkez Bankas piyasa oyuncular ile gl bir iletiim kurmutur. kinci nemli gelime, Merkez Bankas tarihinde ilk kez aklanan 1990 yl Para Programdr. 1990 ylnda Merkez Bankas parasal byklklerin kontrolne 9 dayanan bir para program uygulayacan kamuoyuna aklamtr. Aklanan bu programda, orta vadeli bir bak as ile ekonomik gelimeler anlatlm ve gelecee ilikin beklentiler aktarlmtr. Ancak, gerek bu programn aklanmasnn planlanm ve uygulamaya konmu belirli bir iletiim stratejisinin paras olmamas, gerekse program aklandktan sonra konu ile ilgili bilgilendirme almalarna devam edilmeyii, bu aklamann bugn anladmz anlamyla iletiim politikasnn bir unsuru olarak deerlendirilmesini mmkn klmamaktadr. 1990 yl sonrasnda; 2000 ylna dein, Krfez sava, erken seim ve ekonomide giderek artan belirsizlik ortamna da bal olarak uygulanmakta olan para ve kur politikalarnn gl bir iletiimi yaplamamtr. Deerli Dinleyiciler, 2000 yl ise para politikalar asndan nemlidir. Bu tarihte 90l yllarda bir trl salanamayan makroekonomik istikrar tesisi etmek zere enflasyonla mcadeleyi ve kamu maliyesine disiplin getirmeyi temel alan dviz kuruna dayal bir istikrar program uygulamaya konmutur. ktisat yaznnda iletiim stratejileri dviz kuruna dayal istikrar programlarnn nemli bir unsuru olarak yer almasa dahi Merkez Bankas bu programla beraber iletiim konusunda daha aktif olmaya balamtr. 2000 yl programyla birlikte Merkez Bankasna enflasyonla mcadele konusunda bir misyon verilmi olmasnn iletiim stratejisi oluturma abalarna katksnn ok nemli olduunu bu noktada ifade etmek istiyorum. Bu erevede sz konusu programla Merkez Bankasnn iletiim stratejisi, belirli bir dviz kuru seviyesinin taahht edilmesi ile parasal byklkler ve kur sepetinin deeri ile ilgili uygulama sonularnn belirli aralklarla kamuoyuna ilan edilmesi eklinde gereklemitir. Ayrca, bu dnemde lke apnda sanayi ve ticaret odalar ile ortak bilgilendirme toplantlar dzenlenmeye balanmtr. Ancak 2000 yl program devam ettirilememi ve istikrar programna olan gvenin kaybolmas ile birlikte bir krizle sona ermitir. 10 Deerli Dinleyiciler, 2001 yl Trkiye ekonomisi iin olduu kadar Merkez Bankas iin de bir dnm noktas nitelii tamaktadr. 2001 yl Mays aynda Merkez Bankas Kanununda yaplan nemli deiikliklerle Bankann temel hedefi fiyat istikrarn salamak olarak belirlenmi ve Bankaya hedeflerine ulamak iin kullanaca para politikas aralarn serbeste belirleyebilme yetkisi verilmitir. Bir dier ifade ile Merkez Bankas ara bamszlna kavumutur. Enflasyon gibi toplumdaki herkesin gndelik hayatn dorudan etkileyen bir alanda sorumluluk alnmas ve bu ynde politikalar uygulanmas, Merkez Bankasn gemite hibir dnemde olmad kadar kamuoyunun gndemine tam; effafl ve hesap verebilir olmay Banka politikalarnn ayrlmaz bir paras haline getirmitir. Byle bir ortamda Merkez Bankas kamuoyuyla iletiimi uygulamalarnn merkezine yerletirmitir. Bu kapsamda ilk olarak hesap verebilirliin iletiim politikalarmza yansmalarndan bahsetmek istiyorum. Hesap verebilirlik erevesinde, Merkez Bankasnn faaliyetleri ile uygulanm ve uygulanacak olan para politikalar hakknda her yl Nisan ve Ekim aylarnda Bakanlar Kurulu, ylda iki kere de Trkiye Byk Millet Meclisi Plan ve Bte Komisyonu bizzat Merkez Bankas Bakan tarafndan bilgilendirilmektedir. Bir dier nemli hesap verme arac ise, Bankamzn belirlenen enflasyon hedeflerine ilan edilen srelerde ulalamamas veya ulalamama olaslnn ortaya kmas halinde, bunun nedenlerini ve alnmas gereken nlemleri Hkmete yazl olarak bildirme ve kamuoyuna aklama ykmllnn bulunmasdr. 2001 yl sonrasnda iletiim politikalarnn n plana kmasnda etkili olan ikinci unsur ise 2002 ylnda rtk olarak uygulanmaya balanan 2006 ylndan itibaren ise ak olarak uygulanmakta olan enflasyon hedeflemesi rejimidir. Enflasyonun dorudan kendisinin hedeflendii ve bu amaca ynelik olarak para politikasnn kurumsallat bir strateji olan enflasyon hedeflemesi rejimi, iktisat yaznnda da sklkla bahsedildii zere, aktif bir iletiim stratejisi izlenmesini gerektirmektedir. 11 Ekonomik birimlerin konulan enflasyon hedeflerini nominal apa olarak kullanmalar lsnde baarl olan enflasyon hedeflemesi rejiminde, bu dorultuda uygun ve etkin bir iletiim politikas izlenmesi ve iletiimin kurumsal bir yapya kavuturulmas bir zorunluluktur. 2002 ylnda Bankamz bnyesinde letiim Genel Mdrlnn kurulmas ile Merkez Bankas iletiim stratejisinin enflasyon hedeflemesi rejiminin de gerektirdii gibi kurumsal bir yapya kavuturulmas ynnde nemli bir adm atlmtr. Bu erevede fiyat istikrarna ulamada uygulanan politikalarn doru alglanmasn salamak, basn ile ilikileri yrtmek ve politikalar tek elden kamuoyuna duyurmak bu Genel Mdrln temel grevleri olarak tanmlanmtr. 2001 ylndan itibaren Merkez Bankas iletiimde kulland aralar da gelitirmeye ve eitlendirmeye arlk vermitir. Bankamz, dier lke rneklerinde olduu gibi, politika kararlarnn ilk elden kamuoyuna duyurulmasnda basn duyurularn etkin olarak kullanmaktadr. Merkez Bankasnn ksa vadeli faiz oranlarna ilikin kararlar, Para Politikas Kurulu toplantsnn ardndan eanl bilgilendirme stratejisi kapsamnda elektronik ortamda asimetrik bilgiye yer vermeyecek ekilde tm medya kurulularna gnderilmekte ve nternet sitemiz zerinden kamuoyuna ilan edilmektedir. Medya temsilcileri ile gerekletirdiimiz dzenli toplantlar, sivil toplum rgtleri nezdinde Anadolunun eitli kentlerinde gerekletirdiimiz konferanslar ile niversitelerde yaptmz konumalar politika uygulamalarmzn belli bir iletiim stratejisi erevesinde kamuoyuna dorudan aktarlabilmesi amacn tamaktadr. Bunlarn yan sra, Bankamz yaynlar ile para politikasna ve ekonomik gelimelere dair bilgiler kamuoyuna aktarlmaktadr. Ylda drt kere bir basn toplantsnn ardndan yaymladmz Enflasyon Raporu ile enflasyona ilikin gelimeleri ve enflasyon grnmne ilikin grlerimizi kamuoyu ile paylamaktayz. Ylda iki kere yaymladmz Finansal stikrar Raporu ile de fiyat istikrar temel amacmzn yannda destekleyici ve tamamlayc amacmz olan finansal istikrara ilikin deerlendirmelerimizi sizlerle paylamaktayz. te yandan, nternet sitemizi de etkin bir iletiim arac olarak kullanmaktayz. Tm basn duyurularmza, yaynlarmza, raporlarmza, verilere ve yaplan tm konuma metinleri ile sunumlara sitemizden ulalabilmektedir. 12 Deerli Katlmclar, letiim erevesinde gerek kurumsal gerek stratejik anlamda Bankamzn ald mesafeden bu ekilde bahsettikten sonra, ksaca bu yapnn politika uygulamalarmza dorudan ve dolayl yansmalarndan bahsetmek istiyorum. ncelikle, enflasyon hedeflemesi rejimi erevesinde 2002 ylndan itibaren Hkmetle Bankamz tarafndan ortaklaa belirlenen yl sonu enflasyon hedefleri st ste drt yl tutturulmu, enflasyon otuz yl aradan sonra tek haneli seviyelere dmtr. Bu kazanmlar, 2005 yl banda paramzdan alt sfr atlmasyla Trk parasnn itibar kazanma srecine katkda bulunmu; uyguladmz etkin iletiim politikas ile birlikte ise hem uygulanan politikalarn hem de Merkez Bankasnn gvenilirliini artrmtr. Hedeflerin tutturulmas ve iletiim politikas ile artan gvenilirlik, zaman ierisinde giderek artan lde enflasyon bekleyilerini ekillendirmede etkin olmutur. Bugn itibaryla Trkiye ekonomisinde en etkili alan kanal bekleyiler kanaldr. Elbette yaklak otuz yllk yksek enflasyon gemiinin yaratt atalet, bekleyilerin ynetiminde nemli bir zorluk yaratmaktadr. Ancak bugn baktmzda, enflasyon hedefinin karar alma srelerinde giderek artan oranda nominal apa olarak kullanlmaya balandn memnuniyetle grmekteyiz. Bankamzn ayda iki kere uygulad Beklenti Anketinin sonular da zaman zaman dalgalanmalar grlse de ekonomik birimlerin enflasyon beklentilerinin zaman iinde enflasyon hedefine daha fazla yaknsadn gstermektedir. Ancak lkemizde ekonomide elde edilen kazanmlarn sadece son be ylda olduu gz nne alndnda, en ufak bir olumsuz gelime nedeniyle bekleyilerin, bu gelimenin gerektirdiinden ok daha gl tepki vermesi artc deildir. Bu durum, iletiim politikasn ve bekleyilerin ynetimini her zaman gndemin ilk sralarnda tutmaktadr. te yandan, enflasyon hedeflemesi rejimi ve bu erevede gerekletirilen kurumsal dzenlemeler de, politikalarn ngrlebilirliinin artmasna katkda bulunmutur. Para Politikas Kurulunun kurulmas, toplant tarihlerinin nceden aklanmas ve ksa vadeli faiz oranlarna ilikin kararlarn toplant sonras ilan edilmesi, bu kararlarn zamanlamas ve ynnn daha effaf ve daha ngrlebilir hale gelmesi bekleyilerin ynetimine nemli lde katkda bulunmutur. 13 Her ne kadar henz arzu edildii lde kuvvetli ve kalc olmasa da, ksa vadeli faizler ile uzun vadeli faizler arasndaki iliki de giderek glenmektedir. Dier bir ifadeyle, effaf, tutarl ve drst iletiim politikamz ve beklenti ynetimi erevesinde faiz kararlar ile ekonominin gidiatna ilikin verilen sinyaller, ekonomik birimlerin yatrm ve tketim kararlarn ve fiyatlama davranlarn belirlemede gemie gre daha etkili olmaktadr. Aktarm mekanizmasnn kuvvetlenmesine ve ngrlebilirlik artna paralel olarak, Bankamz bnyesinde yaptmz almalara gre13, lkemiz ekonomisinde Merkez Bankas politika faiz oranlarndaki deiimin ekonomi zerindeki etkisi giderek artmakta ve bu etki gemie kyasla daha gecikmeli olarak gereklemektedir. Bu da para politikas karar alma srecinde orta vadeye doru uzayan bir srecin dikkate alnmasn gerektirmektedir. Bu erevede 2006 ylnda enflasyon hedefleri  yllk bir hedef ufku iin ilan edilmeye balanmtr. Ekonomimiz normalleme yolunda nemli bir mesafe kaydetmitir. 2007 Ylnda Para ve Kur Politikas balkl duyurumuzda da belirttiimiz gibi, 2006 ylndan farkl olarak nmzdeki yl enflasyonun seyrine ilikin tahminlerimizi olutururken 1,5 yl yerine 2 yllk bir bak asn dikkate alacaz. Bu ekilde ekonomik birimlerin yatrm ve tasarruf kararlarn daha ngrlebilir bir ortamda almalarn amaladmz da ayrca belirtmek isterim. Deerli Dinleyiciler, Szlerimi burada noktalarken, unu belirtmek isterim ki, son on be yllk dnemde merkez bankalar tarafndan giderek artan bir nemle zerinde durulan iletiim politikalarnn temelinde para politikas uygulamalarnn, bu uygulamalarn altnda yatan nedenlerin sizlerle, kamuoyuyla paylalmas suretiyle geliecek olan karlkl anlay srecinin nemi yatmaktadr. Dolaysyla sizlerin de bu srece katks bizim amzdan olduka nemlidir. Trkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankas 2001 ylndan itibaren nceki dnemlerden farkl olarak belirli bir iletiim stratejisi izlemeye balamtr. Bu tarihten itibaren, her trl bilgi, ngr ve risk kamuoyuyla paylalmaya balanm olup, bu yapnn kuvvetlenerek devam etmesi ngrlmektedir. 13 2007 Yl Para ve Kur Politikas. 14 Bu kapsamda iletiim politikalar asndan aldmz mesafenin nemini yadsmamakla birlikte, iletiimin kavram olarak dinamik bir sreci nitelemesinden hareketle, nmzde daha alacamz nemli mesafeler olduunu da ifade etmek isterim. Title: Anadolu Agencys Interview with Governor Murat Uysal
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Anadolu Agencys Interview with Governor Murat Uysal 15 July 2019 Anadolu Agencys Interview 15 July 2019 In the press release regarding your appointment as the new Governor of the Central Bank, you gave us some messages. One of them was related to communication policy. You made a commitment that communication channels will be utilized at the maximum level. What are the steps that you are thinking of taking in the period ahead regarding the communication of the monetary policy? Communication policies are essential in terms of the effectiveness of the policies implemented by the Central Bank in pursuit of price stability and in terms of accountability. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey (CBRT), particularly after the amendment to its law in 2001, developed strong corporate communication channels and invested a great deal in this field. In the new period, altogether with my colleagues, we will try to take these endeavors much further. I believe that establishing effective, transparent and inclusive communication with the public concerning our Banks activities on various platforms will provide major contributions to achieving our targets. We are engaged with certain improvements to increase corporate transparency and strengthen our policy communication. In this context, I can mention a few practices that may come up at the top of the agenda. For instance, we will share more information on the monetary policy decision-making process and the reasons underlying the decisions taken. We will strengthen our data sharing practices regarding Central Bank market operations. Moreover, we will also be sharing more concrete information on a more frequent basis through various media regarding the Central Banks approach to monetary policy and general issues. Apart from these, we are working on preparations for a range of aspects of our general communication practices. Accordingly, investors, financial institutions and corporate sector representatives, but above all the financial press, will continue to be our major stakeholders. We aim to sustain our activities to explain the importance of price stability as well as the Central Banks role in this process to all segments of the society. We will announce our communication framework in detail in the period ahead. In your first statement, there was also an emphasis on financial stability in addition to price stability. How should we read this? A highly inclusive and advanced financial system is a prerequisite for the smooth functioning of the monetary transmission mechanism. Economic actors access to financing means is a key factor for a stable macroeconomic outlook, particularly for production and exports. Moreover, price stability and financial stability are integral parts of one inseparable whole. Financial stability cannot be achieved unless price stability is established. On the other hand, in an economy that lacks strong financial stability, achievement of lasting price stability is out of the question. Therefore, as the CBRT, we closely monitor the interaction between the financial sector and the corporate sector and update our macroprudential tool kit by observing the soundness of the financial system. In the upcoming period, we will be using all available instruments, particularly reserve requirements, to contribute to financial stability. In the meantime, we will continue contributing to long-term structural efforts towards financial stability. Availability of alternative financing sources and increased instrument diversity will underpin the financing and saving decisions of households and other economic actors, primarily the corporate sector. In this regard, we, as the Central Bank, will be contributing more to steps towards deepening capital markets. 2 Anadolu Agencys Interview 15 July 2019 Then you are of the opinion that there is no contradiction between price stability and growth? These two concepts do not contradict each other; in fact, they support each other. Sound and inclusive growth strengthens the sustainability of price stability. Price stability reduces uncertainties and lowers interest rates, thereby underpinning the growth potential. I assess that continuity of the disinflation process in the current period in particular is essential to a reduced country risk premium and a strengthened economic recovery. Can we expect a noticeable change in the monetary policy strategy in the new period? I would like to indicate that the design of monetary policy processes in the new period will be based on a data-focused approach that takes into account all macroeconomic indicators, primarily inflation and economic activity. Additionally, we will continue to closely monitor micro dynamics and field data. In order to enhance effectiveness of the monetary policy, we will work in tandem with all parties that will provide input to the processes, primarily the financial sector, corporate sector and public sector. What are your assessments of recent inflation developments and your monetary policy stance in the new period? How will the course of the monetary policy be in the upcoming period? We see that inflation has been on the decline since October on the back of the monetary policy and other measures taken. Besides, inflation expectations are also on the decline in line with the decline in the level and volatility of inflation in the recent period. Both inflation dynamics and pricing behavior have started to improve. We expect that the disinflation process will remain in place on account of reduced cost pressures and weakened domestic demand conditions in 2019. All these developments suggest that there is room for maneuver in monetary policy. Thus, the Monetary Policy Committee will analyze all data releases and give the most appropriate decision guided by common sense and consultation. Needless to say, to achieve an ever-improving inflation outlook it is crucial to maintain a cautious monetary policy, but the level of tightness here can be best described through real rates rather than nominal rates. I can affirm that, by closely watching all factors affecting the inflation outlook, we will develop a framework that is built upon both expectations and our own projections and maintains a reasonable rate of real return. There have been growing hopes of monetary easing across major central banks recently. How do you think this will affect an emerging economy such as Turkey? Amid sharply weakening global economic activity and foreign trade and marked downside risks to inflation across advanced economies, we see mounting hopes of policy easing by major central banks, with the Fed and the ECB in the lead. Hopes of global monetary easing appear to boost the demand and the investor appetite for emerging market economy (EME) financial assets. Nevertheless, we are monitoring any development regarding protectionist trade policies and other global uncertainties. Looking at the domestic macroeconomic outlook, how do you see growth and the balance of payments? Recent data point to a moderate economic recovery driven by private and public expenditure as well as net exports. Despite the subdued global economic growth, both trade of goods and tourism and transport remain on the rise. Turkeys market share in world exports has been growing since 2013, which is evidence of improved competitiveness for Turkey. These developments have led to a rapid improvement in the current account balance. We expect the current account balance to approach zero by the end of the year. 3 Anadolu Agencys Interview 15 July 2019 Reserve adequacy has been a hot topic lately. Do you have any plans to increase reserves? Recently, there has been some improvement in reserve adequacy indicators thanks to the narrowing in the current account deficit and the downtrend in short term indebtedness. We still maintain our intention to increase international reserves as an insurance against external shocks provided that the necessary conditions are fulfilled. Currently, we already have the capacity to accumulate reserves via the rediscount credits. Nevertheless, foreign exchange sales to energy importing public institutions decrease reserves. We may take some steps towards increasing our reserves in the upcoming period depending on the global conjuncture and trend of capital flows. A draft omnibus bill was sent to the Parliament on 8 July 2019, what are your evaluations of the sections regarding the CBRT in this draft bill? The draft bill includes proposals on rearrangement under three main headings: reserve requirements, high-frequency data collection from financial institutions, and reserve funds. The regulation regarding reserve requirements will expand the Central Banks mandate pertaining to reserve requirements, taking into account the in-balance sheet and off-balance sheet items deemed appropriate. With the change to be introduced, the Central Banks tool kit will be expanded and therefore the CBRTs contribution to financial stability will increase. Similarly, access to high-frequency data will reinforce the CBRTs dataset and support the CBRTs new data-oriented monetary policy decision-making processes. Lastly, the rearrangement regarding reserve funds will harmonize the legal infrastructure with the Turkish Commercial Code. Fitch has downgraded Turkey over doubts about the Banks independence. What is your view here? We should make a distinction between instrument independence and goal independence while making evaluations about central bank independence. Central bank independence essentially means instrument independence. This means that a central bank determines the instruments and methods that it will implement to fulfill its duties at its own discretion. The concept of instrument independence has been clearly described in the Central Bank Law. Accordingly, the Bank is authorized to determine and implement the monetary policy instruments at its own discretion to fulfill the duties entrusted to it. There has been no change in this statement. Allow me one last question before we finish. You mentioned a press conference earlier. Do you have a date in mind? What I wanted the most when I assumed this position was to have this meeting. I find the media quite essential to our communication, but I've had a busy schedule since day one. The MPC meeting is approaching, so is the Inflation Report. We intend to meet with members of the press at the press conference for the Inflation Report to be held at the Bank. 4

Title: Speech of Chairman Murat etinkaya at the Informative Meeting on the Introduction of "Inflation Report 2017-III"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: 2017 JULY INFLATION REPORT INFORMATION MEETING Murat Cetinkaya 1 August 2017, Ankara Dear Guests, Welcome to the informative meeting where we will share the main messages of the July 2017 Inflation Report with you. In the report, as always, we share our assessments of macroeconomic developments with the economic outlook that forms the basis for monetary policy decisions and present our medium-term inflation forecasts and monetary policy stance updated in line with the developments in the last three months. In addition to the main sections, we included seven boxes on various topics in the report. These studies shed light on important issues related to the Turkish economy that are currently at the center of current discussions. You see the titles of the boxes on the mirror. The report includes studies that provide information on the expanded new export-weighted global growth index and analyze recent developments in food prices. In addition, discussing which indicators of economic activity should be followed after the publication of the new national income series and which variables would be useful to use in forecasting models; There are boxes that examine the resilience of Turkey's exports to foreign demand shocks. In addition, anticipating the reaction of exchange rate swap market rates of different maturities to policy rate surprises; There are also studies examining the impact of the share of foreign investors in the domestic debt stock on long-term domestic borrowing rates and finally analyzing the effects of unexpected changes in credit supply on key macroeconomic variables such as growth and inflation. I recommend you to read these studies, which will be published on our website within the scope of the Inflation Report in a moment. Dear Guests, I will begin by referring to the global economic outlook, which continues to play an important role in our policies. The second quarter of 2017 was a period in which global risk appetite remained strong. Although the positive outlook for global economic activity has become evident, the fact that global inflation rates are still at low levels supports risk appetite. Although the statements of the central banks of developed countries cause short-term fluctuations in the markets, the expectation that the normalization process in global monetary policies will be moderate is maintained. Market volatilities remained low and long-term bond yields of developed countries remained close to horizontal (Chart 1), contributed by increasing global risk appetite due to optimistic mood in financial markets. In this context, since the last Report period, this 2 Strong portfolio inflows into developing country debt and equity markets have continued since (Chart 2). Thanks to supportive macroprudential policies, public measures and incentives in the first half of 2017, the significant acceleration in credit utilization recorded in the second quarter began to stabilize from the end of the quarter. In this context, in the recent period, financial conditions have contributed to supporting economic activity. Consumer inflation, which has been on an upward trend since December 2016, showed a limited decline in the second quarter of the year and fell to 10.90 percent. While this partial improvement was determined by the decline in oil prices and the appreciation trend observed in the Turkish lira in the near term, the support given by demand conditions to the decline in inflation decreased as of the second quarter. In the first quarter of 2017, we saw that the recovery trend in economic activity continued. Leading indicators indicate that the recovery in economic activity maintained its strength in the second quarter. In addition, signals are being received that the sectoral spread of the recovery in the economy is increasing. While domestic demand is improving, the positive effect of the increase in the demand of European Union countries on exports continues. With the contribution of the supportive incentives and measures taken, we expect economic activity to continue to maintain its strength. 3 1. Monetary Policy Practices and Monetary Conditions Dear Guests, As you have been following closely, at the beginning of the second quarter, although there was a relative improvement in global financial conditions, the mobility in the foreign exchange market continued in part. With the assessment that rising inflation with the effect of the delayed effects of the depreciation of the Turkish lira, the rise in import prices and the increase in food prices pose a risk to pricing behavior, we decided to strengthen monetary tightening at the April PPK meeting and raised the lending interest rate from 11.75 percent to 12.25 percent from 11.75 percent at the April PPK meeting. In addition, we continued to source a large part of the system's funding needs from GLP during this period (Chart 3). In June and July, we observed that the upward update of growth forecasts for the global economy and falling volatility supported risk appetite; however, we maintained our tight stance on monetary policy by noting that risks to pricing behavior remained (Chart 4). Despite the positive course in global risk appetite in recent months and the limiting effect of cost-side developments, the high levels of inflation and the recent decrease in the inflation-reducing effect of aggregate demand conditions pose a risk to pricing behavior. Therefore, we will maintain our tight stance on monetary policy until there is a significant improvement in the inflation outlook. We are closely monitoring developments in inflation expectations, pricing behavior and other factors affecting inflation. I would also like to express that we can make additional monetary tightening if the need arises. Dear Guests, In the second quarter of 2017, we see that the upward trend in consumer loans continues due to the positive course in consumer confidence and the effect of supportive macroprudential policies. In addition, commercial credit growth continued to accelerate due to incentives such as KOSGEB loans and the Treasury-backed Credit Guarantee Fund guarantee facility (Chart 7). First of all, I would like to summarize the recent inflation developments. Then, I will talk about the domestic and international demand outlook that we base our forecasts on in the base scenario. Consumer inflation was 10.9 percent in June, a level consistent with our April Inflation Report forecast (Chart 9). Consumer inflation without processed food and non-alcoholic tobacco was slightly below forecasts as energy prices were more positive than forecast due to the decline in oil prices (Chart 10). The realization of consumer inflation close to the upper limit of forecasts was due to high increases in the price of unprocessed food. Figure 9. The first of these was the depreciation of the Turkish lira, which reached 25 percent on a basket basis, the second was the acceleration in food prices due to the effect of supply conditions, and the third was the increase in the price of oil. We found that consumer inflation, which approached 12 percent in April, slowed to a limited extent over the following two months (Chart 9). While oil prices have declined recently, the Turkish lira has appreciated somewhat after the high depreciation at the beginning of the year. Based on these developments, we see that energy inflation has decreased since March (Chart 11). With this outlook in the exchange rate, price increases in items such as durable goods slowed down. On the other hand, the delayed effects of the cumulative depreciation of the Turkish lira on inflation continued through clothing and non-durable (other) basic goods. Another prominent factor in the high inflation trend in the second quarter was food prices (Chart 11). Food inflation was mainly driven by the fresh fruit and vegetable group, with the impact of the lower base from last year. Although the pressures from producer prices in the second quarter of the year were partially weakened, they maintained their strong course with cumulative effects from the past period. In economic activity 7 With the strengthening of the recovery, the support of demand conditions to reduce inflation decreased as of the second quarter. The ongoing deterioration trend in medium-term inflation expectations has been replaced by a horizontal outlook. Under this outlook, we can say that the spread index and key inflation indicators indicate an improvement in the main trend of inflation. However, we should note that in this improvement in the main trend, the temporary effects of the method change in the weight system of the clothing group stand out, and when the method-induced effects are removed, the improvement in core inflation trends is more limited (Chart 12). Dear Guests, Economic activity was stronger in the first quarter of the year compared to the outlook set out in the April Inflation Report. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased by 5 percent annually in the first quarter of 2017; quarterly growth was 1.4 percent. Thus, while the recovery trend in economic activity continues (Chart 13), we see that the main drivers of the quarterly growth are exports, construction investments and public consumption, respectively. The weak course in machinery and equipment investments continued, and private consumption slowed down due to the demand pulled forward. The high contribution of net exports to growth in this period indicates a positive growth composition in terms of the current account balance (Chart 14). Figure 13. Fiscal policy, in addition to the measures and incentives put into practice, economic through public investment and consumption expenditures 8 supported growth. Thanks to macroprudential policies and public incentives, the revival in consumer loans and the improvement in consumer confidence indices indicate that consumption demand is strengthening. In the first half of 2017, the contribution of net exports to growth increased with the positive course in foreign demand conditions, especially in European Union countries. As you know, energy, import and food prices also play an important role in inflation forecasts. So, before we move on to the predictions, I will briefly convey our assumptions about the variables in question. We updated the 2017 average of crude oil price, which we assumed to be 55 USD in the April Inflation Report, to 50 USD within the framework of recent developments (Chart 17). We have raised our assumption of import prices in US dollars for 2017 (Chart 18). Food inflation, which rose in the second quarter of 2017, was 14.34 percent, slightly above our April Inflation Report projections. This rise in food inflation was largely due to the unprocessed food group. The current situation in food inflation and past food inflation realizations for the July-December periods indicate that the year-end food inflation assumption given in the April Inflation Report needs to be updated upwards. At this point, I would like to state that with the decision of the Council of Ministers in July 2017, we have reflected in the estimates of the Inflation Report that the increase foreseen within the framework of the automatic mechanism in the amount of excise duty on cigarettes and other tobacco products has not been made. 3. Inflation and Monetary Policy Outlook Dear Guests, I will now present to you our inflation and output gap estimates that we have produced within the framework I have drawn. The upward-updated output gap due to the improvement in the economic activity outlook had an effect on the 2017 year-end forecast by 0.2 points. Another factor influencing the forecasts was the update of food inflation forecasts for 2017 from 9 percent to 10 percent. The update added 0.2 percentage points to the 2017 year-end inflation forecast compared to the previous Report period. On the other hand, while the Turkish lira has been stable in the recent period, a significant decline has been observed in oil prices. Thus, despite the upward update to the assumption of import prices in US dollars, Turkish lira denominated import prices lowered the 2017 year-end inflation forecast by 0.1 percentage point. In addition, as a result of the absence of automatic tax increases on tobacco products, the impact of alcohol-tobacco products on year-end consumer inflation was 0.1 percentage point lowering, according to the previous Inflation Report estimate. The 2018 year-end inflation of the closing of the output gap was 0.1 percentage point. 11 We anticipate that the update in assumptions about Turkish lira denominated import prices will compensate for this effect. In addition to these forecasts I have mentioned, in the Risks and Monetary Policy section of the Inflation Report, we summarize the different risk assessments related to the macroeconomic outlook and monetary policy in general. You can find the details in the Report. Dear Guests, As I end my speech here, I would like to express my gratitude to all my colleagues and participants who contributed to the preparation of the Report, especially the members of the Monetary Policy Committee and the employees of our Research and Monetary Policy General Directorate. Thank you for listening. 12

text: 2017- IV INFLATION REPORT INFORMATION MEETING Murat Cetinkaya 1 November 2017, Istanbul Dear Guests, Welcome to the informative meeting where we will share the main messages of the last Inflation Report of 2017 with you. In this Report, by evaluating the macroeconomic developments in the last three months, we share with you our outlook and medium-term inflation forecasts for the Turkish economy, which form the basis of our monetary policy decisions. As you know, in addition to the main sections, the Inflation Reports also contain boxes where special issues related to different areas of the economy are examined in detail. For example, the first box introduces the balance sheet reduction program that the US Federal Reserve started to implement as of October and discusses the possible effects of the program. The second box analyzes the transitivity from producer prices to consumer prices. In addition, focusing on the real improvement in the current account deficit in Turkey in 2017; There are boxes that provide information about the new index, which is derived by expanding the country scope of the current unit labor cost-based real exchange rate index. In addition, there are studies examining the relationship between capacity utilization rates and machinery and equipment investments in the manufacturing industry and using the Bank Loans Trend Survey data to reveal the importance of the credit channel in the transmission of monetary policy in Turkey. Dear Guests, I will begin by referring to the global economic outlook, which continues to play an important role in our policies. In the recent period, the recovery in advanced economies has become evident and the ongoing upward trend in global trade volume pointed to a more positive growth performance in the global economy, albeit limitedly, compared to the previous Report period. In the current reporting period, although commodity and oil prices have risen slightly, global inflation remains moderate. However, in September, the U.S. Federal Reserve's emphasis on its determination in the normalization process led to a limited rise in market volatility and developed country bond yields (Chart 1).
