Dear Guests, We can say that 2017 was a difficult period in terms of inflation dynamics in general. After the significant shocks we experienced in 2016, a sharp movement in the exchange rate was observed with the deterioration of the global outlook in early 2017. At the same time, the significant movement in commodity prices led to an increase in cost pressures, resulting in a significant rise in inflation. As the Central Bank, we have made the necessary tightening to limit the upside risks related to pricing behavior. We also took important steps throughout the year in terms of increasing the predictability of monetary policy. In the recent period, we have further strengthened the cautious level of our monetary stance and increased the emphasis on determination. However, we have not yet seen the desired improvement in inflation due to delayed effects. In particular, the rapid credit expansion and other supportive policies that emerged during the year were the main factors that delayed and limited the effects of the tightening in monetary policy. The recent exchange rate volatility and the increase in oil prices may cause the rise in inflation to continue in the short term. However, with the contribution of the steps we have taken, we expect the process of decline in inflation to begin as of December. 11 When we look at 2018, we can say that many factors will contribute more positively to inflation compared to the current year. First of all, it should be emphasized that while creating our projections, we are based on a more moderate and converging economic activity for the coming period. As seen in the forecast chart just now, the output gap is expected to contribute downward to inflation from mid-2018. There is also a relatively positive outlook for assumptions about cost-side variables. We also expect a normalization in loans compared to last year. In this context, when inflation falls to single-digit levels in the coming months, the effects of monetary policy will be observed more clearly with the contribution of the expectation channel. Considering our determined and tight monetary stance, we anticipate that inflation will be close to 7 percent at the end of 2018, in line with the path to the target. In case of the risk of deviation from this path, we will take the necessary measures with all the tools at our disposal. Title: Interview with Reuters News Agency
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: President Naci Abal's Interview with Reuters News Agency 5 February 2021, Istanbul Since you took office, you have raised interest rates by 675 basis points. Foreign investors have had considerable inflows. The Turkish lira gained around 15%. How do you evaluate the first 3 months? Are you moving where you want to be? In the last three months, we have undergone a significant paradigm shift in the monetary policy approach and the stance of monetary policy. The steps we have taken and the additional steps we will take will reinforce this change and I hope that the confidence in monetary policy will increase even more. So far, we have acted within the framework of the principles of transparency, accountability and predictability in monetary policy, and we will continue to do so. As the Central Bank, it is our most important indispensable duty to ensure permanent price stability. In this respect, our most important priority is to stabilize at 5 percent in 2023 by gradually reducing inflation and to create a permanent price stability. We work day and night with our team for this purpose. We are aware that we are in a difficult process. With the steps we have taken and will take, we will continue to create and resolutely implement a monetary policy framework that will serve this purpose. We have clearly and clearly shared with the public that we will implement the reaction function of monetary policy under what conditions and on the basis of which strategic criteria and indicators. This has increased predictability and accountability in monetary policy. We will maintain monetary policy by 2023 with a tight stance, in other words, until we achieve the 5 percent target with a monetary policy set to a degree that will have a strong disinflationary effect. At the same time, the fact that the level reached has indicated permanent price stability is as important as achieving the target. Until the 5 percent target is reached, the level between the actual/expected inflation rate path and the monetary policy interest rate path will be established by observing a strong disinflationary balance and this balance will be maintained continuously. Why do we care about the continuation of the tight monetary policy stance for a long time? Because at an early stage, if you leave the tight monetary policy stance when you see inflation coming down for temporary reasons, past experience shows that inflation is moving upwards again. In this case, you can also lose your gains in the period when you apply tight monetary policy. Therefore, we will be patient until we meet the 5 percent target. We will implement the open inflation targeting regime that started in 2006 with all its elements in the coming period. With the decisions we will take and the strong communication we will make, we will move the pricing behaviors to the point we want in line with the aim of price stability by going in front of the market and managing expectations. As you know, we have ended the flexible monetary policy approach. We will act within the framework of simple monetary policy. The central bank's main funding instrument will continue to be the one-week repo rate, which is the policy rate. There will be no funding via the corridor method or through the late liquidity window. Thus, predictability and transparency in monetary policy will continue. Second, we are taking tight monetary policy steps taking into account the upside risks to the future that arise in the inflation outlook. Within this framework, we first increased the policy interest rate from 10.25 percent to 15 percent and then to 17 percent. Taking into account the risks that may arise on inflation, we can make additional tightening if necessary. In this context, we closely monitor many indicators such as the main trend of inflation and indicators related to pricing behavior, spread indices, demand and cost factors and the alignment of inflation expectations with targets within the forecast horizon. We will tighten further ahead if any new data points to the risk of deviation from the medium-term target path in inflation expectations and pricing behavior. The necessary response to risks in monetary policy allows you to manage inflationary pressures at an early stage. Past experience has shown that the economic costs of a delayed reaction can be more severe. In addition to fighting inflation, during this period; We have also taken important steps in the Central Bank's TL and foreign currency liquidity management. In order to ensure the healthy functioning of the monetary transmission mechanism and to limit the risks related to macrofinancial stability, mandatory reserves and other TL and foreign currency 2 we have taken decisions to use liquidity tools effectively. In terms of financial stability, we shared with the public our aim of strengthening the Central Bank's foreign exchange reserves and that we will use the tools for this in a transparent manner, within a certain plan and under appropriate conditions. Since November, the country's risk premium, exchange rate volatility and long-term interest rates have declined, and capital inflows have increased as positive expectations for Turkish lira assets have emerged. Money and credit indicators, which constitute risk factors on the financial system, also improved. The predictable decision framework we have established in monetary policy and our tight stance will contribute to the downward trend of inflation on the one hand and the reduction of the country's risk premium, the encouragement of Turkish lira savings, the initiation of reverse currency substitution, the upward trend of foreign exchange reserves and the permanent decline in financing costs. How long will interest rates stay that high? What factors lead to a rate hike or a cut, can you explain your reaction mechanism a little bit? Are you ready, for example, to keep the policy rate at 17% when inflation starts to fall, as predictably in May? We are far from our medium-term inflation target of 5 percent. The forecasts we present in the January Inflation Report show that we can reach this target in 2023. Therefore, the tight and prudent stance in monetary policy needs to be resolutely maintained for a long time until 2023, when the 5 percent target is expected to be reached. Upside risks remain important on our inflation forecast path for this year. As a matter of fact, both CPI and PPI realizations for January show that the cumulative reflections of the exchange rate on inflation, the ongoing increases in international commodity prices, the strong upward trend in producer prices and supply constraints remain important. Our Monetary Policy Board will assess whether these effects on the inflationary outlook indicate the risk of deviation from the medium-term forecast target path we established in the January Inflation Report. Considering the fact that the upside risks we foresee in the near term on the inflation path will remain important and the expected slope of the path, it does not seem possible to put the interest rate cut on the agenda for a long time this year. In this respect, it is extremely important that monetary policy shows a strong disinflationary effect through the transmission mechanism and that the tightening in financial conditions reveals a generally strong downward outlook on demand-driven inflationary pressure through the expectation channel. At this point, I would like to emphasize that we want to see a "permanent" decrease in inflation, but not only that, there should also be indicators pointing to price stability. In this context, we will closely monitor the main trend of inflation and the alignment of indicators of pricing behavior, spread indices, demand and cost factors and inflation expectations with the targets within the forecast horizon. At a time when world economies are breaking records in interest rate cuts and supports during the pandemic, Turkey is implementing a tight monetary policy. What purpose do you have? Is this difference normal? In line with the widespread practice around the world, the Central Bank displayed an important supportive stance during the pandemic period. In addition to the interest rate cuts and targeted liquidity opportunities provided to the banking sector, the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency's Asset Ratio regulation, which directs banks to extend loans and buy securities, clarified the expansionary macro policy stance. The rapid expansion provided in a short time by monetary policy and financial policies in loans and monetary magnitudes supported the rapid recovery in economic activity. 3 On the other hand, it adversely affected the current account balance, external financing opportunities and the inflation outlook. The point that should not be overlooked here is that we have entered the pandemic period with an inflation rate far above our medium-term target. While the focus was on policies to reduce the effects of the epidemic, the assessment that the predicted weakening of total demand due to the epidemic would have a reducing effect on inflation was dominant. However, in 2020, the demand-side effects due to the strong credit momentum were decisive on inflation through direct and indirect channels. Inflationary pressures increased in groups where demand conditions remained strong. In addition, the rapid recovery provided by credit expansion created a negative cycle between reserves, risk premium, dollarization and inflation expectations, and played an important role in the rise in inflation through the exchange rate. At this point, it is obvious that in order to eliminate the risks related to the inflation outlook, to control inflation expectations and to re-establish the disinflation process as soon as possible, a strong monetary tightening is required and this must continue for a long time until the permanent price stability target is achieved. In the last Inflation Report, you made a tight monetary policy discourse that would postpone the market's interest rate cut expectations. Can you elaborate on that? Many central bank governors have set low single-digit inflation targets when they take office. But the result was double-digit or near-double digit inflation. How will you make your difference? As I stated at the beginning of my speech, we have made a fundamental change in the framework of monetary policy and in our monetary policy stance. We have established an open, simple, predictable and transparent monetary policy framework. We want to create a medium-term purpose function rather than a short-term purpose function to ensure that expectations are formed around this goal. In the medium term, we have set as an anchor the uninterrupted implementation of tight monetary policy until the 5 percent target is reached. This framework and target anchor will lead us to price stability. Domestic demand conditions, international commodity prices, supply constraints evident in some sectors, wages and managed price adjustments continue to pose risks to the medium-term inflation outlook. We expect the delayed effects of the slowdown in loans to become evident in the coming period. In addition, due to supply-side inflationary factors, which are very effective in the short term, we expect annual inflation to remain upward for a certain period of time within the path we foresee. We think that the minimum wage will create additional inflation rigidity, especially through service prices. This requires that the tight stance on monetary policy be maintained for a longer period of time compared to past forecasts. Tight monetary stance; It will serve as an important buffer against external and temporary volatilities in the context of inflation expectations, pricing behaviors and financial market developments. In many developed and developing countries, we see that highly predictable monetary policy within the framework of inflation targeting or similar price stability is successful in controlling inflation. Likewise, in our country, we have been able to achieve success in combating inflation in periods when monetary policy was established decisively and patiently with a focus on price stability. On the other hand, during periods when inflationary pressures increase, when the reaction is delayed, monetary tightening is then made at a higher cost, or periods in which the inflation outlook improves quickly and early and then turns into rising inflation. In the light of these experiences, we will resolutely maintain our tight and prudent stance in monetary policy not only to reach the 2021 year-end forecast target, but also to reach our medium-term inflation target of 5 percent in 2023. 4 In this context, market expectations are that interest rate cuts will begin, albeit limited between 3-6 months of maturity. Markets expect year-end inflation of 11-12% and are drawing a scenario in which interest rate cuts will be started by Q3, albeit limited. Is the market pricing you right? As we shared in the January Inflation Report, we anticipate that wages, food prices and international commodity prices inflation will be upwards, while managed/directed prices and inflation expectations will affect inflation downwards in the forecast path we have announced for 2021. In this context, as a result of the tight monetary stance, we anticipate that inflation will decrease to 9.4 percent at the end of 2021. However, upside risks to these forecasts remain markedly significant. Therefore, the tight monetary policy stance must be resolutely maintained for a long time. Many different factors play a role in market pricing. Inflation expectations and the inflation uncertainty contained in these expectations are at the top of these factors. Dier taraftan, enflasyon basklarnn artt dnemlerde tepki verilmesinin geciktii dnemlerde sonradan daha yksek maliyetle parasal sklamaya gidildii veya enflasyon grnmnn iyilemesinden hzl ve erken ekilde gevemenin de sonrasnda tekrar ykselen enflasyon eklinde dnd dnemler de tecrbelerimiz arasnda yer alyor. Bu tecrbeler nda, para politikasndaki sk ve ihtiyatl duruumuzu yalnzca 2021 ylsonu tahmin hedefine ulaacak ekilde deil, orta vadeli enflasyon hedefimiz olan yzde 5e 2023 ylnda varacak ekilde kararllkla srdreceiz. 4 Bu kapsamda piyasa beklentileri 3-6 ay vade arasnda snrl da olsa faiz indirimlerinin balayaca eklinde. Piyasalar %11-12 arasnda ylsonu enflasyonu bekliyor ki ve 3. eyrek itibaryla faiz indirimlerine snrl da olsa balanaca bir senaryo iziyor. Piyasa sizi doru mu fiyatlyor? Ocak Enflasyon Raporunda paylatmz zere, 2021 yl iin akladmz tahmin patikasnda cretler, gda fiyatlar ve uluslararas emtia fiyatlar enflasyonu yukar ynl, ynetilen/ynlendirilen fiyatlar ile enflasyon beklentilerinin ise enflasyonu aa ynl etkilemesini ngryoruz. Bu erevede sk parasal duru sonucunda 2021 yl sonunda enflasyonun yzde 9,4 dzeyine gerileyeceini ngryoruz. Ancak, bu tahminler zerinde yukar ynl riskler belirgin bir ekilde nemini koruyor. Bu nedenle, sk para politikas duruunun kararllkla uzun bir mddet srdrlmesi gerekli. Piyasa fiyatlamalarnda birok farkl etken rol oynuyor. Enflasyon beklentileri ve bu beklentilerin ierdii enflasyon belirsizlii bu etkenler arasnda ba ekiyor. Yukar ynl risklerin varln kabul ediyoruz ve bu risklerin gereklemesi durumunda ilave sklamaya gidip bunlarn enflasyon grnm zerindeki etkisini azaltacaz. Dolaysyla, bu kararllmz piyasa tarafndan teyit edildike enflasyon beklentileri yl sonu tahmin hedefimize yaknsayacaktr. Faiz indirim srecinin zamanlamas, enflasyon gereklemelerinin ve orta vadeli grnm ngrlerimizin Enflasyon Raporunda ngrdmz patikayla uyumlu ekilde gereklemesine bal olacak. Politika faizini her halkrda yalnzca 2021 hedefine deil, orta vadeli enflasyon hedefine de ngrlen srede ulamay salayacak bir dzeyde tutmaya devam edeceiz. Enflasyon ile faiz arasnda denge gzeteceiz ama matematiksel hesap yapmayn eklinde alglanan aklamalarnz olmutu. Bu denge ne olacak? Reel faiz oran m belirlediniz? Ortaya konan para politikas duruu ve faiz seviyesine ilikin bir referans verilemez, yanl olur. nk o andaki enflasyon grnmnn ortaya kard koullar dezenflasyonist etkiyi meydana getirmek iin daha yksek seviyelerde bir duru sergilemenizi zorunlu klabilir. Dolaysyla para politikas duruunu genel olarak kabul edilmi bir referans zerinden konumlandrmak ve piyasa ile iletiimi bunun zerinden kurmak doru olmayacaktr. Merkez Bankas enflasyon grnmn, gelecee ilikin tahminlerini ve enflasyona etki eden faktrleri teker teker deerlendirecek. Yapt deerlendirmelere gre hangi dzeyde bir para politikas faiz orannn bu bask unsurlarn telafi edecek kadar gl etki yapacan belirleyecek. Bunu belirlerken ayn zamanda enflasyon grnm yannda finansal riskleri de hesaba katarak risk oluturan faktrlerin de dengelenmesini salayacak seviyede bir politika faizi oluturacak ve bunu srdrecek. zetle, politika faizi, gerekleen ve beklenen enflasyonun zerinde bir seviyede olacak ama bu iki seviye arasndaki aralk enflasyonist basklarn yaygnlna, younluuna, para politikas tepkisine duyarl olup olmadna bal olacak. Ayrca finansal risk gstergelerinin de iyilemesine reaksiyon gsterecek, tepki verecek. Merkez Bankas kendi bilgisiyle, yaklamyla gerekleen, beklenen enflasyonla politika faizi arasndaki araln seviyesini oluturacak. Bu seviyenin %5 hedefine varncaya kadar dezenflasyonist bir aralkta olmas konusunda zel bir dikkat gsterecek. Hibir zaman iin %5 hedefine ulamadan bir ara dnemde geici nedenlerle sreklilik arz etmeyen faktrlerle hareket ederek bu dezenflasyonist aralktan vazgemeyecek. Bu son derece nemli bir yaklam. %5 fiyat istikrar hedefi bizim iin bir pa. Ona varrken para politikasnn duruuna ilikin oluturduumuz bu referans aral piyasayla srekli ve gl bir iletiim kurarak 5 neden o seviyede tuttuumuzu aklayacaz. Para politikas, aktarm mekanizmas zerinden gerekli etkiyi douruyor ve enflasyon eilimleri Merkez Bankasnn ngrd patika dahilinde ilerliyorsa demektir ki politika faizi dzeyi gerekleen ve beklenen enflasyona gre etkili bir basklama yapabiliyor. Bunu her PPKda piyasayla gl bir etkileim ierisinde paylamaya devam edeceiz. Merkez Bankas hala dier merkez bankalaryla swap anlamas yapmaya alyor mu? Bildiiniz gibi 11. Kalknma Planmzda uluslararas ticarette milli para birimlerinin kullanmnn yaygnlatrlmasna ilikin bir hedef yer alyor. Swap anlamalar da yerel paralarla ticaretin gelitirilmesi konusunda kullanlan destekleyici mekanizmalardan bir tanesi. Bu hedef dorultusunda, lkemiz iin ekonomik, ticari ve stratejik adan nem arz eden baz lkelerin merkez bankalaryla swap anlamalar yapld ve snrl tutarda da olsa kullanmlarn olduu gzlenmektedir. Sz konusu swap anlamalar Merkez Bankas rezervleri zerinde de dolayl olarak artrc ynde bir etki yapmaktadr. Title: Speech of Chairman Murat etinkaya at the Istanbul Finance Summit on 6-7 September 2016
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: ISTANBUL FINANCE SUMMIT Murat 82etinkaya 6 September 2016, Istanbul Dear Guests, First of all, I would like to thank the organizers of this important platform, the Istanbul Finance Summit, and express my satisfaction for being here. After touching upon global developments in my speech and their reflections on central banking, I will try to share with you some of my views on price stability and structural issues. Dear Guests, The global crisis has caused many game breakdowns in the field of economy and finance. Central banks have designed and implemented unprecedented policy instruments in a way that has never been seen in history. However, almost eight years after the implementation of these policies, the speed of the recovery in the global economy and the fragility of the economies are still a matter of debate. In such an environment, we see that the limits of monetary policies are increasingly being pushed. The historical process has repeatedly shown that problems that are inherently structural cannot be solved by non-structural means. As a matter of fact, the failure to support the monetary measures taken during the global crisis period with strong structural reforms brings with it the risk of blockage of the transmission mechanisms. Central banks seem to have stayed in the game longer than they would have liked, with some abstention. It is not easy to predict the next stages. It is likely that central banks will continue to use the tools at their disposal to the fullest. However, it is now very clear that the structural problems accumulating on a global scale cannot be solved by monetary policies. It is imperative that all stakeholders responsible for the economy make a joint effort with a holistic approach. While all these accumulated issues remain important, the global economy is facing new shocks in the background. In particular, geopolitical risks have become very important in terms of trust factor. The fragile course of the global economy can turn into a self-sustaining vicious circle by interacting with geopolitical risks from time to time. In such an environment, we see that the volatility in global markets continues. 2 In this process, the countries that can keep their economic foundations intact will be the countries that overcome the turmoil with the least damage. At this point, despite the various shocks experienced in recent years, we can say that the Turkish economy has followed a very resilient course with its strong banking system, prudent fiscal policy and a risk-oriented monetary policy approach. I find it useful to emphasize that increasing coordination in the economy and structural adjustment efforts in all dimensions are very important in this context. Dear Guests, I talked about the importance of economic foundations. I think that a critical aspect of this issue is to increase the predictability and persuasiveness of economic policies. Therefore, today I would like to share with you our view of some important issues in order to contribute to this dimension from the perspective of the central bank. First of all, I will touch on the concept of financial conditions. This is an issue that is extremely important, but not emphasized enough by economic units. In the pre-global crisis period, the idea prevailed that the short-term interest rate set by central banks largely reflected monetary and financial conditions. In the period following the global crisis, we see that the indicators of the monetary policy stance have gained a multidimensional character. The new picture that emerged after the crisis indicates that when considering central bank policies, all kinds of developments that affect the general financial conditions in the economy should be evaluated together. In other words, the view that it is healthier to make a communication not only over a single rate but also through general monetary and financial conditions prevails. Today, we see that the extraordinary balance sheet movements of central banks and the regulations on financial institutions on a global scale have serious effects on monetary and financial conditions. More importantly, in a world where the global financial system is so integrated, we see that domestic policies are not always sufficient to explain general financial conditions. Financial conditions can be affected by many factors outside of monetary policy. For example, we know that global liquidity plays a very important role. In recent studies, it is seen that the most important determinant of the long-term interest rates of developing countries is the global long-term interest rates. Therefore, for developing countries, global long-term interest rates are as low as whether the central banks of developed countries will raise interest rates in the short term. 3 I think it is worth noting that the issue of whether it will remain at the levels or not may be more important. In such an environment, it would not be healthy to carry out the discussions on the financial transmission mechanism through the short-term interest rates of the central banks. If we take the example of Turkey, many indicators of financial markets point to financial tightness. For example, in an economy such as Turkey, where financial intermediation is carried out mainly through banks, credit growth rates give an idea on this issue. In addition to the growth rate of total loans, the distribution of loans is also an indicator that should be carefully monitored. Other elements that are among the conditions for financial consumers' access to credit are also important. As a result, in the current conjuncture, it is important to take into account the big picture, which includes general financial conditions as well as the interest level of the central bank or general financing costs. More importantly, it should not be overlooked that central banks, as stability-oriented institutions, act in a way that balances financial cycles, not magnifies them. Dear Guests, We look at financial conditions not from a quantitative point of view, but from a qualitative perspective, that is, from a qualitative perspective. From the point of view of the credit market, I can say that we attach importance to three issues: The first is that all segments of the society receive a balanced share from the credit growth, the second is that loans are given at reasonable conditions and pricing, and the third is that they are distributed efficiently. We assess that a credit growth of this structure, which also provides moderate financial deepening, is healthy and sustainable. We also adopt this approach in terms of the effective functioning of the monetary transmission mechanism. The transmission mechanism needs to work not only in good periods but also in times of slowdown in the economy. Because the fact that financial intermediaries continue to carry out their functions in a healthy way during periods when the economy slows down allows monetary policy to soften cyclical fluctuations by following an anti-cyclical policy. 4 Undoubtedly, the softening of financial cycles is also of a structural nature. After the global crisis, this issue has been frequently discussed in international platforms and continues to be discussed. In the discussions here, the importance of the correct creation of the business model and incentive mechanisms of the financial sector should be mentioned as well as the development of anti-cyclic structural tools. As the central bank, we also attach importance to the structuring of the banking system and the general financial architecture in a way that softens the financial cycles. Maximizing the efficiency of the financial system will both support social welfare and expand the field of action of economic policies. In summary, the qualitative development of the credit market is important for us. As long as the monetary transmission mechanism operates healthily and there is no threat to price stability from the financial system, we can consider credit growth rates as reasonable. We find it useful to clarify this issue in this way. Dear guests, In terms of the planning of economic units, especially medium and long-term interest rates are important. In addition to structural factors such as the savings rate, the stance of central banks is also decisive on long-term interest rates. So what is the duty of the central bank to reduce long-term interest rates, which are the most important interest rates in terms of investments? We can put the answer to this very clearly: to ensure and maintain price stability. A structure where inflation is low and stable will provide a favorable environment for deposit and loan rates to be reduced to lower levels and for their maturities to be extended. There is a consensus in the literature on the long-term benefits of price stability to the economy. Accordingly, the permanent stabilization of price stability increases predictability in the economy; growth, investments and employment are also positively affected. Therefore, it is critical to understand the contribution of price stability to prosperity and the importance of fighting inflation. This issue can be looked at from different dimensions. If we look at it from the point of view of individuals who work, consume and save in the economy, we can say that inflation reduces the purchasing power of fixed income earners. When we look at it from the point of view of the companies sector, we know that inflation uncertainty can adversely affect investment appetite by making it difficult to see ahead. 5 There is a similar inefficiency for banks and other financial institutions. In situations where inflation and inflation uncertainty are high, banks are more reluctant to meet the long-term credit demands of firms, which is one of the major obstacles to the development of productive capacity. In addition, fluctuations in inflation can adversely affect the capital structures of banks. As a result, the direct contribution of price stability to social welfare in the medium and long term is quite clearly demonstrated in the economic literature. All these effects can increase trade-offs by narrowing the field of action of economic policies. Therefore, it is necessary to emphasize the critical role of price stability in terms of the fundamentals of the economy and its importance for the well-being of the country in the long term. In summary, it is obvious that price stability is a public value and we need to strive to achieve this goal. So, how can we achieve the goal of price stability? First, let's talk about the role of monetary policy in price stability. The Central Bank has been defined as the main institution responsible for price stability in Turkey. In this context, the construction of monetary policy for price stability and the credibility of the strategy applied in the eyes of economic units is an indispensable prerequisite for the fight against inflation. Therefore, we, as an institution, will continue to use all the tools at our disposal for price stability by strengthening communication in the new period. However, it is worth emphasizing that it may be costly to achieve price stability with only monetary policy tools at this point. The experience we have gained in the process of inflation targeting over the last decade tells us that we need to make additional efforts in some areas in order to achieve price stability permanently and at a lower cost. The first of these issues is the coordinated and joint efforts of economic units to manage cyclical fluctuations, and the second is to make progress on structural issues that increase inflation rigidity and reduce the effectiveness of the monetary policy transmission mechanism. Past experience has shown that structural factors play an important role in price stability. The course of food prices is an important example of this. In the last 10 years in our country, we see that food prices have increased faster than in other countries and their volatility is relatively much higher. On this topic 6 You can reach our detailed technical determinations in the recent period from the studies and reports on our website. Food prices are not an issue that can be solved only through monetary policy tools. Controlling food prices through interest rate policy can lead to undesirable fluctuations in the economy. Therefore, it is important to develop a systematic, structural and long-term perspective on food prices in the coming period, and the studies carried out within the scope of the Food and Agricultural Products Monitoring and Evaluation Committee (Food Committee for short), which has been established with the participation of relevant institutions in recent years, constitute a valuable example of making joint efforts on structural issues. Significant gains were made under the Food Committee. First of all, a public awareness was created that the upward trend and volatility of food prices pose a risk to price stability and that this situation should be controlled. Inter-institutional communication channels were opened and a broad-based cooperation was established. Detailed due diligence was made on the causes of general and product-based price movements, structural problems were listed. Information and data sharing was ensured with the coming together of all stakeholders. And finally, a discussion platform was created on which institutions can make what kind of policy interventions in order to solve the structural problems identified. Are all these gains enough? In the coming period, we assess that the deepening of these studies and communication within the framework of a result-oriented and rule-based mechanism will make significant contributions to price stability. Similarly, there are many important areas in the economy that can contribute to price stability in a structural sense. For example, we assess that the issue of savings rates is very important. In this context, I would like to emphasize that important steps have been taken recently to increase savings rates. Automatic participation in the private pension system is perhaps the most important of these measures. We also assess that other savings incentives and demographic change given by the public may alleviate the problem in the coming period. However, we cannot say that our savings problem has been solved yet. Therefore, as the central bank, one of the important items of our research agenda in the coming period will be to examine this issue in depth. 7 The following questions inevitably come to mind here: What can be the contribution of the central bank, which does not have a direct instrument in structural matters, to these issues? Would it be a more appropriate option for monetary authority to focus solely on its area of responsibility? All of these questions are debatable, but I think it is useful to make a reminder at this point. First, the structural issues we focus on are directly related to price stability. Secondly, the Central Bank is also obliged by law to act as an advisor to the Government in economic fields. Therefore, in line with this duty, we assess that it will be beneficial under all circumstances to conduct qualified research on structural issues in the economy and bring them to the attention of stakeholders. Here, we aim to contribute to taking structural steps to support price stability by increasing social awareness and developing concrete proposals on specific issues. In this respect, we aim to be a more active and solution-oriented institution in structural issues in the new period. We think that the human capital we have imposes such a responsibility on us. Here it is worth highlighting an important point. In the new period, it is important to know that we will continue to actively use our own tools with an appropriate combination while referring to structural issues. We will continue to take steps to make our monetary policy framework even stronger within an effective communication strategy. As a matter of fact, the steps we have taken recently to simplify monetary policy and strengthen the transmission mechanism should be seen as stages of creating a more effective monetary policy framework. However, we also know that taking steps to support price stability in some structural issues at this point will support achieving price stability by opening an important area in economic policies. That is why we feel the need to emphasize the importance of coordination and joint efforts in the economy at every opportunity. Dear Guests, I started my speech with the global financial crisis and geopolitical risks, but as a central banker, I ended with inflation again. Why did I give a speech focused on inflation when there are so many different scale problems on a global and geopolitical scale? 8 The main reason for this is the role of high and volatile inflation that makes it difficult to cope with all these risks. No matter how harsh the waves are outside, we can remain resilient as long as our own foundations are strong. The world economy continues to pass serious tests, and developing countries need to continue to consolidate their economic foundations to overcome this process without permanent damage. Therefore, as the Central Bank, we will focus on price stability in order to strengthen economic fundamentals in the coming period. In this direction, we will continue to make every effort to increase the welfare of our country. We will be patient and determined on this path. We will strive to create lasting solutions and reduce trade-offs in communication with stakeholders. Raising awareness of the importance of price stability for economic stability and the benefits it will provide to all economic actors will be one of our main priorities. Despite all the difficulties experienced, we have full confidence that Turkey will be positively differentiated in the medium and long term. In closing, I would like to congratulate everyone who contributed to the organization of this important conference. Thanks for listening, regards... 9

Title: Speech Titled "Macroeconomic Outlook and Price Stability"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: MACROECONOMIC OUTLOOK AND PRICE STABILITY Murat cetinkaya 8 March 2017, Denizli Mr. President, Dear Participants, Dear Members of the Press; As the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, I would like to start by expressing our satisfaction with being in Denizli within the scope of our meetings with the real sector. Thank you for your close attention and hospitality. In my speech today, after touching on the economic outlook in general, I will talk about our monetary policy implementations. I will then summarize our strategy to ensure price stability and some of the steps we have taken recently to achieve this goal permanently. 1. Economic Outlook and Monetary Policy First of all, I would like to start with the global conjuncture. Although ten years have passed since the global crisis in 2007, the global economy has still not achieved a stable outlook. Despite the extraordinary monetary measures taken, the low growth environment on a global scale and the questioning of traditional approaches that have dominated economic policies in recent history cause uncertainty about economic policies to remain high. This process, along with increasing protectionist trends, weak global trade and geopolitical risks, leads to the postponement of new investments, limiting the growth potential of the global economy. In such a conjuncture, the capacity of countries to take steps to strengthen their economic foundations becomes even more important. Chart 1. While a significant slowdown in economic activity emerged as a result of the shocks, inflationary pressures arising from the depreciation of the exchange rate in the near term and the risk of deterioration in the medium-term outlook were observed. In this context, while designing the policy steps, we aimed to alleviate cost-side inflationary pressures from the exchange rate without creating additional tightness on financial conditions. A Holistic Approach to Price Stability Dear Participants, Our goal is for inflation to remain at consistently low levels. Monetary policy is shaped in this direction. However, past experience within the framework of different policy approaches indicates that the fight against inflation should be supported by a holistic effort and a structural approach for a permanent solution. In order to minimize trade-offs and achieve permanent results, it is of great importance that the relevant institutions and stakeholders in the economy contribute to the process. In terms of joint effort and holistic approach strategy, the work of the Food Committee sets a valuable example. The aim of the Food Committee can be summarized as closely monitoring the main factors affecting supply and price formation in the food market, developing and implementing measures to support price stability and increase predictability in inflation. Significant gains have been made from the work to date. A high level of public awareness has been created in all segments of public opinion about food inflation and the effects of food prices on overall inflation. A solution-oriented cooperation process developed between stakeholders and the Committee's work began to bear fruit. We expect the positive effects of the steps taken to be felt more and more prominently. In the coming period, we will take the necessary steps to expand and implement the joint institutional effort exhibited in the Food Committee in other structural areas related to price stability. In this context, we evaluate the studies on the indebtedness of the real sector in foreign currency in the context of structural areas where progress can be made. These factors ensure that the cash flows of our companies are less affected by exchange rate fluctuations. However, the ability to monitor the foreign currency position of our companies more comprehensively is important in terms of risk perception, financial stability and price stability towards our country in the long term. In this process, it will be beneficial for companies to maintain the link between foreign exchange income and foreign exchange and borrowing and to use financial instruments and natural protection that will limit exchange rate risk. From a more holistic perspective, it is necessary to emphasize that all structural measures to improve the external balance are critical in order to increase the resilience of the economy against external financing and exchange rate shocks. Issues such as increasing domestic savings, supporting productivity and added value in production, reducing dependence on imported inputs are of great importance. Dear Participants, I mentioned the importance of supporting efforts on structural issues in monetary policy with a holistic approach in order to achieve price stability permanently. In this context, in recent years, we have sought to strengthen our efforts to closely monitor and understand the real sector. As the Central Bank, we regularly visit companies in different cities of our country in order to follow the current developments in the economy and strengthen our communication network with the real sector. In this direction, on the one hand, evaluations of the activities and expectations of the companies are reported, and on the other hand, structural problems are tried to be identified. The results obtained from the talks constitute an important source of information about the Turkish economy for us. For example, communication with the real sector is extremely useful in terms of having timely information about the investment, production, export, employment and borrowing decisions of the real sector or understanding the effects of any regulations that concern the sector of firms. In the next stage, we aim to share the information and inferences we have obtained from these interviews directly with decision-makers and the public and contribute to the transformation of these findings into more concrete policies. In this context, we plan to regularly share the evaluations we have obtained from our meetings with the real sector with the public in the near future. I would like to take this opportunity to thank all our companies that did not spare their valuable ideas and suggestions by meeting with us. I hope that this cooperation will become stronger in the coming period. 10 As the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, we will continue to strive to better understand the dynamics of the real sector. We consider this interaction as an important component of our strategy to achieve price stability permanently. Dear Participants, In recent years, our country's economy has shown significant resilience in the face of shocks of different nature. The contraction experienced in the third quarter of 2016 was not permanent and the economy again entered a moderate recovery trend. Likewise, the increase in inflation and current account deficit in the near term is expected to reverse in the coming months. The coordinated and strong policy response of the Central Bank and public authorities, as well as the dynamism and resilience of our real sector, constitute the basic components of this resilience. As we go through a period of low predictability on a global scale, our most important task is to maintain the main focus and move forward in line with the basic objectives. If the policies implemented in coordination in the economy are supported by structural arrangements, our resilience will increase even more. Whatever the circumstances, as long as steps are taken to consolidate economic foundations, the influence of external factors will remain temporary. The main support that the Central Bank can give to our country's economic resilience and sustainable growth in this process is to increase predictability by maintaining its price stability-oriented approach. Price stability is important for our companies to see ahead better while making their contracts and plans and to access financing on favorable terms. Within this framework, we believe that we will gradually advance to our goal. As I conclude my speech here, I would like to thank you once again for your interest and offer my respects. 11

text: CBRT 83rd ORDINARY GENERAL ASSEMBLY MEETING Erdem BAcI President 09 April 2015, Ankara Dear Shareholders of our Bank, Distinguished Guests, Distinguished Members of the Press, 83rd Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey Welcome to the Ordinary General Assembly. Before proceeding to the agenda items to be discussed in the General Assembly, I would like to summarize the important economic developments we are experiencing in the world and in Turkey and give information about the monetary policy we are implementing. First of all, starting with the inflation developments, I will make an assessment of the developments in economic activity and the balancing process. In the light of these developments, I will try to summarize how monetary and financial conditions were shaped in 2014. When we evaluate the years after the difficulties experienced by the Turkish economy in 2001 in terms of fighting inflation and price stability, it would be appropriate to say that our economy is in the process of falling inflation (Chart 1). I would like to remind you that consumer price inflation has declined from 73 percent in January 2002 to 6.2 percent at the end of 2012, the lowest level in the last 44 years. Figure 1. In line with the international findings in the academic literature, we have seen that the permanently low inflation rate has a positive effect on growth in the Turkish economy. As a matter of fact, with the reforms carried out in many areas, especially in the finance, financial sector and monetary policies, and the fiscal discipline maintained, the relative per capita real income in Turkey increased significantly during the period of falling inflation (Chart 2). 2 If we take a closer look at the developments in inflation over the past two years, we see that the inflation rate at the end of the year remains above the target of 5 percent. Since the end of 2013, excessive movements in the exchange rate and the increase in volatility in financial markets have adversely affected the inflation outlook and macro-financial stability. Therefore, as you know, as the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey (CBRT), we underwent a strong and front-loading monetary tightening in monetary policy on 28 January 2014 in order to control the deterioration in the inflation outlook and to support financial stability. We have started to see the results of this policy from the second half of last year. We can clearly see that cautious monetary and fiscal policies and macroprudential measures have positively affected the core inflation indicators (Chart 3). Chart 3. Despite the positive outlook for core inflation indicators, inflation expectations have not yet reached the desired levels (Chart 4). The rise in headline inflation since the end of 2013 has also led to a deterioration in inflation expectations. As a result of the measures taken, we believe that the corrective effect of the positive outlook on inflation expectations in the main trend of inflation is limited by the increases in food prices. When we make a detailed evaluation of the recent price developments, it is possible to say that the high course and volatility in food prices due to the drought and other adverse weather conditions observed in 2014 have adversely affected CPI inflation (Chart 5 and Graph 6). On the graph on the left, there is a gap between food inflation and non-food inflation in the last two years. 3 I would like to draw your attention to how obvious the difference we have observed is. Therefore, we consider the launch of the "Food and Agricultural Product Markets Monitoring and Evaluation Committee", in which the CBRT is represented at the highest level, in December 2014 as a very important step in terms of enabling the developments in food prices to be discussed on a common platform and necessary measures to be taken. In the coming period, in addition to the passing of the negative effects of weather conditions in 2014, we believe that the measures to be taken by the Food Committee will contribute to the reduction of food inflation (Chart 7). When we evaluate the general trend in economic activity, we see that Gross Domestic Product (GDP) exhibits a moderate upward trend (Chart 8). In general terms, it is possible to say that global growth rates continue to be weak and that domestic demand contributes to growth at a moderate level. When we look at the separation of country groups, we see that growth rates in developing countries have entered a process of decline after the rapid recovery period after the global crisis. It is observed that the slowdown in growth rates in developing countries other than China and India has become more pronounced in the past year and is approaching the growth rates of developed countries (Chart 9). On the opportunities side 9 When we look at it, we see two main elements: first, commodity prices, which are low; the second is the long-term interest rates, which are also low. One of the lessons that the global crisis has reminded us of is that coordinating macroeconomic and financial policies is crucial to supporting sustainable economic growth. It is well known by policymakers today that economic decisions taken independently of each other by different economic units such as households, firms and the financial sector can lead to the accumulation of macro-financial risks when evaluated as macro. From this point of view, the Financial Stability Committee established in our country in 2011 has met an important need. As you know, the Financial Stability Committee, under the chairmanship of the Minister to whom the Undersecretariat of the Treasury is affiliated, consists of the Undersecretary of the Treasury, the President of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, the Chairman of the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency, the Chairman of the Capital Markets Board and the Chairman of the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund. The main task of the Financial Stability Committee can be summarized as identifying and monitoring the systemic risks that may affect the financial system as a whole and determining the necessary measures and policy recommendations to reduce such risks. Information shall be provided to the Council of Ministers by the Minister on the results of the meetings of the Committee and the decisions taken by the Committee. In this context, the Council of Ministers is authorized to determine the measures to be taken, and all relevant institutions and organizations are authorized and responsible for implementing these measures immediately. The Financial Stability Committee closely monitors the issues of preventing excessive borrowing by the private sector in the Turkish economy and improving the quality of financing. The macroprudential policies put into practice in recent years have been successful in reducing the credit expansion rate to sustainable levels and have also played an important role in transforming the composition of credit into an incentive to production rather than consumption. text: CBRT 84th ORDINARY GENERAL ASSEMBLY MEETING Erdem Ba?8df5 President 11 April 2016 Ankara Dear Shareholders of our Bank, Dear Guests, Dear Members of the Press, The 84th Anniversary of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey. Welcome to the Ordinary General Assembly. Before moving on to the agenda items to be discussed in the General Assembly, I would like to give information about inflation and the monetary policy we are implementing. First, I will make an overview of the monetary indicators and inflation relationship, the balancing process and growth developments. In this context, I will try to summarize how monetary and financial conditions were shaped in 2015, the measures taken during the year and the results of these measures. Since 2002, Turkey has switched to an implicit inflation targeting regime and there has been a significant decline in inflation. Since 2006, the open inflation targeting regime has been implemented and inflation has been permanently reduced to single digit levels. With the contribution of inflation targeting regime and fiscal discipline, inflation has been brought under control, but the desired low single-digit levels have not yet been reached. Consumer price inflation fell from 73 percent in January 2002 to 6.2 percent at the end of 2012, the lowest level in 45 years. Inflation completed 2015 at 8.81 percent and decreased to 7.46 percent as of March 2016 (Chart 1). In line with international findings in the academic literature, we observe that the persistently low inflation has a positive impact on economic growth in the Turkish economy. As a matter of fact, with the reforms carried out in many areas, especially in finance, monetary and financial sector policies, and the fiscal discipline maintained, real income per capita in Turkey increased significantly compared to EU countries during the falling inflation period (Chart 2). 1 Figure 1. We can say that inflation is in a downward trend, albeit slowly. However, as seen in the chart, inflation follows a very volatile course (Chart 3). Figure 3. One of them is the volatility in food prices, and the other is the volatility in monetary indicators. If we talk about the measures taken regarding food prices, the "Food and Agricultural Product Markets Monitoring and Evaluation Committee" was put into operation in December 2014. It is considered that the measures taken under the coordination of this committee provide structural and cyclical contributions to reduce food inflation. As a matter of fact, measures were taken by the Ministries for some food products during the year with the proposal of the Committee, especially red meat. The effects of these measures on inflation have begun to be seen. These measures will also be able to reduce the volatility in food prices in the coming period. As we stated in our January 2016 open letter to the government, "... Our 10 years of experience in inflation targeting have shown that fighting inflation requires a collective effort. Public revenues and wage policies and structural elements of food prices are an important part of the fight against inflation. In addition, macroprudential measures for prudent borrowing provide a favorable basis for combating inflation by contributing to balanced growth. Therefore, it is important that all institutions continue the efforts made in recent years with a decisive stance in order to permanently reduce inflation to the 5 percent target." The main task of the Central Bank in the fight against inflation is to take the necessary measures regarding monetary indicators. (2) 3 As we have already mentioned, changes in the money supply and the rate at which money circulates determine the change in nominal aggregate demand. The first of these indicators, the broadly defined money supply; monetary policy, fiscal policy, financial sector policy and global conditions. Monetary policy affects the large money supply by adjusting the degree of tightness of liquidity policy. Fiscal policy is also an important factor that has an impact on the broad money supply. If high budget deficits are given, there may be monetary expansion through the increase in public loans opened by the banking sector. Financial sector policy, on the other hand, can change the pace of quantitative easing by influencing the rate of increase in loans to the private sector. Global financial conditions also affect quantitative easing by having an impact on the deposit and credit growth of bank balance sheets and exchange rates. As the second factor determining nominal aggregate demand, the speed at which money is circulating is an important variable that cannot be neglected, especially during periods when inflation is in the single digits. The factors that determine the speed of movement of money can be summarized as fiscal policy, global conditions and social attitudes and behaviors. If we consider this issue through the example of Turkey, the average annual M2 money growth from 1987 to the end of 2005 in the period before the inflation targeting regime was around 52%. In contrast, inflation was around 47%. Therefore, we see that the main problem at that time was excessive quantitative easing. In the aforementioned period, excessive quantitative easing was caused by the high borrowing need of the public sector and the monetization of this need by the central bank. This situation continued in the form of a vicious circle in the period up to 2002. Unhealthy quantitative easing and high inflationary uncertainty at the time damaged growth by causing real interest rates to rise to extraordinarily high levels. This problem has been solved by ensuring fiscal discipline in the public sector, reducing the borrowing needs of the public sector and preventing public expenditures from financing directly from central bank sources. The period 2002-2006 was a transition period that reduced inflation to single digit levels. Since 2006, the open inflation targeting regime has been adopted. In this period, with the contribution of fiscal discipline in the public sector, the growth rate of money reached more reasonable levels and decreased to an average of 16.4 percent in the 2006-2015 period. This significant slowdown in the rate of quantitative easing has not caused any harm to the real growth of the economy, but has benefited growth. With the approach to price stability and increasing predictability, the average real growth rate increased from 3.3 percent in the 1987-2005 period to 4.9 percent in the 2006-2015 period (Chart 4). 4 Chart 4. The speed at which money is circulating is similarly volatile (Chart 5). The Central Bank has been working on the tools that can be used in relation to monetary quantities since 2006 and has been strengthening and expanding its toolkit. The main goal here is to increase the resilience of our economy to internal and external shocks. Many different factors can have an impact on monetary indicators. When we look at the examples of monetary policy implementation in the past years, it is noteworthy that each period has its own characteristics. For example, in the quantitative easing observed in 2006, measures were taken against the rapid increase in inflation by tightening the liquidity policy of the Turkish lira quite strongly. In 2008, there was also an increase in inflation and monetary magnitudes in the period before the global financial crisis. But late 2008 also saw a sharp decline in global demand. Due to the market conditions at that time, the growth in the speed of circulation of money and monetary sizes slowed down by itself, and the Central Bank took the balancing measure by reducing interest rates this time. During the Eurozone debt crisis, a monetary tightening in liquidity policy, which was not as severe as in 2006, was enough to ensure stability. Then, on May 22, 2013, 5 Against the announcement of the Central Bank of America that it would end quantitative easing, the Central Bank again ensured stability by taking the necessary monetary tightening measure (Chart 6). The Central Bank strengthened its monetary control by adding two new dimensions in addition to the Turkish lira liquidity dimension. Therefore, according to the unique needs of each period, the Central Bank has managed to keep inflation under control by using new tools and methods (Chart 7). The most accurate policy combination has increased the resilience of macroeconomic indicators to shocks. Thus, the Central Bank ensured that the downward inflation trend continued even under difficult conditions. 6 Figure 7. We are approaching the pace of quantitative easing, which is in line with the macroeconomic objectives in the Medium-Term Program. In addition to the tight liquidity policy implemented here, policy instruments aimed at reducing the negative effects of global conditions on loans and exchange rates also benefit. Newly developed tools have played an important role, especially in monetary control. All central banks use domestic monetary liquidity policy as the most basic monetary control tool. In addition, especially in the last year, the Central Bank has made significant innovations in its foreign exchange liquidity policy and developed effective tools. In the summary of the Monetary Policy Committee's meeting on 31 March 2016, it is stated that "The Board considers that the effective use of the policy tools specified in the roadmap published in August 2015 increases the resilience of our economy against global shocks. It is observed that the extreme volatility observed in both exchange rates and loans has decreased thanks to the introduction of these new tools. As a matter of fact, a significant decrease in the relative volatility of the Turkish lira has been observed among developing countries since September. The improvement in the current account balance and the gradual decrease in foreign exchange demand due to the low course in energy prices support this process. Foreign exchange liquidity instruments are also used to stabilize the value of the Turkish lira. All these developments reduce the need for a broad interest rate corridor to some extent." 7 Similarly, with the guidance of the Financial Stability Committee, measures to prevent excesses in the financial sector were planned and implemented in cooperation with the BRSA and other institutions. The means of monetary control can be considered in three dimensions. These are Turkish lira liquidity policy, foreign exchange liquidity policy and financial sector policy. In these three dimensions, the CBRT's general stance was stated in the summary of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting dated 31 March 2016 as follows: "Monetary policy decisions in the coming period will depend on the inflation outlook. Taking into account developments in inflation expectations, pricing behaviors and other factors affecting inflation, the tight stance in monetary policy will be maintained. In addition, global and domestic volatilities will be closely monitored and necessary measures will continue to be taken in the foreign exchange and Turkish lira markets. In summary, the policy stance will remain tight against the inflation outlook, stabilizing currency liquidity and supportive of financial stability. ". Dear shareholders, I would like to remind you of two important documents we published last year on monetary control. The first is the announcement of the "Road Map in the Normalization Process of Global Monetary Policies" published on August 18, 2015. This document is a list of measures related to the measures to be taken in three dimensions. These measures have begun to be implemented and continue to be implemented. The second important document is the presentation on "Foreign Exchange Liquidity Instruments" dated February 1, 2016. This document is a presentation that summarizes the effects of newly developed instruments on exchange rates and loans. You can access both documents on our website. The tools used against excessive volatility in the exchange rate can be grouped into automatic stabilizers and rule-based stabilizers. Reserve options (ROM) and foreign currency collateral facility (FX) fall into the class of automatic stabilizers, while flexible foreign exchange auctions (EDI) and TL liquidity policy (TLP) are stabilizers based on extreme volatility rules. After the implementation of these measures, a significant decrease in Turkey's relative exchange rate volatility is observed as can be seen in the chart (Chart 8). The scaled area in the chart shows the area between the country with the highest volatility and the country with the least volatility. Thanks to the implementation of the measures in the road map, Turkey has entered the group of countries with relatively low volatility. 8 Chart 8. The most important elements that help control monetary control are healthy public financing and healthy private sector financing. Healthy financing in the public sector refers to fiscal discipline. Turkey's budget deficit, which was at the level of 11-12 percent before 2001, has decreased to 1 to 1.5 percent thanks to the measures taken. The significant improvement in the public debt burden also contributes significantly to the management of inflation expectations and thus to the fight against inflation. In summary, sound public financing makes a significant contribution to reducing inflation. In addition to public finance, private sector financing can also lead to volatility in monetary indicators, causing inflation to deviate from the target. The Financial Stability Committee, which was established in mid-2011, has made a significant contribution to the healthier structure of private sector financing. A significant part of the macroprudential measures implemented in recent years has been taken under the coordination of the Financial Stability Committee. These measures help to ensure that money and credit expansion is much healthier and in line with macro targets. Positive effects of healthy financing on external balance are also observed. Because with the effect of the macroprudential measures taken, financial flows have started to support production rather than consumption. This situation is beneficial both in terms of internal and external balance and in terms of the speed and sustainability of growth. As can be clearly seen in the graph below, excessive borrowing for consumption purposes adversely affects the current account balance and leads to excessive volatility in the current account balance (Chart 9). Therefore, it is observed that the measures taken regarding loans have provided a significant improvement in the current account balance. In addition, 9 lending measures limit household over-borrowing in Turkey and support macroeconomic stability by helping to increase savings. As a reflection of the policies implemented for healthy financing in recent years, it is observed that the improvement in the current account balance has continued uninterruptedly since 2011. The current account deficit, which reached its highest level with 76.1 billion dollars as of October 2011, decreased to 32.1 billion dollars at the end of 2015 (Chart 10). The improvement in the current account balance is expected to continue in the coming months. The fact that the opportunity provided by the fall in oil prices does not turn into overspending and excessive borrowing indicates that the financing position of households is gradually improving. Monetary policy supports the long-term potential growth of the economy through its contribution to combating inflation and balanced growth. Advances in structural reforms will increase our growth potential and make an additional contribution to our determination to fight inflation. As a result of all these efforts, 2016 is likely to be a year in which our country is one step closer to achieving all its macroeconomic targets, especially the projected decline in inflation. We offer our sincere thanks and respect to you, our valued shareholders, for the support you have given us in this process. 11
