Title: Speech Titled "Macroeconomic Outlook, Monetary Policy and Sustainable Growth" delivered by President Murat Uysal at Bursa Chamber of Commerce and Industry
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Macroeconomic Outlook, Monetary Policy and Sustainable Growth Murat UYSAL Governor of Bursa Chamber of Commerce and Industry Assembly Meeting, 25 February 2020 Distinguished Members of Bursa Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Distinguished Guests, Distinguished Members of the Press, Before I start my speech, I would like to thank the President Mr. brahim Burkay and Bursa Chamber of Commerce and Industry for their kind invitation. As the Central Bank, we try to incorporate the evaluations of the real sector, which is one of our main stakeholders, into our decision-making processes. In this context, we have previously met with our sector representatives in Ankara and Istanbul Chamber of Industry. Today we are in Bursa. I begin by summarizing our macroeconomic outlook and policy framework. With the effect of prudent macro policies implemented in coordination, significant gains were achieved in inflation, economic activity and external balance in 2019. The fact that these gains continue to strengthen in the coming periods is of great importance in terms of price stability, financial stability and sustainable growth. Accordingly, in the second part of my speech, I will address the issues of productivity, exports and sustainable growth. In the last part of my speech, I will share some of our observations about Bursa, which reflects one of the best examples of the relationship between productivity, exports and sustainable growth. Dear Guests, I would like to begin the macroeconomic outlook and policy framework section of my speech by summarizing the current situation in the global economy. The weak course in global economic activity continued simultaneously in the last quarter of 2019 in developed and developing economies. The trade agreement between the US and China, the reduction of uncertainties regarding the Brexit process and, on the other hand, the supportive stance of global monetary policies since the second half of 2019 stand out as developments that have a positive impact on the global growth outlook. As a matter of fact, while economic activity in the European Union region improved somewhat in January, this reflected positively on our external demand and exports. However, despite the agreement between the US and China, uncertainties remain high, ongoing geopolitical risks and the recent epidemic keep the downside risks on global growth alive. The weak course of global economic activity is decisive on commodity prices and inflation. Although inflation rates have risen slightly in the last quarter due to food prices in some countries, they are expected to continue to show a horizontal outlook in 2020. This outlook strengthens expectations that the central banks of developed countries will continue their monetary policies in an expansionary direction, while allowing supportive monetary policies in developing countries. Due to the increasing uncertainties regarding global growth in the recent period, portfolio flows and risk appetite have been fluctuating. We closely monitor the effects that all these global developments may have on capital flows, foreign trade and commodity prices. Dear Guests, We see that economic activity has entered a moderate recovery trend starting from the first quarter of 2019. In the balancing process, net exports made a high contribution to the recovery; In the near term, domestic demand is seen to be strengthening with the disinflation process and the improvement in financial conditions. 2 We see that the recovery in the economy has exhibited an increasing sectoral spread during the year and has gained strength recently. Industrial production data for December and survey indicators for the last quarter confirm this development. As a matter of fact, sectoral confidence indices show that the improvement in trade, service and construction activities continues. In addition to the recovery in economic activity, investment and employment developments are also important for the permanence and inclusiveness of growth. In this context, when we first look at investment developments, we see that the investment trend of companies continues to improve to include small and medium-sized companies. We believe that the improvement in financial conditions has contributed to this development. In addition to interest rate cuts, other measures such as reserve requirements also facilitate access to credit. Due to the recovery of economic activity, non-agricultural employment increased in the last quarter and unemployment rates declined slightly. The leading indicators we follow give signals that this trend will continue. The continuation of the improvement in employment opportunities is important for the healthy continuation of the interaction between financial intermediation and economic activity. Supporting the real sector's access to long-term finance will continue to contribute to financial stability by reflecting positively on investments and employment. On the external balance side, the current account balance has improved significantly in the last year and has started to run an annual surplus for the first time since 2002. Thus, we have given a current account surplus in a year of positive growth. The positive effect of real exchange rate-induced competitiveness on the external balance, market diversification flexibility and the increase in exports of goods and services played an important role in this development. Current levels of the real exchange rate support Turkey's competitiveness in the global trade market. Competitiveness gains play an important role in moving the economy towards a more balanced and sustainable growth path by giving our export potential a significant resilience and flexibility against external shocks. As a matter of fact, although the weakening in the global growth outlook has slowed down foreign demand in recent years, we see that the positive effect of the developments in competitiveness continues. Respected representatives of our real sector, Consumer inflation declined significantly in 2019. Tight monetary policy and coordinated policies have been the main determinants of the decline in inflation. The decline in inflation supported the decline in inflation, as well as the reduction in cumulative exchange rate effects, demand conditions and moderate import prices, as well as inflation expectations and improvement in pricing behavior. Two key factors were decisive in the significant improvement in inflation expectations. The first is the decline in actual inflation; the second is that inflation since late 2018 has been very close to, or even below the forecasts shared by the Central Bank in its Inflation Reports. Another important point about the improvement in inflation expectations is that the improvement is spread to the general public and a consensus is formed around this expectation. At this point, the inflation outlook is largely in line with the forecasts we announced in the January Inflation Report. Focused on reducing inflation, cautious monetary policy stance and strong 3 Under policy coordination, we maintained our 2020 year-end inflation forecast at 8.2 percent. We estimate that inflation will stabilize at 5 percent in the medium term after declining to 5.4 percent at the end of 2021. The large number of indicators we follow for the main trend points to a course in line with the targeted downward path in inflation. We anticipate that inflation will gradually decline towards our year-end forecast after remaining flat at current levels for a while. Dear Guests, In 2019, while determining the monetary policy stance in a way to ensure the continuation of the process of decline in inflation, we also used our tools for financial stability effectively. While we kept the policy interest rate stable at 24 percent in the first half of 2019, we gradually reduced it to 10.75 percent as of July, depending on the improvement in the inflation outlook. The cautious stance in monetary policy and the steady decline in inflation have been instrumental in the rapid decline of inflation expectations. The decline in the country's risk premium and inflation expectations led to a decrease in medium and long-term bond yields. I would like to emphasize once again that the continuity of the process of decline in inflation is of great importance in terms of the decline in the country's risk premium and the coming down of long-term interest rates. We see that the reductions in the policy rate are strongly reflected in the loan and deposit rates. While maintaining our monetary policy stance focused on reducing inflation, we continue to implement other macro policies in coordination to support financial stability. In this context, in August, we made changes to the reserves that banks have to keep at the Central Bank. This change, initially led by public banks, helped banks make their lending conditions more supportive. As the second stage, with the application change we announced in December, we aimed to encourage long-term commercial loans and long-term housing loans, which have a strong relationship with production and investment. In addition, we have recently made an arrangement to make the fees and commissions that can be charged by banks for products or services to be offered to commercial customers more transparent, understandable and comparable. We hope that this arrangement will be beneficial in terms of reducing the difficulties in our firms' access to finance and increasing transparency in the financial services market. Dear members of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, While the decline in loan interest rates in the second half of the year stimulated credit demand, the strong liquidity and capital structure of banks, as well as the decrease in funding costs, supported the supply of loans. Loans showed momentum above historical averages as of July 2019. In particular, the acceleration in consumer loans, which started in August with the effect of the compulsory reserve regulation, has recently started to be observed in company loans. In parallel with the signs of recovery in the revived economic activity and investment demand, we anticipate that the increase in company loans will continue. However, credit growth and 4 We are also closely monitoring the effects of developments in its composition on the external balance and inflation. I would like to underline that it is important for the macro policy composition that the current account balance, which has shown a significant improvement in the recent period, follows a moderate course in the coming period. Before moving on to the issue of export-oriented, balanced and sustainable growth, I would like to briefly summarize our monetary policy stance within the framework of these evaluations of the macroeconomic outlook. In order for the decline in inflation to occur in line with the targeted path in the coming period, our cautious stance on monetary policy must be maintained. In this context, we will determine our monetary stance in a way to ensure the continuity of the decline in inflation by taking into account the indicators of the main trend As the Central Bank, we will continue to use all the tools at our disposal in line with our objectives of ensuring price stability and supporting financial stability. Dear Guests, Studies show that there is a strong relationship between exports, productivity and sustainable growth. Productivity gains and continuity of investments are important for high rate sustainable growth. In this context, price and non-price competition conditions in export markets lead companies to use their resources effectively. Exporting companies increase their product quality on the one hand and maintain their competitiveness by producing new technology or incorporating new technologies produced on a global scale into their production processes. However, studies in the field of international trade conclude that efficient firms that can bear the cost of entry are able to enter export markets. Empirical studies also support this finding. I would like to emphasize that exports have important contributions to sustainable growth other than productivity. As the business world is well aware, export increases positively affect the current account balance, thus macroeconomic stability, and support investment appetite. Dear guests, I would like to continue my presentation by looking at the export-productivity relationship from the perspective of the Turkish manufacturing industry. The company-based studies carried out at our Bank show the strong relationship between exports and productivity. As the export intensity, in other words, the ratio of exports to total sales, increases, it is observed that the productivity of the company increases. In addition to productivity, the export rate is also positively related to profit margin, which is one of the most important company indicators. In the analyzes we have made for the motor land vehicles and other transportation vehicles sector, which has a very important place in the economy of Bursa, it is seen that the companies with high export rates have higher efficiency and profitability. Similar findings are emerging in other sectors. Exports support sustainable growth through direct and indirect channels. However, when we consider that every market has a certain level of saturation, sustainable export increases 5 Market diversification is critical. As a matter of fact, in Turkey, it is seen that exports and country diversification act in parallel. In addition to supporting export growth, market diversification reduces fluctuations in export revenues by increasing the resilience of exports to regional risks. For example, despite the recession in the EU region after the 2008 global crisis, the orientation of our companies to alternative markets has been a balancing factor in the total export performance. The number of markets, which we define more broadly as the product-country intersection, increased by 56 percent between 2006 and 2018. The number of our exporter companies has nearly doubled. The fact that the increase in exports is fed through different channels supports our expectations that the increases will continue in the long term. Compared to the G-20 countries, we see that Turkey is the most successful country in increasing market diversity and at the level of market diversification. In other words, Turkish exports have spread throughout the world instead of concentrating on a specific country or region. As a result of the dynamic structure of our companies, the share of the top 15 countries with the highest share in our exports together with the diversification in our exports was 65 percent in 2006 and 58 percent in 2019. Although Germany, England and Italy, which are our largest markets in exports, maintained their places in the ranking, significant increases were seen in the shares of other countries in our exports. In line with the change in exports, country and product composition over time, differentiations are also observed in the composition of the sector. Our exports, which were approximately 86 billion dollars in 2006, doubled to 172 billion dollars in 2019 with the contribution of factors such as the increase in market diversity, the entry of new companies into the export market and the opening up to new markets. In the same period, the rate of increase in global exports is much more limited. As a result, Turkey's share of world trade increased significantly compared to 2006. As the Central Bank, it attaches importance to the contribution of exports to macroeconomic stability and sustainable growth through productivity and current account balance; we anticipate that our total exports and added value in export products will increase even more. In this context, I would like to share some of our observations from our meetings with you in this part of my speech. 6 Bursa is one of the provinces we attach importance to with its dynamic real sector and export-oriented production structure. As one of the cities that produce the most added value in Turkey, Bursa, which makes a significant contribution to our economy with its industrialized structure, also draws attention with its export performance. Our province, which has undertaken an important role especially in the export of automotive, textile, ready-to-wear clothing and machinery, is the production base for many of our sectors. In this respect, we see Bursa as a very important center where we can follow the pulse of our manufacturing industry in our field studies. In Bursa, we have had and continue to hold more than 500 very productive meetings with the representatives of approximately 250 companies, including many member companies of Bursa Chamber of Commerce and Industry. Our observations show that Bursa companies have achieved a great success in improving their production capabilities and export performances in many sectors and continue to work with devotion to make this success permanent. I would like to emphasize that what makes our Bursa companies special for our country is the power they have in productivity and high value-added production. In this context, we closely monitor the efforts of our companies in critical areas such as increasing the domestic value-added content of production, investing in new technology areas, improving their position in global value chains, increasing market and product diversity, and design. We believe that this approach is very valuable in terms of sustainable growth. Our field observations indicate that public incentives and policy implementations provide significant support to the success achieved by our private sector. As the Central Bank, we act with the aim of supporting sustainable growth by considering our goal of providing price stability. In this direction, we aim to further enrich our work in the coming periods by developing mutual trust, cooperation and communication. While concluding my speech here, I would like to thank all our companies that sincerely share their valuable ideas and suggestions with us and contribute to our work. I believe that this cooperation will become stronger in the coming period. I would also like to express my gratitude to Bursa Chamber of Commerce and Industry for their hospitality. Thank you. 7

Title: Speech at the Assembly Meeting of the Ankara Chamber of Industry
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Economic Outlook and the Central Bank's Real Sector Studies Murat UYSAL, Governor of Ankara Chamber of Industry Assembly Meeting, 25 September 2019 Dear Members of Ankara Chamber of Industry, Dear Guests, Dear Members of the Press, As the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, we take care to work in harmony with the real sector and all our other stakeholders in order to increase the effectiveness of the policies we implement. On this occasion, I attach great importance to and thank this kind invitation of the Ankara Chamber of Industry, which has adopted the mission of contributing to the production of high added value for its industrialists, increasing its competitiveness and being a guide in the economic, technological, social and cultural development of our country. I would like to begin with a brief assessment of the macroeconomic outlook. We are going through a conjuncture in which increasing trade tensions have significant repercussions on global growth and monetary policies. This has the potential to have significant impacts on developing countries, including Turkey, through trade and capital flows. As a matter of fact, we see that the slowdown trend in global growth has become evident in the recent period and that this loss of momentum is more pronounced for the European Union countries, which are our most important foreign trade partners. Although this slowdown affects our trade with the European Union, the strong course in our exports continues thanks to the flexibility of our companies in market and product diversification and competitive gains. On the other hand, the moderate course of global inflation supports risk appetite and portfolio flows to developing countries with expansionary monetary policy steps. However, due to uncertainties related to trade disputes and geopolitical developments, we see that portfolio flows to developing countries follow a fluctuating and weak course. Since external financing conditions affect our economy through the risk premium, exchange rate and expectation channel, we closely monitor their impact on global developments and capital flows. Dear Listeners, When we look at the domestic developments, we see that economic activity has entered the balancing process since the second quarter of 2018. Following the contraction in the second half of last year, we observed a moderate recovery in the first half of 2019 in Gross Domestic Product. During the stabilization period, the contribution of net exports to growth reached its highest levels historically, significantly limiting the slowdown in economic activity. This change in growth composition led to a marked improvement in the external balance, resulting in the 12-month cumulative current account balance posting a surplus for the first time since 2002. Leading indicators, especially industrial production, show that the recovery in economic activity and the stabilization in the economy continued in the second half of the year. In the coming period, with the decrease in inflation, the country's risk premium and financial volatilities will decrease; With the gradual improvement in financial conditions, we anticipate that the recovery in economic activity will continue in a moderate way. In the current period, the fact that the real exchange rate is at low levels supports Turkey's competitiveness in the global trade market and therefore the improvement in the foreign trade balance. Competitiveness gains give our export potential a significant resilience and flexibility against external shocks, thus playing an important role in moving the economy towards a more balanced and sustainable growth path. As a matter of fact, despite the recovery process in the economy in recent months, we see that there is no deterioration in the main trend of the current account balance. With the contribution of the strong increase in tourism revenues, we expect the improvement in the current account balance to continue in the rest of 2019. 2 Dear Listeners, We have seen a significant decline in consumer inflation since October 2018. As a result of tight monetary policy and coordinated policy efforts, the reduction of cumulative exchange rate effects and the moderate course of domestic demand stand out as the main drivers of the decline in inflation. With the contribution of these factors, we anticipate that the improvement trend in inflation will continue in the coming period Due to the decline in inflation, we also see an improvement in inflation expectations. Anchoring inflation expectations is critical to the effectiveness of monetary policy and reducing the inflation-growth trade-off. We assess that expectations will continue to improve in the coming period depending on the improvement in the inflation outlook. Dear Members of Ankara Chamber of Industry, Dear Guests, Taking into account all the factors affecting the inflation outlook, we cut the policy rate by 325 basis points in September after a 425 basis point cut in July. As I mentioned before, we have been observing an improvement in inflation dynamics in the recent period. With the effect of global developments, we preferred to use a significant part of the movement area in monetary policy in a front-loading manner in July and September. While taking this decision, we aimed for a monetary policy stance that is largely in line with the disinflation path we are targeting. At this point, we assess that the monetary policy stance supports the process of decline in inflation. On the other hand, inflation in Turkey is still at high levels compared to the developing country group. We need to maintain our cautious stance on monetary policy in order to make the decline in inflation permanent. In this context, we will determine the level of monetary tightness in a way that ensures the continuity of the decline in inflation. We see that the decisions we take as the Central Bank have an impact on the credit market. With the interest rate cuts in July and September, deposit and loan rates declined. We observed the decline in loan interest rates in both company and consumer loans. In addition, the credit growth rate increased to be more pronounced in consumer loans, and a moderate revival in credit growth rates was observed. Depending on the delayed effects of the monetary transmission mechanism, we can see that the revival in the credit market becomes more pronounced in the coming period. Dear Listeners; In this part of my speech, I would like to briefly talk about the relationship between price stability and growth. First of all, I would like to state that these two concepts do not contradict each other, but on the contrary, they are complementary to each other. Growth based on productivity growth strengthens the sustainability of price stability; Ensuring price stability supports investments and growth potential by reducing uncertainty and lowering interest rates. At this point, I would like to mention how the monetary policies implemented by central banks affect the relationship between price stability and sustainable growth. As you know, central banks ultimately play a decisive role on inflation by influencing aggregate demand, credit conditions and similar macro variables through the monetary policy they implement. Central banks determine only the short-term interest rate with their interest rate policy, and this rate is called the "policy rate". The Central Bank's policy rate is set at the one-week repo auction rate. Monetary policy primarily affects pricing in the financial system. Banks whose costs change then reflect this change in loan and deposit rates by taking into account some other factors. 3 When evaluated from the point of view of firms operating in the real sector, monetary policy is especially important in two respects: borrowing cost and predictability. Long-term loan rates in the market are formed by adding factors such as credit risk premium, maturity premium and inflation expectations on top of the policy rate determined by central banks. Therefore, when central banks raise policy rates at a time of inflationary pressures, even if they have increased the short-term cost of banks, they can facilitate the borrowing of real sector firms by positively affecting long-term interest rates to the extent that they can reduce risk premiums and inflation expectations. Another importance of the monetary policy stance for the real sector is to ensure predictability with its signal strength and guidance feature about the course of inflation in the coming period, especially in periods of high volatility. Controlling inflation expectations; For a company operating in the real sector, it is important to reduce input costs, to make forward-looking pricing, to plan investment and production processes. Therefore, when making monetary policy decisions, central banks adopt an understanding to ensure price stability and sustainable growth with a medium and long-term perspective. In periods of high inflation, depreciation pressures on the exchange rate and high volatility, it should not be forgotten that the tight monetary policy stance can relieve the real sector through both predictability and long-term borrowing costs. Dear Participants, Today, the central banks of many countries attach great importance to diversifying and enriching the information sets they use when constructing their monetary policies. In this context, especially the information obtained from the real sector, the evaluations and needs of the real sector are increasingly included in the decision-making processes. We, as the Central Bank, act with a data-oriented approach in the design of monetary policy processes. In this context, we also use micro data, which allows us to closely analyze micro-level dynamics and field information, intensively in this process. For example, we analyze in depth the issues faced by you, the real sector representatives, access to credit, foreign currency indebtedness, use of imported inputs and similar issues with the microdata we access at the level of companies and banks and evaluate the results of these analyzes in our policy processes. In order to maximize policy effectiveness, we attach particular importance to two-way communication with the real sector, one of our main stakeholders, in order to support healthy and inclusive economic growth. In order to keep the pulse of the real sector, we evaluate the valuable information we obtain from the field in the policy-making processes by blending it with all other data. I can say that this information constitutes one of the most valuable inputs in terms of our decision-making processes. Dear Participants; In this part of my speech, I would like to talk about these field studies that we, as the Central Bank, carry out in interaction with the real sector. Since 2013, we have been holding face-to-face meetings with you, our esteemed real sector representatives, in order to closely follow the course of economic activities on a regional and sectoral basis by going to the field. As those of you who participated in these meetings know, these meetings are held between the managers and employees of our Bank and the decision-making senior managers of the companies. With a team of 50 people consisting of our competent employees who are specialized in their fields, we carry out these interviews every month all over Turkey. In this context, we visit approximately 2,000 companies from different sectors and scales every year at regular intervals. Today, we have had very productive meetings with many representatives of Ankara Chamber of Industry member companies and we continue to do so. To date, we have conducted more than 500 interviews with approximately 250 companies in Ankara within the scope of field studies. 4 During these visits, we focus on many issues from demand conditions to investment stance, from financing conditions to pricing behaviors and obtain comprehensive and simultaneous information about the decision-making mechanisms of companies. This information is even more critical for us, especially since it is compiled more timely and detailed than official statistics, especially in periods of increasing uncertainty and changing business cycles. In addition, we can instantly monitor the effects of developments at home and abroad and legal and institutional regulations on real sector dynamics, and better analyze the conjuncture and transmission mechanisms for the near future. There is no doubt that the information we have compiled through company visits on the feelings and stance of our real sector firms towards the economic outlook deepens and enriches our information pool that we use in our monetary policy decision-making processes. Face-to-face meetings with our companies are very useful in terms of obtaining information about cyclical developments as well as structural issues and understanding the effects of an arrangement that concerns our companies. And I want you to know that our meetings with you impose another responsibility on us as the Central Bank. We share your expectations and suggestions that you convey to us during the meetings with the relevant public institutions and try to be an intermediary in solving your problems. Because we are aware that a healthy and efficient real sector is an indispensable element for price stability and financial stability. I would also like to point out that company visits also contribute to the communication of monetary policy directly and more effectively. As the Central Bank, while we can explain our policy steps to you better, we can directly learn the reflections of the policies implemented from you. This two-sided communication contributes to our efforts to raise public awareness of price stability and cyclical and structural issues. Thus, we aim to further strengthen the communication bridge between the Central Bank and the real sector. Dear ASO Members, Dear Guests, We observe that you continue your activities with great devotion both in the statistics we have compiled through surveys and in the research studies we have done and in our field studies. In the recent negotiations, we see that Ankara companies, especially in the defense industry, machinery equipment, fabricated metal and furniture sectors, have a strong motivation to increase exports, focus on efficiency, increase market diversity and product quality. In this context, we are pleased to observe that our companies have taken important steps in terms of dynamism, renewal and adaptation to global competition conditions and have increased their contribution to the country's economy. As the Central Bank, we act with the aim of contributing to healthy and inclusive growth by considering our goals of ensuring price stability and supporting financial stability. By developing mutual trust, cooperation and communication, we aim to continue our work by further enriching it in the coming periods. While concluding my speech here, I would like to thank all our companies that sincerely share their valuable ideas and suggestions with us and contribute to our work. I believe that this cooperation will deepen and become stronger in the coming period. I would like to express my gratitude to Mr. President Nurettin 85zdebir and our Ankara Chamber of Industry for their invitation and hospitality. Thank you for listening to me. 5

Deerli Dinleyiciler, Yurt ii gelimelere bakldnda, iktisadi faaliyetin 2018 ylnn ikinci eyreinden itibaren dengelenme srecine girdiini gryoruz. Ayrca, kredi byme hz, tketici kredilerinde daha belirgin olmak zere ykselie geti ve kredi byme oranlarnda lml bir canlanma gzlendi. Parasal aktarm mekanizmasnn gecikmeli etkilerine bal olarak nmzdeki dnemde kredi piyasasndaki canlanmann daha belirgin hale geldiini grebiliriz. Saygdeer Dinleyiciler; Konumamn bu blmnde ksaca fiyat istikrar ile byme ilikisinden bahsetmek istiyorum. ncelikle, bu iki kavramn birbiriyle elimediini, aksine birbirini tamamlayc nitelikte olduunu belirtmek isterim. Merkez Bankasnn politika faizi bir hafta vadeli repo ihale faiz oran olarak belirlenmitir. Para politikas ncelikle finansal sistemdeki fiyatlamalar etkiler. Maliyetleri deien bankalar daha sonra dier baz baka faktrleri de dikkate almak suretiyle bu deiimi kredi ve mevduat faizlerine yanstrlar. 3 Reel sektrde faaliyet gsteren firmalar asndan deerlendirildiinde para politikas zellikle iki adan nemlidir: Borlanma maliyeti ve ngrlebilirlik. Para politikas duruunun reel sektr asndan bir baka nemi ise, zellikle yksek oynaklk dnemlerinde enflasyonun gelecek dnemde izleyecei seyre dair sinyal gc ve rehberlik zelliiyle ngrlebilirlii salamaktan geer. Enflasyon beklentilerinin kontrol altna alnmas; reel sektrde faaliyet gsteren bir firma asndan girdi maliyetlerinin drlmesi, ileriye dnk fiyatlama yapabilmek, yatrm ve retim srelerini planlamak asndan nem arz etmektedir. Dolaysyla merkez bankalar para politikas kararlarn alrken orta ve uzun vadeli bir perspektifle fiyat istikrarn ve srdrlebilir bymeyi salamaya ynelik bir anlay benimsemektedir. Enflasyonun yksek olduu, dviz kuru zerinde deer kayb basklarnn ve oynakln fazla olduu dnemlerde, sk para politikas duruunun gerek ngrlebilirlik gerekse uzun vadeli borlanma maliyetleri zerinden reel sektr rahatlatabileceini unutmamak gerekir. Saygdeer Katlmclar, Gnmzde birok lke merkez bankas para politikalarn kurgularken kullandklar bilgi setlerini eitlendirmeye ve zenginletirmeye byk nem vermektedir. Bu balamda zellikle reel sektrden edinilen bilgiler, reel sektrn deerlendirmeleri ve ihtiyalar karar alma srelerine artan dzeyde dhil edilmektedir. Biz de, Merkez Bankas olarak, para politikas srelerinin tasarmnda, veri odakl bir yaklam ile hareket etmekteyiz. Politika etkinliini en st dzeye karmak amacyla, salkl ve kapsayc ekonomik bymeyi desteklemek adna, ana paydalarmzdan biri olan reel sektrle ift ynl iletiim kurmaya zel nem veriyoruz. Reel sektrn nabzn tutmaya ynelik olarak sahadan elde ettiimiz deerli bilgileri, dier tm veriler ile birlikte harmanlayarak politika oluturma srelerinde deerlendirmekteyiz. Bu bilgilerin, karar alma srelerimiz asndan en kymetli girdilerden birini oluturduunu ifade edebilirim. Deerli Katlmclar; Konumamn bu ksmnda, Merkez Bankas olarak reel sektrle etkileim ierisinde yrttmz bu saha almalarndan bahsetmek istiyorum. 2013 ylndan bu yana sahaya inerek ekonomik faaliyetlerin seyrini blgesel ve sektrel bazda yakndan takip etmek amacyla, siz deerli reel sektr temsilcileriyle yz yze grmeler yapyoruz. Aranzda bu grmelere katlanlarn da bildii zere, bu toplantlar, Bankamz yneticileri ve alanlar ile firmalarn karar alc st dzey yneticileri arasnda gerekletiriliyor. Konusunda uzmanlam yetkin alanlarmzdan oluan 50 kiilik bir ekiple her ay Trkiyenin drt bir yannda bu grmeleri yrtyoruz. Bu kapsamda her yl, dzenli aralklarla, farkl sektr ve leklerden yaklak 2.000 firmay ziyaret ediyoruz. Bugn de aramzda bulunan Ankara Sanayi Odas yesi birok firma temsilcisi ile olduka verimli grmeler yaptk ve yapmaya devam ediyoruz. Bugne kadar saha almalar kapsamnda Ankarada yaklak 250 firmayla 500n zerinde grme gerekletirdik. 4 Bu ziyaretlerde talep koullarndan yatrm duruuna, finansman koullarndan fiyatlama davranlarna kadar pek ok konuya odaklanyor ve firmalarn karar alma mekanizmalarna ilikin kapsaml ve ezamanl bilgi ediniyoruz. Bu bilgiler zellikle belirsizliin artt, i evrimlerinin deitii dnemlerde resmi istatistiklerden daha zamanl ve detayl olarak derlendiinden bizler iin daha da kritik bir nem arz ediyor. Buna ek olarak, yurt iinde ve yurt dnda yaanan gelimeler ile hukuki ve kurumsal dzenlemelerin reel sektr dinamikleri zerindeki etkilerini anlk olarak izleyebiliyor, yakn gelecee dair konjonktr ve aktarm mekanizmalarn daha iyi analiz edebiliyoruz. Kuku yok ki firma ziyaretleri yoluyla derlediimiz, reel sektr firmalarmzn ekonomik grnme ynelik hissiyat ve durularna ilikin bilgiler para politikas karar alma srelerimizde kullandmz bilgi havuzumuzu derinletirip zenginletiriyor. Firmalarmzla yaptmz yz-yze grmeler, konjonktrel gelimelerin yan sra yapsal konular hakknda bilgi edinmek ve firmalarmz ilgilendiren bir dzenlemenin etkilerini anlamak asndan olduka faydal oluyor. Ve bilmenizi isterim ki sizlerle yaptmz grmeler Merkez Bankas olarak bize ayr bir sorumluluk daha yklyor. Grmelerde bize ilettiiniz beklentilerinizi ve nerilerinizi de ilgili kamu kurumlaryla paylayor ve sorunlarnzn zmnde arac olmaya alyoruz. Zira salkl ve verimli ileyen bir reel sektrn fiyat istikrar ve finansal istikrar iin vazgeilmez bir unsur olduunun farkndayz. Firma ziyaretlerinin para politikasnn iletiiminin dorudan ve daha etkin bir ekilde yaplmasna da katk saladn belirtmek isterim. Merkez Bankas olarak politika admlarmz sizlere daha iyi anlatabilirken, sizlerden de uygulanan politikalarn yansmalarn dorudan renebiliyoruz. Bu ift tarafl iletiim, fiyat istikrar ile konjonktrel ve yapsal konular hakknda kamuoyunda farkndalk oluturma abamza katk salyor. Bylelikle Merkez Bankas ve reel sektr arasndaki iletiim kprsn daha da glendirmeyi amalyoruz. Title: Speech at the Information Meeting on the Introduction of the "Inflation Report 2022-I"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: /3EL REPUBLIC OF TURKEY \Mt CENTRAL BANK Speech Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey Prof. Dr. ahap Kavcolu, Central Bank Governor Inflation Report Briefing 2022-1 27 January 2022, Ankara Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Participants, Welcome to the first Inflation Report Briefing of 2022. Today, due to the severe winter conditions, the number of physical participants is less than in previous meetings. I would like to greet our guests who are not here but follow us on their screens and wish that our meeting will be beneficial. After conveying the global and domestic economic developments since our Inflation Report Briefing Meeting held in October 2021, I will share with you our assessments on the inflation outlook. Later, I will make statements on our medium-term inflation forecasts and make an overview of monetary policy. In the last part, we will answer your questions and hopefully complete our meeting efficiently. Macroeconomic Outlook While global PMI indices declined compared to their peaks, they remained above the 50 threshold level for both the manufacturing and services sectors. Despite the recovery in global economic activity and the increase in vaccination rates, new variants in the pandemic and geopolitical risks keep the downside risks to global economic activity alive and continue to increase uncertainties. The fact that the risks related to the variants remained alive negatively affected the growth outlook for 2022 in some countries and caused the growth forecasts to be revised downwards. Growth forecasts for Turkey's main trading partners were revised upwards for 2021 compared to the October reporting period, while growth forecasts for 2022 were revised slightly downwards. However, we assess that the risks to global economic activity are limited thanks to the level of vaccination rates and the experience of maintaining activity under pandemic conditions. In light of these developments, Turkey's external demand outlook remains positive. Commodity prices remain high across the board. Although the emergence of the Omicron variant and the increase in global commodity demand uncertainty caused crude oil prices to decline in December, prices increased again in January. While energy prices declined compared to the previous reporting period, the decline in natural gas prices was effective in this development. However, natural gas prices remain quite high compared to 2020 levels. On the other hand, non-energy commodity prices continued to increase compared to the October reporting period. Significant increases in global inflation are observed due to factors such as the recovery in global demand, the high course of commodity prices, the prolongation of supply delivery times, historically high levels of global freight costs, and supply-demand mismatches. Around the world, both headline and core inflation have accelerated. Especially for developed countries, we see that inflation has reached historic highs, exceeding the 2008 level. The effects of the rise in global inflation on inflation expectations and international financial markets are closely monitored by central banks. In this context, central banks state in their communications that the inflation trend is more persistent than anticipated. It is considered that the supply and supply problems, which are expected to disappear with the weakening of the effects of the pandemic, have not yet started to improve and continue to have an increasing effect on inflation, especially from developed countries. We are witnessing an increase in the discourse divergence among the Central Banks of developed countries. While asset purchases continue to decline, the supportive outlook is maintained in the current situation. In many developing countries, both current inflation realizations and inflation expectations are above the target. We observe that there have been portfolio inflows to developing countries recently. Despite the inflow trend that started in November, portfolio flows to emerging economies have still not reached pre-pandemic levels. Unlike previous periods, there have been inflows into equity markets outside of China. In this process, capital inflows to Turkey continued in the equity markets in November, while capital outflows were observed in both GDDS and equity markets in December. We believe that expectations regarding the course of the pandemic and the monetary policies of central banks in advanced economies will continue to have an impact on global risk appetite and portfolio movements in the upcoming period. Distinguished Participants, I would like to continue my speech with the domestic macroeconomic outlook. In the third quarter of 2021, national income increased by 2.7 percent quarter-on-quarter and 7.4 percent year-on-year. Economic activity remained strong in the said period with the strong momentum in vaccination, the easing of restrictions and the recovery in tourism activity. Thanks to this situation in tourism and the strong export performance, the contribution of net exports to annual growth was quite high with 6.8 percentage points. Thus, Turkey was among the countries where net exports contributed the most to annual growth among OECD countries in the third quarter. Capacity utilization levels and other leading indicators show that economic activity remained strong in the last quarter of the year, supported by both external and domestic demand. Industrial production continued its upward trend in the fourth quarter. In particular, we assess the high levels of foreign turnover indices as foreign demand continuing to support industrial production in the fourth quarter. The acceleration of vaccination supports the recovery process in the global economy. With the increase in vaccination rates in Turkey and all over the world, the gradual lifting of epidemic measures emerges as a factor that increases the contribution of foreign demand to economic activity. On the other hand, although there is an increase in the number of cases due to the emergence of new variants of the virus, isolation measures are kept more relaxed on a global scale with the help of vaccination. The spread of vaccination to the general population allows services, tourism and related sectors, which have been adversely affected by the pandemic, to maintain their strength and to maintain a more balanced mix of economic activity. Retail sales volume and services turnover indices continue to increase, especially with the support of tourism-related items. The easing of restrictions along with the strong momentum in vaccination played an important role in the recovery trend in tourism activity and related service items. As a matter of fact, according to the data on card spending, we see that the rate of increase is higher in the service sectors that are more affected by the epidemic. Survey data indicate that companies plan to increase their investment expenditures for the future in the last quarter of the year. Excluding the vehicle sector, where supply problems are limiting production, the foreign trade and production indices as of November confirm that the demand for fixed capital goods remained strong in the last quarter of the year. In this period, we see that the capacity utilization rate of the manufacturing industry has exceeded its pre-pandemic level. We consider that this need for additional capacity is a factor that can support investment demand in the coming period. Therefore, we believe that long-term Turkish lira-denominated financing opportunities are especially important in terms of meeting the investment demand. High-frequency data indicate that the improvement in the employment outlook and the positive course in the labor market continue in line with the economic activity outlook. While employment maintained its upward trend led by the services sector due to the positive course in tourism, we saw a limited increase in the labor force participation rate. In the fourth quarter, industrial employment increased with the support of strong exports, while services employment increased with the positive course of tourism. Surveys show that employment expectations in the manufacturing industry remain at high levels. In this context, we anticipate that employment growth will continue in the upcoming period. Exports continued their upward trend in the last quarter of 2021, which it has achieved since the second half of 2020. On the other hand, despite the decline in the real exchange rate, imports increased due to the increase in energy prices. Excluding price effects, the amount of exports maintained an upward trend due to the recovery in global demand and the level of the real exchange rate. Imports, on the other hand, remained flat and the real rebalancing process continued. The increase in the number of tourists, which started with the end or relaxation of travel restrictions to a large extent following the spread of vaccination, continued in the last quarter of the year, and service revenues reached their pre-pandemic levels. The improvement in the 12-month cumulative current account balance, which shows a long-term trend, continued in November, but lost some momentum. Excluding gold and energy, we see that the improvement in the annual current account balance continues. The strengthening of the improvement in the current account balance is expected to have a positive impact on the country risk premium by reducing the need for external financing in the upcoming period. Accordingly, we anticipate that the current account balance will post a surplus in 2022. Moving on to financial conditions, annual loan growth slowed to 13.8 percent and followed a moderate course. In the fourth quarter, the loan growth rate converged to historical averages with the support of the decline in interest rates. The increase in loans to firms in this quarter was the most important determinant of loan growth. As of the end of 2021, the exchange rate-adjusted growth rates of commercial loans and consumer loans were 10.9 percent and 20.2 percent, respectively. While corporate and housing loans accelerated, consumer loan growth continued to be flat. We attach importance to the developments in commercial loans for investments that increase capacity and eliminate supply constraints. I would like to emphasize that the relatively moderate growth of personal loans is important to limit the risks to the inflation outlook and the external balance. Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Participants, I will now briefly evaluate the inflation outlook shaped by this macroeconomic framework. Consumer inflation stood at 36.08% at the end of 2021, with annual inflation rising in all subcategories. In the last quarter of the year, exchange rate developments were one of the most important determinants of the rise in inflation. Supply-side factors such as the strong course of economic activity in the fourth quarter, increases in imports and international food prices, as well as agricultural drought, disruptions in the supply process, and the continued high course despite the partial recovery in transportation costs continued to adversely affect the inflation outlook. In this context, the rise in inflation was driven by core goods, food and energy groups. Dear Participants, Before moving on to our medium-term forecasts, I think it would be useful to include our assessments of the main macro determinants of inflation. The output gap indicators monitored by the Central Bank continue to point to economic activity above the potential in the last quarter of the year. With the reduction of pandemic-related risks, deferred expenditures were realized quickly in the third quarter and domestic demand accelerated. In the following three-month period, we observe that domestic demand maintained its positive course, albeit with a slight decline. In this period, external demand maintained its positive course due to both the goods and services sectors. We assess that growth takes place in a more balanced composition. In the last quarter, the pricing behavior indexed to exchange rates due to unhealthy price formations in the foreign exchange market was the most important determinant of the rise in inflation. In this context, core goods and energy groups came to the fore, while items with high exchange rate sensitivity diverged negatively within the food and services groups. The high course of international commodity prices continues to have an impact on producer and consumer prices, as is the case all over the world. Agricultural product prices rose again after following a moderate course in the third quarter. Although international energy and industrial metal prices declined slightly after October, they completed the last quarter of the year with an increase. In addition to exchange rate developments and import prices that maintain an upward trend, disruptions in supply chains that have become evident again cause producer prices to rise. When we look at the supplier delivery times published within the scope of Turkey PMI data, we see that the ongoing improvement trend has reversed in the last months of the year and delivery times have been extended again. Freight prices, although they have retreated slightly, maintain their course at high levels, confirming that supply-side problems continue. Medium-Term Forecasts Dear Participants, I would like to move on to our medium-term forecasts after briefly evaluating the monetary policy developments within the framework I have summarized so far. We evaluated the analyses aimed at decomposing the effects of demand factors, core inflation developments and supply shocks that monetary policy can affect, and we cut the policy rate by a total of 500 basis points in the September-December period. As we mentioned in our December communication, we have completed the use of the space implied by the temporary effects of supply-side and non-monetary policy incidental factors on price increases. When we came to January, we decided to keep the one-week repo auction rate constant at 14 percent. We closely monitor the cumulative effects of the decisions taken and carry out a comprehensive policy framework review process that prioritizes the Turkish lira in all policy instruments of the CBRT in order to reshape price stability on a sustainable basis. While producing medium-term forecasts, we have taken the economic outlook that I have summarized so far as a starting point. We have reviewed and updated our assumptions for external factors such as import prices, food prices, global growth and fiscal policy. Although international commodity prices maintained their high levels compared to the previous reporting period, they followed a volatile course due to uncertainties caused by the omicron variant. While crude oil prices fell in December on concerns about the pandemic, they rose again in January on the expectation that the effects of the omicron variant on global energy demand will be limited. Natural gas prices, which declined after the increases seen in the previous reporting period, still remain at high levels. Futures price curves indicate that crude oil prices will remain slightly above the October Inflation Report assumptions in the upcoming period. Accordingly, our assumptions for crude oil prices have been revised to an average of USD 80.4 in 2022 and an average of USD 74.3 in 2023. Non-energy commodity prices continued to rise due to supply-demand mismatch, increases in transportation costs and agricultural drought. Our assumptions regarding the general level of import prices have also been revised upwards. We revised food prices upwards for 2022 and 2023, taking into account the cumulative effects of ongoing increases in international food prices, especially exchange rate developments, and agricultural drought developments. Due to the increasing uncertainties on global economic activity due to the omicron variant, we revised our assumptions regarding external demand slightly down compared to the previous reporting period. We also assumed that financial conditions would be tighter in 2022 than projected in the previous reporting period due to the rise in global inflation. While producing medium-term forecasts, we took as a basis an outlook in which macroeconomic policies are determined in a coordinated manner with a medium-term perspective focused on reducing inflation. Dear Participants, Now, I will share with you our inflation forecasts that we have produced within this general framework. Within the framework of our basic assumptions and short-term projections, we anticipate that inflation will gradually converge to the targets with the disappearance of base effects, under an outlook in which the monetary policy stance will be determined in line with the sustainable price stability target. An important element I would like to point out regarding our forecasts is related to our forecast ranges. As inflation rises, the distribution in inflation expectations widens, thus widening the range within which inflation can be predicted. This is reflected in our forecast path. Accordingly, the midpoints of our inflation forecast range correspond to 23.2 percent at the end of 2022, 8.2 percent at the end of 2023 and 5.0 percent at the end of 2024. Thus, we raised our end-2022 inflation forecast by 11.4 points from 11.8 percent to 23.2 percent. Compared to the previous reporting period, the revision based on import prices in Turkish lira increased the inflation forecast by 4.2 points; A contribution of 2.5 percentage points came from the increase in the assumption of food prices. On the other hand, administered prices raised the year-end inflation forecast by 3 percentage points, largely due to the increase in alcohol-tobacco prices and electricity and natural gas prices. In addition, unit labor costs had an upward effect of 2.0 points due to the minimum wage increase determined for 2022, while the revision in the output gap lowered the estimates by 0.3 points. We also raised our end-2023 inflation forecast from 7 percent to 8.2 percent. The effects of the revision in initial conditions on the underlying trend of inflation increased the end-2023 inflation forecast by 0.8 points. On the other hand, the revision in the food inflation assumption increased the forecast by 0.1 percentage points. Import prices in Turkish lira contributed to the forecast by 0.5 percentage points, while revisions in the output gap decreased by 0.2 points. Before concluding my speech, I would like to briefly share with you some other points that I consider important. In the recent rise in inflation; For some time, supply-side factors such as increases in global commodity prices and disruptions in supply processes and demand developments have been effective. In recent months, in addition to these, pricing behaviors indexed to exchange rates due to unhealthy price formations in the foreign exchange market have played an important role. With the steps taken to establish price stability and financial stability, the basis for unhealthy price formations has been eliminated. In addition to the results of the steps taken to establish price stability and financial stability, we anticipate that the disinflation process will start in the coming months with the gradual reduction of supply-demand mismatches and disruptions in supply processes. Capacity utilization levels and other leading indicators indicate that domestic economic activity remains strong on the back of external demand. We attach importance to eliminating supply-demand mismatches and capacity constraints that increase inflation and strengthening the trend in the current account balance. In this context, we closely monitor commercial and personal loans. We consider it necessary for sustainable price stability that the resources provided to the economy are effectively directed to activities that are suitable for their purpose. We are closely monitoring the cumulative effects of the decisions taken with the first quarter of the new year. In this period, in order to reshape price stability on a sustainable basis, we are conducting a comprehensive policy framework review process that prioritizes the Turkish lira in all policy instruments of the CBRT. In this context, the "Liraization Strategy" is one of the essential elements of the CBRT's policy review process. As we have stated in our box study in the report, the "Liraization Strategy" is created with a holistic approach that focuses on the use of the Turkish lira in the system through new financial products, collateral diversification and liquidity management practices. As part of this strategy, the CBRT has recently implemented a number of measures. As you know, in December 2021, a step was taken to strengthen the preference for TL deposits by supporting the conversion of foreign currency and gold deposits into TL. With the complementary product of the Ministry of Treasury and Finance, unhealthy price formations in exchange rates have been prevented. In terms of the effectiveness of the monetary policy transmission mechanism, elements of liquidity management such as the amount of funding, the instruments used, distribution, maturity and collateral structure are important. In this context, the size of OMO and swap transactions, their share in total toning, their distribution on the basis of facilities and the collateralization structure, which are the main components of the current Turkish Lira liquidity management, are reviewed within the scope of the "Liraization" strategy. The use of the loans provided by the financial system to the real sector in accordance with their stated purposes is essential for strengthening the foundations of the Turkish lira as the meeting strengthens financial stability. In this context, the CBRT supports exports and investments through rediscount and Advance Loans with Investment Commitments (YTAK). On the one hand, by supporting exports and current account balance, investments and employment with targeted loans; On the other hand, we will contribute to the establishment of price stability on a sustainable basis by taking steps to stabilize credit growth with a balanced composition. Within the framework of the liraization strategy of the CBRT in the policy review process, the focus of all the measures to be put into effect in the short, medium and long term will be to ensure the liraization of the financial system in order to reshape price stability on a sustainable basis. In closing, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to all members of the Monetary Policy Committee and the staff of the Research and Monetary Policy Department, as well as all those who took part in the preparations for the Report and the press conference. Once again, I would like to express my gratitude to our esteemed guests who followed our meeting from afar. Now, I can take the questions from you, taking into account our time.

Title: Speech at the Assembly Meeting of the Istanbul Chamber of Industry titled "External Balance, Sustainable Growth and Price Stability"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: ISTANBUL CHAMBER OF INDUSTRY (ISO) SPEECH 27 November 2019 Murat UYSAL Dear Members of Istanbul Chamber of Industry, Dear Guests, Dear Members of the Press, Before I begin, I would like to thank Mr. President and the Istanbul Chamber of Industry for their kind invitation. As the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, I have previously expressed the importance we attach to better understanding the real sector and strengthening communication in this direction on various platforms. I consider this meeting as an important step towards the implementation of the framework I have mentioned. In my speech today, I will touch upon the issue of external balance, which is one of the important agenda items in terms of balanced and sustainable growth in our country's economy. As you have all followed, the current account balance has improved significantly in the last year and has started to run an annual surplus for the first time since 2002. According to current projections, we will have a current account surplus in a year of positive growth by the end of this year. With the effect of prudent macro policies implemented in coordination, the gains we have achieved in the external balance will continue in the coming periods; price stability is of great importance for financial stability and sustainable growth. In this context, my speech consists of three parts: In the first part, I will talk about the sources of the rapid improvement in the current account balance in Turkey in 2019. In the second part of my speech, in terms of sustainable growth and price stability in Turkey, foreign countries 2 I will point out the decisive role of balance. In the last part, I will emphasize the structural and macroprudential policy steps that have been implemented and will be implemented for the strong continuation of the concrete gains we have achieved in the external balance. Dear Guests, The external balance of a country, in its simplest definition, shows the economic transactions that the residents of an economy have made with the residents abroad in a certain period. On the one hand, the concept of external balance reflects the consumption, saving, investment and production decisions of the economic units in that country, and on the other hand, it plays a decisive role in ensuring sustainable growth, price stability and financial stability. Therefore, in a country like Turkey, which has been experiencing a current account deficit for many years, considering the external balance dynamics together with cyclical and structural factors is of critical importance for the continuation of macroeconomic stability. The current account balance improved rapidly with the stabilization process that started in the second quarter of 2018 and gave an annual surplus in June of this year for the first time in many years. The improvement in the current account balance continued in the third quarter and reached an annual surplus of approximately USD 6 billion as of September. Thus, it is estimated that the current account balance, which had a deficit of 6.5 percent as a proportion of national income in the second quarter of 2018, reached a surplus of approximately 1 percent as of the third quarter of 2019. At this point, I would like to remind you that the current account balance is the most in our history. 3 Following one of its deep crises, it last posted an annual surplus in November 2002 and ran a continuous deficit from that time until June 2019. From this point of view, it is of great importance to compare the dynamics that bring about the current correction in the current account balance with previous periods and to identify the differences. As you know, there is a close relationship between growth and imports in Turkey depending on the production structure. For this reason, we see that historically, the improvements in the current account deficit generally coincide with periods when economic activity weakened significantly. However, the recent stabilization process incorporates different features compared to past periods. First of all, I would like to underline that the correction in the current account balance in the current period has been much healthier compared to the crises of 2001 and 2009, when the economy contracted sharply. The fact that we have reached the point of current account surplus in a period when the slowdown in economic activity is relatively limited points to a transformation beyond cyclical effects. Dear Guests, As the Central Bank, how do we read the improvement in the current account balance? When we examine the last decade, we see that the main determinant of the improvement in the current account balance in the periods of 2009 and 2011-2014 was the import developments. In addition to the slowdown in imports, it is possible to say that the strong upward trend in exports of goods and services is also effective in the rapid recovery in the near term. At this point, the current 4 I would like to explain a little about the main factors that have been decisive on the recent improvement in the balance. First of all, let's consider import developments. Academic studies on Turkey show that imports can be explained at a meaningful level by changes in real income and real exchange rates. These studies indicate that the income elasticity of imports is higher than relative prices. In this context, we can say that the slowdown in domestic demand since the second quarter of 2018 has significantly limited imports. However, we also observe that the relationship between imports and national income has weakened significantly in the recent period. We assess that the long-term adaptation in the real exchange rate and the change in the production structure of the companies are effective in this development. In this context, in a conjuncture in which economic activity will gradually recover in the future, we can expect the effect of growth on the current account balance to be relatively less due to the limiting effect of relative prices. Another factor that should not be ignored in the improvement in the current account deficit is the developments in crude oil and commodity prices. Due to the high energy and commodity-based imported input component in Turkey's production and export structure, excessive movements in international prices, especially oil and metal, can create fluctuations in imports independent of demand conditions. For example, as we mentioned in a box study we included in our last Inflation Report, 5 We can say that the significant decline in oil prices since the end of 2014 has significantly limited the current account deficit. Similarly, in a conjuncture where the Brent oil price, which averaged USD 71 in 2018, is at more moderate levels due to the slowdown in global growth, it seems highly likely that our energy imports, which were USD 43 billion last year, will be more limited this year. Dear Guests, I would like to open a separate paragraph on the effect of the real exchange rate on the current account balance. Studies conducted within our Bank indicate that relative price developments are an important determinant of exports as well as imports. We see that the real exchange rate sensitivity of exports is stronger in services, especially in tourism and transportation, and that it can be quite different in terms of regions and country groups such as the European Union, the Middle East and North Africa. When we evaluate the recent developments in this context, I should state that the strong course in exports has also made an important contribution to the improvement in the current account balance. Despite the weakening in the global growth outlook, especially in the European Union region, exports of goods and services continue to increase with the positive effect of the companies' orientation to exports, the flexibility of market and product diversification and the developments in competitiveness. Under this outlook, Turkey is able to counteract the effects of the slowdown in global trade volume by increasing its share of the trade pie. 6 However, as I mentioned earlier, the positive outlook in exports is not only driven by manufacturing industry-led trade in goods. We see that the tourism sector, which weakened significantly in 2016 due to geopolitical developments and greatly limited economic growth, entered a rapid recovery process in the following period and the number of foreign visitors continued to increase strongly. When we examine the composition of tourists in terms of countries, reaching significant figures in regions outside Europe and the Commonwealth of Independent States provides significant flexibility. Just as in the export of goods, the increasing diversity of markets in tourism allows us to soften the negative effects of shocks specific to certain countries or regions. In addition to its direct effects, this trend in tourism is one of the important components of the recovery and stabilization process in the economy through related sectors, especially transportation services. In summary, in recent years, with the support of competitiveness gains, we have been able to increase our share of world trade in goods and services. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey also supports this process by providing credit financing to exporters through Eximbank and commercial banks. In recent years, we have made a number of arrangements to increase the limits on export rediscount loans, to expand the scope of credit and to provide ease of use. The financial architecture we are carrying out for the hedging and pricing of Turkish lira-denominated assets in the coming period 7 In addition to our work, we will continue to support the real sector in financial risk management and access to credit by effectively using macroprudential tools such as reserve obligations. Although we are always urgently implementing the necessary arrangements in these areas within the framework of our toolkit, it is critical that these policies are supported by structural steps to ensure that the improvement in the current account balance is permanent. It should not be forgotten that the long-term drivers of exports will be supply-side competitiveness gains such as productivity and quality. We find that there have been promising developments in this direction recently. At this point, I would like to share some of our observations from our recent meetings with valuable real sector representatives, including you. During the fluctuation in our economy last year, we observed that the majority of our companies focused on the management of production processes, increased their productivity and quality studies, and attached importance to strengthening the production chain they are in and protecting their suppliers. We assess that these efforts will contribute to a stronger and more competitive structure of our companies. Despite the slowdown in foreign markets, trade wars and geopolitical risks, our real sector makes a significant contribution to the stabilization in the economy with a strong export performance. We assess that the success achieved in product and market diversity plays a critical role in export performance. In this process, 8 In addition to our traditional exporting sectors, our companies have achieved significant success in new markets, especially in the defense industry, chemical, furniture and construction sub-industry sectors. Expanding into new markets contributes to the diversification and deepening of our export composition. Although we have observed significant increases in the domestic content of production in recent years in sectors such as defense industry, textile, machinery-equipment, fabricated metal, medicine, chemistry and energy, we are aware that there is a long way to go in this field. Undoubtedly, policy steps to be taken to reduce the rate of imported inputs of production will make a significant contribution to the direction of the economy on a balanced and sustainable growth path. Dear Guests, I must say that the increasing awareness and steps taken in recent years regarding the structural elements of the current account balance have yielded positive results in terms of permanent improvement. Macroprudential measures to link foreign currency borrowing by firms with foreign currency revenues, the implementation of the Automatic PPS Participation application to increase domestic savings and the support given to exports contribute to this improvement. In addition, the fact that fiscal policy is based on a framework that does not disrupt fiscal discipline while supporting growth supports the improvement process in the current account balance. 9 In this context, I can say that since the second quarter of 2018, there has been an improvement in the current account balance beyond what the cyclical factors imply. Title: Speech of President Ba at the Press Conference on the Introduction of "Inflation Report 2014-I"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: 2014 JANUARY INFLATION REPORT PRESS CONFERENCE Erdem BACI 28 January 2014, Ankara Dear Guests, Welcome to the press conference where we will share the main messages of the Inflation Report with you. I would like to present to you an overview of the Report, which will be published on our website in a moment. In the Report, as always, we share our assessments of macroeconomic developments with the economic outlook that form the basis for monetary policy decisions and present our medium-term inflation forecasts and monetary policy stance updated in line with the developments in the last three months. In addition, in addition to the main sections in the Report, we have included eight boxes on various topics. Each of these boxes contains analyses of current and interesting topics. I recommend you to take the time to read these studies, which will be published on our website within the scope of the Inflation Report in a moment. Dear Guests, Since developments in the global economy continue to play an important role in our policies, I will begin by referring to the global economic outlook. We can say that the most important development that has marked the economic conjuncture in recent months is the significant slowdown in capital flows to developing countries with the exit process from the Fed's quantitative expansion policy. Capital flows, which showed a weak outlook since May 2013, continued their similar course in the last quarter of the year. In particular, the downward trend in portfolio flows continued (Chart 1). In the first period when the quantitative expansion exit strategy was announced, we observed more limited pricing movements in the exit application due to the fact that most of the repricing in financial assets was experienced. Although this development shows that the perceptions of uncertainty about global monetary policies have partially eased, the continuation of risks related to the recovery rate of the global economy in the coming period keeps the uncertainties alive about the exit process from quantitative expansion and other components of monetary policy, such as verbal guidance. As you have all been following closely, these developments, coupled with domestic uncertainties, have led to a significant increase in volatility in our financial markets in the recent period. Therefore, we also focus on inflation and monetary policy 2 We had to make important updates to the view. Before moving on to our forecasts, I would like to mention the developments that have affected the inflation outlook since the October Inflation Report period and our monetary policy practices. Monetary Policy Practices and Monetary Conditions Dear Guests, In the last quarter of 2013, mainly due to food inflation being higher than expected and exchange rate volatility, inflation exceeded our forecasts in October. In order to prevent this course in inflation from disrupting pricing behavior, we strengthened our cautious stance in monetary policy. In this context, we ended the 1-month repo auctions and ensured that the average funding rate was above the level of 6.75 percent. We followed a liquidity policy with overnight interest rates in the BIST interbank money market close to 7.75 percent (Charts 2 and 3). Since the last Inflation Report, the CBRT has continued to provide foreign currency liquidity to the market through foreign exchange auctions. As a result of our failure to sterilize foreign exchange auctions, the financial system's need for liquidity has increased. We have also shortened the maturity of the average funding we provide. As a result of these developments, the CBRT's average funding rate and BIST interbank overnight repo rates increased (Chart 2). 3 Chart 2.
