Accordingly, on the days when we deemed it necessary to implement additional monetary tightening, we decided to ensure that the interest rates in the interbank market would be around 9 percent instead of 7.75 percent (marginal funding rate). In other words, by designing a more flexible policy framework than in the previous period, we have been able to react more quickly to realizations in possible risks. In the last 3 months, interest rates increased in all maturities with the effect of our cautious stance on monetary policy, the Fed's reduction in the quantitative expansion rate and internal uncertainties (Chart 6). The fact that short-term interest rates are above long-term interest rates means that there is a strong tight stance in monetary policy. At the moment, short-term interest rates and long-term rates are very close to each other. The interest rate corridor system has functioned as a very powerful and effective tool in the past, as it allows us to influence this slope in a short time. The increase in credit rates and risks in the economy affects both credit demand and credit supply. In this context, the growth of consumer loans, in particular, slowed down slightly in the recent period and is still above the reference value (Chart 9). Source: CBRT. 2. Macroeconomic Developments and Basic Assumptions Dear Guests, I will now touch upon the macroeconomic outlook and assumptions that form the basis of our forecasts. First of all, the recent inflation developments 6 I want to summarize. Then, when producing forecasts, I will talk about the domestic and international demand outlook that is based on the base scenario. In 2013, consumer inflation increased by 1.2 percentage points compared to the previous year, exceeding the uncertainty range around the target with a rate of 7.4 percent (Charts 11 and 12). Inflation, which rose at the beginning of the year with the effect of tax adjustments on tobacco products, followed a fluctuating course depending on the price developments of the unprocessed food and energy group in the following period. In the second half of the year, the depreciation of the Turkish lira caused the core inflation indicators to rise, especially through the basic goods group. In addition, the annual increase in food prices beyond the default also affected inflation upwards. On the other hand, the relatively horizontal course of US dollar-based import prices throughout the year and the moderate outlook of managed energy prices limited the rise in inflation. Chart 11. Source: TurkStat, CBRT. * The probability that inflation will remain within the forecast range is 70 percent. Source: TurkStat, CBRT. When we examine the contributions to inflation on the basis of subgroups in 2013, we see that the total contribution of food and energy did not change compared to the previous year; we see that the rise in inflation is due to core inflation indicators and tax adjustments. In this period, the contribution of the service and basic goods groups to inflation was 0.8 points, and the contribution of the alcohol-tobacco group to inflation was 0.4 points. While the increase in basic goods was largely due to the exchange rate, there was no significant change in the outlook for services inflation compared to the end of the previous year, except for definitional differences and temporary movements. 7 Dear Guests, I would now like to summarize the economic activity developments and the short-term outlook that form the basis for inflation forecasts. According to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data for the third quarter of 2013, economic activity was largely in line with the outlook we set out in the October Inflation Report. Final domestic demand increased modestly in the third quarter (Chart 13). When we examine the final domestic demand components, we see that private sector demand continues its steady upward trend, while public sector demand, which recorded a very strong increase in the first quarter, declined in the third quarter as well as in the second quarter. In this period, net exports made a positive contribution to the growth of the period. Chart 13. When evaluated by production, the industrial production index was above the average of the previous quarter in the October-November period and continued its steady upward trend on a periodical basis. When examined by spending, production, import and survey data for both consumer and investment goods show that private sector demand will maintain its steady upward trend in the last quarter. On the other hand, when considered as trade in goods excluding gold, the stabilization process continued in the last quarter of the year (Chart 14). Excluding the temporary volatility in gold trading in the recent period, 12 months reflecting the main trend in the current account balance 8 we see that the current account deficit, excluding cumulative gold, continues its improving trend (Chart 15). While the Turkish lira has depreciated in the recent period, we have seen an increase in loan rates and a decrease in consumer confidence. In this context, we anticipate that private sector demand will decline in the first quarter with the decline in durable consumption and investment expenditures, which are sensitive to exchange rate, financing and confidence conditions. In the following period, the course of private sector demand will depend on how long and at what level the exchange rate and interest rates, consumer and investor confidence will come to balance. In producing our forecasts in the Inflation Report to be published shortly, we assumed that domestic demand developments would partially limit the cost-side price pressures observed in the near term. The slowdown we expect in domestic demand will also contribute to the improvement we have recently observed in the current account deficit and the balancing process. In addition, with the support of the recovery in the demand of European countries, we expect a partial acceleration in exports in the coming period. As a result, we have based on an outlook in which aggregate demand for the upcoming period will have a decreasing effect on inflation and the demand components will be positively balanced. Dear Guests, As you know, food, energy and import prices also play an important role in inflation forecasts. So, before we move on to the predictions, I will briefly convey our assumptions about the variables in question. While U.S. dollar-based import prices in the last quarter of the year were slightly below our assumptions in the October Inflation Report, oil prices 9 in line with projections (Chart 16). We have updated our assumption of average import price increase for 2014 to a limited extent upwards. On the other hand, we maintained the levels in the October Inflation Report for the 2014 average oil price assumption. In other words, we have taken as a basis a framework in which there was no significant pressure on inflation in 2014 from import prices. However, in this Report we assumed that the impact of exchange rate movements on the 2014 year-end inflation forecast would be 0.5 percentage points higher than in the October Inflation Report. Taking into account the negative price movements and historical averages we observed in food prices in the recent period, we lowered our assumption about the 2014 year-end food price increase rate to 8 percent. The impact of this update on our 2014 year-end inflation forecast was about 0.3 percentage points upwards. In addition, we anticipate that the tax adjustments made in automobile and tobacco prices at the beginning of January will affect inflation at the end of 2014 by approximately 0.5 percentage points. We assumed that there would be no additional adjustment in these prices for the rest of the year, and that there would be increases in electricity and natural gas prices in line with the inflation target. As always, we have taken the Medium-Term Program projections as the basis for the fiscal policy stance. Against this backdrop, we assumed that the cautious fiscal stance would continue and that non-interest spending would be kept under control. 10 3. Inflation and Monetary Policy Outlook Dear Guests, I will now present to you our inflation and output gap estimates that we have produced within the framework I have drawn. While formulating our medium-term forecasts, we assumed that monetary policy was tightened further and that the annual credit growth rate converged to the reference value of 15 percent as of the second half of 2014 with the contribution of the macroprudential measures taken. In this context, we estimate that inflation will be in the range of 5.2 percent to 8 percent, with a 70 percent probability and a midpoint of 6.6 percent at the end of 2014. Our 2015 year-end forecast is in the range of 3.1 percent to 6.9 percent, with a midpoint of 5 percent. We anticipate that inflation will stabilize at 5 percent in the medium term (Chart 17). Source: CBRT. As a result, we have updated our 2014 year-end inflation forecast by 1.3 percentage points upwards according to the October Inflation Report, mainly due to food and exchange rate developments and tax adjustments. Accordingly, we anticipate that inflation will remain significantly above the 5 percent target in the short term. We estimate that the secondary effects of the policy measures we have taken and will take and the exchange rate developments will be limited and that inflation will decrease from the second half of the year to 6.6 percent at the end of the year (Chart 17). 11 In addition to these forecasts I have mentioned, in the Risks section of the Inflation Report, we refer to the inflation outlook and alternative scenarios for the global economy. You can review the Report for details. Dear Guests, In the last part of my speech, I would like to give some additional messages. On the current account balance side, we expect more positive developments to be observed in 2014. Under a scenario where the growth rate of loans falls to 15 percent, our current account deficit may fall below 5 percent at the end of the year. It will take time for us to see these improvements as the data is delayed disclosed. On inflation, upside risks have become evident recently. As the Central Bank, we are focused on the impact of recent developments on inflation. We will hold an off-calendar Monetary Policy Committee meeting this evening to assess recent developments in this regard and to discuss the policy measures necessary for price stability. Our aim will be to take steps to ensure price stability by preventing the deterioration in pricing behavior. Dear Guests, Before concluding my speech, I would like to emphasize here again that we will do our part to ensure and maintain price stability. It is our main duty to protect and further the gains we have made in the fight against inflation since 2002. Accordingly, no one should doubt that the Central Bank will effectively use all the tools at its disposal to bring inflation under control and towards the 5 percent target. In concluding my speech here, I would like to express my gratitude to all my colleagues and participants who contributed to the preparation of the Report, especially the employees of our General Directorate of Research and Monetary Policy and the members of the Monetary Policy Committee. 12

Title: Speech at the Informative Meeting on the Introduction of "Inflation Report 2021-I"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Naci A?bal, Central Bank Governor Inflation Report Briefing Meeting 20201-I 28 January 2021, Ankara 2 Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the Information Meeting of the first Inflation Report of this year. In my speech, I will share with you our evaluations of the economy and inflation outlook and make statements about our medium-term inflation forecasts and monetary policy strategy. Then I will answer your questions. Macroeconomic Outlook Dear participants; The pandemic measures implemented in some countries in the last quarter of 2020 slowed the recovery trend in global growth, but positive developments in vaccines and treatment strengthened the expectation of a faster recovery in the second half of 2021. Inflation is low in both developed and developing countries. However, in 2021, the risks on global inflation are considered to be predominantly upwards. In addition to rising commodity prices and a possible improvement in demand conditions, the high volume, fiscal and monetary expansion implemented against the epidemic has the potential to create inflationary pressure for the coming period. Under this outlook, the expansionary stance in monetary policy in developed and developing countries is expected to continue. The monetary policy outlook of developed countries and positive expectations for the global recovery increase risk appetite for developing country assets. As a matter of fact, we see that portfolio inflows to developing countries have accelerated recently. In our country, economic activity shows a significant recovery in the third quarter of 2020 due to domestic demand with the support of strong credit momentum. We see that economic activity followed a strong course in the fourth quarter as well. Industrial production, retail sales and turnover indices also showed a strong increase in the fourth quarter compared to the third quarter. The strong recovery in economic activity is also spread across sectors. In this period, apart from some sectors related to exports and tourism, the pre-pandemic production levels of the manufacturing industry in general were also exceeded. Especially in the durable consumer goods sector, which includes vehicles, furniture and white goods, production, order and capacity utilization rates showed a very strong recovery. In the construction-related intermediate goods sectors, the same indicators point to a stronger course. On the other hand, the improvement in tourism-related manufacturing sectors, especially clothing, has been limited. In the services sector, turnover in many sub-sectors exceeded pre-pandemic levels, while in the accommodation, food, airline and travel agency sector, which was adversely affected by the epidemic, there is still a course below the pre-epidemic levels. The strong recovery in economic activity has also led to an improvement in the employment market, with a significant presence in the industrial sector. While employment opportunities are expanding, the labor force participation rate is also recovering. However, in the recent period, the effects of pandemic-related restrictions on the employment of the services sector have begun to be seen. Near-term indicators of the level of economic activity also indicate some slowdown due to pandemic-related restrictions and the tightening of financial conditions. We see that the most important determinant of the strong recovery that started in the third quarter of 2020 is strong credit growth. Annual credit growth accelerated from the second quarter onwards, leading to an expansion well beyond the rapid credit expansion from the Credit Guarantee Fund in 2017. 3 caused. This strong credit expansion is evident in corporate loans as well as in personal loans, especially in housing and consumer loans. As of the second quarter, the net loan volume opened by banks in Turkish lira was 518 billion Turkish Liras. Due to the monetary tightening and other policies implemented in the third quarter, loan rates began to rise, and a significant slowdown was achieved in the acceleration of loans. With the effect of credit expansion, a significant monetary expansion took place during the epidemic period. The broadly defined M2 money supply, which includes foreign currency deposit accounts including gold, increased by 33 percent to 833 billion Turkish liras compared to February 2020. The increase in the use of net credit, especially personal loans, well above historical averages, caused the current account deficit to rise significantly in 2020, when gold imports rose rapidly and tourism revenues declined sharply. As of November, the 12-month cumulative current account deficit had risen to around 38 billion. Along with the increasing current account deficit, capital outflows in line with global developments have also led to a significant loss of reserves. As a result of the increasing macrofinancial risks due to the deterioration in the external balance, the country's risk premium increased, volatility and depreciation in exchange rates were observed and borrowing costs increased. Under this outlook, the dollarization of deposits of domestic residents has increased. Dear Members of the Press, Dear Participants, Now, I would like to share with you our information and evaluations about the inflation outlook shaped under this macroeconomic outlook. The cumulative cost effects of the exchange rate, especially domestic demand conditions, the rise in international food and other commodity prices and the high course of inflation expectations continue to adversely affect pricing behavior and the inflation outlook. Consumer inflation increased from 11.75 percent in September 2020 to 14.60 percent at the end of the year. Thus, inflation was above the forecast band we shared in the October Inflation Report. Basic goods and food groups have been decisive in the rise in inflation. In the period following the October Inflation Report, the contribution of the basic goods group to annual inflation increased by 1.5 points to 4.7 points, while the contribution of the food group increased by 1.3 points to 4.7 points. On the other hand, the energy and alcoholic beverage and tobacco groups significantly limited consumer inflation with a total contribution of 0.7 percentage points. Inflation is relatively low in items such as clothing, accommodation, education, entertainment and cultural services, where demand conditions are weak due to the pandemic. On the other hand, inflation is quite high in some subgroups where demand is strong due to credit expansion, especially durable goods. When the sub-items of consumer inflation are examined, it is seen that the annual inflation in basic food products and durable goods has risen well above the historical averages. The annual inflation and trend of the core indicators are also high. While the inflation trend remains high in basic goods, there is a gradual rise in services, while in processed food, upside risks are significantly increasing. It is also seen that the tendency to increase prices is high compared to historical averages and is generalized. Producer inflation maintains its upward trend. Annual inflation in producer prices reached 25.15 percent in December 2020. Despite the positive contribution of the exchange rate in the recent period, producer prices, which have been high under the leadership of international commodity prices, continue to exert upward pressure on consumer prices. As of sub-items 4 When examined, inflation is quite high in metal and metal-related groups, paper and paper products, food, motor vehicles and transportation vehicles. Dear Participants, At this point, I think it would be useful to mention the factors affecting inflation. First of all, the development of the output gap on aggregate demand conditions affected inflationary pressures as an important indicator. With the cumulative effects of rapid credit expansion, demand conditions remained strong in the second half of 2020 and output gap indicators reached inflationary levels. Despite the limiting effect of the weak course in the tourism and service-related sectors most affected by the pandemic limiting the total output gap, the strong course in the generalized spending groups stimulated by the rapid credit expansion was decisive in this development. In the third quarter of 2020, due to the improvement in financing conditions and the effect of deferred demand, private consumption demand was well above the increase in national income and was the spending component that made the highest contribution to growth. Despite the limiting effect of tourism, it is understood that the aggregate demand conditions in the last quarter of 2020 are still at inflationary levels with the cumulative effects of strong credit momentum and the contribution of external demand. However, we think that economic activity reached its peak cyclically in the last quarter of 2020 and began to converge to its trend with the slowdown in the first quarter of 2021. The impact on consumer and producer inflation from the exchange rate, which is one of the important determinants of inflation, also strengthened in the second half of 2020. Although the reflection of the developments in exchange rates on inflation may differ according to the conjuncture, it is basically realized through three separate channels. These are the demand channel, the cost channel, and the expectation channel. Exchange rate transitivity is higher than historical averages during periods of economic upswing and periods when the exchange rate increases rapidly. The decline in exchange rates in recent months indicates that the exchange rate-induced effects on inflation will weaken in the coming period. Another factor that has an impact on inflation is the upward developments in international commodity prices, especially in the recent period. The upward trend in the prices of oil, industrial metals and agricultural commodities creates an upward pressure on inflation through energy, food and basic goods through input costs. On the other hand, as we mentioned in the January Monetary Policy Committee decision, when the worldwide supply problems and increases in freight costs are taken into consideration, we assess that the supply constraints that have become evident in some sectors also increase the risks on consumer prices. Finally, high levels of survey-based and market pricing-based inflation expectations continue to pose risks to pricing behavior and the inflation outlook. Medium-Term Forecasts and Risks Dear Participants, Before moving on to our forecasts for the medium-term inflation outlook, I would like to share with you our basic assumptions on which we base our forecast. When producing medium-term forecasts, we based the macrofinancial conditions and inflation outlook that I have summarized so far. In addition, we have reviewed and updated our assumptions for external factors such as import prices, food prices and fiscal policy. With the recent rise in oil prices and the strengthening of global recovery expectations, expectations for crude oil prices have been updated upwards. Futures price curves show that the average crude oil price is 54.4 for 2021; For 2022, 5 It points to a 52.1 issue. On the other hand, in addition to oil, we see a trend above forecasts in commodity prices such as industrial metals and agricultural products. Accordingly, we have updated our assumption of import prices in US dollars for 2021 upwards. Taking into account the recent trends in unprocessed food prices, exchange rate developments and international prices, we revised our assumption of food inflation for 2021 to 11.5 percent, an increase of 1 point. We consider the most obvious upside risks to our food assumption as demand effects due to the course of international prices and the possible improvement in the tourism outlook during the year. We have taken as a basis a medium-term outlook in which fiscal and fiscal policies will be determined and implemented in a macro framework in coordination with monetary policy and in line with the predicted path of decline in inflation. In this respect, we assess that the Central Government budget deficit target for 2021, which has recently been revised downwards as 3.5 percent compared to national income, will support the monetary policy targets. In addition, within the framework of a strong policy coordination, we anticipated that credit policies would develop in line with monetary policy objectives during the year. Dear Participants, I will now share with you our inflation and output gap estimates that we have produced within this general framework that I have drawn. Within the framework of basic assumptions and short-term projections, we assess that inflation will gradually converge to targets. Under a view that the tight monetary policy stance will be resolutely maintained for a long time until there are strong indicators pointing to a permanent decline in inflation and price stability, we estimate that inflation will stabilize at 9.4 percent at the end of 2021, to 7 percent at the end of 2022 and to the medium-term target of 5 percent at the end of 2023. Thus, we have maintained the 2021 and 2022 year-end inflation forecasts foreseen in the October Inflation Report. However, we are also aware that upside risks to these forecasts remain significantly significant. Therefore, we have to maintain our strong tight monetary policy stance. For 2021, the update due to import prices in Turkish lira compared to the previous Report period, while the inflation forecast decreased by 0.4 points; The unit labor cost had an increasing effect of 1.0 points depending on the minimum wage increase determined for 2021. On the other hand, the predicted high course in food prices increased the inflation forecast by 0.2 points; managed/directed prices lowered the forecast by 0.3 percentage points, largely driven by tax adjustment on tobacco products. In addition, we assess that the projected improvement in inflation expectations with the continuation of the tight monetary stance will contribute to the year-end forecast by 0.5 percentage points. The forecasts were produced under the assumption of a level of monetary tightness that would allow inflation to align with the forecast targets for 2021 and 2022. In addition, we have taken as a basis a view that a negative shock caused by the pandemic will not be experienced again in the global growth and external demand outlook, and that the improvement in Turkey's risk perceptions will continue with the positive developments in global risk appetite. In the forecast path we have created for 2021, wages, food prices and international commodity prices inflation is upwards, while managed/directed prices and inflation expectations affect inflation downwards. In this interaction, we anticipate that the strong effect of the tight monetary stance will enable year-end inflation to decline to 9.4 percent. Monetary Policy Strategy In this context, I would like to explain how we will reach our medium-term 5 percent target, which points to both the year-end forecast target and price stability, within a strategy and process. First of all, I have to do some due diligence. The current level of inflation and upward 6 When the risks are evaluated together, we are far from our 5 percent target. Within the forecast path we have shared, we can only reach the 5 percent target by the end of 2023. In order to achieve this goal, we will resolutely implement the inflation targeting regime in all its elements in 2021. Our tight and prudent stance on monetary policy will be resolutely maintained for a long time until 2023, when we will reach the 5 percent target. In the 2021 Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy document, I shared that we will resolutely take a tight monetary stance this year with strong indicators pointing to a permanent decline in inflation and price stability. In this context, I also stated that we will use all the tools at our disposal effectively by simplifying the monetary policy operational framework. As a result, we tightened monetary policy strongly and raised the policy interest rate from 10.25 percent to 15 percent and then to 17 percent. Taking into account the risks arising on inflation, we have also stated in the latest Monetary Policy Committee decision that we will make additional tightening if necessary. Therefore, in order to reach the 5 percent target, the Monetary Policy Committee will continue to use all the tools at its disposal. We will also closely monitor the development of inflation within the framework of the forecast path we foresee. In the event that any new data to be obtained in addition to the existing data indicate the risk of deviation from the medium-term target path in inflation expectations and pricing behavior, additional tightening will be made with determination. In this context, we will closely monitor the main trend of inflation and indicators related to pricing behavior, spread indices, demand and cost factors and the alignment of inflation expectations with the targets within the forecast horizon. It is possible to describe the tightness level of the monetary stance on the way to reaching the 5 percent target as follows. The level between the expected inflation rate path and the monetary policy interest rate path until the 5 percent target is reached will be established by observing a strong disinflationary balance and this balance will be maintained continuously. This tight stance in monetary policy will contribute to the reduction of the country's risk premium, the encouragement of Turkish lira savings, the initiation of reverse currency substitution, the upward trend of foreign exchange reserves and the permanent decline in financing costs within the target horizon, that is, until 2023. Thus, while macroeconomic and financial stability will be positively affected, it will also allow the tightness level of monetary policy to be adapted under these conditions. On the other hand, fiscal consolidation, which will be provided by strengthening the coordination between monetary and fiscal policy within the framework of strong policy coordination in achieving the medium-term 5 percent target, will provide a very important input to our inflation targets. In addition, the reform steps to be taken by our government in the field of law and economy will provide an important support to the disinflationary process through expectation. Dear Members of the Press, Before I end my presentation, I would like to share with you once again the importance of price stability for our country. Price stability is a prerequisite for sustainable growth, employment, social welfare and equitable income distribution. Price stability increases confidence in the economy, so that investments and production increase and unemployment decreases. If we ensure price stability permanently, we will protect the value of our money and strengthen the ability of our money to be a means of exchange and saving. If we permanently establish price stability, we will reduce the risk premium of our country, reverse the dollarization trend, reduce and reduce the borrowing costs of the public and private sectors. We extend the borrowing maturities of the public and private sectors, and thus strengthen our economy and financial system, like many developed and developing countries. For this reason, we will continue to make a patient and determined effort for this goal without losing sight of the importance of price stability. When we reach this goal, we will all benefit from it as a nation. Within this framework, permanent 7 In order to establish and sustain price stability, the necessity of a determined and determined struggle based on common sense with the contribution of all stakeholders maintains its importance. In line with the goal of ensuring price stability, as the Central Bank, we will continue to implement all the tools at our disposal in a full-time, effective, strong and decisive manner. We will carry out an open, sincere and effective cooperation and communication policy in order to transform this process into a process that is embraced by all parties. In this context, the call for support and cooperation for price stability jointly made by the Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Turkey, the Confederation of Tradesmen and Craftsmen of Turkey, T86S?AD and M86S?AD is very important and I thank them. In this context, we are launching visits, meetings and media programs in order to share the importance of price stability and our anti-inflation policies that we have implemented in this direction with all stakeholders and to create social awareness about the fight against inflation. I hope that the meetings and organizations we will hold in this context will bring about a widespread ownership of price stability throughout the society. As a matter of fact, what is essential in the inflation targeting regime is that all layers of the society focus on the price stability target, believe in it, that decision-makers and policymakers take decisive steps in this direction and see the results of these steps, and then all pricing behaviors and inflation expectations converge to the target set, so we attach great importance to this. I would also like to thank you for your participation in this meeting.

Kamu ve zel sektrn borlanma vadelerini uzatrz ve bylelikle birok gelimi ve gelimekte olan lke gibi ekonomimiz ve finansal sistemimizi glendirmi oluruz. Bu sebeple fiyat istikrarnn nemini aklmzdan hi karmadan bu hedef iin sabrl ve kararl bir aba gstermeye devam edeceiz. Bu hedefe vardmzda ise bundan hepimiz millet olarak istifade edeceiz. Title: Speech of Chairman Murat etinkaya at the Informative Meeting on the Introduction of "Inflation Report 2017-II"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: 2017 APRIL INFLATION REPORT INFORMATION MEETING Murat Cetinkaya 28 April 2017, Istanbul Dear Guests, Welcome to the informative meeting where we will share the main messages of the April 2017 Inflation Report with you. In the report, as always, we share our assessments of macroeconomic developments with the economic outlook that forms the basis for monetary policy decisions and present our medium-term inflation forecasts and monetary policy stance updated in line with the developments in the last three months. In addition to the main sections, we included six boxes on various topics in the report. These studies include analyses of current and interesting topics. The report analyzes the change in inflation dynamics during the inflation targeting period; There are studies that examine the change in the weight structure of the clothing and footwear group in the CPI and examine the recent acceleration in automotive exports from the perspective of EU demand. In addition, introducing the market of foreign exchange deposits in exchange for Turkish lira deposits that we opened in January; There are also studies that examine the cyclical characteristics of tax revenues in Turkey and explain the credit channel, which is important for a better understanding of the monetary policy transmission mechanism and financial stability, through a structural model. You see the titles of the boxes on the mirror. Each sheds light on important issues related to the Turkish economy that are already at the center of current debates. I recommend you to read these studies, which will be published on our website within the scope of the Inflation Report in a moment. Dear Guests, I will begin by referring to the global economic outlook, which continues to play an important role in our policies. Since January 2017, the normalization of the perception of post-election economic policies in the United States, the reduction of uncertainties regarding Fed policies and the positive outlook for global economic activity have reduced volatility in financial markets. Due to the optimistic mood in global financial markets, the rapid upward trend in long-term bond yields of developed countries after the November elections in the US has stopped (Chart 1). In this context, portfolio inflows to developing country debt securities and equity markets have been observed since the last reporting period (Chart 2). 2 Figure 1. 10-Year Bond Yields (Percent) Germany ABD 3,5 England 3,0 Japan 2,5 2,0 1,5 1,0 0,5 0,0 -0,5 Figure 2. Source: EPFR. When we look at the domestic economic outlook, portfolio inflows to Turkey, as in other developing countries, have increased recently. With the effect of the tightening steps in monetary policy, short-term interest rates continued to rise gradually, the slope of the yield curve reversed. However, a decline was observed in the level and volatility of the Turkish lira. On the other hand, macroprudential policies that support the financial system, public finance incentives and supports, and credit growth follow a strong course compared to previous years. This development is mainly due to the improvement of credit conditions for enterprises due to public credit guarantees. The first quarter of the year was a period in which cost pressures on producer prices became evident due to increases in exchange rates and commodity prices, and core inflation indicators increased. In this period, price increases accelerated with the effect of the relative recovery in demand conditions and the rise in inflation expectations. As a result of these developments, consumer inflation rose to 11.29 percent in the first quarter of the year. In the last quarter of 2016, economic activity recorded a moderate growth due to domestic demand after a temporary slowdown in the previous quarter. With the acceleration in exports in the last quarter, the contribution of net external demand to the growth in the period was quite high, and we expect this trend to strengthen in 2017. Indicators for the first quarter indicate that the recovery in economic activity has lost some momentum compared to the last quarter of last year due to the increase in uncertainty caused by volatility in financial markets, the weak course of the labor market and the rapid rise in inflation. However, we anticipate that the outlook for the elements I mentioned will be more positive for the rest of the year. In addition, with the contribution of the strong upward trend in goods exports as well as the supportive incentives and measures taken, we expect the revival in economic activity to gain strength as of the second quarter of the year. 3 1. Monetary Policy Practices and Monetary Conditions Dear Guests, As you have been following closely, at the beginning of January 2017, we carried out a strong monetary tightening in order to limit the reflections of excessive activity in the foreign exchange market, which is not compatible with economic fundamentals, on the inflation outlook. Against this background, as of January 12, 2017, we suspended repo auctions with a maturity of 1 week, gradually reduced marginal funding, and began to provide an increasing part of the system's funding needs through the late liquidity window (GLP) (Chart 3). In addition, we further strengthened monetary tightening by increasing the marginal funding rate by 75 basis points at the January PPK meeting and the GLP lending rate by a total of 225 basis points at the January, March and April PPK meetings. This monetary tightening was also reflected in other money market interest rates (Chart 4). In this period, the fact that BIST overnight repo rates and exchange rate swap market rates acted in line with the CBRT's weighted average funding cost and that the foreign exchange market stabilized relatively indicates that monetary policy transfer took place as intended. Therefore, we will maintain our tight stance on monetary policy until there is a significant improvement in the inflation outlook. When formulating monetary policy, we take into account the medium-term inflation outlook and focus on the developments in the main trend of inflation rather than the fluctuations in inflation due to base effects expected to be observed during the year. We can closely monitor developments in inflation expectations, pricing behavior and other factors affecting inflation and make additional monetary tightening if necessary. Dear Guests, In the first quarter of 2017, despite the rise in the CBRT's funding cost, credit conditions continued to recover thanks to macroprudential policies supporting the financial system, public finance incentives and public loan guarantees. Due to the impact of macroprudential policies and other measures taken to support access to credit, the increase in both consumer and commercial loan rates in this period was limited compared to the increase in the CBRT's average funding cost (Chart 7). With the contribution of the incentives and measures taken, we observe that the growth of commercial loans in Turkish lira has gained momentum in recent months (Chart 8). 5 Figure 7. Macroeconomic Developments and Basic Assumptions Dear Guests, In this part of my talk, I will touch on the macroeconomic outlook and assumptions that form the basis of our forecasts. First of all, I would like to summarize the recent inflation developments. Then, I will talk about the domestic and international demand outlook that we base our forecasts on in the base scenario. Consumer inflation was 11.29 percent in March, above the upper band of our January Inflation Report forecasts (Chart 9). A similar outlook was observed in the forecast of consumer inflation in unprocessed food and non-alcohol-tobacco (Chart 10). In addition to the depreciation of the Turkish lira and the rise in import prices, the effect of the increase in food prices was felt in the upward trend in inflation. While core inflation increased during this period, the increase in the contribution of non-core items such as unprocessed food, energy and alcohol-tobacco to inflation was more pronounced (Chart 11). While adverse supply conditions were particularly decisive on fresh fruit and vegetable prices, exchange rate and import price effects were felt more in other food products. Thus, food annual inflation was slightly above the path we assumed in the January Inflation Report. The first reflections of the depreciation of the Turkish lira were observed on energy prices, where exchange rate transitivity is fast. Energy prices increased significantly in the first quarter with the rise in oil and managed water prices, as well as exchange rate effects. Cost developments also adversely affected basic goods group inflation; In this group, inflation rose markedly despite temporary tax cuts on furniture and white goods products, with exchange rate effects spreading across the group. Accordingly, the biggest contribution to the rise in consumer inflation after food came from the basic goods group. Figure 11. In this course of service inflation, the impact of the increases recorded through exchange rate-sensitive services was felt as well as the delayed reflections of the increase in fuel prices. Rent inflation also maintained its high level, especially in Istanbul. Under this outlook, the upward trend in the main trend of core indicators, which started in December 2016, continued to strengthen in the first quarter of the year (Chart 12). A similar upward movement was also observed in the alternative basic inflation indicators that we followed within the CBRT. 7 Dear Guests, The data for the last quarter of 2016 confirmed the predictions that the slowdown in economic activity in the third quarter was temporary. During this period, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased by 3.8 percent compared to the previous quarter and by 3.5 percent compared to the same period of the previous year (Chart 13). When compensation for workday losses in the third quarter is excluded, moderate growth was recorded in the last quarter. On the other hand, the upward updates made by TURKSTAT for the first three quarters of 2016 revealed that the level of economic activity was higher than in the previous Report period. As a result, growth in 2016 slowed by 2.9 percent compared to the previous year, but it exceeded expectations. Annual growth in the last quarter of the year was driven by domestic demand (Chart 14). Special consumption expenditures increased both on an annual and periodic basis with the support of the depreciation of the TL, the demand brought forward by the tax adjustment in the automobile, the relaxed macroprudential measures and financial conditions. In this period, the increase in investments remained lower than consumption. The weak course of machinery and equipment investments limited the recovery in investments. With the acceleration in exports in the last quarter, the contribution of net external demand to the quarterly growth was quite high, while the contribution to annual growth improved compared to the first nine months. In this case, exchange rate developments, normalization of relations with Russia, positive reflections of market diversification on exports of goods and services and horizontal course in imports were effective. So, before we move on to the predictions, I will briefly convey our assumptions about the variables in question. We updated the 2017 average of crude oil price, which we assumed to be 57 USD in the January Inflation Report, to 55 USD within the framework of recent developments (Chart 17). We have significantly raised our assumption of import prices in US dollars for 2017 due to the upward trend in commodity prices (Chart 18). Title: Speech of President ahap Kavcolu at the Informative Meeting on the Introduction of the "Inflation Report 2022-II"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Prof. Dr. ahap Kavcolu, Central Bank Governor Inflation Report Briefing Meeting 2022-II 28 April 2022, Ankara 2 Dear Members of the Press, Distinguished Participants, Welcome to the Inflation Report Information Meeting, which we organized for the second time this year. I would like to greet our guests who physically participate and follow us on their screens and wish that our meeting will be instrumental for good. I will begin by reflecting on our assessments of the macroeconomic outlook, which forms the rationale for our policies. Then I will make statements about our medium-term inflation forecasts and finally make a general assessment of our policies. After answering the questions that will come from you, I hope to finish our meeting efficiently. Macroeconomic Outlook Geopolitical risks, which turned into conflict in February, are causing disruptions in supply chains and worsening supply constraints again in the wake of the pandemic. The expansion of quarantine measures taken as a result of the increasing number of cases in China also deepens the deterioration in the continuity of supply. The fact that the conflict between Russia and Ukraine affects the global economy, especially the Eurozone, through commodity prices, supply and trade channels increases the risks on the global growth outlook. Accordingly, growth expectations in our trading partners are also updated downwards compared to the previous Report period. Inflation, which increased as a result of supply problems during the epidemic process, is rising this time through commodity prices following the increase in geopolitical risks. Strong negative supply shocks triggered by regional conflicts have led to large increases in global raw material prices. Worldwide, both headline and core inflation rates have reached high levels. On the other hand, supply and supply problems, which are expected to disappear with the weakening of the effects of the epidemic, have not yet started to improve. At the same time, geopolitical risks continued to adversely affect inflation through the aforementioned channels. Dear Participants, I would like to continue my speech with the domestic macroeconomic outlook. In the fourth quarter of 2021, economic activity remained strong with the continuation of the post-pandemic normalization process and the support of external demand, and the growth in 2021 was 11 percent. On the manufacturing side, the highest contribution to annual growth in the fourth quarter came from the services and industrial sectors. On the spending side, both domestic and foreign demand contributed to annual growth in the fourth quarter. Net exports contributed 4.2 points to annual growth in the fourth quarter. Thus, in the fourth quarter of 2021, Turkey was among the OECD countries where net exports contributed the most to annual growth. The data for the first quarter indicate that the improvement trend in the composition of economic activity continues. In this period, although domestic demand lost some momentum, production maintained its strength with the contribution of external demand. Industrial production increased by 2 percent compared to the previous quarter, adjusted for seasonal and calendar effects, on the average of January-February. Adjusted for calendar effects, industrial production increased strongly by 13.3 percent year-on-year in the first quarter. While this increase in production is spread throughout the manufacturing industry, industrial production is stronger in the exporting sectors. Industrial turnover indices also show that foreign demand positively affects industrial production. Despite long-standing supply constraints, industrial production supports growth and the labor market with its flexible and resilient structure. 3 Capital expenditures tend to increase strongly. Investments in machinery and equipment, one of the drivers of potential growth, have been increasing year-on-year for nine consecutive quarters since the last quarter of 2019. In the said period, the average annual growth rate of machinery and equipment investments was approximately 20 percent. On the other hand, the contribution of components that support the current account balance, such as net exports, was realized at high levels after the outbreak. This indicates that sustainable components are strengthened in the composition of growth. In 2021, the share of machinery and equipment investments and net exports in gross domestic product increased to 17.4 percent, reaching the highest level of the last decade. The survey data indicate that as of April, companies plan to increase their investment expenditures in the coming period. We observe that this trend is growing stronger by spreading to all sectors, especially the sectors that produce and export investment goods. Looking at the average of January-February, the increases in investment goods imports and industrial production, especially capital goods, confirm that the demand for fixed capital goods remains strong. Capacity utilization rates have exceeded historical averages in some sectors. We assess that the need for additional capacity is an element that can support investment demand in the coming period. In this context, it is important to meet the increasing investment need with long-term Turkish lira investment loans. The reflections of the growth strengthened in the composition on the labor market are also satisfactory. While domestic production remains strong with the contribution of exports, we see that the employment generation capacity of our economy is constantly increasing. As of February, seasonally adjusted employment increased by 2.4 million people in the last year. While the labor force participation rate increased during this period, the unemployment rate decreased from 13.2 percent to 10.7 percent. Turkey has been the country that has increased its employment the most among OECD countries after the outbreak. High-frequency data indicate that the improvement in the employment outlook and the positive course in the labor market continue in line with the economic activity outlook. While the industrial sector made a strong contribution to the employment increases after the outbreak, surveys show that employment expectations in the manufacturing industry are at high levels. In this context, we anticipate that the increase in employment will continue in the coming period. Export-based growth is important for sustainable price stability. When the Turkish economy is compared with the neighboring countries, the nearby region or peer countries, the manufacturing industry stands out in terms of its share in exports, the number of products and markets exported and export diversity. The share of manufacturing industry products in Turkey's exports is about 78 percent, higher than most of the other peer and surrounding countries. Our country has reached a higher market and product diversification compared to similar countries by selling around 4300 kinds of products to more than two hundred countries. The fact that the share of the three most exported products in total exports is relatively low as approximately 29 percent indicates that exports are not concentrated in certain products. During the pandemic period, Turkey's position in global trade gained importance and a window of opportunity was created in which our economy could evaluate its relative advantages. In this period, our economy is rapidly turning into a regional production center. Turkey is experiencing an important export-oriented transformation in the structure of its growth. While our exports reached 225 billion dollars in 2021, the growth in exports compared to the pre-pandemic period showed one of the best performances among OECD countries. 4 Our exports maintained the upward trend they had achieved during the epidemic period despite the rising regional risks in the first quarter of 2022. While our exports to Russia and Ukraine inevitably decreased due to the effects of the regional conflict, our exports to the EU increased significantly in the same period and the possible losses in exports could be compensated in a very short time. However, imports increased in the first quarter as a result of the acceleration of record increases in energy prices due to the effect of geopolitical developments. When gold and energy are excluded, imports of intermediate goods continued to rise in parallel with increases in non-energy commodity prices, while imports of consumer and investment goods increased relatively limitedly. We assess that sustainable current account balance is critical for lasting price stability. When we examine our foreign trade on the basis of quantity by eliminating price effects, we see that the amount of exports has achieved a significant improvement compared to imports. In 2021, the amount of exports excluding gold increased by 21.3 percent, while the annual increase in imports excluding gold was 4.4 percent. In line with this, the basic current account balance indicator, adjusted for business and price cycles, was positive for the first time at the end of 2021. In the second half of 2021, the upward trend in the number of foreign visitors, accelerated by the spread of vaccination and the relaxation of travel restrictions, remains strong. Thus, the positive contribution of the balance of services to the current account balance continues to increase. On the other hand, risks arising from energy prices remain in the current account balance. The 12-month cumulative current account deficit, which shows a long-term trend, has increased in recent months due to the effect of rising energy prices. When we look at gold and energy, it is seen that the improvement in the annual current account balance continues. One of the most important components of our liraization strategy is to ensure that loans act in harmony with economic activity. In order to establish a sustainable current account balance, it is critical that long-term Turkish lira resources are directed to investments, exports, capacity increases and especially to SMEs. Within the framework of the liraization strategy, the growth rate and composition of loans will be harmonized with price stability and financial stability. The increase in loans given to companies in the first quarter of the year was the most important determinant of credit growth. As of April, the exchange rate-adjusted commercial credit and consumer loan growth rates stood at 47.9 percent and 17.7 percent, respectively. As a result of geopolitical risks, increases in global commodity prices have played an important role in the increase in commercial loans by increasing the demand for working capital. However, commercial credit growth has been slower than inflation. On the other hand, we expressed our discomfort with the part of the acceleration in commercial loans that is not compatible with economic activity in the PPK decisions and stated in our final decision text that we would strengthen our macroprudential instruments in this direction. In this context, we resolutely implement our macroprudential measures for the use of loans for production, investment and export. Dear Members of the Press, Dear Participants, I will now briefly assess the inflation outlook. Consumer inflation was 61.14 percent in the first quarter of the year and increases were observed in all subgroups. Seasonally adjusted data show that monthly increases tend to slow down although they are high. In the first quarter of the year, strong increases in global commodity prices, especially energy and food, were the main determinants of the rise in inflation. Indeed, one of the historically highest monthly increases in international commodity prices was recorded in March. In addition to the increase in import prices, supply-side factors such as high transportation costs and disruptions in the procurement process have led to the inflation outlook 5 continues to adversely affect. Energy and food groups came to the fore in the rise in inflation due to sharp increases in commodity prices. Dear Participants, Before moving on to our medium-term forecasts, I think it would be useful to include our assessments of the main macro determinants of inflation. Our analyses indicate that the main determinants of the rise in inflation are global commodity prices, exchange rate and supply-side disruptions. In the first quarter of the year, the import unit value index showed significant increases following commodity prices and was one of the main factors driving up inflation. Ongoing price increases due to supply-demand imbalances in commodity markets have been further strengthened by the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. While the energy index stands out with a quarterly increase of 44 percent, we see that commodity price increases are spread across sub-indices. With the geopolitical developments returning to the hot conflict at the end of February, the risks related to food prices became evident and high increases were observed in the prices of international agricultural commodities, especially wheat and sunflower oil. During this period, international food prices reached their historic highest. We see that disruptions in global supply chains continued in the first quarter of the year. China's tightening of epidemic measures due to geopolitical problems as well as rising cases is limiting the improvement in supply times and causing international transportation costs to maintain high levels. In addition to global problems, developments in domestic energy prices also put pressure on producer prices. The output gap indicators we followed within the Central Bank pointed to an economic activity above potential in the last quarter of 2021. We see that domestic demand conditions, which were lively last year, slowed down in the first quarter of 2022. In this period, foreign demand maintained its strength despite geopolitical developments, and the strong course of goods exports was accompanied by a recovery in service exports. After the slowdown observed in the use of credit reversed in the last quarter of 2021, it entered an upward trend in the first months of 2022 and became one of the factors supporting economic activity. When sectoral breakdowns were examined, it was observed that TL denominated company loans drove credit developments. With retail loans trajecting close to the historical average, the effects on inflation from consumer credit remained moderate. Although the output gap indicators slowed down compared to the previous quarter in the first quarter of the year, they remained in positive territory, and the effect of demand conditions on the rise in inflation was low compared to other main determinants such as exchange rate, global commodity prices, supply-side disruptions. Medium-Term Forecasts Dear Participants, I would like to move on to our medium-term forecasts after briefly evaluating the monetary policy developments within the framework I have summarized so far. As we mentioned in our December communication, we have completed the use of the space implied by the temporary effects of incidental factors outside the supply-side and monetary policy impact area on price increases. We decided to keep the one-week repo auction rate stable at 14 percent between January and April. 6 Central Bank funding was carried out through Open Market Operations and money swap transactions within a simple operational framework, and overnight interest rates were formed around the Central Bank policy rate. Thanks to the Central Bank's predictable liquidity management, Borsa stanbul overnight repo rates continued to fluctuate around the policy rate. When producing medium-term forecasts, we based our starting point on the economic outlook I have outlined so far. We have reviewed and updated our assumptions for external factors such as import prices, food prices, global growth and fiscal policy. Due to the tension between Ukraine and Russia, which turned into a hot conflict environment, international commodity prices increased significantly compared to the previous Report period. The first quarter of the year saw high increases in electricity and natural gas prices. The forward price curves on which we base our forecasts indicate that crude oil prices will remain significantly above the assumptions of the January Inflation Report in the coming period. Accordingly, we will base our assumptions on crude oil prices by an average of 102.2 in 2022; In 2023, we updated it to an average of 93.9. Non-energy commodity prices continue to rise due to supply-demand mismatch, increases in transportation costs, geopolitical developments and agricultural drought. Our assumptions about the overall level of import prices have also been updated upwards. Taking into account geopolitical risks, the cumulative effects of ongoing increases in international food prices, and agricultural drought developments, we have updated our assumptions on food prices upwards for 2022 and 2023. We have revised down our assumptions about external demand due to increasing uncertainties about geopolitical risks, rising energy costs and possible supply shortages on global economic activity compared to the previous reporting period. We also assumed that financial conditions in 2022 would be tighter than projected in the previous Report period due to the rise in global inflation. While producing the forecasts, we based on an outlook in which macroeconomic policies are determined in a coordinated manner within the scope of liraization steps focused on reducing inflation with a medium-term perspective. Dear Participants, Now I will share with you our inflation forecasts that we have produced within this framework that I have described. Within the framework of our basic assumptions and short-term projections, we anticipate that inflation will gradually decrease and converge to the targets as the monetary policy stance will be determined in line with the goal of sustainable price stability, with the restoration of the global peace environment and the elimination of base effects. An important element that I would like to point out about our forecasts is also related to our forecast intervals. As inflation rises, the distribution of inflation expectations widens, thus widening the range in which inflation can be predicted. This is reflected in our forecast path. In this context, the midpoints of our inflation forecast range correspond to 42.8 percent at the end of 2022, 12.9 percent at the end of 2023 and 8.3 percent at the end of 2024. Thus, we raised the 2022 year-end inflation forecast by 19.6 percentage points from 23.2 percent to 42.8 percent. Compared to the previous reporting period, the update based on import prices in Turkish lira increased the inflation forecast by 5.5 points; The increase in the assumption of food prices contributes 2.8 percentage points. On the other hand, managed/directed prices raised the year-end inflation forecast by 2.1 percentage points, largely due to the increase in alcohol and tobacco prices and electricity and natural gas prices. 7 The contribution of the update in the initial conditions to the main trend of inflation caused an increase of 9.3 points on the forecasts. In addition, the update in the output gap contributes 0.1 percentage point to our estimates. We also raised the 2023 year-end inflation forecast from 8.2 percent to 12.9 percent. The effects of the update in the initial conditions on the main trend of inflation increase the 2023 year-end inflation forecast by 1.9 percentage points. On the other hand, the update to the food inflation assumption pushes the forecast up by 0.7 percentage points. Import prices in Turkish lira contribute to the forecast by 2.2 percentage points, while updates in the output gap affect a 0.1 point reduction direction. Dear Participants, With supply constraints created by geopolitical risks and increasing uncertainty, global inflation is exceeding recent highs and global growth prospects are rapidly deteriorating. However, our economy is strengthening its position in global trade after the pandemic, and there is a structural development in our growth, which is manifested by an increase in the contribution of investment and net exports. In this context, labor market indicators are constantly improving after the outbreak and the increase in the employment generation capacity of the economy is fed by the sectors that strengthen the current account balance. The amount of exports shows a strong increase compared to the amount of imports, and our current account balance, adjusted for cyclical effects, indicates a surplus. Energy and raw material prices, which pose a risk to our current account balance in the recent period and have peaked with the conflicts in our region, also adversely affect inflation. As long as there is a normalization in energy price levels, which we do not find sustainable in terms of the global economy, we will reach our targets of a decrease in inflation and a sustainable current account balance. We are determined to carry out this process with strong steps that we will take within the framework of the liraization strategy. In the last part of my speech, I will give information about the Central Bank's liraization strategy, which is an essential element of the policy review process. We have included the basic lines of our Liraization Strategy in the January 2022 Inflation Report. The permanent increase in the weight of our national currency in the balance sheets of households, companies and banks and the fact that the only means of payment in our country is the Turkish lira is the ultimate goal of our liraization strategy. As you know, we have recently implemented a series of applications whose review process has been completed within the scope of the liraization strategy. In line with the principle of establishing the mandatory reserves held for Turkish lira obligations only in Turkish lira, we have terminated the possibility of establishing them in foreign currency. By allowing our rediscount loans to be used only in the designated Turkish lira denominated spending areas for net exporter companies, we ensured that there was no demand for foreign currency arising from the Central Bank's funding and that the rediscount loans were evaluated in accordance with their purpose. In December 2021, we took an important step towards strengthening the TL deposit preference by supporting the conversion of foreign currency and gold deposits to TL. This practice increased the share of TL in bank balance sheets and extended the funding term. We clearly see the contribution of the implementation to financial stability by strengthening bank balance sheets. An important component of our liraization strategy is that cost-effective and long-term loans support sustainable price stability through production, investment and export increases. We continue to use our macroprudential tools strongly to meet long-term and cost-effective Turkish lira loans with the right composition and with economic activity spread across the base. 8 Within the scope of the liraization strategy, the steps to be taken for the collateral structure of the liquidity management, the review process of which is ongoing, have been completed by our technical teams. In the very near future, in line with our roadmap in the text of the Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy, we will take additional steps to increase the use and demand of Turkish lira-denominated securities as collateral in the funding structure. On the other hand, as the Central Bank, we attach importance to the fact that our companies make their payments in Turkish lira within the scope of liraization. Being aware of the losses of money substitution and indexing behavior to foreign currency that make monetary transfer inefficient and increase inflation, we find the recent steps taken in this regard valuable. Providing the infrastructure of the robust, strong and stable Turkish Lira is the top priority threshold towards our goal of permanent price stability. As a whole, we carry out comprehensive studies with all parties to increase the effectiveness of our monetary policy instruments. Our ultimate goal is to complete a financial architecture in which all our economic units can save in Turkish lira without the need for any currency other than lira in all kinds of decisions and where they can make all their financial decisions in Turkish lira. In closing, I would like to express my gratitude to all our employees who took part in the preparations for the report and the press conference, especially our members of the Monetary Policy Committee and the employees of the General Directorate of Research and Monetary Policy, and who worked hard with great effort for the development of these policies. On this occasion, we congratulate you on your Ramadan Feast, which we will realize in the coming days; I pray Allah Almighty to bring health, peace and well-being to our country and the whole world. Now I can take the questions from you, taking into account our time.

Trkiye ekonomisi komu, yakn blgedeki veya emsal lkelerle karlatrldnda imalat sanayinin ihracattaki pay, ihracat yaplan rn ve pazar says ile ihracat eitlilii bakmndan ne kmaktadr. Trkiyenin ihracatnda imalat sanayi rnlerinin pay yaklak yzde 78 ile dier emsal ve evre lkelerin ouna kyasla daha yksektir. lkemiz, iki yzden fazla lkeye 4300 civarnda eitte rn satarak benzer lkelere kyasla daha yksek bir pazar ve rn eitlenmesine ulamtr. En fazla ihracat yaplan  rnn toplam ihracat iindeki paynn yaklak yzde 29 gibi grece dk bir oranda olmas ise ihracatnn belli rnlerde younlamadna iaret etmektedir. Salgn dneminde Trkiyenin kresel ticaretteki konumu nem kazanm, ekonomimizin sahip olduu greli avantajlar deerlendirebilecei bir frsat penceresi olumutur. Bu dnemde ekonomimiz hzla blgesel bir retim merkezine dnmektedir. Trkiye bymesinin yapsnda ihracat odakl nemli bir dnm yaamaktadr. hracatmz 2021 ylnda 225 milyar dolara ularken salgn ncesi dneme kyasla ihracattaki byme OECD lkeleri arasnda en iyi performanslardan birini gstermitir. 4 hracatmz, salgn dneminde yakalad art eilimini 2022 ylnn ilk eyreinde ykselen blgesel risklere ramen korumutur. Blgesel atmann etkileriyle kanlmaz olarak Rusya ve Ukraynaya olan ihracatmz azalrken, ayn dnemde ABye olan ihracatmz belirgin art gstererek ihracattaki olas kayplar ok ksa sre iinde telafi edilebilmitir. Bununla birlikte jeopolitik gelimelerin etkisiyle enerji fiyatlarndaki rekor artlarn ivmelenerek srmesi sonucunda ithalat ilk eyrekte ykselmitir. Altn ve enerji hari tutulduunda ara mallar ithalat, enerji d emtia fiyatlarndaki artlara paralel olarak ykseliini srdrm, tketim ve yatrm mallar ithalat nispeten daha snrl artmtr. Srdrlebilir cari dengenin kalc fiyat istikrar iin kritik nemde olduunu deerlendiriyoruz. D ticaretimizi fiyat etkilerinden arndrarak miktar baznda incelediimizde ihracat miktarnn ithalata kyasla belirgin bir iyileme saladn gryoruz. 2021 ylnda altn hari ihracat miktar yzde 21,3 orannda artarken altn hari ithalattaki yllk art yzde 4,4 orannda gereklemitir. Bununla uyumlu olarak i ve fiyat evrimlerinden arndrlm temel cari denge gstergesi 2021 yl sonunda ilk defa pozitif olmutur. 2021 ylnn ikinci yarsnda alamann yaygnlamas ve seyahat kstlamalarnn gevetilmesiyle ivmelenen yabanc ziyareti saysndaki art eilimi gcn korumaktadr. Bylelikle hizmetler dengesinin cari dengeye sunduu olumlu katk artarak srmektedir. te yandan, cari ilemler dengesinde enerji fiyatlarndan kaynaklanan riskler devam etmektedir. Uzun dnemli eilimi gsteren 12 aylk birikimli cari ilemler a ykselen enerji fiyatlarnn etkisiyle son aylarda artmtr. Altn ve enerji hari bakldnda ise yllk cari dengedeki iyilemenin srmekte olduu grlmektedir. Liralama stratejimizin en nemli bileenlerinden biri de kredilerin iktisadi faaliyetle uyumlu hareket etmesini salamaktr. Srdrlebilir cari dengenin tesis edilmesi iin uzun vadeli Trk liras kaynaklarnn yatrmlara, ihracata, kapasite artlarna ve zellikle KOBlere ynlendirilmesi kritik nemdedir. Liralama stratejisi erevesinde kredilerin byme hz ve kompozisyonu fiyat istikrar ve finansal istikrarla uyumlu hale getirilecektir. Yln ilk eyreinde firmalara verilen kredilerdeki art kredi bymesinin en nemli belirleyicisi olmutur. Nisan ay itibaryla kur etkisinden arndrlm ticari kredi ve tketici kredisi byme hzlar srasyla yzde 47,9 ve yzde 17,7 dzeyinde gereklemitir. Jeopolitik riskler neticesinde kresel emtia fiyatlarndaki artlar iletme sermayesi talebini artrarak ticari kredilerdeki artta nemli rol oynamtr. Bununla birlikte, ticari kredi bymesi enflasyona kyasla daha yava seyretmitir. Dier taraftan, ticari kredilerdeki ivmelenmenin iktisadi faaliyetle uyumlu olmayan ksmndan duyduumuz rahatszl PPK kararlarnda dile getirmi ve son karar metnimizde makroihtiyati aralarmz bu dorultuda glendireceimizi belirtmitik. Bu kapsamda kredilerin retim, yatrm ve ihracat iin kullandrlmasna ynelik makroihtiyati tedbirlerimizi kararllkla uygulamaktayz. Saygdeer Basn Mensuplar, Deerli Katlmclar, imdi enflasyon grnmn ksaca deerlendireceim. Tketici enflasyonu yln ilk eyreinde yzde 61,14 olarak gereklemi ve tm alt gruplarda artlar gzlenmitir. Mevsimsellikten arndrlm veriler ise aylk artlarn yksek seyretmekle birlikte yavalama eiliminde olduunu gstermektedir. Yln ilk eyreinde enerji ve gda bata olmak zere kresel emtia fiyatlarndaki gl artlar enflasyondaki ykseliin ana belirleyicisi olmutur. Nitekim, uluslararas emtia fiyatlarnda Mart aynda tarihsel olarak en yksek aylk artlardan biri kaydedilmitir. thalat fiyatlarndaki artn yan sra, yksek seyreden tamaclk maliyetleri ve tedarik srecindeki aksaklklar gibi arz ynl unsurlar enflasyon grnmn 5 olumsuz etkilemeye devam etmektedir. Emtia fiyatlarndaki keskin artlara bal olarak enflasyondaki ykselite enerji ve gda gruplar ne kmtr. Deerli Katlmclar, Orta vadeli tahminlerimize gemeden nce, enflasyonun temel makro belirleyicilerine ilikin deerlendirmelerimize yer vermenin faydal olacan dnyorum. Yaptmz analizler enflasyondaki ykseliin temel belirleyicilerinin kresel emtia fiyatlar, dviz kuru ve arz ynl aksaklklar olduuna iaret etmektedir. Yln ilk eyreinde ithalat birim deer endeksi emtia fiyatlarn takiben belirgin artlar gstermi ve enflasyonu yukarya eken esas unsurlardan biri olmutur. Emtia piyasalarndaki arz-talep dengesizlikleri nedeniyle sregelen fiyat artlar, Rusya ve Ukrayna arasndaki atmayla birlikte daha da glenmitir. Enerji endeksi yzde 44 orannda eyreklik ykselile ne karken emtia fiyat artlarnn alt endeksler geneline yayldn gryoruz. ubat ay sonunda scak atmaya dnen jeopolitik gelimelerle birlikte gda fiyatlarna ilikin riskler belirginlemi, bata buday ve ayiek ya olmak zere uluslararas tarmsal emtia fiyatlarnda yksek artlar gzlenmitir. Bu dnemde, uluslararas gda fiyatlar tarihsel olarak en yksek seviyesine ulamtr. Kresel arz zincirlerindeki aksaklklarn yln ilk eyreinde de srdn gryoruz. Jeopolitik sorunlarn yan sra artan vakalar nedeniyle inin salgn tedbirlerini sklatrlmas, tedarik srelerinde iyilemeyi snrlamakta ve uluslararas tamaclk maliyetlerinin yksek seviyelerini korumasna neden olmaktadr. Kresel sorunlarn yan sra yurt ii enerji fiyatlarndaki gelimeler de retici fiyatlar zerinde bask oluturmaktadr. Merkez Bankas bnyesinde takip ettiimiz kt a gstergeleri 2021 ylnn son eyreinde potansiyelin zerinde bir ekonomik aktiviteye iaret etmitir. Getiimiz yl canl seyreden i talep koullarnn 2022 ylnn ilk eyreinde yavaladn gryoruz. Bu dnemde d talep, jeopolitik gelimelere karn gcn korumu, mal ihracatnn gl seyrine hizmet ihracatndaki toparlanma elik etmitir. Kredi kullanmnda gzlenen yavalama 2021 yl son eyreinde tersine dndkten sonra 2022 ylnn ilk aylarnda ykseli eilimine girmi ve iktisadi faaliyeti destekleyen unsurlardan biri olmutur. Sektrel krlmlar incelendiinde, kredi gelimelerini TL cinsinden firma kredilerinin srkledii izlenmitir. Bireysel kredilerin tarihsel ortalamasna yakn bir seyir izlemesiyle enflasyon zerinde tketici kredisi kaynakl etkiler lml seyretmitir. Yln ilk eyreinde kt a gstergeleri bir nceki eyree kyasla yavalasa da pozitif blgede kalmaya devam etmi, talep koullarnn enflasyondaki ykselie etkisi dviz kuru, kresel emtia fiyatlar, arz ynl aksaklklar gibi dier ana belirleyicilere kyasla dk olmutur. Enerji d emtia fiyatlar arz-talep uyumsuzluu, tamaclk maliyetlerindeki artlar, jeopolitik gelimeler ve tarmsal kurakla bal olarak ykseliine devam etmektedir. thalat fiyatlarnn genel seviyesine ilikin varsaymlarmz da yukar ynl gncellenmitir. Tahminler retilirken, makroekonomik politikalarn orta vadeli bir perspektifle enflasyonu drmeye odakl, liralama admlar kapsamnda koordineli bir ekilde belirlendii bir grnm esas aldk.
