Title: Interview with Star-Parametre Supplement
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: INTERVIEW GIVEN BY PRESIDENT SERDENGEcTIN TO STAR-PARAMETRE SUPPLEMENT (18 MAY S 2003) Sureyya Serdengecti. He is the Governor of the Central Bank, which has never fallen off the agenda in almost every period and closely follows the every move of economic actors. We talked with Serdengecti about the Central Bank, the future of the economy, and even his private life. Serdengecti keeps his savings in TL. Not only because he has his own signature on it, but because it provides more returns than foreign currency in the long run. He already carries only TL in his pocket. He is of the opinion that there will be no revision in economic targets in the current situation. Instead of issuing new banknotes, he considers it more necessary to throw 6 zeros out of the money when the appropriate time comes. He is optimistic about the future of the economy. But he is cautious. Here is Serdengecti's Descriptions: Do you think the Central Bank is independent enough? - We have a Central Bank that has the independence of means, not the goal. While setting the inflation target, which is the goal, it acts jointly with the government. In our opinion, this should be the case. If you consider the impact of the economic policies of past governments on inflation, the government must be involved. In this respect, we are satisfied. We have not had a problem with the law so far. On the contrary, over time, this whole structure has been linked to us and economic programs. 1 Since we also see the credibility it provides, we have no problem with independence. - What is the Central Bank's reflex ability in the face of sudden developments? - I can easily say that the reflex ability is quite high. Especially in the floating exchange rate regime, since his hands are not tied, he can take the necessary decisions about liquidity instantly and satisfactorily. In making these decisions, it benefits from the high-tech opportunity at its disposal and the knowledge base it has greatly expanded. His immediate response to financial stability during the recent Iraq War is a prime example of this. - Are you having problems with the government? - The relationship with the government is going as it should. I don't think there is a problem between us to the extent that it is sometimes reflected in the press. The government also complains about the high level of interest rates, and so do we. We know that the way to reduce interest rates is to provide an environment of confidence and that the way to do this is to implement economic policies with determination. There is no question of the government interfering in our exchange rate or short-term interest rate policy, and it would not be right anyway. Not only will the Central Bank be harmed by its intervention, but the Government will also suffer because the environment of trust will be disrupted. - What awaits the Turkish economy in the near future? 2 - A"To the extent that we have resolutely continued in the program, the economy has become more resilient to shocks, as we saw in 2002 and 2003. The latest Iraq Crisis is a good example of this. That is why we must continue to implement the program with determination. If we take timely measures against external shocks as in Iraq, there is no reason why the outlook should not continue positively. But while the Central Bank is optimistic, it will remain cautious. Everyone needs to watch the process of public finance and structural reform with attention. - When do you think we will see additional digit inflation? - If we continue the program decisively, we will be able to achieve this in 2005. I believe it will happen. - So, do you think the program is being implemented with determination? - There were setbacks in the election process. However, I think significant progress has been made in this regard. The most important indicator of determination will be the healthy completion of the reviews with the IMF. - When you were buying foreign currency after the last dollar fell below 1.5 million, you said, "We are not bothered by the current level of exchange rates." What did you mean? For one thing, the Central Bank's target is inflation and it does not have to keep the exchange rate at a certain level in a floating exchange rate regime. Exchange rate, economy in this regime 3 It is formed as a result of policies, the foundations of the economy and expectations. Those expectations can sometimes be overly optimistic when we are cautiously optimistic. However, we intervene in the currency markets against instability, against excessive volatility. In addition, if there is a surplus supply in foreign exchange, we try to increase our reserves. Despite the great desire of some, it is not right for the Central Bank to express an opinion on the level at which the exchange rates should be at the current stage of the stabilization program. People still want us to pursue goals other than price stability, as they have done in the past. We need to overcome these bad habits, such as the hot money habit of old times. - Can we talk about a hot money danger at this stage? - The danger of hot money has decreased incomparably with the previous one since the introduction of the floating exchange rate regime. The more guarantees you give to the markets regarding the level of the exchange rate, the more you encourage hot money. A significant part of the hot money does not like the fluctuating rate, and more or less expects a currency store in the country where it will enter. There are also those who are in search of this guarantee today. In addition, during the Iraq War, there is quite a bit of trouble who panicked and received foreign currency from 1 million 700 thousand. It is not possible to understand this problem. At this point, I put exporters in a separate place. Although they sometimes complain about the level of the exchange rate, they generally know how the floating exchange rate regime works. 4 However, they want exchange rate stability at least as much as we do. Because there are high costs on them that need to be solved within the framework of structural reforms. - Is it possible to ensure exchange rate stability on your own? - This is not something that can happen with frequent interventions by the Central Bank. Once again, it is understood that even if the reason for the crises we have entered in the past is not predictable exchange rates and hot money, these have had a great impact on the deepening of the crises. We cannot cause the same situation again by reversing the exchange rate policy. The only thing that the Government needs to do in this regard is to implement the stabilization program with determination, to show sensitivity to institutional arrangements and thus to make the debt stock sustainable by giving a positive effect to high real interest rates. As long as governments behave in this way, they will give the greatest support to monetary and exchange rate policy, as well as to exchange rate stability. - Considering that the supply of foreign currency will increase in the summer months, what kind of a course should we expect in the exchange rates? - There is always an increase in the supply of foreign currency during the summer months. The Central Bank's foreign exchange purchase tenders were launched taking this element into consideration. In my opinion, after a difficult winter, the exchange rate will gain relative stability. However, it will take us a little longer to reach the level of stability we want in the exchange rate. I can clearly say that there is no need to hesitate in terms of exchange rates. The Central Bank has achieved its goal. 5 It has largely avoided excessive volatility in the currency. If you ask whether the Turkish lira will gain or lose value in the future, it depends on the fundamentals of the economy, the program and the waits implemented. If people in this country think that the balance of payments will be disrupted, they should buy in foreign currency just in anticipation of the deterioration, without even waiting for this deterioration to occur. Because the deterioration in the balance of payments is compensated only by the depreciation of the TL. However, when we look at it today, there is not much foreign exchange taker other than the Central Bank. In the floating exchange rate regime, the probability of a problem that will lead to a crisis in the current account balance or in the balance of payments as a whole is much lower than in fixed/predictable exchange rate regimes. Nevertheless, people have not forgotten the profound impact of those great devaluations. When we wake up one morning, isn't there a chance of encountering a high devaluation? - The risk of devaluation may arise if the exchange rate regime is stable or predictable and the Central Bank tries to keep the exchange rate at a certain level, as it was until 2 years ago in our country. However, if the Central Bank does not set any target in the exchange rate, as it is today, or even does not comment on the level of the exchange rate at this stage of the economic program, then there is no need for such a concern. If people think that the economy is going to be bad, they buy foreign currency and take the rate to where it should be. 6 - How does it feel to be the Governor of the Central Bank? Do you ever feel like a rich boss? - I worked for many years at the Central Bank in international reserve management and then in open market operations. Despite this, I have never felt the sense of wealth due to trading high amounts. I felt more awareness and satisfaction of public duty. - Feki, ya st r es? After working at the Central Bank for quite a long time, such as 23 years, seeing all the turmoil and crisis, you learn to manage stress. If you don't learn that, you won't be able to keep up with it. - Does your current position coincide with the goal you set for your future during your student years? - I graduated from university at the end of the 1970s. At that time, in the conditions of the country, it was very difficult to determine a healthy career goal. When I was studying at METU Department of Economics, I was most impressed by Nur Keyder's "money" course. My grade was also good. I think that my teacher and that lesson brought me closer to these issues. Other than that, I said whatever I did in working life to do well, and the rest came. If I were to aim for a position, I guess I am in this position today. I couldn't be. 7 - We always talked about money. Let's talk a little bit about your hobbies and phobias. - I love listening to classical music. I closely follow publications related to classical music and collect CDs. If I had the time, I would want to learn and do more about the environment, especially afforestation. I'm interested in coastal sport sailing, but so far I haven't had the opportunity. I don't have many phobias, but there are issues that I am uncomfortable with. I have always been disturbed by the fact that it has not been understood for a long time that inflation has been the biggest problem in Turkey since the past. I do not welcome statements of opinion and impolite attitudes that are not based on information. - Have you ever had a livelihood problem? - In a middle-class family, my parents did not make their children feel that even if we had financial difficulties. - Do you use credit card or cash for your purchases? - I use a credit card. I also carry as much cash as necessary. In Turkish lira, of course. I have never had foreign currency in my pocket except for foreign travels. - As the Central Bank Governor, how do you evaluate your investments? Do you keep it in foreign exchange? - All my investments are in Turkish lira. One reason for this is that I am the head of the institution that issues Turkish lira. But the other reason, in my opinion, is that the Turkish lira investments are long 8 This is because it has better returns in the term. Look at the last 10 years, although we have experienced two major devaluations, those who had Turkish lira deposits 10 years ago had much higher returns than those who had equal amounts of foreign exchange deposits. The return of those who invested in treasury bills was even higher. This is despite the devaluations. - What happens in the period after this? - It will continue as it is, Turkish lira yields will be higher. Also, if you are holding foreign currency above or below your foreign currency debt in a floating exchange rate regime, the exchange rate risk is on you. So you can win or you can lose. For those who do not know the subject well, keeping foreign currency when there is no foreign currency debt or borrowing foreign currency when there is no foreign currency asset or income is nothing but gambling. Because no one has a goal with the exchange rate. - Is there a new banknote or a zero from the Turkish lira in the next period? - We now need to bring up the issue of throwing 6 zeros from the money after the conditions are created. But it's a little early. In my opinion, it is especially important to meet this year's inflation target. Before that, the process can be started by holding the necessary negotiations with the Government. If we implement our program with determination, I think it would be healthier for us to go in the direction of throwing 6 zeros instead of issuing a new banknote. I don't want to give an exact deadline for that right now. 9 - Revision of economic targets is being discussed? Do you think revision is necessary? - We have never talked about revision until today. Even in the Iraq War. We found it strange that some circles demanded revision at the beginning of the Iraq War. If there was to be a revision because of the economic effects of the Iraq War, shouldn't it be necessary to see the course of the War? At this stage I still do not see a revision in the targets. As long as we continue our program with determination, there is no reason why the inflation target should not be met. If there is a deviation, which can come from agriculture, there is nothing that monetary policy can do against most agriculture. But it's too early to talk about it. - What do you intend to do after the completion of your term of office? - My term of office is over 2 years, I have about 3 more years. What I have seen in the Central Bank for years is that you cannot be chaired by thinking about the next stage in the Central Bank. If the next stage is considered, if we act with thoughts such as what will I be after the presidency, the presidency is very healthy. I don't think it can be done. 10

Title: Monetary Policy Practices
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: MONETARY POLICY RELATED PRACTICES GAZ ERCEL PRESIDENT REPUBLIC OF TURKEY HURIYET M ERKEZ BANK ISTANBUL MILITARY ACADEMY ADVANCED ISTANBUL 12 M ART 1997 The aim of the Central Bank is to implement a monetary policy that will not include quantitative easing that will feed inflation by controlling reserve money from balance sheet variables, and to fulfill this by providing the liquidity need required by the market and attracting the surplus in a way that does not disturb the stability of the markets. Due to the increasing political uncertainty since the last months of 1995, the volatility observed in all monetary indicators continued for part of 1996. In such a conjuncture, money markets aimed to keep the reserve money, which is one of the intermediate objectives of monetary policy, within the program limits, and at the same time to minimize the fluctuation in the exchange rate and at the same time to adjust the amount of liquidity needed by the market in a way that takes care not to disturb the delicate balances and stability in the market. On the other hand, it is useful to remind once again that the intended target variable is not Central Bank Money or balance sheet or emission, as perceived in some circles, but reserve money. Therefore, it is necessary to base the monetary policy analysis on reserve money. Looking at the issue in this context, it has been observed that the relative contribution of net internal assets to reserve money has increased in some months and decreased in other months,*that is, in these months, reserve money growth has been brought under control through open market transactions with short-term advance repayments, and in this period, the contribution of net external assets to reserve money growth in relative terms has increased*. When we look at the figures for the second half of 1996, it is seen that the Central Bank gave money to the market through open market operations in September and October and withdrew money from the market in this way in the other months. The fact that the Treasury borrowed more than the amortization amount in September and October forced the Central Bank to give money to the markets that were squeezed for this reason. That is, the reason for the liquidity provided by the Central Bank in September and October is not to provide resources to the Treasury, but on the contrary, to provide temporary liquidity to the markets that are stuck because the Treasury borrows more than its amortization. Although our foreign exchange reserves decreased slightly in December, they increased from 12.4 billion to 16.5 billion to approximately 4.1 billion during the year, increasing net external assets while positively affecting expectations that the Central Bank would be able to intervene in the exchange rate if necessary, increasing the credibility of the Central Bank's policies. In addition, exchange rates followed a course at parity in real terms with inflation within the framework of purchasing parity. For this reason, there is no real depreciation or gain in exchange rates. As it is known, real interest rates in the economy are determined mainly as a result of the borrowing needs and strategy of the public, which is the institution that demands the largest funds from the markets. The role of the Central Bank in this process can only be to reduce the "premium" (contributing to the reduction of these uncertainties) created by the uncertainties in the economy on interest rates. Indeed, one-night interest rates in the interbank money market averaged between 63 percent and 95 percent per month during the year, while they were less volatile in the second half.
text_original: PARA POLTKASI LE LGL UYGULAMALAR GAZ EREL BAKAN TRKYE CUM HURYET M ERKEZ BANKASI STANBUL HARP AKADEM LER STANBUL 12 M ART 1997 Merkez Bankas'nn amac enflasyonu besleyecek parasal genilemeye yer vermeyecek bir para politikasn bilano deikenlerinden rezerv paray kontrol ederek uygulamak ve bunu piyasalardaki istikrar bozmayacak ekilde piyasann gerektirdii likidite ihtiyacn temin edip, fazlasn da ekerek yerine getirmektedir. 1995 ylnn son aylarndan itibaren artan politik belirsizlik nedeniyle tm parasal gstergelerde izlenen oynaklk 1996 ylnn bir ksmnda da devam etmitir. Para piyasalar byle bir konjonktrde, para politikasnn ara amalarndan olan rezerv paray program limitleri iinde tutmak, bunu yaparken de dviz kurundaki dalgalanmay en aza indirgemek ve ayn zamanda piyasann ihtiyac olan likidite miktarn piyasadaki hassas dengeleri ve istikrar bozmamaya zen gsterecek ekilde ayarlamak amacn gtmtr. te yandan, amalanan hedef deiken baz evrelerde algland gibi Merkez Bankas Paras veya bilano ya da emisyon olmayp, rezerv para olduunu bir kez daha hatrlatmakta yarar vardr. Dolaysyla para politikas analizini rezerv paraya dayandrmak gerekmektedir. Meseleye bu erevede bakldnda, net i varlklarn greli olarak rezerv paraya katksnn baz aylarda artarken, dier aylarda ise dt gzlenmitir,*yani bu aylarda ksa vadeli avans geri demeleriyle birlikte ak piyasa ilemleri yolu ile rezerv para bymesinin kontrol altna alndn ve bu dnemde, net d varlklarn relatif olarak rezerv para bymesine katksnn arttnn altn izmek isterim*. 1996 ylnn ikinci yars iin rakamlara bakldnda Merkez Bankas'nn Eyll ve Ekim aylarnda ak piyasa ilemleri ile piyasaya para verdii dier aylarda ise bu yolla piyasadan para ektii grlmektedir. Hazine'nin Eyll ve Ekim aylarnda itfa miktarndan fazla borlanmas, Merkez Bankas'n bu nedenle skan piyasalara para vermek zorunda brakmtr. Yani, Eyll ve Ekim aylarnda Merkez Bankas'nn salad likiditenin nedeni, Hazine'ye kaynak salamak deil, tam tersine Hazine'nin itfasndan fazla borland iin skan piyasalara geici likidite salamaktr. Dviz rezervlerimizin Aralk aynda bir miktar azalmasna ramen yl iinde 12,4 milyar dolardan 16,5 milyar dolara yaklak 4,1 milyar dolara artmas, bir yandan net d varlklar artrrken, bir yandan da Merkez Bankas'nn gerektiinde kura mdahele edebileceine ynelik beklentileri olumlu ynde etkileyerek Merkez Bankas'nn politikalarnn inanrlln artrmtr. Ayrca dviz kurlar da satn alma paritesi erevesinde reel olarak enflasyonla baaba bir seyir izlemitir. Bu nedenle de kurlarda reel olarak bir deer kayb veya kazanc sz konusu deildir. Bilindii gibi ekonomideki reel faiz oranlar temelde, piyasalardan en byk fon talep eden kurum olan, kamunun borlanma ihtiyalarnn ve stratejisinin bir sonucu olarak belirlenmektedir. Bu srete Merkez Bankas'nn rol ancak ekonomideki belirsizliklerin faizler zerinde yaratt "prim"in (bu belirsizliklerin azalmasna katkda bulunarak) drlmesi olabilir. Nitekim, bankalararas para piyasasndaki bir gecelik faiz oranlar yl iinde aylk ortalama yzde 63 ila yzde 95 arasnda deiirken, ikinci yarda daha az oynak bir seyir izlemitir.

Title: Interview Published in Radikal Newspaper
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: INTERVIEW OF PRESIDENT SERDENGEcT PUBLISHED IN RADIKAL NEWSPAPER ON 21-22 NOVEMBER 2005 There are debates in the public regarding the expiration of your term of office and whether you will be reappointed. What do you think about whether or not to be reassigned? This task is entrusted for five years, it is carried out independently, as required. At the end of five years, the authority and responsibility for the appointment lies with the Government. All over the world, the appointment is made by the legislative or executive branch. In connection with this issue, positive and negative opinions are expressed. This how do you respond to the controversy? It's normal to have arguments. When price stability is largely achieved and growth outperforms expectations, it is quite normal to have positive opinions. However, after three decades of economic instability, there have been those who have been adversely affected by the normalization process of the economy, and their interests have been shaken. There are those who want monetary policy to address a certain sector, to aim at goals that are not written in the Central Bank's Law. It is quite normal for them to express negative opinions. There will be these discussions. But the controversies are completely beyond me. In particular, some opposition political party representatives criticize that "you have adopted an extremely optimistic atmosphere with the wish that your term of office will be extended, and that you have made everything look rosy." In the decisions taken by the Central Bank, the connection should be established regarding the expiration of your term of office. how do you greet it? The fact that we point to the distance taken in stability and the positive results obtained may not be liked by certain segments for various reasons. When they point out the risks and make criticisms and warnings, they may not like other people. The independent and accountable Central Bank must always tell the truth, good or bad, without hesitation. The fact that we receive criticism from all walks of life is perhaps an indication that we are doing our job correctly. Central bank governors are, and should be, the loneliest people in the world. Would you say that the Central Bank is fully independent? First of all, we need to understand what the concept of independence is. Independence has been granted to central banks by society all over the world through legal processes and a need, and it also requires transparency and accountability. As a result of the final understanding of the same need in our country, the Law was amended in 2001 and the Central Bank had instrument independence. It should be noted at once that there is no such thing as a perfect law. It can always get better. As important as the law is the mindset in people and institutions. It is necessary to understand the independence of the Central Bank and to develop the mentality that will protect independence. In addition, the stance of the people in charge of the Central Bank is always important. The current Act has worked so far. However, there was always a tendency to pierce with other laws. On the other hand, independence has also been beneficial in combating inflation, ensuring economic stability and building confidence in policies. The role of independence in increasing the credibility of the Central Bank is very large. In the EU Progress Report, the necessary steps to be taken regarding the Central Bank were listed. (The determination of the inflation target by the central bank alone, not "with the government"; Duties of the members of the Bank Assembly 2 reconsideration of their duration; Change in the legal regulation regarding the removal of the President, etc.) Is there a working process regarding these? It needs to be addressed at a later stage of the accession and negotiation process. Then, I am sure that other amendments will be required to the Act. Implicit inflation targeting has been carried out since 2002. In this process, you also receive criticism from time to time. Do you think it's not understood or explained enough? In the past, the Central Bank was not as transparent as it is today, it could not be monitored. But now everything is explained. We publish detailed announcements and reports on developments in the economy, our policies and practices. Of course, it is not possible to say that it is read and understood by everyone. But when I look at the general, I can still say that a lot of progress has been made in terms of both telling and being understood. In the process since June, you have been criticized by saying that "no interest rate cuts were made in the summer months, interest rate cuts were made despite the high inflation in the last two months." What do you think? We always look forward, not backwards, in our decisions about interest rates. We scan a very broad set of information to see the trend in inflation. This set of information is constantly being updated with incoming data. We have our own inflation forecasts. Therefore, we need to look at what happened at the beginning of the summer and what happened next. At the beginning of the summer, there were mixed signals and uncertainties. In recent years, it has been seen that the increase in domestic demand continues to be controlled, there has been a gradual improvement in the special comprehensive CPI indicators as of months and the trend is downward today. It is important that the productivity growth and output gap continues. 3 There have also been important external developments during this time. In particular, full membership negotiations with the EU have begun, which have had a positive effect on expectations. We are cautious though. We closely follow all developments in the economy. As you know, the impact of monetary policy decisions should be delayed. For this reason, the decisions taken today are aimed at influencing the course of inflation in 2006 and beyond. We must not forget this. There are also criticisms that "you only follow and maintain price stability", "you make Turkey pay an interest rate 2-3 points above normal interest rates"... The ultimate goal of economic policies is to promote economic prosperity. Prosperity will increase only if there is an environment of sustainable growth, if sustainable employment growth can be achieved. For sustainability, it is essential to ensure and maintain price stability as a prerequisite for economic stability and economic stability. For this reason, the main purpose of the Central Bank is determined to ensure price stability. Because the Central Bank makes the greatest contribution to economic stability, sustainable growth and employment growth, welfare growth, price stability. will do so by providing it. It is not easy for those who think that they have not suffered from the inflationary environment for years, but that they cannot adapt to the new economic environment when inflation falls, adopt this approach. The main policy tool used by the Central Bank to ensure price stability is short-term interest rates. When the Central Bank makes interest rate decisions, it looks at the course of inflation in the future. That is his duty. Since the targets are met, monetary policy decisions are taken on time. There are criticisms that "interest rates are kept high to put the exchange rate under pressure, so that inflation is also brought under control"...? 4 As I said, what is expected from monetary policy is other than ensuring price stability, the criticisms are also different. Interest rates are said to be high, but in the last three years, nominal interest rates have fallen from 70 percent to 14 percent and real interest rates have fallen from 30 percent to 8 percent. But as we always say, this level is not enough. The general level of interest rates should fall further. This is not because the Central Bank lowers its interest rate in some way by looking at factors other than inflation; more progress will be made in stability, reduction of the fragility of public debt, structural reforms and improvement in expectations. Moreover, the strong and permanent relationship between the Central Bank interest rate and the general level of interest rates has not yet been established to the extent desired. Depending on the risk perceptions, the direction and strength of the relationship may change over time. Therefore, the general level of interest rates may not follow the Central Bank rate. Since the beginning of 2005, the Central Bank has continuously lowered short-term interest rates, while from February to the end of September, Treasury rates have been above the Central Bank rates. I would also like to add an important statement regarding the short-term interest rates of the Central Bank. As it is known, there are different channels through which the Central Bank's interest rate decisions affect inflation: Credit channel, interest rate channel, asset prices, expectations channel. As I have already said about interest rates, asset prices and credit channels are not yet functioning effectively enough. Among these channels, the most effective channel to date has been the expectations channel. Thanks to the stability program implemented and the CBRT's forward-looking signals and confidence in these signals, historic highs have been reached in the private sector's investment and consumption expenditures in the last three years. As for real interest, although the public debt has fallen for the time being, it is still high and the maturity is relatively short. In our country, investments have been more than savings since before. Structural reforms are not yet complete, they are ongoing. All this determines the level of real interest rates, which are still high due to risk perceptions. If, as it is said, it was possible to reduce inflation only by appreciating the Turkish currency, the country's inflation problem would have been solved years ago. 5 In 2006, the current account deficit is expected to be 25 billion. Will we be able to continue to finance it in the years to come? As progress is made in macroeconomic stability and the resilience of the economy against shocks increases, the sustainability of higher current account deficit amounts becomes possible. Recent experiences in the world and in other countries already show this. Moreover, the current account deficit alone is not an indicator of the crisis. When the crisis broke out in Asian countries in 1997, the current account balances were in surplus. In this context, when we look at the financing of the current account deficit, we see that the structure of the capital account in the balance of payments has changed. The share of long-term capital inflows and foreign direct investments in total capital movements is increasing rapidly. While the amount of foreign direct capital coming to our country in the period of 1980-2000 was around 500 million USD annually, this figure increased to 2 billion USD in the period of 2000-2004. In the January-September period this year, USD 3.7 billion in foreign direct investment came. The performance shown in privatization has contributed greatly to this process. A significant part of the short-term capital inflow is the loans used by the banking sector, which is also at risk as the banking sector strengthens. Decreases. In addition, criticisms such as "the current account deficit can be financed thanks to the hot money that comes with the effect of high interest rates" continue ...? As for hot money, there have been periods in this country in the past when the real interest rate was higher, while hot money came out. In the recent period, real interest rates have been steadily declining and have even reached historic lows; however, hot money is still in the mix. From this point of view, I think that the effect of waits on hot money inflows is much greater than the effect of the level of real interest. 6 As long as the positive expectations about the outlook of our country's economy continue, this process will continue. Also, hot money isn't just foreign-sourced. There is also a significant amount of hot money from residents. Residents who keep their money abroad bring these investments domestically with the improvement in the economy. But when assessing the effects of hot money, let's not forget that the conditions of the Turkish economy today are different from those of the past. In a floating exchange rate regime, the exchange rate risk is in the market, so those who bring hot money carry the exchange rate risk. The prolongation of the maturities of public papers, the consolidation of economic fundamentals slow down the movements of hot money and have negative effects Reduces. From time to time, we witness that criticisms about your monetary and foreign exchange policy are missed. What is your opinion on this? First of all, it should be understood very well that the Central Bank has to take into account the whole economy while carrying out its policies and cannot produce policies according to a specific sector or sectoral problems. Then in the criticisms, style is important. People need to pay attention to the style they use when criticizing. Especially those who have held or have held important positions are also responsible for setting an example to society. Look at what has been written in recent years. The Central Bank does not deal with people with such style. Can there be an "opposition" from different quarters against the bank? Is it possible to categorize this? facade" Since the beginning of this year, we have been saying it continuously in various speeches and interviews. One of these groups does not want interest rates to fall for a long time, but instead of saying this openly, it constantly tries to disrupt the waits. According to them, the fight against inflation should not be given so much importance, in 2001 7 It has been said  there will be no floating exchange rate regime, no growth with tight fiscal policy, no  no  monetary reform cannot be carried out, it will go on like this. Another section constantly emphasizes the exchange rate. According to this group, the Turkish currency is overvalued. There are always different opinions about how overvalued it is. When you look at this segment, you see that despite the progress made in stability, they still keep their assets in banks or vaults at home or in foreign currency abroad. It is possible to say that these groups are in opposition to the stabilization program because of the damages they have suffered. Do you think the public is adequately prepared in the era of implicit targeting and is prepared for the deficit inflation targeting of 2006? Since 200l, we have stated it both in our press releases, in our speeches and in our publications on monetary policy. There is nowhere else to go as a monetary policy regime. When we started to implement implicit inflation targeting in 2002, the conditions for explicit inflation targeting had not yet been established. Financial dominance was high, the financial system was not strong enough. We told them about it. The conditions did not exist and therefore we said that we are applying implicit inflation targeting. In fact, this process was the convergence process to the open inflation targeting. We then anticipated a gradual transition to open inflation targeting. This was also necessary for the formation of economic conditions and the preparation of public opinion. Within the scope of this gradual transition, since the beginning of 2005, the meetings of the Monetary Policy Committee have been held at the predetermined date and time. Interest rate decisions, as it is known, are announced after these meetings and at 9 o'clock, taking into account the views at the meeting, and then an "Inflation and Outlook" report is published explaining the reason for the decision. In preparation for clear inflation targeting, these are important changes. 8 There will be other changes in 2006 along with clear inflation targeting. But not all the details of the elements of clear inflation targeting have yet been clarified. This will be announced in December. Do you think the 5'1 percent level is a "threshold" in terms of inflation? Many opinions have been put forward regarding the threshold: various figures have been put forward. While the fight against inflation continued successfully, we were constantly told that "Now that the threshold has been reached, it is very difficult to reduce inflation further." However, the threshold in inflation occurs where there are expectations. Currently, both year-end and 12-month waits are in line with the targets. If there are developments that prevent expectations from getting better, such as a deterioration in the fundamentals of the economy, a disruption in the stabilization program and so on, then the threshold will appear. What about growth? When the first quarter figures were released in 2005, there was much debate about whether the economy was heading for a recession. At that time, we said many times in our monthly announcements that, given both the base effect and seasonality, the data that came out did not indicate a recession, in fact, the figures would be even lower in Q2, but would start to rise again from Q3. In the intervening time, growth indicators have confirmed us. On this occasion, I would like to underline that Turkey is moving towards a sustainable growth environment, but it is not there yet, and that structural reforms should be given importance in order to achieve a satisfactory sustainable growth rate. Do you find the rapid increase in housing loans and real estate prices in the last year "alarming"? 9 In this regard, I would like to underline three points: The first is that the increase in total loans affects domestic demand; It is important that domestic demand follows a controlled course in the coming period. We are closely following the developments here. The second point The ratio of housing loans to national income in our country is still far behind developed countries and many European countries. This rate will increase further with the progress made in the normalization process in the economy. Mortgage-based housing financing, also known as mortgages, will have an important role in this process. Finally, it may be the case that the recent rapid growth in the construction sector will increase the supply of housing and slow down this demand-driven rise in prices. We are watching carefully in terms of these three points. Do you think there is a bloating in real estate prices? At what point is the increase in housing loans and real estate prices disturbing for the Central Bank? It is not yet possible to say that there is a bulge for today. On the other hand, if the increase in real estate prices becomes a threat to inflation by affecting domestic demand, it will be disturbing for the Central Bank. At that stage, there is no doubt that the Central Bank will share its opinion on this issue with the public. Work on the infrastructure of the mortgage is accelerating. As a monetary authority, do you think this will work effectively in the current circumstances? For years we have said that the development of derivatives and long-term markets and instruments is delayed due to high inflation and the uncertainty it creates. As inflation falls, as the general level of interest rates reaches reasonable levels, these markets are finally beginning to develop. In February 2005, the Futures and Options Market began operating. The volume of transactions is gradually increasing. 10 In order for mortgage markets to work effectively, the supply of long-term funds needs to increase, the transaction volumes at these maturities and the market depth need to increase. As more progress is made in stability and more progress is made, these markets will also work effectively and will make a great contribution to the deepening of our country's financial markets. What are the main risks for inflation in the coming period? We are already putting the main risks related to inflation in our monthly "Inflation and Outlook" announcements. As mentioned there, under conditions where income policies in line with the tight fiscal and inflation target are on track, it is important that the increase in domestic demand is controlled and that the reform process does not lose momentum. In this context, the non-disruption of expectations is another risk factor that comes to the fore considering the significant impact of expectations on inflation. Movements in oil prices, price rigidities in the services sector will have an impact on the course of inflation. In addition, agricultural and raw material prices that are out of our control are always risk factors. Due to the developments in international markets, do you see it as likely that global liquidity conditions will continue as they are? Developments in global liquidity vary largely depending on developments in interest rates in the US and Europe. As long as we, as a country, do our homework well and take steps to ensure macroeconomic stability, we will be less affected by negative developments in liquidity conditions. When we compare it with the past, it is obvious that the Turkish economy is at a very different point today. The fundamentals of the economy are stronger today. The Turkish economy has undergone a structural transformation. 11 As of August, the total amount of "net errors and shortcomings" for the last year reached 9.3 billion. How should such a high error item be explained? Although the net error deficiency (NHN) item is perceived as high in annual cumulative terms, it is seen in our comparisons with other countries that NHN is not high when we look at it as a ratio of GN. In this pen, many minus and plus elements already drive each other in the long run. We have also put a study on the subject on our website. The main sources of the NHN item are the inability to fully monitor the foreign exchange assets of the non-banking private sector, the movement of goods in imports and exports and the fact that the payment may be in different balance sheet periods, the differences in declarations related to customs procedures, the acquisition of tourism and suitcase trade through surveys. differences arise. In addition, we see that the NHN item tends to give a positive balance in periods of reverse money substitution and relative stability, and a negative balance in times of crisis and instability. In other words, there is a relationship between reverse money substitution and NHN. The increase in the NHN item in the recent period is; As a result of the increased confidence, it confirms the private sector's ability to bring foreign assets from abroad or under the pillow into the country, that is, the capital inflow. Will the policy of increasing foreign exchange reserves continue? Yes. The ratio of reserve to external debt is still not at the desired level, but low. In addition, as we have stated many times, as the Central Bank, we want to get rid of our high-cost obligations over time. The Central Bank was losing money because of one of these costly obligations: remittance accounts. You have continued to reduce the interest rates on these accounts. Is the damage still going on? 12 Although the Central Bank has been gradually reducing the interest rates on labor remittances since 2002, since these accounts have maturities of up to 3 years, it was only possible for the interest burden on us to begin to decrease with the year 2005. From 2006 onwards, the damage will be visibly reduced. Within the framework of the Central Bank's reserve management, in which currency are foreign exchange reserves kept? The euro? Dollar? Is there a tendency for a prospective preference in this regard? Since now, it has been held in about 2/3 of the European currency and l/3 of it in the US dollar and other currencies. Because the proportions of our obligations are like this. There is detailed information on our website. For the excess position in foreign currency, the expected foreign exchange inflows and outflows of the Treasury are taken into account. Will there be a difference in exchange rate policy during the open targeting period? The floating exchange rate regime is one of the main elements of open inflation targeting. Under this regime, no commitment is made to the level of the exchange rate. In the open inflation targeting regime, you should not make any commitments other than inflation. The stability of the exchange rate is of course important, but it must be considered within the framework of financial stability and general stability. In other words, the exchange rate policy will continue in the same way. 13
text_original: BAKAN SERDENGET' NN 21-22 KASIM 2005 TARHLERNDE RADKAL GAZETESNDE YAYIMLANANMLAKATI Kamuoyunda, grev srenizin dolmasyla ve yeniden atanp atanmayacanzla ilgili olarak tartmalar var. text: REMARKS DELIVERED BY GOVERNOR, SuREYYA SERDENGEcT 19 MARCH 2001 As a consequence of the financial turmoil in the financial markets in the second half of November 2000, substantial increases in interest rates were observed and the high foreign exchange demand resulted in the 6 billion USD fx reserve erosion of the CBRT in the period between 22 November and 5 December. The support of the international financial institutions together with the enhancement of the policies described in the context of the program contributed to the partial establishment of financial tranquility and the fx reserves of the CBRT increased by the amount of 5 billion USD in the following period. However, the financial turmoil that was experienced in late November increased the fragility of the banking sector building on the before-crisis existing structural deficiencies. The sharp increases in interest rates had a negative impact on the financial structure of the state-owned banks and some private banks, which in turn increased the structural deficiencies in the banking sector significantly. The unfavorable developments preceding the Treasury auction in February resulted in the complete depletion of the credibility of the program and brought about a serious attack against the Turkish lira. Consequently, faced with an FX demand of 7.6 billion USD at one-day value, the CBRT responded by squeezing the TL liquidity. The result of the general liquidity deficiency in the system together with the excessive daily liquidity needs of the state owned banks resulted in the complete non-intermediation of the payments system. Under these circumstances, considering the potential negative impact of defending the existing exchange rate policy on the economy, the previous exchange rate policy framework was abandoned in favor of a floating exchange rate regime. The program implemented in the year 2000 included an exchange rate policy framework foreseeing a widening band around the central exchange rate path starting from mid-2001 and finally ending up with a floating exchange rate regime at the end of the third year after the attainment of single digit inflation rates. However, as a consequence of the loss of confidence in the financial markets, the abandonment of the former exchange rate policy framework and the introduction of a floating exchange rate regime appeared as a compulsory action. The Central Bank has carried out a number of operations under the new floating exchange rate regime in order to reestablish the smooth functioning of the financial markets. In this respect, the demand for Turkish lira has been met after February 26 to reestablish a healthy payments system. Following the Central Bank funding that met the financial markets demand for liquidity, the interest rates that reached 2000 percent per annum in simple terms during the crisis fell down to 80 percent level. In this operational framework, CBRT favored providing the banking system with the necessary sources to meet their foreign liabilities without any delay through the use of fx depos. Recently, the foreign exchange market has calmed down. Nevertheless, the equilibrium in the foreign exchange market has not been attained due to shallow transaction volume. The CBRT will continue to provide the necessary fx liquidity that will allow banking system to meet their foreign liabilities. However, it does not make any commitment about the level of the foreign exchange rate. In the following period, CBRT will give priority to reestablishing the financial stability. Accordingly, CBRT will carry its operations in line with this objective. At this stage, it will be useful to give some information about the operations concerning the state-owned banks. Currently, state-owned banks are facing a need for making a substantial volume of overnight borrowing due to their structural problems. The overnight borrowing requirement of the state-owned banks that reaches approximately 17 quadrillion Turkish lira prevents the attainment of the equilibrium level in interest rates and limits the extent that the monetary policy can be implemented. This problem, which continuously feeds up the fragility in the financial market, has a priority. In order to solve this problem, the Treasury will give bills and bonds to the state-owned banks in order to cover their duty losses. Within the framework of a predetermined program, state-owned banks will reduce their overnight liabilities to the banking and non-banking sectors with the help of the liquidity provided by CBRT through repurchase agreements or direct purchases via these bonds and bills. In addition, CBRT and Treasury will withdraw the increasing liquidity via reverse repurchase agreements and direct sales of bonds and bills. In the forthcoming period, CBRT will give priority to the control of monetary aggregates to reduce the inflationary pressures in the economy. However, in practice, the efficiency in the functioning of the payments system and the foreign exchange markets will also be considered. In the implementation of monetary policy, Net Domestic Assets and Net International Reserves figures will be followed and the inflationary expectations will be influenced through the monetary aggregates. CBRTs interventions in the foreign exchange market will only be directed towards dampening the excessive volatility in the foreign exchange rates and increasing the smooth functioning of the market. However, CBRTs intervention will not restrict market forces in determining foreign exchange rates. On the other hand, the new Central Bank Law draft will be submitted to the parliament in the near future. In this draft, the primary objective of the Central Bank is foreseen as to establish the price stability. The draft will also include the establishment of a Monetary Policy Committee that would be responsible for designing and implementing the monetary policy, the revisions about the procedures of designation and resignation for the positions in the governing bodies of CBRT and many other changes. In addition, accountability and transparency in the monetary policy implementation will also be enhanced. As part of this practice, periodic reporting system will be introduced. With the establishment of stability in the markets, the monetary policy will be directed towards the price stability. In the medium term, CBRT will introduce the inflation-targeting regime after providing the necessary initial conditions. As emphasized by the Minister, Turkey is obliged to overcome the inflation. The primary source of many problems observed in the society has been the high inflation experienced in the last 20 years that directed the society towards speculative behavior. We will overcome this problem in complete harmony with the government and with the support of a strong fiscal policy.

Title: Anadolu Agencys Interview with Governor Murat etinkaya
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Anadolu Agencys Interview with Governor Murat cetinkaya 14 February 2019 Anadolu Agencys Interview 14 February 2019 How do you assess recent developments in the global economy? How important is the role of global developments in designing current policy framework? Global developments affect the economy through various channels, particularly finance and trade. Recently, financial markets have been relatively calm; nevertheless, the slowdown in global growth and concerns over trade policies may curb the risk appetite. We assess all these developments and the possible risks in the formulation of our monetary policy response. I should emphasize that the critical point is to boost the economys resilience against external shocks. From this point of view, we believe that strong adherence to macroeconomic policy coordination is crucial. The recent policy mix is a reflection of this awareness. We believe that the most important contribution of the Central Bank of Turkey to this process will be to maintain the focus on price stability. In your presentation at the latest Inflation Report Briefing, you stated that the Central Bank will maintain the tight monetary policy stance until inflation outlook displays a significant improvement. How should we interpret this statement? We have to see a sustained improvement in the indicators related to underlying trend of inflation and overall pricing behavior. That means, one-off base effects or external cost factors leading to a change in relative prices, would not be enough to declare a significant improvement. We have to observe simultaneous improvements in various trend indicators and pricing behavior. In this context, with a forward-looking perspective, we closely monitor micro data on pricing behavior and expectations formation. Achieving a significant decline in inflation in a short period is crucial for the improvement in expectations and pricing behavior. Establishing the monetary policy framework and the policy stance with this determination will surely contribute to disinflation process through the expectations channel. Views on the course of the economic activity display heterogeneity in the current context. How is your assessment on the potential growth of the economy and developments in the economic activity for the upcoming period? We need to differentiate between short-term cyclical developments and long-term structural dynamics in addressing the concept of potential growth. Recent deceleration in the economy largely reflects cyclical developments. It is important first to maintain the rebalancing process through coordinated policies, and then to support this process by structural policies that will bring lasting improvement. The recent steps reflect this perspective. The ongoing efforts in structural areas will support a stable and sustainable growth path. What is your evaluation on the relation between the monetary policy stance and the economic activity? The determined stance towards price stability supports a balanced growth in current conditions. The coordinated policies implemented to reduce inflation uncertainty contribute to the decline in risk premium, thus improve the Turkish lira-denominated stable funding facilities, and lower longterm interest rates. This, in return, supports the recovery in economic activity and investments. The decisive monetary policy stance has supported the decline in long-term interest rates since September. Increased predictability in pricing will improve financing conditions and further extend maturities, contributing to the advancement of the economy on a sound path. 1 Anadolu Agencys Interview 14 February 2019 In the period ahead, can we expect steps from the CBRT regarding financial stability? How should we interpret the interaction of these steps with the monetary policy? A sound functioning of the financial system is key to the effectiveness of monetary policy. We assess that, in the current context, maintaining a strong focus on price stability improves predictability and supports financial stability. Effective functioning of financial intermediation is important in terms of both monetary transmission mechanism and a balanced and efficient distribution of resources. Accordingly, the Central Bank employs its liquidity and reserve requirement tools when needed. In this sense, we think that the various steps taken last year proved effective in alleviating market volatilities and strengthening the transmission mechanism. In view of cyclical conditions, liquidity steps can be taken to support financial stability. These tools and associated steps do not have a direct signal with respect to the monetary policy stance. It would be more appropriate to evaluate liquidity-related practices within the context of financial transmission. Our stance on the monetary policy is clear; the tight stance will be maintained until we observe a significant improvement in inflation dynamics. How do you evaluate the rapid correction in the current account balance? We have been observing a rapid contraction in the current account deficit after the economic rebalancing became evident by mid-2018. Part of the correction in the current account balance is due to the economic slowdown. However, it should be emphasized that the strong course of exports and tourism revenues has also supported the rebalancing process in the recent period. In other words, the improvement cannot only be attributed to weak domestic demand. Supporting the improvement in the current account balance with structural measures will contribute to a balanced growth and price stability in the long run. In particular, structural steps to boost productivity and competitiveness are important. Reinforcing savings and financial awareness is critical to ensure a lasting improvement in the current account balance. Moreover, macroprudential measures encouraging prudent borrowing would support this process. Looking ahead, we will maintain our efforts to ensure further focus on these issues. 2

Title: Speech at the "International Risk Management Summit"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey 1. INTERNATIONAL R SK Y85NET M Z RVES ANGLE TOPIC MASI March 7, 2007, Istanbul Today, I am very pleased to be with you at the opening of the "International Risk Management Summit". I would also like to thank Active Academy for organizing this meeting and all those who have worked in the organization. Firstly, I would like to express that it is of particular importance for us as the Central Bank that the issue of risk management is raised in such a meeting where different sectors and institutions are represented. The progress made in the last year to achieve price stability and therefore macroeconomic stability can only be taken further and permanent with the steps to be taken at the micro level. In the formulation of this microframework, modern risk management principles serve as a guide for all economic units. Effective risk management requires that all relevant sources of risk are identified and included in the dataset with appropriate escalation. Otherwise, failure to be aware of the risks and not to calculate them well can lead to large losses1. In our country, either the aforementioned crises have been renewed, both in the reasons for the emergence of the crises and in the large costs caused by these crises, the lack of effective risk management in both the public and private sectors has a great impact. The importance of macroeconomic stability is extremely important in effective risk management, in establishing markets where risk can be managed, in implementing legal regulations, in short, in the formation and adoption of a risk culture in the modern sense in economic units and society. The leading element of macroeconomic stability is price stability. Either the aforementioned experience or the academic writing, an environment in which there is no price stability, in particular, creates the greatest source of uncertainty in social life in general, in the economy. 1 Hildebrand, P. (Member of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Sweden). 2006. "Risk Management". 1 Guests in Turkey At this point, I would like to go briefly to the concepts of uncertainty and risk. risk, which has many definitions in economic literature and in daily use, is in a simple way; it can be expressed as "the situation that can be calculated by numerical probabilities". Therefore, risk is a predictable, calculable and measurable concept, and markets exist to manage this risk. Uncertainty is a different concept than risk.2 Uncertainty; it cannot be measured, calculated and predicted. Its effects can occur in all areas and in many different forms. Therefore, it is also possible to manage uncertainty and avoid its negative effects. Therefore, inflation, which is a source of uncertainty, is a significant obstacle to the arrival of effective risk management. Inflation and inflationary volatility disrupt the relative price structure by affecting the pricing behavior of firms; prevents prices from acting as signals. In such an environment, it is almost impossible to make healthy investment and consumption decisions and to achieve the desired results in the decisions taken. Resources in the economy cannot be used efficiently. A growth process is observed with a high and low scale. Permanent employment cannot be guaranteed. This uncertain process in the economy leads to negative consequences in the social and political sphere; society's confidence in the future is shaken. High inflation is again the biggest obstacle to the arrival of well-functioning financial markets, which are the prerequisite of effective resource and temperance in free market economies, and to fulfill their intermediary duties in a healthy manner. With the uncertainty of the reference point or nominal anchor required for long-term pricing and decision-making, the maturities in the markets are shortened and predictability decreases. In such an environment, it is extremely difficult for both the financial and real sectors to implement effective risk management. The thirty-year-old chronic, highly inflationary process in the Turkish economy is the most concrete proof of this situation. 2 Knight, F. 1921. d2Risk, Uncertainty and Profitd3. 2 In the inflationary process that started in the second half of the 1970s in the Turkish economy, annual inflation was real at an average level of 60 percent, while inflation exceeded 100 percent in periods or anmi ; the volatility in inflation is 25 points. As a result of this process, the average annual growth between 1976 and 2001 is around 3.5 percent, and the volatility in growth is 5.1 points. The inflationary environment also negatively affects the competitiveness of our country with the uncertainty it has created. The devaluations have increased its competitiveness and Turkey's place in the global competition has lagged far behind compared to other countries. In this process, financial markets are deeply absorbed; long-term and financial risk management markets are not profitable. In such an economic environment, is it very difficult to fully apply modern risk management principles? Within the framework of fixed and/or predictable exchange rate regimes applied, the exchange rate risk is assumed by the Central Bank and economic units prefer the use of foreign currency in order to protect themselves from the uncertainty caused by inflation; dollarization increase ; The reputation of the Turkish currency is decreasing. De erli Guests, As the Central Bank, our aim with the fight against inflation is to prepare a healthy economic environment for economic units to make investment and consumption decisions by ensuring price stability. In other words, our effort to fight inflation is an effort to scratch the ground that has been decided. The distance taken in the last year in the direction of achieving price stability is very important. Inflation has fallen by 58.3 percentage points since the end of 2001, and volatility has decreased significantly. Efficiency in financial markets is increasing in parallel with the point reached in macroeconomic balances, including inflation; maturities are getting longer; investment tools are being pushed ahead. In this context, the derivative lems, which are an important tool of financial risk management in our country, gain an institutional structure and 3 The Options Exchange has made a certain distance in the fight against inflation; After inflation fell to single digits, it is also a coincidence that it was established in 2005. De erli Guests, The monetary and exchange rate policies implemented also play an important role in creating the appropriate environment for the effective effectiveness of risk management in our country. Overall, in addition to making price stability their main objective, central banks should also set well-defined numerical targets in the most economic structure and in the heat of increasing uncertainty profits; It is extremely important for them to be institutionally committed to achieving these goals and to explain their policies to the public in a clear manner with their results for predictability plus in the economy. In this context, the importance of the contribution of the inflation targeting regime to the increase of the predictable in the economy of the institutionalized and transparent in terms of risk management cannot be denied. Under the inflation targeting regime, which has been applied since 2002, first implicitly and in an open manner in 2006 and beyond, the predictable value of monetary policy has increased significantly. The Central Bank sets policy interest rates within the framework of a pre-announced calendar; The fact that the Monetary Policy Committee shares its grudging information and opinions on the economy through communication tools such as the Monetary Policy Committee meeting summaries and the Inflation Report and publishes numerical inflation forecasts covering a period of two years provides an important opportunity for better prediction of the direction of policy decisions and provides an important opportunity for economic units to manage their risks more effectively when making decisions. Subject to institutional and growing confidence in monetary policy, inflation targets are also increasingly being used by economic units as nominal anchors. When the results of the Expectations Survey conducted twice a month by our Bank are examined, it is noteworthy that even if fluctuations are seen from time to time, the inflation expectations of the economic units have converged to the target and the deviation from the average has decreased. In addition to the inflation targeting regime, the floating exchange rate regime that is being implemented has led to the adoption of risk management principles in the modern sense in our country. 4 contributed to the tour. Under this regime, the determination of the exchange rate in the free market under the conditions of supply and demand indicates that in addition to the increases in exchange rates, the rates are also low or anabilece. Therefore, unlike previous periods, exchange rate risk is now above economic units. This, as the Central Bank has expressed at every opportunity, makes the exchange rate a risk factor to be managed. On the other hand, the Central Bank defines the establishment of financial stability as a "supporting objective" and in this context, the Central Bank should take action in the financial markets and implement policies The increase in transparency also increases the predictability and confidence in these markets. De erli Guests, With all these things, as I have just emphasized, at the point where we have come to macro balances, the markets are influencing the market; A suitable environment is being prepared for the opening of new markets and the promotion of existing financial instruments. However, it is also possible to say that the distance taken is still sufficient. First of all, it is yet to have price stability. To put it another way, inflation is that I have just reached a level that economic units can neglect in their decisions. At this point, I would like to draw your attention to one point in particular. While we are coming from high figures to single digits in the fight against inflation, the increasing support of the i world and the public opinion over time has been one of our greatest helpers. The continuation of this deck is extremely important. Inflation should not be allowed to become an inertia at the levels it has reached today. The fact that inflation reaches our target level of 4 percent is at least as important as the distance we have taken in this area in the last year. Therefore, in the fight against inflation and uncertainty, one should never say "but". De erli Guests, It is very difficult to erase the traces of many years of macroeconomic instability and lost confidence in just one short period of time. This process takes time. 5 Similarly, risk management takes time to come and expand. During this time, a number of tasks have been carried out on both the financial and the real sector. In this context, the financial sector is expected to be more effective and innovative by observing the risk management rules in order to provide resources to the real sector. It is inevitable for the real sector to strive to make progress in the principles of risk management in the modern sense in parallel with the distance taken and targeted in the macroeconomic field under the conditions of global competition today. The fact that the real sector makes transparent balance sheets and defines the risks in their management is the first step to be taken in this regard. In addition, it is extremely important that they constantly focus on derivative instruments in order to effectively manage their risks in the most financial markets and that they closely follow what is happening in the world. In addition to financial risk management, the steps taken by firms in terms of corporate risk management will strengthen firms on the one hand and contribute to making the economy more resilient to profit by reducing the fragility of the economy. De erli Guests, In addition to our own ancestor steps within the country, it is becoming more and more important than in the past to exchange international information and ideas on risk management as it has been in our world most globally, and to establish common principles to the extent that borders have disappeared. In this context, I believe that the close cooperation of international boards and the creation of weighing environments such as the conference held here today will play an important role in producing complete solutions on complex issues such as risk management. I would like to take this opportunity to thank the organizers of this meeting again. 6
