Title: Speech on "Dollarization" at the Opening Ceremony of T.R. Anadolu University in Eskiehir
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey DOLLARIZATION / REVERSE DOLLARIZATION Sureyya Serdengecti October 3, 2005, Eskisehir DOLLARIZATION AND REVERSE DOLLARIZATION Dear Academicians, Students; Dear Guests, When we look at the distance we have made within the framework of the stabilization program, which has been implemented continuously for nearly four years, we see that the Turkish economy has made significant progress in the normalization process: Our economy has become more predictable and more resilient to shocks. In this whole process, we, as the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, did not only inform the public, the Turkish Grand National Assembly and the Government about the stability program or the economic conjuncture: We tried to bring up issues related to our economy, which are mostly known in academic circles, but have not been discussed much by large segments of society, from time to time and when necessary. We stated that concepts such as price stability, sustainable growth, sustainable employment growth, good governance, central bank independence and financial stability, which are well known in the economies of developed countries, are now important for our economy and should be known and discussed. In this context, today I will tell you about another issue that I think is important in this process, "dollarization / reverse dollarization". In this context, in my speech, I will first talk about what dollarization means, how and why it emerged, and its negative effects on economies. Then, I would like to explain where and how the exit from the dollarization process took place, in other words, reverse dollarization, within the framework of the examples of other countries. Finally, I will end my speech with the issue of where Turkey stands in the dollarization and reverse dollarization processes today. Dear Listeners, The concept of dollarization; It is under two main subheadings in academic literature. The first of these is full dollarization. Full dollarization is when a country completely abandons its national currency and uses a foreign currency as its official currency. If we consider the eurozone as a different example because it is a monetary union, I can say that there are only a few examples of small countries such as Panama and Ecuador for full dollarization. The second sub-heading of the concept of dollarization is partial dollarization, which constitutes the main theme of my speech today, since it is closely related to the Turkish economy. Partial dollarization; economic units in a country, high inflation 2 In order to protect the national currency from depreciation, it has started to choose financial assets denominated in foreign currencies instead of financial assets denominated in national currency. Partial dollarization comes in different forms depending on the reasons for its emergence and the specific conditions of the countries. These differences in practice require many dollarization definitions under the heading of partial dollarization. Now I would like to touch briefly on these definitions depending on the process of historical development. In the early economic literature, partial dollarization was associated with the dynamics of money demand, especially the concept of "money substitution" within the framework of the relationship between dollarization and inflation. In this context, dollarization or currency substitution used in the same sense from time to time is the use of foreign currency denominated assets in transactions as payment and account units. In general, it is seen that the first stage of dollarization develops in the form of "asset substitution", which is the use of foreign currency denominated assets as a means of accumulating value, and turns into money substitution with the chronic state of high inflation.1 On the other hand, the banking crises that have been frequently experienced in the recent past, especially in emerging markets, have added the concept of "obligation dollarization" as well as asset dollarization to the economic literature. Liability dollarization; is that all economic units in the country, including banking and the public sector, have a large amount of liabilities in foreign currency. On the other hand, in this process of historical development, both asset and liability dollarizations have been grouped under a single heading in the literature: "Financial dollarization". At the point reached today, financial dollarization; it is defined as the tendency of residents in a country to keep both their assets and liabilities in foreign currency.2 In fact, in open and financially free economies, financial dollarization is normal to a certain extent so that the sectors involved in foreign trade can be protected from foreign currency risk. 1 Armas, A. ve Webb, R. (2003). Monetary Policy in a Highly Dollarized Economy: The Case of Peru. (Editor: P.C. Ugolini, A. Schaechter, M.R. Stone). Washington: International Monetary Fund. 2 Levy-Yeyati, E. (2003). Financial Dollarization: Where Do We Stand?. Conference on Financial Dedollarization: Policy Options, IADB, Washington, D.C., December 1-2, 2003. 3 it is a phenomenon that must be met. In this context, financial dollarization; It plays a certain role in the integration of both goods and financial trade in economies with the world, the deepening of national markets and the diversification of instruments. However; The spread of financial dollarization to the whole economy, the fact that it is not protected from the risks it creates and the use of foreign currency becomes inevitable can also lead to the emergence of a structure that leads to imbalance in the economy. Real dollarization, which is the last definition I will mention, is another concept of dollarization in the literature as the indexation of domestic prices and wages to foreign currency. After making these definitions, in the next part of my speech, rather than expressing each concept of dollarization separately that I have just mentioned, I will briefly use the general expression "dollarization", and I will mean partial dollarization, which is a process that has also been experienced in our economy. Dear Guests, Dear Students, Now, I would like to touch on the issue of how and for what reasons the phenomenon of dollarization, which has been quite common in economic literature, especially since the 1990s, has emerged in a country. There are three main factors behind the phenomenon of dollarization: The first is macroeconomic instability, the second is the disruptions in the regulatory framework and the deficiencies in the market structure, and the third is the loss / lack of credibility, which occurs both as a cause and a consequence of the instability. In this context, I can say that dollarization is primarily a natural reaction to an unstable macroeconomic environment and reflects a desire to protect against instability. As both the economic literature and the examples of countries, especially Turkey, have shown, the primary source of macroeconomic instability is high and volatile inflation. In 2002, in my speech titled "Price Stability", which I made at the beginning of the process of fighting inflation, I explained in detail how much inflation damages the economy. As I mentioned in that speech, high and volatile inflation, in addition to all the other damages it causes to the economy, is also a very important determinant in the dollarization process in a country. High inflation environment; Since it leads to a decrease in the purchasing power of the national currency against foreign currencies, foreign currency is preferred in order to protect it from the decrease in purchasing power. 4 to be made. Especially in economies that have lived with inflation for many years, this effect is very pronounced. However, dollarization is not only associated with the level of inflation, as Ize and Levy-Yeyati noted in their 2003 study.3 Similarly, Armas and Webb explain dollarization in terms of the relative magnitude between volatility in inflation and exchange rate volatility. Within the framework of this approach, also called the "portfolio approach" in the economic literature, the driving force that strengthens dollarization is the relative relationship between the expected volatility in the real exchange rate and the expected volatility in inflation. If the volatility of inflation is high, that is, the purchasing power of the national currency is decreasing while at the same time it is unstable according to the purchasing power of foreign currencies; on the other hand, if the exchange rate regime tried to be applied is the fixed/predictable exchange rate regime, the residents prefer foreign currency. The relative volatility in question is; it also partly explains that even if stabilization programs are successful and inflation rates are reduced to reasonable levels, dollarization can continue afterwards. Portfolio approach; It concludes that fixed/predictable exchange rate regimes encourage dollarization with high inflation, while the duo of floating exchange rate regime and inflation targeting discourage dollarization. Dear Guests, In the economic literature, the high and fragile debt stock of the public sector as a result of high budget deficits is seen as another important cause of both macroeconomic instability and dollarization. As it is known, high budget deficits and fragile public debt dynamics cause the need for public borrowing to remain high on the one hand and increase the risk premium paid during borrowing on the other. In addition, countries where domestic savings rates are at a low level, as in our country, are forced to resort to external resources/borrowing and the increase in foreign currency denominated external debt also increases dollarization. On the other hand, high risk premiums, together with the tendency to low savings, adversely affect the competition conditions of the private sector in domestic markets. As a result, the private sector has been able to overcome the time 3 Ize, A., Levy-Yeyati, E. (2003). Financial Dollarization. Journal of International Economics, 59. 5 it is unable to compete with the public in debt markets and to obtain resources from within the country (crowding-out).4 This situation is becoming one of the reasons for dollarization, leading to a significant increase in the weight of foreign currency in private sector borrowing as well. Similarly, the problem of "original sin", a concept introduced to the economic literature by Eichengreen and Haussmann5 in 1999 and used abroad for countries that cannot borrow in terms of their national currencies and long-term, leads to an increase in the weight of external debt in foreign currency and thus contributes negatively to the dollarization process. On the other hand, as Levy-Yeyati stated in his 2003 study, the concept called "time inconsistency" in the literature is closely related to dollarization.6 Time inconsistency; is that governments tend to reduce their debt burden in real terms by creating surprise inflation after borrowing in a lower inflation environment. In a situation where the concern of "time discrepancy" is high, policymakers prefer to borrow in foreign currency instead of national currency, sending the message that they will not pursue policies that will lead to surprise inflation and that such a policy costs them as well. Therefore, the dollarization of the public debt can sometimes appear as a conscious choice of the public. The second factor that is effective in the emergence of dollarization is the disruptions in the regulatory framework and market deficiencies. The state guarantee/insurance for deposits in foreign currency is an example of this situation, especially when it is in a way to cover all deposits. In such a case, if banks go bankrupt due to companies that have lost their ability to repay due to currency risk and other reasons as a result of the financial crisis and devaluation, foreign currency depositors are protected against the risk of non-payment. Such a structure also raises the market value of banks, as it guarantees the value of foreign currency deposits on their balance sheets. For these reasons, the financial system or the banking system, the national currency 4 Levy-Yeyati, E. (2003). Financial Dollarization: Where Do We Stand? Conference on Financial Dedollarization: Policy Options, IADB, Washington, D.C., December 1-2, 2003. 5 Eichengreen, B., Haussmann, R. (1999). Exchange Rates and Financial Fragility, NBER Working Paper7418 6 Levy-Yeyati, E. (2003). Financial Dollarization: Where Do We Stand? Conference on Financial Dedollarization: Policy Options, IADB, Washington, D.C., December 1-2, 2003. 6 in the face of which foreign currency can be turned to more attractive sword applications; this encourages dollarization. Similarly; In regulations such as tax, penalty rate and market applications, the fact that the cost of trading with the national currency is higher than the cost of trading with foreign currency can also encourage the use of foreign currency, that is, dollarization. Dear Listeners, The macroeconomic instability I have just mentioned and the loss/lack of confidence in economic policies, which is a result of the incomplete regulatory framework, is the third factor I will explain among the reasons for dollarization. Monetary policy credibility eroded by high and chronic inflation; With the increasing risks related to the ability of the public to pay and the loss of faith in economic policies, it is extremely effective in the emergence of dollarization as an extension of macroeconomic instability. A loss of credibility, especially when combined with the moral collapse that develops as a result of regulatory failures and market deficiencies, can lead to significant dollarization.7 An example of this is the guarantee by governments against exchange rate risk and the moral collapse that ensues. In other words, economic units that think that they will be saved by governments in the face of possible large depreciations in the national currency may not act in accordance with the principles of risk management when borrowing in foreign currency. Since governments often do not directly and presupposedly explain that there will be no such bailout, the choice of a regime in which exchange rates are controlled can be perceived as an implicit bailout statement. Under these circumstances, a high level of foreign exchange reserves and fixed or predictable exchange rate regimes can encourage dollarization. Dear Listeners, Dear Students, All these reasons that constitute dollarization can also be evaluated as a whole. In such a situation, a weak institutional structure; macroeconomic instability plays a supporting role in the triple relationship between incomplete regulatory framework and loss of credibility. 7 Nicolo, G., Honohan, P. ve Ize, A. (2003). Dollarization of the Banking System: Good or Bad?. IMF Working Paper 146. 7 Good policies, the right rules and the resulting trust require strong institutions. More specifically, weak institutional structures increase the likelihood of governments intervening in markets, disrupt market functioning, and indirectly pave the way for dollarization. Studies show that the form and degree of dollarization between countries can be explained to a significant extent by the quality of institutions in these countries, the regulatory framework and the macroeconomic environment.8 Dear Listeners, After talking about the reasons for dollarization, we now come to the issue of the effects of dollarization on the economy. These effects are multifaceted. I want to evaluate these from two perspectives. First, I will address the relationship between dollarization and the vulnerabilities of economies. The experiences of both our country and other countries, especially Latin American countries where dollarization is high, show quite clearly that dollarization significantly increases the fragility of an economy. In fact, this result is that various segments of the economy; It is also easily reached by examining the financial sector, the public sector and the real sector. Let's start with the effects of dollarization on the financial sector. In particular, the Argentine crisis in 2002 and its impact on neighboring countries where dollarization is high have revealed how much dollarization can greatly increase the fragility of the financial system. More specifically, increased dollarization in the financial sector can increase financial fragility due to the risks associated with solvency and liquidity risk. In terms of the risks associated with the ability to pay, the main cause of fragility is the situation in which the national currency has lost a great deal of value. While this situation directly affects the balance sheets of the financial sector, it also indirectly affects the quality of the foreign currency denominated debt portfolio. To put it more clearly, where the financial sector has a large amount of foreign currency obligations, it has to be protected from exchange rate risk either by holding assets in foreign currency or by lending domestically in foreign currency. However, the issuance of domestic loans in foreign currency, on the one hand, transfers the exchange rate risk to the customer, while the other 8 Nicolo, G., Honohan, P. ve Ize, A. (2003). Dollarization of the Banking System: Good or Bad?. IMF Working Paper 146. 8 on the other hand, it increases the risk of non-payment in case of depreciation of the national currency; therefore, it adversely affects the quality of the loan portfolio. In economies where dollarization is widespread and continuous, the balance sheets of economic units are not only affected by the depreciation of the national currency. Fluctuations in the value of the foreign currency, which is widely used instead of the national currency, against other foreign currencies, that is, cross-exchange rate movements, also affect economic units significantly. For example; Latin American countries with high dollarization, because of the dominance of the U.S. dollar in their own dollarization, are not only the value of their own currencies against the dollar; They can also suffer losses from the fluctuation of the value of the U.S. dollar against other currencies.9 On the other hand, dollarization also shows its negative impact on the financial sector through liquidity risk. Liquidity risk in economies with high dollarization; In situations where crisis perceptions increase and there are fluctuations in the economy, the decrease in demand for national assets occurs with the conversion of deposits or national money kept under the pillow and in safes into foreign currency or their transfer abroad as foreign currency, or the recall of short-term loans. Therefore, if the foreign currency deposits are not sufficient for foreign currency assets, a liquidity shortage arises in the financial system. This shortage directly leads to a process that increases and triggers vulnerabilities in the economy. Dear Listeners, Dear Students, The negative effects of dollarization are not only observed in the financial sector. Similar effects are seen when looking at the public sector. As it is known, while the tax revenues of the governments are in the national currency; external borrowings are mostly made and domestic borrowings are sometimes denominated in foreign currency or indexed to foreign currency. Therefore, there may be incompatibilities caused by exchange rates. To put it more clearly; In cases where dollarization is high, the public has almost the same problems and faces similar risks as a company that has foreign currency debt but does not deal with foreign trade and therefore does not have foreign exchange income. 9 Hira, Anil ve Dean, James W. (2004) Distributional Effects of Dollarization: The Latin American Case. Third World Quarterly, Vol. 3. No: 3. Sayfa: 461-482. 9 Moreover, incompatibilities in the public debt can easily be reflected in the financial sector. Especially if there is a high percentage of public paper in the balance sheet of the banking sector, in other words, if public financing is provided through banks; The high rate of depreciation of the national currency adversely affects the sustainability of the public debt on the one hand and the ability of the banking sector to pay on the other. Therefore, problems related to the ability to pay in the public sector can also lead to problems of solvency in the immediate banking sector. In the context of the effects of dollarization on the fragility of the economy, the third and last section I would like to mention is the real sector. Looking at the real sector, I would like to underline two points within the framework of the relationship between dollarization on a firm basis and vulnerability. First, when we look at the pricing behaviors, it is seen that; In countries where dollarization is high, the transition effect of the exchange rate on prices is high. This situation, together with the widespread pricing in foreign currency and the continuous and permanent perception of the depreciation of the national currency, leads companies to frequently make price adjustments. The second is the effect of dollarization on firms' balance sheets. In this context, how firms balance their income and expenses in foreign currency on their balance sheets determines the extent to which they will be exposed to exchange rate risk. Both the experiences and the results obtained from the studies conducted in the literature show that dollarization on the basis of firms is a serious problem and that the real sector is significantly affected by the movements in the value of the national currency, especially in countries where there are no developed derivatives markets. Dear Listeners, After mentioning how dollarization negatively affects the fragility of the economy on the basis of segments, I would like to talk to you about the importance of the issue for central banks and monetary policy. In this context, I can say that the most important negative effect of dollarization for central banks is that it leads to instability in the demand for money and therefore makes it difficult to predict and control inflation. 10 Another effect of dollarization on central banks and monetary policy has to do with the chosen exchange rate regime. Depending on the chosen exchange rate regime, dollarization can neutralize monetary policy and reduce the role of central banks to providing foreign currency to the system. In fixed or managed exchange rate regimes, central banks defend a certain level of exchange rates and assume a great deal of exchange rate risk; It encourages dollarization both because it leads to the disregard of risk management principles by economic units and because the relative relationship between inflation volatility and exchange rate volatility is in favor of the exchange rate, in other words, the exchange rate is less volatile, especially in economies with high inflation. Dear Listeners, Within the framework of the dollarization relationship with exchange rate regimes, the selection and implementation of the floating exchange rate regime instead of the fixed/predictable exchange rate regime can be evaluated in two dimensions. First, the floating exchange rate regime plays a crucial role in preventing dollarization when implemented correctly and inflation can be kept under control through reliable monetary policies. Secondly, in economies where dollarization has started long ago and reached a significant level, the selection of a floating exchange rate regime may raise implementation problems and may complicate and delay the reverse dollarization process despite the fluctuating exchange rate. If there is also high dollarization in the floating exchange rate regime, the fragility of the financial system and the transition effect of the exchange rate on inflation can cause "fear of floating". This may lead monetary authorities to think that they should intervene in fluctuations in the exchange rate at all costs within the framework of their past habits. Dollarization in the presence of such fear; it can put decision-makers and policy practitioners in a trade-off between controlling inflation and therefore considering monetary policy, the fragility and transitional impact of the financial system. 11 Dear Listeners, Up to this point, I have drawn up a framework for what dollarization is; I explained the factors that determine dollarization, the effects of dollarization on various segments of the economy, and its interaction with monetary policy. Today, the focus of the debates on dollarization in the economic literature is active views on taking and combating dollarization, rather than passive views such as dollarization is a normal development in globalizing economies. In this context, I would like to share with you the process and solution proposals on how and when dollarization will be reversed. I believe that identifying problems in the way we have done so far will reveal where and how the solutions should be. However, I would like to immediately state that; the solution has to be twofold. In this context, the solution should include practices aimed at discourageing the use of foreign currency on the one hand and encouraging the use of national currencies on the other. Therefore, when considered from all angles, although it seems that it is quite difficult and costly to reverse the dollarization process, it can be said that the initiation and success of this process is closely related to three basic concepts: macroeconomic stability, elimination of market deficiencies, and consistent legal regulations and credible policy implementations. I would like to underline that the issues I will touch on in the next part of the speech, especially micro measures, should be evaluated within the framework of other country examples and should not be perceived as a solution proposal directly for Turkey. Dear Listeners, First of all, I would like to emphasize that ensuring macroeconomic stability is a prerequisite for the success of the reverse dollarization process. The most important point in the context of macroeconomic stability is the implementation of tight monetary and fiscal policies to combat inflation and the continuation of decisive policies to prevent inflation. In this context, the most important step initiating the reverse dollarization process is; preventing inflation, which is one of the main causes of dollarization; in other words, to ensure price stability, and 12 to maintain credible commitments by the authorities. In the meantime, I would like to point out that central bank independence is the most important factor in the credibility of commitments. As I mentioned before; The application of an implicit or explicit inflation targeting regime along with a floating exchange rate regime within the framework of monetary and exchange rate policies makes a significant contribution to the reverse dollarization process by reducing inflation volatility according to exchange rate volatility.10 As a result of leaving the exchange rate to fluctuate and the authorities openly saying that they have no commitments or targets regarding the level of the exchange rate and following a transparent policy in accordance with their discourse, the exchange rate is perceived as a risk factor. In such a case, creating foreign currency assets or liabilities for economic units is costly because the exchange rate risk is now on them. In this way, reverse dollarization in an economy is somewhat encouraged. Dear Guests, Ensuring price stability and applying floating exchange rates are prerequisites for the reverse dollarization process. However, country examples have also shown that the reversal of the dollarization process does not depend only on the fulfillment of these preconditions. In this context, I would like to talk about the important factors and country experiences regarding the effects of policies that can be implemented on both macro and micro basis on the reverse dollarization process. First of all, I would like to point out that in the examples of the country, the reverse dollarization process in the public sector is progressing faster than in the private sector. Therefore, the fact that governments act in national currencies as much as possible is an important step towards reverse dollarization. In this context, as Galindo and Leiderman noted in their 2003 study, Israel and Mexico are good examples of this practice.11 With the adjustments made to the composition of public debt in Israel, the entire public debt in 1985 was either 10 De la Torre ve Schmukler (2003). Coping with Risk Through Mismatches: Domestic and International Financial Contracts for Emerging Economies , Conference on Financial Dedollarization: Policy Options, IADB, Washington, D.C., December 1-2, 2003. 11 Galindo ve Leiderman (2003). Living With Dollarization and the Route to Dedollarization, Conference on Financial Dedollarization: Policy Options, IADB, Washington, D.C., December 1-2, 2003. 13 While it was indexed to foreign currency or denominated in dollars, in 2002 only 39 percent was indexed to foreign currency or denominated in dollars. 61 percent was converted into national currency. Similarly, in Mexico, more than 80 percent of total debt was denominated in foreign currency in 1995, while in 2002 this ratio was reduced to approximately 50 percent. In addition to the harmonization of monetary and fiscal policies implemented in this development, it is also important that the Mexican government takes an active role in the development of long-term markets that will provide borrowing in national currency. In reversing the dollarization process, practices aimed at eliminating market deficiencies and sound legal regulations can also be effective. A strategy proposed in the literature for this process is the "carrot-stick" strategy, which can also be called reward-punishment.12 According to this strategy, while increasing the cost of foreign currency denominated intermediation, on the other hand, measures should be taken to increase the attractiveness of the national currency. In this context, in the "stick strategy"; in general, there are regulations on capital adequacy ratios, deposit guarantee and the obligation to hold liquid assets. The success of this strategy depends on the deepening of national currency markets and the creation of alternative instruments in this context. Therefore, the "carrot strategy" requires measures to encourage saving and borrowing in the national currency. However, at this point, it should not be ignored that making the use of foreign currency more costly is not the best solution, it should be remembered that reverse dollarization is not a process that can only be carried out by law. While practices such as higher required reserves in foreign currency transactions and higher deposit guarantee premiums for foreign currency deposits help break dollarization, this time they can adversely affect financial intermediaries. Dollarization is a hedge method developed against the uncertainties brought about by the inflation environment. Therefore, eliminating the uncertainties that lead to dollarization is of great importance in solving the problem of dollarization without the need for strict legal regulations. The reverse dollarization process, in which reliability comes to the forefront, emerges as a result of the process of fighting inflation and stability. As the examples of Chile and Israel show, 12 Levy-Yeyati (2003). ). Financial Dollarization: Where Do We Stand?. Conference on Financial Dedollarization: Policy Options, IADB, Washington, D.C., December 1-2, 2003. 14 a sound monetary policy is required. But as the examples of Argentina, Uruguay and Peru show, sometimes, just a sound monetary policy is not enough. In addition to monetary policy, it is necessary to include practices that will encourage the use of the national currency and create confidence, as well as measures to eliminate deficiencies in the markets, as well as sound and consistent regulations. Dear Participants, In the part of my speech so far, I have talked about the processes of dollarization and reverse dollarization within the framework of the framework and country examples drawn up in the economic literature. Now, I will tell you about the stages that our country's economy has gone through in this process, where we have come and the possible developments in the reverse dollarization process. In this context, I would like to first mention how the dollarization process emerged in Turkey and then how this process began to reverse. As you know, the beginning of the inflationary process in our country dates back to the 1970s. A chronic inflationary process of nearly three decades and the crises that have taken place have led economic units to foreign currency to protect themselves from unexpected increases in inflation and devaluations. Especially in the past periods when hedging tools and markets in the modern sense could not develop, the easiest and most cost-effective way of hedging for economic units was perceived as investing in foreign currency. Some adjustments to the markets supported this process triggered by macroeconomic instability. From a historical perspective, it can be said that the introduction of foreign exchange transactions to the Turkish economy started with the applications of Foreign Exchange Convertible Deposits and Foreign Exchange Deposit Account with Letters of Credit in order to eliminate the foreign exchange shortage that emerged as a result of the oil crises in the 1970s. A reflection of the policies then put in place in the 1980s is that at the end of 1983, barriers to commercial banks transacting in foreign currency were removed and residents could have deposits in foreign currency. Since then, foreign exchange deposit accounts have been an important part of the broadly defined money supply. At the same time, the share of foreign currency assets and liabilities of the banking system has also begun to increase. 15 In 1989, the financial system was opened to the outside world in the process of integration with international markets. With the arrangements made in this context, the costs of transactions in foreign currency have been reduced. Since then, dollarization has continued despite the fact that the real rate of return of foreign exchange deposit accounts is lower than the real rate of return of assets denominated in Turkish currency. This indicates that political and macroeconomic instability are significant explanatory factors in the dollarization process. When we look at it today, it is very clear what kind of negativities the liberalization of foreign exchange controls and capital movements lead to without ensuring macroeconomic stability. The 1990s were a period in which the Turkish economy was exposed to intense capital flows accompanied by weak macroeconomic fundamentals, institutions and regulations. In this period, policies focused on different priorities rather than stability, structural reforms were not made, a loose fiscal policy was implemented, and the monetary policy of the Central Bank, which is not independent, was to adapt to this process and postpone a possible crisis as much as possible. As a result, inflation has risen to the level of 80 percent, and the need for public borrowing has risen to the level of 15 percent of gross national product. This structure made the economy extremely vulnerable to external shocks in an environment where capital movements were free, and the 1990s were a period when the Turkish economy frequently faced crises and turbulences. This period is also a period in which dollarization naturally accelerates. Dear Listeners, Dear Students As Savastano pointed out in his 1996 study on dollarization in the Latin American region, the replacement of the national currency with foreign currency is a gradual process.13 The national currency first loses its function as a means of accumulating value and enters the process of financial dollarization; and finally, it loses its function of being used as a means of exchange and money substitution occurs. In our country, dollarization has been realized gradually as a result of macroeconomic instability and incomplete market regulations. In this context, we see that the first stage of dollarization has been experienced in Turkey. In other words, foreign currency is used as the most valuable accumulation tool in our country. This situation is closely related to the concept called "Gresham's Law" in the literature. Accordingly, economic units hide good money, that is, foreign money; it removes bad money, that is, the national currency, by using it in payment and similar transactions. 13 Savastano, M.A. (1996). Dollarization in Latin America: Recent Evidence and Some Policy Issues. IMF Working Paper 96/4. 16 Dear Listeners, At the end of this process, as of 2001, Turkey has become one of the countries with the highest dollarization rate among the developing economies. To put it more clearly; The share of foreign exchange deposits in total deposits, which is one of the rates commonly used to measure dollarization, increased from 25.5 percent in 1990 to 57.6 percent in 2001 in our country.14 On the same date, in 2001, this rate was 49.3 percent in Romania, where dollarization is considered high, 46.8 percent in Russia and 47 percent in Peru. Dear Guests, After briefly reviewing the process from the 1970s to 2001 in this way, when we look at the last three years as of today, we see that the dollarization process is reversing. Although it has been stalled from time to time due to changes in perceptions of elections, wars and global liquidity and some developments in the internal and external conjuncture, the reverse dollarization process has begun. When we look at why this process has reversed in the last three years, we see that the picture is as follows: First of all, very important progress has been made towards ensuring macroeconomic stability. As a result of the stable monetary and fiscal policies and structural reforms implemented in the last four years, inflation has been reduced to single digit levels and significant gains have been achieved to ensure price stability. At this point, I would like to state that the Central Bank's achievement of independence with the amendment made to the CBRT Law in May 2001 was an important turning point. As I have always said, this change, which comes after thirty years of embarrassment, has been effective not only in the process of fighting inflation, but also in the process of reverse dollarization. The institutional structures of central banks and the independence of central banks in this context are shaped by the interaction of the preferences of the society, whether the policy implementers follow pro-inflation policies and the needs of the economy within the monetary policy process. Economic units determine their expectations in line with the targets only after they feel confident in the policies implemented. As it is known, the fact that economic units create their expectations in line with the targets ensures the realization of the targets set in the next stage. Therefore, independent central banks perform better in the fight against inflation because they are more reliable institutions that will not depart from the goal of price stability than other units in society. 13. Bu kapsamda, Bankamz, bamsz ve hesapverebilir olmamz erevesinde yaymlad, gerek basn duyurular ile gerekse para politikalar ve enflasyondaki gelimelerin yer ald raporlar ile hem ald politika kararlarnn uygulamasnda hem de uygulanan politikalarn sonularnn bildirilmesinde son derece effaf bir politika izlemektedir. 49. effaflk: Siyasal effaflk bal altnda amalarn, dier bir deyile mevcut uygulamamzda enflasyon hedefinin, net bir biimde tanmlanmasn ve belirlenmesini; para politikas effafl erevesinde uygulamalarmzda temel enstrmanmz olan faiz oranlarna ynelik aldmz kararlarn ve nedenlerinin veya benzeri dier hususlarn yazl olarak duyurulmasn; operasyonel effaflk kapsamnda piyasa mdahalelerinde ve para ve kur politikas uygulamalarnda kamuoyununbilgilendirilmesini; ekonomik effaflk 18 bal altnda ekonominin deerlendirildii, gemie ve gelecee ynelik tespitlerin yapld raporlarn yaymlanmasn ifade etmektedir. Ayrca, Bankamz, gerek nternet sitesinde yapt deiikliklerle gerekse dzenledii toplantlarla toplumla iletiim yollarn da gelitirmektedir. 50. Tm bu hususlar erevesinde ve son olarak Bamsz Denetim Raporu'nun da yaymlanmas ile birlikte, effaflk asndan Bankamz gelimi lke rnekleri ile ayn seviyededir. 19

Title: Speech at the Workshop on "Global Crisis and Turkish Economy"
CentralBank: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
text: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey The Global Financial Crisis and Its Effects on the Turkish Economy: How Did It Start, What Stage Are We At? Durmu Ylmaz President 27 December 2008 Ankara Esteemed Academicians, Dear Guests, Today, we have gathered here to discuss the reasons for the developments in the global economy and the effects of these developments on the Turkish economy from various perspectives. I congratulate everyone who contributed to the preparation of this workshop, especially the President of the Turkish Economic Institution Prof. Dr. Ercan Uygur and the valuable employees of this esteemed institution. I would like to start my speech with a brief summary of how the global financial crisis began. With the emergence of signs of a slowdown in the world economies at the end of 2000, the central banks of Europe and Japan, especially the United States, lowered interest rates by making a significant easing in their monetary policies. The loose monetary policies pursued in this period, on the one hand, created an inflation in asset prices, and on the other hand, encouraged banks to borrow at short-term and low interest rates and to make long-term loan placements, especially housing loans. For example, in the US and the European Union, the rate of credit growth increased rapidly and remained at double digit levels on a real basis for a long time. The expansion in the volume of loans in developing countries was more pronounced. In Central and Eastern European countries and the Baltic countries, the rate of increase in the volume of loans given to the private sector reached an average of 40 percent in real terms. The diversification of loans by banks in order to increase the demand for housing loans and the flexibilization of credit conditions also led to a rapid increase in the credit utilization rate, especially for consumers who are unlikely to repay. In this period, the expanding global liquidity supply and the low levels of long-term interest rates increased the demand for risky assets that offer high returns. One such asset was high-risk mortgage-based mortgage loans. These assets were securitized and re-marketed and widely traded within the global financial system. The trading volume of derivatives increased rapidly and reached astronomical levels. However, the fact that such securities do not have a liquid secondary market and cannot be adequately audited has prevented the risks from being priced correctly. The fact that the audit, regulation and information activities in the financial sector and the risk management of the private sector lag behind the rapid change in the business world are also excessive. 1 It paved the way for problems such as risk-taking, maturity mismatches and asset price inflation. Beginning in the second quarter of 2004, the U.S. Federal Reserve began raising interest rates in an attempt to contain inflationary pressures. Housing demand slowed down starting in mid-2005 and the increase in housing prices gave way to recession. In this period, payment difficulties emerged in all housing loans, especially variable interest housing loans. The reversal of the upward trend in housing prices also limited the ability of customers to close their loan debts by selling their houses. The payment difficulties that arose in housing loans since 2006 led to pricing difficulties in the securities issued depending on the loan returns. Investors have reduced their demand for asset-backed securities and trading papers due to the loss of confidence and have turned to less risky treasury papers. Financial institutions have begun to have problems collateralizing asset-backed securities they own to meet their short-term liquidity needs. The problems that initially emerged as liquidity crunch in the markets put these institutions in danger of bankruptcy with the fact that financial institutions wrote a high amount of losses on their balance sheets after a while. When we look at the current situation, we see that the problem that started in the subthreshold housing loans market has spread to other parts of the housing loan market and other financial markets over time and has reached a dimension that threatens financial stability. With the effect of the loss of confidence in the markets, financial institutions' attempts to close their positions and return to cash cause a sharp tightening in credit conditions. The bankruptcy filing of Lehman Brothers, one of the leading investment banks in the United States, in September showed that any financial institution, regardless of its size, could come to the brink of bankruptcy and even go bankrupt. As a result, the tension in the markets escalated, and with the effect of the deterioration in risk perceptions, financial institutions tended to be reluctant to lend to each other and started to demand higher risk premiums. The issuance of complex securities has come to a standstill and the risk premium in the private sector bond market has risen significantly. In developed countries, central banks and governments have been unable to ensure that the effects of financial turmoil on their economies are limited and that confidence is limited. 2 they have taken various measures to restore the environment. However, negative news about the financial situation of financial institutions, the continuing increase in losses and the fact that economic data were below expectations limited the effectiveness of these measures and caused concerns about financial stability and economic trajectory. In the 2003-2007 period, when liquidity conditions were favorable, countries with high external resource needs, and countries with unsound budget structures were the countries most affected by financial turmoil. In the light of these developments, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has gradually lowered its global growth forecast for 2008 and 2009 in its quarterly reports. Dear Guests, With the emergence of problems in the financial sector, the issue of a divergence in the growth dynamics of developed countries and developing countries was discussed for a long time both in the public opinion and among policy makers. In a period when globalization is gaining momentum and the growth cycles of countries are converging with each other with increasing foreign trade between countries, it has become clear that it is not realistic to expect a separation between countries. On the other hand, depending on the exchange rate regime applied, it is seen that countries are affected differently by both liquidity abundance and liquidity contraction. In other words, the divergence is experienced between countries that implement a fixed exchange rate regime and countries that implement a floating exchange rate regime. In this part of my speech, I want to address where the difference comes from. In the period before 2007, when liquidity opportunities were high, the central banks of the countries that applied the fixed exchange rate regime purchased the domestic foreign currency as required by the applied exchange rate regime and gave local currency to the market in return. As a result, the foreign exchange reserves of the central banks of these countries have increased at a high rate, while the money supply has grown rapidly due to the liquidity transferred to the market. Although central banks have tried to sterilize excess liquidity through regulations such as open market operations, they have often failed. 3 The increase in liquidity in the markets has reduced interest rates, led to a high increase in domestic investment and consumption expenditures, an overheating of the economy and, as a result, high increases in wages and prices of goods and services. To summarize, a country that implemented a fixed exchange rate regime achieved high growth rates during the period of liquidity abundance, but at the same time exposed to high inflation. In this period of liquidity abundance in international markets, developments for a country's economy that implements a floating exchange rate regime have shown some differences compared to economies that apply a fixed exchange rate regime. Since the fixed exchange rate regime was not applied in these countries, central banks did not intervene in the foreign exchange market to affect the level of exchange rates, limited the increase in the money supply, and prevented the expansion of domestic demand from getting out of control with the interest rate policies they implemented. As a result, in an economy that applies a floating exchange rate regime, as in an economy that applies a fixed exchange rate regime, there has been an increase in inflation rates along with economic growth; however, the relative increase in both growth and inflation has been more limited. To give a figure, inflation rates in countries whose currencies are pegged to the euro increased from 5 percent at the beginning of 2007 to 14 percent in mid-2008. A similar development has been seen in Middle Eastern countries that keep their currencies stable against the US Dollar, and inflation rates have increased by an average of 4 times. In the same period, the increase in the inflation rate in the countries where the floating exchange rate regime was applied was more limited than the increase in the countries where the fixed exchange rate regime was applied and increased from an average of 3 percent to 7 percent. Dear Guests; At a time of abundance of liquidity in international markets, I have tried to summarize how the exchange rate regime has made a difference in economies. A similar difference manifests itself in the current period of credit contraction. In countries that implement a fixed or managed exchange rate regime, central banks try to maintain the level of exchange rate or keep the exchange rate within a certain band by selling foreign currency against capital outflows. However, this has led to a significant reduction in reserves and an increase in the risk premium. For example, the Central Bank of Russia's international reserves have reached 110 billion US since August. 4 There was a decline in the level of the dollar. In addition, the foreign exchange sales of central banks lead to a sharp contraction of the money supply at home, the rise of market interest rates and the tightening of liquidity conditions beyond the prediction. As a result, there is a sharp slowdown in both economic activity and the rate of inflation. Compared to the fixed exchange rate regime, we see that the floating exchange rate regime gives the monetary authorities a significant flexibility. While the fact that interest rates are under the influence of the central bank and the appreciation of the local currency in periods when liquidity is abundant prevents overheating in economic activity, the controlled easing of interest rates and the depreciation of the currency in the period when liquidity is shrinking limit the extent of the contraction in economic activity. In other words, the floating exchange rate acts as a safety valve that prevents the economy from reacting excessively harshly in both directions to international liquidity conditions in an environment where capital flows are free. As a matter of fact, when we look at the world economies, it is observed that the countries that apply the floating exchange rate regime experience a more moderate decrease in both growth and inflation rates. Dear Guests; In order to understand the monetary policy decisions taken by the Central Bank in the face of the shocks faced by the Turkish economy, the nature of the shocks to which the economy is exposed must be analyzed correctly. In this part of my speech, I would like to address the difference in monetary policy applied by the Central Bank in response to the fluctuation in 2006 and the ongoing global turmoil. In the first months of 2006, domestic and international demand indicators indicated that both demands were strong. GDP growth in the second quarter of 2006 was 9.7 percent, while the domestic consumption growth rate of households increased to 8.8 percent. In this period, the annual increase rate of consumer loans in real terms exceeded 100 percent, while the rate of increase in housing loans increased to 400 percent, and the annual increase rate in total domestic loans reached 50 percent on an annual basis. In the said period, the export growth rate was both in US Dollars 5 The fact that it was at high levels both in terms of terms of real terms indicated that external demand conditions were also strong. In May 2006, international capital conditions changed to the detriment of developing countries. As a result, capital outflows from many developing countries, including Turkey, have been experienced. The new Turkish lira lost approximately 30 percent of its value. This, combined with sharp increases in food prices caused by the drought, has caused inflation to rise and inflation expectations to exceed targets. Inflation rates rose back to double digits, and in June 2006 year-end CPI expectations increased by 4.2 percentage points compared to the beginning of the year. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey issued an unexpected and strong monetary tightening response in order to prevent the capital outflow experienced during the May 2006 turmoil from having lasting effects on pricing behavior. Against this backdrop, short-term interest rates were increased by 400 basis points in June. As a result of the measures taken, inflation expectations were largely brought under control. Inflation was again converging to the path in line with the target. If the Central Bank had not implemented monetary tightening during this period, the inflation rate and inflation expectations would have reached higher levels. Dear Guests; In the current crisis, which started in mid-2007 and strongly affected the Turkish economy over time, we are facing a different economic conjuncture. Therefore, the policy reaction of the Central Bank in this period was different compared to 2006. One of the most important differences observed between the two periods is that the Turkish economy entered the international financial crisis with a relatively moderate domestic demand structure. To give a few examples, credit expansion in mid-2007 was around 15 percent in real terms on an annual basis  or less than a third of the increase in April 2006. The rate of increase in housing loans had decreased from 400 percent to 20 percent. Indicators such as growth rate and domestic durable goods sales were also more balanced compared to 2006. 6 The crisis, which emerged as a liquidity squeeze in the financial markets of developed countries in the middle of 2007, began to make itself felt clearly in developing countries in 2008. A rapid outflow of capital from developing countries has led to a significant depreciation of local currencies in Turkey, as in many other countries. During this period, the Central Bank did not feel the need to tighten its monetary tightening, unlike the May 2006 turmoil; on the contrary, it cut short-term interest rates by a total of 175 basis points in November and December in order to eliminate additional tightening in financial conditions. At the same time, it provided the necessary liquidity by starting to fund the market, took care that overnight interest rates were formed at levels close to the Central Bank's borrowing rate, and excessive interest rate volatility that may arise in the money market was not allowed. In this period, the decline in the rate of increase in food prices and the sharp decline in oil prices positively affected the inflation outlook. As a result of the slowdown in domestic demand, it is observed that the effect of the movements observed in exchange rates on inflation is limited. The recently announced data on domestic sales, production and confidence indices indicate that domestic demand supports the process of decline in inflation. For example, the annual real growth rate in domestic loan volume decreased to 15 percent. While the growth rate was 0.5 percent in the third quarter of 2008, the industrial production index shrank by 8.5 percent year-on-year in October. As a result of the spread of the crisis to all economies and its deep feeling, a sharp slowdown is observed in export and import growth rates, especially in recent months. Estimates made by international organizations show that developed countries will enter a recession in 2009 and that there will be a serious decline in the growth rates of developing countries. In the latest report published by the OECD, the prediction of a recession in 21 of the 30 OECD member countries next year indicates that the negative outlook in external demand will continue for a while. I find it useful to emphasize once again that policy interest rates are not determined according to the level of the exchange rate, but in order to keep inflation permanently within the path compatible with the target. The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey does not and has not had a practice of keeping interest rates high in order to reduce the exchange rate, which is summarized as "high interest, low exchange rate". In exchange rates 7 Although there were sharp rises in both the May 2006 turbulence and the recent financial crisis, the different monetary policy reactions in these two periods are the clearest indication of this. The Central Bank bases its monetary policy decisions solely on the medium-term outlook of inflation. Dear Guests; Most of the crises experienced in many countries in the past were caused by the continuous deficit of public finances and the unsustainable level of public debt. As a matter of fact, the recommendations of international organizations in this period generally focused on giving importance to fiscal discipline, cutting public expenditures and increasing public revenues. In the current period, we see that financial institutions are at the center of the crisis. High losses faced by financial institutions, even bankruptcies, reluctance to extend credit, rising risk premium, falling asset prices, such as problems such as consumer confidence and causing a contraction in demand. In developed countries, we can group the expenditure-increasing budget packages announced in this period into two groups. The first group of packages appeared in the first phase of the crisis in order to prevent financial fluctuations. The main goal of these packages was to help financial institutions that were experiencing liquidity problems or on the verge of bankruptcy. For example, the Federal Reserve has implemented programs such as Market Maker Loan Facility, Securities Futures Lending Facility and, finally, Private Sector Bond Financing Facility to prevent liquidity crunch in the futures financing market. Authorizing the U.S. Treasury Department to take over low-liquidity mortgage loans under the Troubled Assets Recovery Plan developed under the Emergency Economic Stability Act, and the action plans of many European countries covering the transfer of capital to financial institutions through the use of public resources when necessary, can be listed as examples of packages in the first group. The second group of packages began to emerge as the crisis began to spread from the financial sector to the real sector. These include increasing public spending to reduce economic contraction or credit support to the real sector. 8 It includes measures such as provisioning. The financial sector's severe credit crunch and falling asset prices are putting strong pressure on domestic demand. With such packages, it is planned to close the demand gap resulting from the private sector's reduction of consumption and investment expenditures with public expenditures and tax cuts. In the current environment, it is discussed that financial packages should be timely, large-scale, diversified, spread over the medium term, coordinated with other countries and, most importantly, sustainable in terms of public debt stock. When we look at Turkey in particular, we see the following picture. To date, there has been no need for a package of cash measures for the banking system in Turkey. The most important reason for this is that Turkey implemented a similar package after the crisis in 2001 and at the cost of placing a heavy burden on the public budget. In other words, many of the bailouts and regulations introduced by many countries for financial markets have already been implemented in Turkey after the February 2001 crisis. What is being discussed today is whether Turkey needs to prepare a package in the second group, which includes using public resources to revive the real sector or providing credit support to the real sector. Dear Guests; In the current environment, every country needs to make a very good social return and cost analysis of the package while preparing packages of measures to avoid recession. However, in the current environment where policies aimed at mitigating the effects of the global financial crisis are discussed intensively, it is seen that the returns of the policies considered to be implemented come to the fore and the social cost of these packages is ignored. The cost of expansionary fiscal policies is significantly determined by the level of real interest. In many developed countries with deep financial markets, whose local currencies are reserve currencies, expansionary fiscal policies can be financed cheaply, at least for now, and the increase in budget deficits does not create upward pressure on real interest rates. Thus, the societal cost of expansionary fiscal policies remains low in the short term. 9 The capacity of developing countries to implement similar policies is more limited. The implementation of policies to increase the budget deficit in countries where the opportunity to borrow from their own currency abroad is limited, where the financial sector is not sufficiently developed and where capital accumulation is insufficient, on the one hand aggravates the public debt burden and causes the risk premium to increase, and on the other hand, the credit facilities available to the private sector to shrink. Therefore, expansionary fiscal policies in these countries can actually have a narrowing effect on economic activity. Of course, in the current period of a serious slowdown in economic activity, developing countries need to take some financial measures. It is possible to relax the budget to a degree that will not disrupt the general balance of the economy and will not complicate monetary policies. However, it should not be forgotten that the field of action of many countries is quite limited compared to developed countries such as the USA, France or Germany. The success of the fiscal policies implemented depends on the existence of a sustainable public debt structure in the medium and long term. Otherwise, such policies will lose their targeted expansionary effect in the economy, on the contrary, they will increase the risk premium and interest rates, leading to a sharper decline in domestic demand. For developing countries, this danger is more apparent. A similar situation exists in many developed countries with high debt stocks. For example, the fact that the borrowing rates of countries such as Italy and Greece, which have a ratio of public debt to national income above the level of 100 percent, were 150 basis points higher in December compared to Germany, shows that there is a limit to expansionary fiscal policies even for countries in the Eurozone. Due to the compromise of price stability and fiscal discipline over a long period of time in Turkey, real interest rates have been relatively high and borrowing terms have been relatively short. This situation adversely affects the private sector's access to finance. The gradual decline in market interest rates and the extension of borrowing maturities in the post-2001 period are the result of the successful implementation of policies aimed at establishing price stability and fiscal discipline in this period. The ratio of loans extended by banks to the private sector to total deposits increased by 60 points to 80 percent in the period between 2002 and 2008, while the public sector increased to 80 percent in the same period. 10 The gradual decline in the share of debt securities by 35 points to 30 percent is the most striking example of expansionary-tight fiscal policy practices. For this reason, the relatively limited pace of expenditure increase that will lead to fiscal easing, supporting the effective functioning of the credit mechanism and focusing on measures to increase confidence will provide the greatest support to economic activity in Turkey. Provided that it does not conflict with its main objective of ensuring price stability, the Central Bank will continue to take its measures to limit the effects of problems in international markets on our economy in a decisive, measured and timely manner as before. In concluding my speech here, I would like to pay my respects to all participants. 11

Her ne kadar merkez bankalar ak piyasa ilemleri gibi dzenlemelerle fazla likiditeyi sterilize etmeye almlarsa da ounlukla baarl olamamlardr. 3 Piyasalardaki likiditenin artmas faiz oranlarn drm, yurt ii yatrm ve tketim harcamalarnn yksek oranda artmasna, ekonominin ar snmasna ve sonu olarak cretlerde, mal ve hizmet fiyatlarnda yksek artlar meydana gelmesine yol amtr. zetlemem gerekirse sabit kur rejimi uygulayan bir lke, likidite bolluunun olduu dnemde yksek byme oranlar yakalam ancak ayn zamanda yksek enflasyona maruz kalmtr. Uluslararas piyasalarda likidite bolluunun yaand bu dnemde dalgal dviz kuru rejimi uygulayan bir lke ekonomisi iin gelimeler, sabit kur rejimi uygulayan ekonomilere gre baz farkllklar gstermitir. Bu lkelerde sabit kur rejimi uygulanmadndan, merkez bankalar, kurun seviyesini etkilemek iin dviz piyasasna mdahalede bulunmam, para arzndaki art snrlam, uyguladklar faiz politikalar ile i talep genilemesinin kontrolden kmasna mani olmulardr. Sonuta dalgal kur rejimi uygulayan bir ekonomide, sabit kur rejimi uygulayan bir ekonomide olduu gibi ekonomik byme ile beraber enflasyon oranlarnda da art meydana gelmi; ancak greli olarak hem byme hem de enflasyon oranndaki art daha snrl olmutur. Rakam vermek gerekirse, para birimleri Euroya sabitlenmi olan lkelerde enflasyon oranlar 2007 ylnn banda yzde 5 seviyesinde iken 2008 ylnn ortasnda yzde 14 seviyesine ykselmitir. Benzer bir gelime para birimlerini ABD Dolarna kar sabit tutan Ortadou lkelerinde de grlm ve enflasyon oranlar ortalama 4 kat artmtr. Ayn dnemde dalgal kur rejimi uygulanan lkelerde enflasyon oranndaki art ise sabit kur rejimi uygulanan lkelerdeki arta gre daha snrl kalm ve ortalama yzde 3 seviyesinden yzde 7 seviyesine ykselmitir. Deerli Konuklar; Uluslararas piyasalarda likidite bolluunun yaand bir dnemde, uygulanan kur rejiminin, ekonomilerde nasl bir farkllk yarattn zetlemeye altm. Benzer bir farkllk kredi daralmasnn yaand mevcut dnemde de kendini gstermektedir. Sabit veya ynetilen kur rejimi uygulayan lkelerde merkez bankalar, sermaye k karsnda dviz satarak kurun seviyesini korumaya veya kuru belirli bir bandn ierisinde tutmaya almaktadr. Ancak bu durum rezervlerin nemli miktarda azalmasna ve risk priminin artmasna yol amtr. rnein Rusya Merkez Bankasnn uluslararas rezervlerinde Austos ayndan bu yana 110 milyar ABD 4 Dolar dzeyinde bir gerileme yaanmtr. Bunun yan sra Merkez bankalarnn dviz satlar, yurt iinde para arznn sert bir ekilde daralmasna, piyasa faizlerinin ykselmesine ve likidite koullarnn ngrlenin de tesinde sklamasna yol amaktadr. Bunun sonucunda hem iktisadi faaliyette hem de enflasyon hznda sert bir yavalama yaanmaktadr. Sabit kur rejimi ile kyaslandnda, dalgal kur rejiminin para otoritelerine nemli bir esneklik kazandrdn gryoruz. Likiditenin bol olduu dnemlerde faiz oranlarnn merkez bankasnn etkisinde olmas ve yerel para biriminin deer kazanmas iktisadi faaliyette ar snmay nlerken, likiditenin darald dnemde faiz oranlarnn kontroll olarak gevetilmesi ve para biriminin deer kaybetmesi iktisadi faaliyette daralmann boyutunu snrlamaktadr. Dier bir deyile dalgal kur, sermaye aknn serbest olduu bir ortamda ekonominin uluslararas likidite koullarna kar her iki ynde de ar sert tepkiler vermesini engelleyen bir emniyet subab grevi grmektedir. Nitekim dnya ekonomilerine baktmzda, dalgal kur rejimi uygulayan lkelerin hem byme hem de enflasyon oranlarnda daha lml bir azal yaand gzlenmektedir. Deerli Konuklar; Merkez Bankasnn Trkiye ekonomisinin karlat oklar karsnda alm olduu para politikas kararlarnn anlalabilmesi iin ekonominin maruz kald oklarn niteliinin doru analiz edilmesi gerekmektedir. Konumamn bu blmnde Merkez Bankasnn 2006 ylnda yaanan dalgalanmaya ve devam etmekte olan kresel alkantlara kar uygulam olduu para politikasndaki farklla deinmek istiyorum. 2006 ylnn ilk aylarnda yurt ii ve yurt d talep gstergeleri her iki talebin de gl olduuna iaret etmekteydi. 2006 yl ikinci eyrek GSYH bymesi yzde 9,7 olarak gerekleirken, hanehalknn yurt ii tketim byme oran yzde 8,8 seviyesine ykselmiti. Bu dnemde reel olarak tketici kredilerinin yllk art oran yzde 100n zerine karken konut kredilerindeki art oran yzde 400 seviyelerine ykselmi, yurt ii toplam kredilerdeki yllk art oran ise yllk bazda yzde 50 dzeyine ulamt. Sz konusu dnemde ihracat art hznn gerek ABD Dolar 5 baznda gerekse reel olarak yksek seviyelerde seyretmesi d talep koullarnn da gl olduuna iaret etmekteydi. 2006 ylnn Mays aynda uluslararas sermaye koullar gelimekte olan lkeler aleyhine deiti. Bunun sonucunda Trkiyenin de dahil olduu birok gelimekte olan lkeden sermaye klar yaand. Yeni Trk Liras yaklak olarak yzde 30 deer kaybetti. Bu durum gda fiyatlarndaki kuraklktan kaynaklanan sert artlarla birleerek enflasyonun ykselmesine ve enflasyon beklentilerinin hedeflerin zerine kmasna neden oldu. Enflasyon oranlar tekrar ift haneli seviyelere ykseldi ve 2006 ylnn Haziran aynda yl sonu TFE beklentileri yl bana gre 4,2 puan artt. Trkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankas, 2006 Mays alkants srasnda yaanan sermaye knn fiyatlama davranlar zerinde kalc etkiler olumasn engellemek amacyla beklenmeyen ve gl bir parasal sklatrma tepkisi verdi. Bu erevede ksa vadeli faiz oranlar Haziran aynda 400 baz puan artrld. Alnan nlemler sonucunda enflasyon beklentileri byk lde kontrol altna alnd. Enflasyonun, tekrar hedefle uyumlu patikaya yaknsamas saland. Eer bu dnemde Merkez Bankas parasal sklatrma uygulamam olsayd, enflasyon oran ve enflasyon beklentileri daha yksek seviyelere ulaabilecekti. Dolaysyla bu dnemde Merkez Bankasnn politika tepkisi de 2006 ylna gre farkl olmutur. ki dnem arasnda gzlenen en nemli farkllklardan bir tanesi, Trkiye ekonomisinin yaanan uluslararas mali krize, greli olarak lml bir yurt ii talep yaps ile girmesidir. Bu dnemde Merkez Bankas, Mays 2006 alkantsnn aksine parasal sklatrma yapma gerei hissetmemi; tam aksine finansal koullardaki ek sklamay bertaraf etmek amacyla ksa vadeli faiz oranlarnda Kasm ve Aralk aylarnda toplam 175 baz puanlk bir indirime gitmitir. Son dnemde yurt ii sat, retim ve gven endekslerine dair aklanan veriler yurt ii talebin enflasyondaki d srecine destek verdiine iaret etmektedir. rnein yurt ii kredi hacmindeki yllk reel art oran yzde 15 dzeyine gerilemitir. 2008 ylnn nc eyreinde byme oran yzde 0,5 olurken, Ekim aynda sanayi retim endeksi yllk bazda yzde 8,5 klmtr. Krizin tm ekonomilere yaylmas ve derinden hissedilmesi sonucu zellikle son aylarda ihracat ve ithalat art oranlarnda da keskin yavalama gzlenmektedir. Uluslararas kurulularn yapt tahminler, gelimi lkelerin 2009 ylnda resesyona gireceini ve gelimekte olan lkelerin byme oranlarnda ciddi oranlarda d yaanacan gstermektedir. Trkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasnn, yksek faiz, dk kur olarak zetlenen, dviz kurunu drmek iin faiz oranlarnn yksek tutulmas gibi bir uygulamas yoktur, olmamtr. Dviz kurlarnda 7 hem 2006 Mays alkantsnda, hem de son dnemde yaanan mali krizde sert ykseliler yaanmasna ramen, bu iki dnemde farkl para politikalar tepkisi verilmesi bunun en ak gstergesidir. Merkez Bankas, para politikas kararlarnda sadece enflasyonun orta vadeli grnmn esas almaktadr. Deerli Konuklar; Gemite birok lkede yaanan krizlerin byk blm kamu maliyesinin srekli ak vermesi ve kamu borlarnn srdrlemez dzeye kmasndan kaynaklanmaktayd. Nitekim bu dnemde uluslararas kurulularn tavsiyeleri genellikle mali disipline nem verilmesi, kamu harcamalarnn kslmas ve kamu gelirlerinin artrlmasna odaklanrd. inde bulunduumuz dnemde ise finans kurulularnn krizin merkezinde olduunu grmekteyiz. Finans kurulularnn kar karya kald yksek zararlar, hatta iflaslar, kredi kullandrmakta isteksiz davranlmas, risk priminin ykselmesi, varlk fiyatlarnn dmesi gibi sorunlar, tketici gvenini etkileyerek talep daralmasna neden olmaktadr. Gelimi lkelerde bu dnemde aklanan harcama artrc bte paketlerini iki grupta toplayabiliriz. lk grup paketler, finansal dalgalanmalar nlemeye ynelik olarak krizin ilk aamasnda ortaya kmtr. Bu paketlerin temel hedefi likidite problemi yaayan veya iflasn eiinde olan finans kurulularna yardm edilmesi idi. rnek olarak Amerikan Merkez Bankas Piyasa Yapcs Kredi Kolayl, Vadeli Menkul Kymet Bor Verme Kolayl ve son olarak da, vadeli finansman piyasasndaki likidite skkln nlemeye ynelik olarak zel Sektr Tahvil Finansman Kolayl gibi programlar uygulamaya koymutur. ABD Hazine Bakanlna Acil Ekonomik stikrar Yasas kapsamnda gelitirilen Sorunlu Varlklar Kurtarma Plan erevesinde likiditesi dk ipotekli kredileri devralma yetkisi verilmesi, birok Avrupa lkesinin, gerektiinde kamu kaynaklarnn kullanlmas yoluyla finansal kurululara sermaye aktarlabilmesini kapsayan eylem planlar, ilk gruptaki paketlere rnek olarak sralanabilir. kinci grup paketler ise krizin finans sektrnden reel kesime yaylmaya balamas ile ortaya kmaya balamtr. Bunlar, ekonomik klmeyi azaltmaya ynelik olarak kamu harcamalarnn artrlmas veya reel sektre kredi destei 8 salanmas gibi nlemleri iermektedir. Finans sektrnn iddetli bir kredi daraltmasna gitmesi ve varlk fiyatlarnn dmesi yurt ii talep zerinde kuvvetli bir bask yaratmaktadr. Bu tr paketler ile zel sektrn tketim ve yatrm harcamalarn ksmas sonucunda ortaya kan talep ann, kamu harcamalar ve vergi indirimleri ile kapanmas planlanmaktadr. inde bulunduumuz ortamda, mali paketlerin zamannda, byk lekli, eitlendirilmi, orta vadeye yaylm, dier lkeler ile koordineli ve en nemlisi kamu bor stoku asndan srdrlebilir olmas tartlmaktadr. Trkiye zeline baktmzda yle bir resim gryoruz. Trkiyede bugne kadar bankaclk sistemine ynelik bir nakit nlem paketine ihtiya duyulmamtr. Bunun en nemli nedeni Trkiyenin benzer bir paketi, 2001 ylnda yaanan krizin ardndan ve kamu btesine ar bir yk getirme pahasna uygulam olmasdr. Dier bir deyile birok lkenin finans piyasalarna ynelik getirdii kurtarma paketlerinin ve dzenlemelerin birou, Trkiyede ubat 2001 krizi sonrasnda zaten uygulanmtr. Bugn tartlan Trkiyenin ikinci grupta yer alan, reel sektr canlandrmak amacyla kamu kaynaklarn kullanmay veya reel sektre kredi desteinde bulunmay ieren bir paket hazrlamasna gerek olup olmaddr. Deerli Konuklar; inde bulunduumuz ortamda her lkenin, resesyondan kanmak iin nlem paketleri hazrlarken, paketin toplumsal getiri ve maliyet analizini ok iyi yapmas gerekmektedir. Ne var ki kresel mali krizin etkilerini hafifletmeye ynelik politikalarn youn olarak tartld mevcut ortamda, uygulanmas dnlen politikalarn getirilerinin n plana kt, bu paketlerin toplumsal maliyetinin ise gz ard edildii grlmektedir. Genileyici maliye politikalarnn maliyeti nemli lde reel faiz dzeyi tarafndan belirlenmektedir. Yerel paralar rezerv para niteliinde olan, derin finans piyasalarna sahip birok gelimi lkede, genileyici maliye politikalar, en azndan imdilik, ucuz bir ekilde finanse edilebilmekte, bte aklarnn artmas reel faizler zerinde yukar ynl bir bask yaratmamaktadr. Bylece, genileyici maliye politikalarnn toplumsal maliyeti, ksa vadede dk seviyede kalmaktadr. 9 Gelimekte olan lkelerin benzer politikalar uygulama kapasitesi ise daha snrldr. Kendi para biriminden yurt dnda borlanma imkan kstl olan, finans sektrnn yeterince gelimedii, sermaye birikiminin yetersiz olduu lkelerde bte an artrc politikalar uygulanmas, bir yandan kamu bor ykn arlatrarak risk priminin art gstermesine, dier yandan zel sektrn kullanabilecei kredi olanaklarnn daralmasna neden olmaktadr. Dolaysyla bu lkelerde genileyici maliye politikalar, esasnda iktisadi faaliyet zerinde daraltc bir etki yaratabilmektedir. Elbette iktisadi faaliyette ciddi bir yavalama yaand mevcut dnemde gelimekte olan lkelerin bir takm mali nlemler almalar gerekmektedir. Btede, ekonominin genel dengesini bozmayacak, para politikalarn zorlatrmayacak lde gevemeye gidilmesi mmkndr. Ancak birok lkenin hareket alannn, ABD, Fransa veya Almanya gibi gelimi lkelere oranla olduka kstl olduunun unutulmamas gerekmektedir. Uygulanan maliye politikalarnn baars, orta ve uzun vadede srdrlebilir bir kamu bor yapsnn varlna baldr. Aksi taktirde, bu tr politikalar ekonomide hedeflenen geniletici etkisini kaybedecek, tam aksine risk primini ve faiz oranlarn artrarak i talepte daha sert bir d yaanmasna neden olacaktr. Gelimekte olan lkeler iin bu tehlike daha belirgindir. Bor stoku yksek olan birok gelimi lkede de benzer bir durum mevcuttur. rnek olarak kamu borcunun milli gelire oran yzde 100 seviyesinin zerinde olan talya ve Yunanistan gibi lkelerin borlanma faizlerinin Almanyaya kyasla Aralk aynda 150 baz puan yukarda gereklemesi, Euro blgesinde olan lkeler iin bile genileyici maliye politikalarnn bir snr olduunu gstermektedir. Trkiyede uzun bir dnem boyunca fiyat istikrarndan ve mali disiplinden dn verilmesi nedeniyle reel faizler greli olarak yksek, borlanma vadesi ise greli olarak ksa olmutur. Bu durum zel sektrn finansmana eriimini olumsuz ynde etkilemektedir. 2001 yl sonras dnemde piyasa faizlerinin kademeli olarak gerilemesi ve borlanma vadelerinin uzamas, bu dnemde fiyat istikrarnn ve mali disiplinin tesisine ynelik politikalarn baaryla uygulanmasnn bir sonucudur. Bankalarn zel sektre atklar kredilerin toplam mevduata orannn 2002-2008 aras dnemde 60 puan artarak yzde 80 seviyesine kmas, ayn dnemde kamu 10 borlanma senetlerinin paynn kademeli olarak 35 puan azalarak yzde 30lar seviyesine gerilemesi genilemeci-sk maliye politikas uygulamalarna en arpc rnektir. Bu nedenle alnacak nlemlerin, mali gevemeye yol aacak harcama art ayann greli olarak snrl olmas, kredi mekanizmasnn etkin ileyiinin desteklenmesi ve gveni artracak nlemlere arlk verilmesi Trkiyede iktisadi faaliyete en byk destei salayacaktr. Merkez Bankas, fiyat istikrarn salama temel amac ile elimemek kaydyla, uluslararas piyasalardaki sorunlarn ekonomimiz zerindeki etkilerini snrlamak iin zerine den tedbirleri bundan nce olduu gibi bundan sonra da kararl, ll ve zamannda almaya devam edecektir.
